faqs.question: What is the AVANT™ (U)HPLC used for?
faqs.answer: It's a modular HPLC/UHPLC system, used either standalone with UV/UV-Vis detection or integrated with expression CMS for full LC/CMS analysis.

faqs.question: Do I have to choose between standalone and integrated at purchase?
faqs.answer: No, the modular, stackable design supports starting standalone and scaling toward integration later without replacing the core hardware.

faqs.question: What software controls AVANT?
faqs.answer: Mass Express, a dedicated software suite distinct from ClearPeak, which controls Advion Interchim Scientific's separate puriFlash purification line.

faqs.question: How does AVANT fit alongside other expression CMS sample inlets?
faqs.answer: It's one of five confirmed interfaces, alongside Plate Express, ASAP, Touch Express, and vAPCI, all capable of interfacing simultaneously so workflows can switch without reconfiguring the system.

faqs.question: How do I choose between manual and automated UHPLC configuration?
faqs.answer: Match your throughput and budget requirements; the modular design covers everything from simple manual injection HPLC to fully automated UHPLC.

faqs.question: Can AVANT analyze air-sensitive or volatile samples?
faqs.answer: Not directly on its own, but paired with ASAP or vAPCI within the same expression CMS ecosystem, air-sensitive and volatile compound analysis are both confirmed.

faqs.question: What is the relationship between Advion and Interchim?
faqs.answer: Advion Interchim Scientific is the market-facing name of a marketing and distribution partnership between Advion, Inc. (US) and Interchim SAS (France), two separate companies.

faqs.question: Does AVANT support UV/Vis detection without mass spectrometry?
faqs.answer: Yes, standalone operation with UV or UV/Vis detector options is a fully confirmed, independent configuration.

faqs.question: What is the price of the AVANT™ (U)HPLC in India?
faqs.answer: The price depends on your configuration, standalone or integrated, and your modularity level. Contact Inkarp for a quotation once your requirements are confirmed.

faqs.question: Who is the authorized distributor of the AVANT™ (U)HPLC in India?
faqs.answer: Inkarp is the authorized distributor and service provider for the Advion Interchim Scientific AVANT™ (U)HPLC in India, providing demonstration, installation, training, AMC, spare parts, and technical support.

faqs.question: What is the expression® CMS used for?
faqs.answer: It's a compact benchtop mass spectrometer used for reaction monitoring, compound identification, and applications spanning teaching, food safety, environmental, clinical, and forensic analysis.

faqs.question: What sampling techniques does expression CMS support?
faqs.answer: From prep-free direct probe analysis using ASAP or iASAP, through Touch Express open-port sampling and Plate Express TLC reading, up to full LC integration via AVANT Modular (U)HPLC.

faqs.question: How do I choose between the two mass range options?
faqs.answer: Choose m/z 10-1,200 for most standard organic chemistry work, or m/z 10-2,000 if your compounds regularly extend into larger mass ranges.

faqs.question: How do I set up expression CMS for fast reaction monitoring?
faqs.answer: Use the direct probe sampling technique (ASAP or iASAP), which requires no sample preparation, for the fastest possible in-process check.

faqs.question: How do I switch between sampling techniques?
faqs.answer: Interfaces are designed to swap rapidly with minimal sample preparation; confirm your specific technique combination and switching workflow with Inkarp.

faqs.question: Is expression CMS suitable for a teaching laboratory?
faqs.answer: Yes, it's a confirmed application area, with a dedicated product note covering hands-on mass spectrometry experiments for teaching labs.

faqs.question: Can expression CMS integrate with liquid chromatography?
faqs.answer: Yes, via AVANT Modular (U)HPLC, providing full compound separation for samples that need it.

faqs.question: What applications is expression CMS confirmed for?
faqs.answer: Reaction monitoring, teaching chemistry, food safety and ingredients analysis, cannabis and hemp testing, environmental analysis, clinical diagnostics, proteins and peptides synthesis, and forensics.

faqs.question: What is the price of the expression® CMS in India?
faqs.answer: The price depends on your mass range option and sampling interface configuration. Contact Inkarp for a quotation once your application is confirmed.

faqs.question: Who is the authorized distributor of the expression® CMS in India?
faqs.answer: Inkarp is the authorized distributor and service provider for the Advion Interchim Scientific expression® CMS in India, providing demonstration, installation, training, AMC, spare parts, and technical support.

longForm.heroLead: Most labs need more than one way to look at a sample. A quick probe touch for a fast answer, and full chromatographic separation when the mixture actually needs pulling apart. expression CMS is built to do both on the same instrument. Switch between direct probe analysis requiring no preparation at all, and full LC-integrated separation, in the time it takes to change the sampling interface. Choose a system covering m/z 10 to 1,200, or extend to 2,000 for larger compounds. It's designed specifically around how chemists actually work: fast answers during reaction monitoring, straightforward enough for a teaching lab, and versatile enough to support food safety, environmental, and forensic analysis on the same platform.

body: Choosing a sampling technique is really choosing how much sample preparation your workflow can afford, and how much separation your compound actually needs.

At one end, direct probe analysis via ASAP or iASAP needs no sample preparation at all, ideal for a fast reaction-monitoring check. Touch Express extends that simplicity to an open-port sampling interface. Plate Express reads directly from TLC plates. At the other end, AVANT Modular (U)HPLC brings full liquid chromatography integration, for compounds that genuinely need separating before identification.

faqs.question: What is the puriFlash XS 530 used for?
faqs.answer: The puriFlash XS 530 is a compact semi-prep flash purification system that runs normal or reverse phase separations at 300 mL/min and 30 bar. It uses 20mm or 30mm ID columns and is built for high-throughput labs with limited bench space.

faqs.question: What is UPFP in the puriFlash XS 530?
faqs.answer: UPFP stands for Ultra Performance Flash Purification, the design approach behind the puriFlash XS 530's faster run times. Shorter runs use less solvent, which also speeds up the downstream evaporation step in the lab workflow.

faqs.question: What column sizes does the puriFlash XS 530 support?
faqs.answer: The puriFlash XS 530 supports 20mm and 30mm ID preparative columns from the F0004 to F3000 Flash Column range, down to 10μm media. It also supports 15 µm silica columns for higher resolution and increased loading capacity.

faqs.question: Does the puriFlash XS 530 need a fume hood?
faqs.answer: No, the puriFlash XS 530 does not need a fume hood. It has a built-in Fume Encloser, so it can sit anywhere on the bench while keeping the fume hood free for other work.

faqs.question: What detection options does the puriFlash XS 530 offer?
faqs.answer: The puriFlash XS 530 offers standard UV-Vis detection at 200 to 400 nm with multi-wavelength scanning. Optional upgrades include a UV Panorama detector covering 200 to 800 nm and a multifunctional compact mass spectrometer for compound identification.

faqs.question: How does Load & Go injection work on the puriFlash XS 530?
faqs.answer: Load & Go is an automated injection option on the puriFlash XS 530 that loads solid or liquid samples through a multi-way electrical valve. It's available as the 4-ways electrical valve kit and reduces manual handling during high-volume runs.

faqs.question: Can the puriFlash XS 530 run continuously?
faqs.answer: Yes, the puriFlash XS 530 is built for 24/7 operation. It uses high-quality materials designed to lower the total cost of ownership over the system's lifetime.

faqs.question: Can the puriFlash XS 530 be controlled remotely?
faqs.answer: Yes, the puriFlash XS 530 can be started remotely using its controller, and a companion smartphone app converts TLC or HPLC methods into a purification gradient in one click.

faqs.question: What is the price of the puriFlash XS 530 in India?
faqs.answer: The price of the puriFlash XS 530 in India depends on the detection package and injection configuration selected. Contact Inkarp for a quotation once your requirements are confirmed.

faqs.question: Who is the authorized distributor of the puriFlash XS 530 in India?
faqs.answer: Inkarp is the authorized distributor and service provider for the Advion Interchim Scientific puriFlash XS 530 in India. Inkarp provides demonstration, installation, training, AMC, spare parts, and technical support.

faqs.question: What is the puriFlash 5.030 used for?
faqs.answer: The puriFlash 5.030 is an everyday flash purification system built for routine daily separations. It runs at 300 mL/min and 30 bar with a quaternary gradient and multi-wavelength UV/Vis detection.

faqs.question: What is Dry-Load technology on the puriFlash 5.030?
faqs.answer: Dry-Load is the puriFlash 5.030's automated solid sample injection method, run through a 4-way electrical valve. Preparation happens during the equilibration phase, so it doesn't add extra time to your run.

faqs.question: What automation does the puriFlash 5.030 include?
faqs.answer: The puriFlash 5.030 includes RFID detection for columns, racks, and Dry-Load, leak sensors positioned throughout the system, and continuous solvent level monitoring. The system pauses automatically to prevent a column from running dry.

faqs.question: What detection options does the puriFlash 5.030 offer?
faqs.answer: The puriFlash 5.030 offers standard UV-Vis detection at 200 to 400 nm as its base configuration. Optional upgrades include the Pack UVextended for 200 to 800 nm coverage, the Pack iELSD for chromophore-free compound detection, and mass detection for a full triple-mode setup.

faqs.question: How does Genius AI help on the puriFlash 5.030?
faqs.answer: Genius AI is built into the puriFlash 5.030's ClearPeak software and recommends the best purification method directly from your TLC results. It removes the guesswork of converting a TLC separation into a flash method.

faqs.question: Can I transfer a TLC method to the puriFlash 5.030 using my phone?
faqs.answer: Yes, a smartphone app lets you photograph your TLC plate and send the data directly to the puriFlash 5.030 to transfer the method.

faqs.question: How many columns and racks does the puriFlash 5.030 support?
faqs.answer: The puriFlash 5.030 supports flash columns in the F0004 to F0800 format, along with 3 long racks holding 132 test tubes.

faqs.question: Does pairing the puriFlash 5.030 with 15 µm columns save time?
faqs.answer: Yes, pairing the puriFlash 5.030 with 15 µm columns allows higher-than-optimal flow rates, reducing purification time by up to 50% with minimal loss in efficiency.

faqs.question: Does the puriFlash 5.030 need a fume hood?
faqs.answer: No, the puriFlash 5.030 has a built-in Fume Encloser, so it doesn't need to sit under a fume hood and frees that space for other synthesis work.

sections.tabSummary: RFID, leak sensors, solvent monitoring
body: This section covers how RFID detection, leak sensors, and solvent monitoring work together on the puriFlash 5.030.
Every part of a purification run gets a layer of automated oversight here, so fewer things depend on catching a mistake manually.

RFID detection identifies columns, racks, and Dry-Load the moment they're loaded, cutting down on setup errors. Leak sensors sit throughout the instrument, watching for problems before they reach your compounds, which matters most when a sample took several synthesis steps to make. Solvent levels are tracked continuously, and the ClearPeak software pauses the method automatically rather than letting a column run dry. Dry-Load preparation is timed to fit inside the equilibration phase, so automating solid injection doesn't add time to your day.

groups.description: This section covers standard and upgraded detection options on the puriFlash 5.030.
body: Detection here starts strong and scales up through three separate, addable packs, depending on what your samples need.

Standard detection covers UV-Vis at 200 to 400 nm with multi-wavelength and collection scan. From there, the Pack UVextended widens coverage to a full 200 to 800 nm panoramic view. The Pack iELSD adds an integrated evaporative light scattering detector for chromophore-free compounds that UV alone would miss. And the system supports mass detection as part of a triple-mode setup, so UV, ELSD, and mass can work together to make sure nothing slips through.

faqs.question: How is the puriFlash 5.050 different from a standard flash system?
faqs.answer: The puriFlash 5.050 bridges flash chromatography and preparative HPLC in one instrument, reaching up to 50 bar for preparative-scale separations while still supporting routine flash purification. Standard flash systems typically stop at flash-scale pressure and column sizes.

faqs.question: What column sizes does the puriFlash 5.050 support?
faqs.answer: The puriFlash 5.050 supports preparative columns up to 80mm (3") ID and flash columns from F0004 to F3000. It's designed for reusable stainless steel columns filled with low particle size phases.

faqs.question: Why does the puriFlash 5.050 use reusable stainless steel columns?
faqs.answer: Reusable stainless steel columns on the puriFlash 5.050 are the preferred choice for complex reverse-phase reprocessing. They also support a more ecological approach to purification by reducing consumable column waste.

faqs.question: What detection options does the puriFlash 5.050 offer?
faqs.answer: The puriFlash 5.050 offers standard UV-Vis detection at 200 to 400 nm as its base configuration. Optional upgrades include the Pack UVextended for 200 to 800 nm coverage, the Pack iELSD for chromophore-free compounds, and mass detection for a full triple-mode setup.

faqs.question: How does Genius AI work on the puriFlash 5.050?
faqs.answer: Genius AI is built into the puriFlash 5.050's ClearPeak software and recommends the best purification method and column directly from a TLC plate. A free smartphone app can also transfer a photographed TLC plate straight to Genius and attach it to the report.

faqs.question: How does the puriFlash 5.050 protect against solvent and leak issues?
faqs.answer: The puriFlash 5.050 uses level detectors to pause the system before a column runs dry or a waste container overflows. Multiple leak detectors are also built into the device to guard against product loss.

faqs.question: How many columns and racks does the puriFlash 5.050 support?
faqs.answer: The puriFlash 5.050 supports 3 long racks holding 132 test tubes, alongside its full range of flash and preparative column compatibility.

body: This section covers how the puriFlash 5.050's stainless steel columns support complex reverse-phase separations.
Complex separations often call for equipment that can handle repeated, demanding reprocessing, and that's where the reusable column approach earns its place here.

Stainless steel columns filled with low particle size phases are the preferred choice for successful reverse-phase separations on the puriFlash 5.050, particularly for more complex reprocessing work. Because these columns are reusable rather than disposable, the system also takes a more ecological approach to purification overall. Wash discs support that same durability goal, letting water circulate behind the pump heads to guard against crystallization when a purification involves an additive prone to it.

sections.title: Height-Adjustable Needles and Nitrogen Efficiency
sections.tabSummary: What the 30%/50% claims actually depend on
body: A fixed needle height works fine at the start of an evaporation run and wastes gas by the end of it, once the sample level has dropped well below where the needle sits.

XS-Vap's needles adjust to the actual level in each vial, keeping the nitrogen stream close to the liquid surface throughout the run rather than blasting empty headspace as evaporation progresses. That single adjustment is what delivers both confirmed savings together: up to 30% faster evaporation and up to 50% less nitrogen. The supply side reinforces it further, an independent nitrogen line running at just 1.5 to 3 bar through its own dedicated control valve, rather than a shared, unregulated gas line.

faqs.question: What is the TriVersa® NanoMate® used for?
faqs.answer: It's a chip-based nanoelectrospray ionization platform combining LC/MS, infusion, fraction collection, and direct surface analysis, used for applications like shotgun lipidomics, protein characterization, and non-covalent interaction studies.

faqs.question: How much sample does the ESI Chip need?
faqs.answer: As little as 3 µL, sustaining up to 15 minutes of stable spray.

faqs.question: What happens if the spray fails during a run?
faqs.answer: An internal counter electrode senses the failure and the system recovers automatically, rather than losing the run.

faqs.question: How do I choose the right emitter size for my sample?
faqs.answer: Match your analyte type and sample characteristics to one of three confirmed ID sizes, 2.5 to 5.5 µm; Inkarp can confirm the specific recommendation for your application.

faqs.question: How do I set up automated sampling from a well plate?
faqs.answer: The system delivers spray directly from 96 or 384 well plate formats, automated as part of the standard workflow.

faqs.question: How do I re-analyze a result identified during an online LC/MS run?
faqs.answer: Excess LC eluate is physically saved as fractions during the run, which can then be re-analyzed by infusion once a result of interest is identified.

faqs.question: Is TriVersa NanoMate suitable for large analytes like proteins?
faqs.answer: Yes, high-throughput infusion is confirmed for both small and large analytes, including protein characterization applications.

faqs.question: What makes this different from a conventional nano-ESI source?
faqs.answer: The 400-nozzle silicon chip design and integrated LC/MS, infusion, fraction collection, and direct surface analysis capabilities combine into one platform, described as the only automated platform offering high-throughput infusion this way.

longForm.heroLead: Precious samples don't forgive a spray that fails halfway through a run. TriVersa NanoMate is built around a chip that doesn't let that happen. The ESI Chip carries 400 nano-electrospray nozzles etched into a silicon wafer, each one reproducibly fabricated to perform identically. From just 3 µL of sample, that design sustains 15 minutes of stable spray, and an internal counter electrode senses spray failure and recovers automatically rather than losing the run. It combines LC/MS, chip-based infusion, fraction collection, and direct surface analysis in one integrated platform, extracting more information from complex samples than LC/MS running alone. Excess LC eluate gets physically saved as fractions during an online run, so anything interesting in the real-time data can be pulled and re-analyzed by infusion afterward.

longForm.heroHook: Just 3 microliters, 15 minutes of stable spray. 400 nozzles, one silicon chip.
heroParagraphs: Precious samples don't forgive a spray that fails halfway through a run. TriVersa NanoMate is built around a chip that doesn't let that happen.

The ESI Chip carries 400 nano-electrospray nozzles etched into a silicon wafer, each one reproducibly fabricated to perform identically. From just 3 µL of sample, that design sustains 15 minutes of stable spray, and an internal counter electrode senses spray failure and recovers automatically rather than losing the run.

It combines LC/MS, chip-based infusion, fraction collection, and direct surface analysis in one integrated platform, extracting more information from complex samples than LC/MS running alone. Excess LC eluate gets physically saved as fractions during an online run, so anything interesting in the real-time data can be pulled and re-analyzed by infusion afterward.

faqs.question: Do I have to choose between standalone and integrated at purchase?

faqs.question: What software controls AVANT?
faqs.answer: Mass Express, a dedicated software suite distinct from ClearPeak, which controls Advion Interchim Scientific's separate puriFlash purification line.

faqs.question: How does AVANT fit alongside other expression CMS sample inlets?

faqs.question: How do I choose between manual and automated UHPLC configuration?
faqs.answer: Match your throughput and budget requirements; the modular design covers everything from simple manual injection HPLC to fully automated UHPLC.

faqs.question: Can AVANT analyze air-sensitive or volatile samples?
faqs.answer: Not directly on its own, but paired with ASAP or vAPCI within the same expression CMS ecosystem, air-sensitive and volatile compound analysis are both confirmed.

faqs.question: What is the relationship between Advion and Interchim?
faqs.answer: Advion Interchim Scientific is the market-facing name of a marketing and distribution partnership between Advion, Inc. (US) and Interchim SAS (France), two separate companies.

faqs.question: What sampling techniques does expression CMS support?

faqs.question: How do I choose between the two mass range options?
faqs.answer: Choose m/z 10-1,200 for most standard organic chemistry work, or m/z 10-2,000 if your compounds regularly extend into larger mass ranges.

faqs.question: How do I set up expression CMS for fast reaction monitoring?
faqs.answer: Use the direct probe sampling technique (ASAP or iASAP), which requires no sample preparation, for the fastest possible in-process check.

faqs.question: How do I switch between sampling techniques?
faqs.answer: Interfaces are designed to swap rapidly with minimal sample preparation; confirm your specific technique combination and switching workflow with Inkarp.

faqs.question: Is expression CMS suitable for a teaching laboratory?

faqs.question: Can expression CMS integrate with liquid chromatography?
faqs.answer: Yes, via AVANT Modular (U)HPLC, providing full compound separation for samples that need it.

faqs.question: What applications is expression CMS confirmed for?
faqs.answer: Reaction monitoring, teaching chemistry, food safety and ingredients analysis, cannabis and hemp testing, environmental analysis, clinical diagnostics, proteins and peptides synthesis, and forensics.

faqs.question: What is the puriFlash XS 530 used for?
faqs.answer: The puriFlash XS 530 is a compact semi-prep flash purification system that runs normal or reverse phase separations at 300 mL/min and 30 bar. It uses 20mm or 30mm ID columns and is built for high-throughput labs with limited bench space.

faqs.question: What is UPFP in the puriFlash XS 530?
faqs.answer: UPFP stands for Ultra Performance Flash Purification, the design approach behind the puriFlash XS 530's faster run times. Shorter runs use less solvent, which also speeds up the downstream evaporation step in the lab workflow.

faqs.question: What column sizes does the puriFlash XS 530 support?
faqs.answer: The puriFlash XS 530 supports 20mm and 30mm ID preparative columns from the F0004 to F3000 Flash Column range, down to 10μm media. It also supports 15 µm silica columns for higher resolution and increased loading capacity.

faqs.question: Does the puriFlash XS 530 need a fume hood?
faqs.answer: No, the puriFlash XS 530 does not need a fume hood. It has a built-in Fume Encloser, so it can sit anywhere on the bench while keeping the fume hood free for other work.

faqs.question: What detection options does the puriFlash XS 530 offer?
faqs.answer: The puriFlash XS 530 offers standard UV-Vis detection at 200 to 400 nm with multi-wavelength scanning. Optional upgrades include a UV Panorama detector covering 200 to 800 nm and a multifunctional compact mass spectrometer for compound identification.

faqs.question: Can the puriFlash XS 530 run continuously?

faqs.question: What is the puriFlash 5.030 used for?
faqs.answer: The puriFlash 5.030 is an everyday flash purification system built for routine daily separations. It runs at 300 mL/min and 30 bar with a quaternary gradient and multi-wavelength UV/Vis detection.

faqs.question: What is Dry-Load technology on the puriFlash 5.030?
faqs.answer: Dry-Load is the puriFlash 5.030's automated solid sample injection method, run through a 4-way electrical valve. Preparation happens during the equilibration phase, so it doesn't add extra time to your run.

faqs.question: What automation does the puriFlash 5.030 include?
faqs.answer: The puriFlash 5.030 includes RFID detection for columns, racks, and Dry-Load, leak sensors positioned throughout the system, and continuous solvent level monitoring. The system pauses automatically to prevent a column from running dry.

faqs.question: What detection options does the puriFlash 5.030 offer?
faqs.answer: The puriFlash 5.030 offers standard UV-Vis detection at 200 to 400 nm as its base configuration. Optional upgrades include the Pack UVextended for 200 to 800 nm coverage, the Pack iELSD for chromophore-free compound detection, and mass detection for a full triple-mode setup.

faqs.question: How does Genius AI help on the puriFlash 5.030?
faqs.answer: Genius AI is built into the puriFlash 5.030's ClearPeak software and recommends the best purification method directly from your TLC results. It removes the guesswork of converting a TLC separation into a flash method.

faqs.question: Can I transfer a TLC method to the puriFlash 5.030 using my phone?
faqs.answer: Yes, a smartphone app lets you photograph your TLC plate and send the data directly to the puriFlash 5.030 to transfer the method.

faqs.question: How many columns and racks does the puriFlash 5.030 support?
faqs.answer: The puriFlash 5.030 supports flash columns in the F0004 to F0800 format, along with 3 long racks holding 132 test tubes.

faqs.question: Does pairing the puriFlash 5.030 with 15 µm columns save time?
faqs.answer: Yes, pairing the puriFlash 5.030 with 15 µm columns allows higher-than-optimal flow rates, reducing purification time by up to 50% with minimal loss in efficiency.

faqs.question: Does the puriFlash 5.030 need a fume hood?
faqs.answer: No, the puriFlash 5.030 has a built-in Fume Encloser, so it doesn't need to sit under a fume hood and frees that space for other synthesis work.

sections.tabSummary: RFID, leak sensors, solvent monitoring
body: This section covers how RFID detection, leak sensors, and solvent monitoring work together on the puriFlash 5.030.
Every part of a purification run gets a layer of automated oversight here, so fewer things depend on catching a mistake manually.

RFID detection identifies columns, racks, and Dry-Load the moment they're loaded, cutting down on setup errors. Leak sensors sit throughout the instrument, watching for problems before they reach your compounds, which matters most when a sample took several synthesis steps to make. Solvent levels are tracked continuously, and the ClearPeak software pauses the method automatically rather than letting a column run dry. Dry-Load preparation is timed to fit inside the equilibration phase, so automating solid injection doesn't add time to your day.

groups.description: This section covers standard and upgraded detection options on the puriFlash 5.030.
body: Detection here starts strong and scales up through three separate, addable packs, depending on what your samples need.

Standard detection covers UV-Vis at 200 to 400 nm with multi-wavelength and collection scan. From there, the Pack UVextended widens coverage to a full 200 to 800 nm panoramic view. The Pack iELSD adds an integrated evaporative light scattering detector for chromophore-free compounds that UV alone would miss. And the system supports mass detection as part of a triple-mode setup, so UV, ELSD, and mass can work together to make sure nothing slips through.

faqs.question: What is the puriFlash 5.050 used for?
faqs.answer: The puriFlash 5.050 is a cross-over flash and preparative purification system built for more demanding separations. It runs at 250 mL/min and up to 50 bar, moving between normal and reverse phase on reusable stainless steel columns.

faqs.question: How is the puriFlash 5.050 different from a standard flash system?
faqs.answer: The puriFlash 5.050 bridges flash chromatography and preparative HPLC in one instrument, reaching up to 50 bar for preparative-scale separations while still supporting routine flash purification. Standard flash systems typically stop at flash-scale pressure and column sizes.

faqs.question: What column sizes does the puriFlash 5.050 support?
faqs.answer: The puriFlash 5.050 supports preparative columns up to 80mm (3") ID and flash columns from F0004 to F3000. It's designed for reusable stainless steel columns filled with low particle size phases.

faqs.question: Why does the puriFlash 5.050 use reusable stainless steel columns?
faqs.answer: Reusable stainless steel columns on the puriFlash 5.050 are the preferred choice for complex reverse-phase reprocessing. They also support a more ecological approach to purification by reducing consumable column waste.

faqs.question: What detection options does the puriFlash 5.050 offer?
faqs.answer: The puriFlash 5.050 offers standard UV-Vis detection at 200 to 400 nm as its base configuration. Optional upgrades include the Pack UVextended for 200 to 800 nm coverage, the Pack iELSD for chromophore-free compounds, and mass detection for a full triple-mode setup.

faqs.question: How does Genius AI work on the puriFlash 5.050?
faqs.answer: Genius AI is built into the puriFlash 5.050's ClearPeak software and recommends the best purification method and column directly from a TLC plate. A free smartphone app can also transfer a photographed TLC plate straight to Genius and attach it to the report.

faqs.question: How does the puriFlash 5.050 protect against solvent and leak issues?
faqs.answer: The puriFlash 5.050 uses level detectors to pause the system before a column runs dry or a waste container overflows. Multiple leak detectors are also built into the device to guard against product loss.

faqs.question: How many columns and racks does the puriFlash 5.050 support?
faqs.answer: The puriFlash 5.050 supports 3 long racks holding 132 test tubes, alongside its full range of flash and preparative column compatibility.

faqs.answer: The price of the puriFlash 5.050 in India depends on the column, detection, and automation packages selected. Contact Inkarp for a quotation once your requirements are confirmed.

sections.title: Reusable Columns and Reverse-Phase Purification
sections.tabSummary: Stainless steel columns and ecological purification
body: This section covers how the puriFlash 5.050's stainless steel columns support complex reverse-phase separations.
Complex separations often call for equipment that can handle repeated, demanding reprocessing, and that's where the reusable column approach earns its place here.

Stainless steel columns filled with low particle size phases are the preferred choice for successful reverse-phase separations on the puriFlash 5.050, particularly for more complex reprocessing work. Because these columns are reusable rather than disposable, the system also takes a more ecological approach to purification overall. Wash discs support that same durability goal, letting water circulate behind the pump heads to guard against crystallization when a purification involves an additive prone to it.

groups.description: This section covers the puriFlash 5.050's triple detection and built-in protection against solvent and leak issues.
body: Detection and protection work together here, so a missed compound and a damaged run are both accounted for by design.

Triple detection across UV, mass, and ELSD is available to make sure no compound goes undetected, keeping purification yield high even for chromophore-free compositions with the optional iELSD pack. Beyond compound detection, level detectors watch both solvent bottles and the waste container, pausing the system before a column can run dry or a container can overflow. Multiple leak detectors sit throughout the device as an additional safeguard against product loss.

sections.tabSummary: What the 30%/50% claims actually depend on
body: A fixed needle height works fine at the start of an evaporation run and wastes gas by the end of it, once the sample level has dropped well below where the needle sits.

XS-Vap's needles adjust to the actual level in each vial, keeping the nitrogen stream close to the liquid surface throughout the run rather than blasting empty headspace as evaporation progresses. That single adjustment is what delivers both confirmed savings together: up to 30% faster evaporation and up to 50% less nitrogen. The supply side reinforces it further, an independent nitrogen line running at just 1.5 to 3 bar through its own dedicated control valve, rather than a shared, unregulated gas line.

faqs.question: What is the puriFlash® 5.400-UV used for?
faqs.answer: It's an ultra-high-pressure preparative purification system, used for method development and purification of rare, high-value samples requiring maximum resolution.

faqs.question: What does the 400 bar pressure actually enable?
faqs.answer: It's what makes sub-2-micron column compatibility possible, delivering the separating power standard preparative HPLC systems don't reach.

faqs.question: How do I choose between the 5.400-UV and 5.250?
faqs.answer: Choose the 5.400-UV when resolution matters more than throughput for rare or valuable samples; choose the 5.250 when you need higher flow rate, larger columns, or triple detection for routine to complex purification.

faqs.question: How does method development work on this system?
faqs.answer: Develop your method on a 7.8mm analytical column, then move directly to purification on a preparative HPLC column, on the same apparatus.

faqs.question: How does mobile phase heating improve my results?
faqs.answer: It holds the mobile phase at a constant temperature regardless of your lab's ambient conditions, improving reproducibility and sharpening peaks.

faqs.question: How does the solvent level detector protect my column?
faqs.answer: It warns you before a solvent bottle runs empty, preventing air from entering and damaging the preparative HPLC column.

faqs.question: What optional packs are available for the 5.400-UV?
faqs.answer: UVextended, for detection range up to 800nm, and PWD, which rinses pump heads to prevent piston crystallization.

faqs.question: Does the 5.400-UV have the same RFID and software as the 5.250?

faqs.question: What is the TriVersa® NanoMate® used for?
faqs.answer: It's a chip-based nanoelectrospray ionization platform combining LC/MS, infusion, fraction collection, and direct surface analysis, used for applications like shotgun lipidomics, protein characterization, and non-covalent interaction studies.

faqs.question: How much sample does the ESI Chip need?
faqs.answer: As little as 3 µL, sustaining up to 15 minutes of stable spray.

faqs.question: What happens if the spray fails during a run?
faqs.answer: An internal counter electrode senses the failure and the system recovers automatically, rather than losing the run.

faqs.question: How do I choose the right emitter size for my sample?
faqs.answer: Match your analyte type and sample characteristics to one of three confirmed ID sizes, 2.5 to 5.5 µm; Inkarp can confirm the specific recommendation for your application.

faqs.question: How do I set up automated sampling from a well plate?

sections.tabSummary: What the 400-nozzle design actually delivers
body: Reliable spray from a vanishingly small sample volume depends on two things: how the chip is built, and what happens when something goes wrong mid-run.

The 400-nozzle array, etched into a silicon wafer, is fabricated with a highly reproducible method specifically so every nozzle performs equally, not just so there are many of them available. That consistency is what makes 15 minutes of stable spray from only 3 µL achievable in practice, not just on paper. And because an internal counter electrode continuously senses the spray, a failure doesn't end the run, the system recovers automatically.

faqs.question: What is P4PRO with AffiPump used for?
faqs.answer: It's a compact SPR system that runs both static screening and full flow-based kinetic characterization, kon, koff, and KD, on the same instrument.

faqs.question: How is P4PRO different from the P4SPR 2.0?
faqs.answer: P4PRO paired with the AffiPump adds flow mode and full kinetic measurement on top of the static screening capability the P4SPR 2.0 offers, without needing separate hardware.

faqs.question: Do I need to reconfigure the instrument to switch between static and flow mode?
faqs.answer: No, P4PRO switches between static and flow operation without reconfiguring the setup.

faqs.question: What kinetic parameters can P4PRO measure?
faqs.answer: Association rate (kon) from 10³ to 10⁷ M⁻¹s⁻¹, dissociation rate (koff) from 10⁻⁵ to 10⁻¹ s⁻¹, and KD calculated from both.

faqs.question: How much sample does a flow-mode run require?
faqs.answer: Between 5 and 100 µL per injection in flow mode, or 300 µL for static mode runs.

faqs.question: What sensor chemistries are available?
faqs.answer: Covalent surfaces like carboxyl, CMD, and AffiCoat for EDC/NHS coupling, plus capture-based surfaces including Anti-His, NTA, Protein A/G, Streptavidin, Strep-Tactin XT, and Anti-AAVX.

faqs.question: Do sensors need cleaning between runs?
faqs.answer: No, sensors are disposable and pre-characterized, eliminating cleaning and carry-over entirely.

faqs.question: What software does P4PRO run on?
faqs.answer: Affilabs.core, which includes Sparq, a built-in operation support assistant, and is shared across the P4 instrument platform.

Four simultaneous channels run sample and controls together in one injection, whether in static or flow mode.
Flow injection uses just 5 to 100 µL of sample, and static mode uses 300 µL, keeping precious sample material to a minimum either way.
Semi-automated injection cuts hands-on time per run, and direct inline controls give real-time feedback during every measurement.
Disposable, pre-characterized gold sensor chips eliminate cleaning and carry-over between runs, available in covalent and capture-based chemistries.
The same sensors and Affilabs.core software run across both P4PRO and the simpler P4SPR 2.0, so a lab can standardize on one software platform regardless of which instrument handles a given assay.

longForm.heroHook: Real-time SPR. No pump, no fluidics, no clogging risk. Running in under an hour.
longForm.heroLead: Flow-based SPR systems come with a real setup cost: fluidics to manage, clogging to worry about, a specialist to run it. P4SPR 2.0 skips all of it. It's a compact, laptop-powered, 4-channel biosensor built for researchers who need real binding data fast, without flow complexity standing in the way. Detection reaches fM, KD measures down to pM and beyond, and a full cycle runs in under 10 minutes on just 150 µL of sample. No dedicated power supply, no bench space commitment, works wherever the laptop goes.

body: P4SPR 2.0 runs static SPR, capturing sample and controls together in one injection across four simultaneous channels, with no pump or fluidics involved.
Detection limit reaches fM, assay dependent, with KD measurable down to pM.
Sample volume per injection is 150 µL, keeping material use low even across repeated screening runs.
A full cycle completes in 10 minutes or less, fast enough for iterative assay development and condition screening without long waits between results.
The instrument is laptop powered, with no dedicated power supply required, so it runs wherever the laptop does.
A compact 25 x 25 x 6 cm footprint fits on a shared bench without dominating it.
Disposable, pre-characterized gold sensor chips eliminate cleaning and carry-over, available in covalent and capture-based chemistries.

The platform has 100+ peer-reviewed publications behind it, used across 12 countries and 10+ disease areas including drug discovery, oncology, infectious disease, therapeutic drug monitoring, and biomanufacturing QC.
The same sensors and Affilabs.core software run across both P4SPR 2.0 and the flow-capable P4PRO, so a lab can add flow kinetics later without retraining on new software.

P4PRO paired with the AffiPump does both on one bench, switching between static and flow mode without swapping hardware or rebuilding the setup. body: Affilabs.core handles instrument control, data acquisition, and analysis in one desktop application built specifically for the P4SPR and P4PRO instruments.
A live four-channel wavelength plot tracks every run in real time, with automatic injection flags and cycle markers built directly into the view.

Automated calibration handles servo alignment, LED calibration, and S-pol reference capture with a single click, and machine learning further optimizes LED settings and convergence without manual adjustment.
A method queue supports multi-step sequences with templates, and steps can be added mid-run rather than requiring a full restart.
Analysis tools include alignment, ΔSPR cursors, KD fitting, and cycle comparison, all inside the same application used for acquisition.
Data exports directly to Excel, CSV for Origin and Prism, sensorgram images, or the clipboard, no separate conversion step required.
Optical fault detection flags leaks and bubbles with real-time signal quality scoring, catching problems as they happen rather than after a run is wasted.
An experiment notebook tags, annotates, rates, and makes past experiments searchable, keeping a full history without a separate logging system.
IQ/OQ validation ships included with every installation, 12 automated checks for IQ and 43 tests across 6 suites for OQ, generating timestamped qualification reports for regulatory and lab audits.

Sparq, built directly into the software, guides first-time installation, troubleshoots calibration and connectivity issues, answers workflow questions, and escalates to the Affinité team when needed, all without leaving the application.

faqs.answer: It offers variable speed control from 5 to 1000 RPM, suited to both R&D and QC testing scenarios.

faqs.question: What's the difference between the L Series and H Series?
faqs.answer: The L Series covers a temperature range of 5°C to 75°C, while the H Series extends to 50°C to 235°C for higher-temperature material testing.

faqs.question: How is temperature controlled on CAP2000+?
faqs.answer: A built-in Peltier plate delivers precise temperature control across the L or H Series range.

faqs.question: What materials can be tested on CAP2000+?
faqs.answer: It handles medium-viscosity materials like coatings, creams, and inks, as well as high-viscosity materials like adhesives, asphalt, chocolate, and epoxies.

faqs.question: What does Capcalc software add to CAP2000+?

sections.tabSummary: How L and H Series fit different testing needs
body: How CAP2000+'s variable speed range and dual temperature series fit different testing needs.
High-shear viscosity testing rarely happens at a single fixed speed or temperature, and CAP2000+ is built to cover a genuinely wide operating window rather than a narrow one.

Variable speed runs from 5 to 1000 RPM, wide enough to move between exploratory R&D testing and repeatable QC protocols on the same instrument. Temperature control runs through a built-in Peltier plate, split across two model series depending on what a formulation actually needs: the L Series covers 5°C to 75°C for standard ambient-to-moderate testing, while the H Series reaches all the way to 235°C for genuinely high-temperature materials like hot melt adhesives or asphalt. Both series pair that temperature control with the same wide shear rate range, keeping the instrument well suited to small sample volumes where precise, repeatable conditions matter.

paragraphs: Manual viscosity testing works, but it leaves room for operator-to-operator variation, and that's exactly the gap Capcalc is built to close.

With Capcalc, data capture and viscometer control both automate directly, removing the manual steps that introduce inconsistency between operators or between runs. The software supports powerful scripting capabilities and looping functions for repetitive testing tasks, along with math modeling for yield stress calculations and plastic index, calculations that would otherwise need to be done separately. Up to four data sets can be plotted together for direct comparison and analysis, useful when comparing formulations, batches, or test conditions side by side.

sections.tabSummary: Accuracy and repeatability across a wide viscosity range
body: Accuracy and repeatability across a wide viscosity range.

A viscometer that's accurate on a mid-range fluid but drifts at the extremes isn't actually solving the problem most labs have — they need one instrument covering thin inks through heavy industrial pastes without swapping equipment between them. DV2Plus holds ±1.0% accuracy of range and ±0.2% repeatability across that full span.

That precision is what makes the instrument usable for both R&D exploration and regulated QC release testing on the same platform: a method developed during formulation work carries the same measurement confidence into production release testing, without needing to be re-validated on a different instrument because the viscosity range changed.

body: Most rotational viscometers offer a limited set of discrete test speeds, which forces a compromise between the speed a method calls for and the nearest speed the instrument actually has. DV2Plus's 740-speed range removes that compromise, giving ultra-fine control across the full span of testing applications.

Connectivity follows the same philosophy of removing friction rather than adding features for their own sake. Bluetooth and four USB-A ports plus one USB-B port cover PCs, printers, and barcode scanners without cable management becoming its own task. DV360 software extends that into advanced viscosity testing with optional 21 CFR Part 11 compliance, and DV Create builds up to 25-step test methods, live-monitors tests over Bluetooth or USB, and stays compatible with legacy DV2T method files — so a lab moving from DV2T to DV2Plus doesn't lose its existing validated methods in the transition.

paragraphs: A viscosity test involves more than one number, and reading only the final result hides what happened to get there. DV2Plus's 7-inch, 800×480 touchscreen keeps six parameters visible simultaneously: viscosity in cP or mPa·s, temperature in °C or °F, shear rate/stress, percentage torque, spindle and speed, and step program status.

That real-time visibility is what turns a routine test into monitored testing — a torque reading trending toward an out-of-range value shows up while the test is still running, not after the fact in a report. The interface itself is built for that kind of glance-and-check use: a wide viewing angle and a clean, modern layout rather than a menu structure that has to be navigated to find the number that matters.

faqs.question: What is the DVNext Cone/Plate Rheometer used for?
faqs.answer: It's a rheometer for precise absolute viscosity measurement of small sample volumes, used in pharmaceutical, biotechnology, cosmetics, and specialty chemical R&D where sample material is limited or expensive.

faqs.question: How small a sample does it need?
faqs.answer: As small as 0.5–2.0 mL.

faqs.question: How does it calculate viscosity?
faqs.answer: It measures the torque required to rotate a cone spindle immersed in the sample against a plate; that torque is proportional to shear stress and is used to calculate absolute viscosity in centipoise (mPa·s).

faqs.question: What is the torque measurement accuracy and repeatability?
faqs.answer: 1% of full-scale range for accuracy, and 0.2% of full-scale range for repeatability.

faqs.question: How is the spindle attached?
faqs.answer: Via a magnetic coupling attachment, simplifying attachment and removal and minimizing handling errors.

faqs.question: Does the instrument require manual gap adjustment?
faqs.answer: No. Electronic gap adjustment reduces manual intervention and improves repeatability.

faqs.question: What do the auto-zero and auto-range functions do?
faqs.answer: Auto-zero automatically calibrates the instrument for optimal torque accuracy; auto-range automatically defines the full-scale range for every spindle/speed combination.

faqs.question: Why is temperature control faster on this instrument?
faqs.answer: The small sample volume has less thermal mass, so it reaches target temperature faster than larger-volume viscometry, reducing wait time during testing.

faqs.question: Is external gauging needed to set the cone/plate gap?
faqs.answer: No. The relative cone-to-plate position is maintained through simple mechanical setup without external gauges.

faqs.question: Can multiple cone spindles be used?
faqs.answer: Yes, multiple cone spindles are supported and can be calibrated for specific applications.

faqs.question: Is 21 CFR Part 11 compliance available?
faqs.answer: Yes, as an optional feature, including electronic signatures, audit trails, and secure data management.

faqs.question: Can the instrument connect to a LIMS?
faqs.answer: Yes, optional Ethernet and LIMS connectivity is available for integration with laboratory management systems.

faqs.question: How is DVNext Cone/Plate different from DV2Plus?
faqs.answer: DVNext Cone/Plate is built specifically for small sample volumes (0.5–2.0 mL) using cone/plate geometry. DV2Plus is a general-purpose rotational spindle viscometer with a 740-speed range and built-in Gel Timer functionality, suited to larger, more readily available sample volumes.

longForm.heroHook: 0.5 mL of sample. Full rheological data. Nothing wasted getting there.
longForm.heroLead: Some materials can't be spared in the volumes a standard viscometer needs — a biological fluid drawn from a limited source, a formulation that costs more per gram than the instrument itself. DVNext Cone/Plate Rheometer is built specifically for that constraint: accurate absolute viscosity measurement from samples as small as 0.5–2.0 mL. The geometry does the work. A cone spindle rotates against a plate through the small sample volume, and the resistance to that rotation — proportional to shear stress — calculates directly to absolute viscosity in centipoise. Small volume also means fast thermal equilibrium: temperature adjustments happen quickly, cutting the wait time that larger sample volumes impose between test conditions. A magnetic coupling attachment turns spindle changes into a simple placement rather than a fiddly mechanical fitting, and electronic gap adjustment removes manual setup from the equation entirely — both reducing handling error and speeding throughput. Torque measurement holds to 1% of full-scale range accuracy with 0.2% repeatability, on the same 7-inch touchscreen interface found across the DVNext line, with optional 21 CFR Part 11 compliance and LIMS connectivity for regulated environments.

sections.title: Precision at Small Sample Volumes
sections.tabSummary: What 0.5–2.0 mL enables and why it matters
body: What 0.5–2.0 mL enables and why it matters.

Standard rotational viscometry generally assumes sample volume isn't the constraint — there's enough material to fill a beaker and immerse a spindle. Cone/plate geometry doesn't need that assumption. DVNext Cone/Plate measures accurate absolute viscosity from 0.5 to 2.0 mL, which is the difference between testing being possible and testing consuming more of a limited or expensive material than a project can afford.

That small volume carries a second benefit beyond conservation: thermal mass is proportionally small too, so temperature adjustments happen quickly. A test sequence that steps through multiple temperature points doesn't spend most of its time waiting for the sample to equilibrate — it spends that time collecting data instead, directly improving throughput for iterative formulation work.

groups.title: Principle of Operation
groups.summary: How the cone/plate geometry calculates absolute viscosity
groups.description: How the cone/plate geometry calculates absolute viscosity.
body: DVNext Cone/Plate measures the torque required to rotate a cone spindle immersed in a small volume of fluid held against a plate. The fluid resists that rotation, and the resistance is directly proportional to shear stress — which is then used to calculate the fluid's absolute viscosity in centipoise (mPa·s) directly, without an external calibration curve standing between the raw measurement and the result.

The cone-to-plate relative position is what makes the shear rate calculation valid, and that position is maintained through a simple mechanical setup rather than requiring external gauges to verify — one less variable for the operator to manage, and one less source of setup-to-setup variability across a testing programme.

body: Setup variability is one of the quieter sources of test-to-test inconsistency, and digital leveling addresses it directly — ensuring the instrument starts every test from the same reference state rather than depending on a visual bubble-level check.

For regulated environments, 21 CFR Part 11 compliance is available as an option, bringing electronic signatures, audit trails, and secure data management into the testing workflow rather than requiring a separate paper-based compliance layer. Optional Ethernet and LIMS connectivity extends that further, feeding results directly into a laboratory management system rather than requiring manual transcription between the instrument and the system of record.

DVNext Rheometer ships as two versions built around exactly that distinction. The Standard version covers what most labs need day to day: digital leveling for consistent setup, a Start-up Wizard that guides initial configuration, built-in Gel-Timer functionality for tracking gelation, and ±1.0% accuracy with ±0.2% repeatability as the baseline. Magnetic coupling and a barcode scanner are available as options. The 21 CFR Part 11 Compliant version takes that same measurement core and builds a full regulated workflow around it: magnetic coupling attachment as standard, hand-held barcode scanning with automatic accessory detection, Ethernet and LIMS connectivity, and secure non-editable PDF reporting — all under GAMP-compliant audit trails.

Buying more compliance capability than a lab actually needs adds cost and complexity without adding value; buying too little means a regulated workflow has to be retrofitted later. DVNext Rheometer avoids that mismatch by offering the choice upfront rather than layering compliance on as an afterthought.

The Standard version is built for straightforward, high-quality measurement: digital leveling and a Start-up Wizard get a test running quickly, Gel-Timer functionality is built in rather than an add-on, and magnetic coupling or a barcode scanner can be added where the workflow calls for them. sections.tabSummary: The accuracy/repeatability figures matched against DV2Plus
body: The accuracy and repeatability figures matched against DV2Plus.

Entry-level instrumentation usually signals a trade-off somewhere in the measurement chain — a wider accuracy band, fewer discrete speeds, a narrower operating range. DVPlus doesn't carry that trade-off into its core specification: ±1.0% of range accuracy and ±0.2% repeatability, identical to what Brookfield states for the DV2Plus, and a full 740-speed range rather than a reduced subset.

What positions DVPlus as the entry-level instrument is everything built around that core measurement, not the measurement itself. A 5-inch display instead of 7 inches, no stated Viscosity Wizard or built-in Gel Timer functionality, and a simpler connectivity story via the DVPlus Connect App rather than DV360's advanced compliance-ready software layer. For a lab whose real requirement is accurate, repeatable viscosity data without needing guided complex-test setup or regulated audit trails, that's the right trade to make.

paragraphs: Some testing protocols care less about a single-point viscosity reading and more about how a material's behaviour changes over time — how long it takes to reach a target torque, how long temperature equilibration actually takes, or when a test sequence should stop based on a defined condition rather than a fixed duration. DVPlus provides direct access to those three time-based functions rather than requiring them to be configured through a more general step-program interface.

Automatic range calculation works alongside that: the Full-Scale Range at 100% and the maximum measurable viscosity for a given spindle/speed combination are calculated automatically, removing a manual lookup step from method setup and reducing the chance of a test running outside its valid measurement range without the operator noticing.

longForm.heroLead: Gelation studies often mean running one instrument for viscosity and yield stress, then switching to something else entirely to track time-to-gel. DVNext Rheometer with Gel Timer Functionality keeps all three on one platform, purpose-built for applications where knowing exactly when a material gels matters as much as knowing how thick it is. Digital leveling ensures precise setup, a Start-up Wizard guides initial configuration step by step, and Ethernet connectivity supports network integration and remote access as a standard capability. Like the base DVNext Rheometer, it's available in a Standard version and a 21 CFR Part 11 Compliant version — the Compliant version adding hand-held barcode scanning with automatic accessory detection, standard-fit magnetic coupling, LIMS connectivity, and secure non-editable PDF reporting under GAMP-compliant audit trails.

sections.tabSummary: Why tracking gelation on the primary rheometer matters
body: Why tracking gelation on the primary rheometer matters.

Gelation isn't a single point measurement the way a viscosity reading is — it's a transition that happens over time, and catching exactly when it occurs matters directly for resins, epoxies, and other curing systems where working time and cure time are process-critical variables. Running that measurement as a bolt-on to a general viscometer, or on a separate dedicated instrument, adds a step and a potential source of inconsistency between the viscosity data and the gel time data.

DVNext Rheometer with Gel Timer Functionality keeps both on the same measurement platform. Gel-Timer functionality is positioned as a defining capability rather than an incidental feature, so gelation studies and standard viscosity/yield stress testing draw on the same calibration, the same interface, and the same reporting path.

Measurement range runs 40 to 141 KU, 32 to 1099 grams, and 27 to 5274 cP. Accuracy is ±1% of the full-scale range, and reproducibility is ±0.5% of the full-scale range. A magnetic spindle coupling allows quick spindle attachment and removal, and the base accommodates standard pint, ½ pint, and quart cans. The test method requires no weights, and the instrument is fully compatible with ASTM D562. An optional paste spindle extends testing to high-consistency materials such as roller mill pastes, and NIST traceable viscosity standards are available.

sections.title: Krebs Units and ASTM D562
sections.tabSummary: Why this unit system and standard apply to paints and coatings
body: Why this unit system and standard apply to paints and coatings.

Krebs units are the measurement system the paint and coatings industry has used to specify application consistency, and ASTM D562 is the standard method built around that system. A formulation specified in KU can't be directly verified on an instrument reporting only in centipoise without a conversion step, so KU-3 reports in Krebs units, grams, and centipoise at the same time, letting a lab match whichever unit a specification or customer actually requires.

The stated measurement range — 40 to 141 KU, 32 to 1099 grams, 27 to 5274 cP — covers the consistency range Brookfield associates with standard paint, coating, and ink testing. The optional paste spindle extends that into materials outside the standard range, such as roller mill pastes, without requiring a separate instrument.

sections.title: Direct Drive and Dial Readout
sections.tabSummary: How the mechanical measurement principle works
body: How the mechanical measurement principle works.

Unlike Brookfield's touchscreen instruments, Dial Reading Viscometer reads torque off a mechanical dial rather than a digital display. The multi-speed electronic drive behind that dial is a direct drive design, which Brookfield states delivers quiet operation and works reliably across global power sources — a consideration relevant for labs operating across different regions or power infrastructure.

Speed selection uses an ergonomic control knob to move between pre-set speeds directly, rather than navigating a menu. Standard models offer 10 pre-set speeds; LVT models offer 8. Continuous torque sensing keeps the reading live throughout a test, and the underlying accuracy and repeatability figures — 1% and 0.2% of full-scale range — match what Brookfield states for its digital DVNext line, despite the different readout method.

sections.tabSummary: Why the lid fan is the whole speed story
body: Why the lid fan is the real story behind the 25% figure.
Loss-on-drying testing has a bottleneck most people don't think about: the chamber has to cool before the next sample goes in. Every minute spent cooling is a minute the instrument isn't testing.
MAX 4000XL's built-in lid fan solves that directly. It cools the heating chamber fast, and Brookfield states the result plainly: 25% faster throughput than other rapid loss-on-drying instruments.
That's not a marginal gain. Across a full shift of testing, 25% is the difference between finishing the queue and carrying samples into tomorrow.

paragraphs: Not all moisture behaves the same way. Some evaporates fast and easily — free moisture. Some is chemically bound to the material and needs a different temperature, a different endpoint, to release.

MAX 4000XL links multiple test stages into one sequence. Temperature, ending criteria, and timing can all change between segments — so a single run captures both free and bound moisture without manual intervention between stages.
User-adjustable ending criteria go further: the test stops when your material says it's done, not when a generic default says so.

body: Computrac MAX 5000XL vs thermogravimetric analyzers: why 600°C changes the value proposition.

Thermogravimetric analyzers measure moisture, solids, and ash by precisely tracking mass change as temperature rises. They're the reference standard for this kind of testing. They also carry a price tag that puts them out of reach for many labs that only occasionally need that level of capability.

MAX 5000XL closes that gap. A heater reaching 600°C runs both loss-on-drying and loss-on-ignition tests, which is what lets one sample yield moisture, solids, and ash data without switching equipment. Brookfield states this plainly: features typically found in more expensive thermogravimetric analyzers, delivered in a solution built for a fraction of the cost.

heroParagraphs: Thermogravimetric analyzers do this job well. They also cost a lot more than most labs need to spend. Computrac® MAX 5000XL delivers the features typically found in a TGA, at a fraction of the price.

The heater reaches up to 600°C, hot enough to run both loss-on-drying and loss-on-ignition tests on the same sample. That means moisture, solids, and ash content, all from one measurement, not three separate tests on three separate instruments.

Results come back in half an hour or less. One-button operation runs the whole test, no intermediate weighing, no manual cooling steps in between. The enclosure is cast aluminum, built for the production floor as much as the lab bench.

What it replaces: the need for a separate, expensive TGA for many applications. What it adds: a self-cleaning oven cycle, 45 minutes at 550°C, that keeps maintenance simple. Where it fits: plastics, pharmaceuticals, foods, and biomass materials.

sections.title: Moisture-Specific Detection, Not Weight Loss
sections.tabSummary: Why RH-sensor technology changes what gets measured
body: Computrac Vapor Pro XL detection method: why RH-sensor technology changes what gets measured.

Loss-on-drying and loss-on-ignition methods measure how much mass a sample loses when heated, then assume the loss is moisture. That assumption breaks down when a sample contains other volatile compounds. The instrument can't tell the difference, and the result reads high.

Vapor Pro XL sidesteps that problem entirely. RH-sensor technology detects moisture specifically, not total mass loss, which means the result reflects actual water content even in samples where other volatiles are present. Sensitivity reaches 10 micrograms of water, low enough to determine moisture content as low as 10ppm, a level weight-loss methods typically can't resolve reliably.

sections.title: The Nine Measurements
sections.tabSummary: What each output tells you about handling behavior
body: PFT Powder Flow Tester measurement outputs: what each number tells you about handling behavior.

A single flow function number doesn't tell a hopper designer everything they need. PFT's testing produces nine distinct outputs, each answering a different practical question about how a powder will actually behave in equipment.

Bulk density, measured at fill and final states, establishes the baseline the rest of the data builds from. Wall friction predicts how the powder interacts with the specific material a hopper or chute is built from, not a generic assumption. Flow index summarizes overall flowability. Arching dimensions and rat-hole diameter predict the two most common hopper discharge failures before either happens on the production line. Hopper half angle informs the actual geometry a new hopper needs. Carr Index and Hausner Ratio flag compressibility and caking risk. Time consolidation testing, run alongside the full flow function data, captures how flow behavior changes after a powder has sat in storage, a condition standard single-point testing misses entirely.

rows: How dense is the powder, loose and settled?
Will it stick to the hopper wall?
How well does it flow overall?
Will it arch and stop flowing?
Will it rat-hole through the center?
Is it prone to caking or poor compressibility?
Does flow behavior change after storage?

longForm.heroLead: PVS Rheometer is a dynamic coaxial cylinder, controlled shear rate rheometer for measuring viscosity under pressure at elevated or reduced temperatures, where sample boil-off could otherwise be a problem. Brookfield describes it as suited to simulating in-process conditions on small fluid samples, in industries including chemicals, oil, food processing, polymers, and paints. Pressure range extends to 1000 psi, with a temperature range of -40°C to +260°C. An RTD temperature sensor on the inner cylinder surface measures sample temperature directly. The outer cylinder rotates at shear rates up to 1700 sec⁻¹, and the instrument measures down to 0.2 sec⁻¹ for low shear rate viscosity (LSRV) work. A robust motor reaches speeds up to 1000 RPM, with a stationary spindle inside the rotating outer cylinder. Standard construction uses Hastelloy cups and bobs. A triple annulus geometry option is available for increased sensitivity on low-viscosity fluids. The instrument is designed to meet API industry standards, and includes a safety relief valve. Rheovision software automates and controls test parameters. The footprint is 1' x 1' x 2', described by Brookfield as compact enough for site-to-site mobility.

sections.tabSummary: Why boil-off is the problem this design addresses
body: Why boil-off is the problem this design addresses.

A volatile fluid tested at ambient pressure and elevated temperature can boil off before or during measurement, changing its composition and invalidating the result. PVS Rheometer's coaxial cylinder chamber operates under pressure specifically to prevent that — up to 1000 psi, across a temperature range of -40°C to +260°C, which Brookfield states makes it suitable for elevated or reduced temperature testing where boil-off would otherwise be an issue.

An RTD sensor mounted on the inner cylinder surface measures sample temperature directly at the point of shear, rather than inferring it from the chamber wall or an external probe. A safety relief valve is fitted as standard, addressing the operational risk of running a sealed chamber under both pressure and temperature extremes.

cards.title: Accurate measurement at very low shear rates
Coverage into higher shear conditions on the same instrument

paragraphs: Many process conditions — down-hole drilling, slow blending, reactor flow — happen at shear rates well below what a standard rotational instrument resolves accurately. PVS Rheometer measures down to 0.2 sec⁻¹ for low shear rate viscosity (LSRV) work, extending the usable range into conditions that matter directly for in-process simulation.

At the other end, the outer cylinder rotates at shear rates up to 1700 sec⁻¹, with a stationary spindle inside, giving the instrument range across both slow and fast shear conditions on the same coaxial cylinder geometry. Where the fluid itself is low-viscosity and the standard geometry doesn't provide enough measurement sensitivity, the optional triple annulus geometry increases sensitivity specifically for that case.

heroParagraphs: PVS Rheometer is a dynamic coaxial cylinder, controlled shear rate rheometer for measuring viscosity under pressure at elevated or reduced temperatures, where sample boil-off could otherwise be a problem. Brookfield describes it as suited to simulating in-process conditions on small fluid samples, in industries including chemicals, oil, food processing, polymers, and paints.

Pressure range extends to 1000 psi, with a temperature range of -40°C to +260°C. An RTD temperature sensor on the inner cylinder surface measures sample temperature directly. The outer cylinder rotates at shear rates up to 1700 sec⁻¹, and the instrument measures down to 0.2 sec⁻¹ for low shear rate viscosity (LSRV) work. A robust motor reaches speeds up to 1000 RPM, with a stationary spindle inside the rotating outer cylinder.

Standard construction uses Hastelloy cups and bobs. A triple annulus geometry option is available for increased sensitivity on low-viscosity fluids. The instrument is designed to meet API industry standards, and includes a safety relief valve. Rheovision software automates and controls test parameters. The footprint is 1' x 1' x 2', described by Brookfield as compact enough for site-to-site mobility.

sections.tabSummary: Why cone/plate and concentric cylinder on the same platform matters
body: Why cone/plate and concentric cylinder on the same platform matters.

Different materials and test protocols call for different rheometer geometries — cone/plate suits certain viscosity ranges and sample volumes, concentric cylinder suits others. Buying separate instruments for each geometry means separate footprints, separate calibration routines, and separate operator training. RSO Rheometer supports both configurations on the same instrument, described by Brookfield as instrument flexibility suited to a wide range of material testing applications.

A quick connect coupling system attaches spindles without a lengthy fitting process, and automatic gap setting handles the spindle-to-plate distance that cone/plate geometry depends on for accurate shear rate calculation — a step that's traditionally manual and operator-sensitive on other instruments. Spindle barcode recognition identifies which geometry and spindle configuration is fitted automatically, reducing the chance of a test running against the wrong configuration data.

sections.title: High Torque for Difficult Samples
sections.tabSummary: Why 200 Nm matters against a standard motor
body: Why 200 Nm matters against a standard motor.

Testing high-viscosity or highly structured materials — pastes, gels, filled compounds — requires enough torque to actually shear the sample without the motor stalling or the measurement losing accuracy at the top of its range. RSX Coaxial Cylinder's 200 Nm motor is described by Brookfield specifically as an increase over a standard motor, aimed at testing the toughest samples for comprehensive analysis across a wide range of materials.

That torque capacity pairs with coaxial cylinder geometry, which Brookfield states delivers the most accurate results particularly in low-viscosity ranges — meaning the instrument's usable range extends in both directions, from difficult high-torque materials through to precision measurement at the low-viscosity end, on the same geometry.

paragraphs: Temperature-dependent rheology testing needs the sample held at a controlled temperature throughout the measurement, and different lab setups favor different methods of achieving that. RSX Coaxial Cylinder supports two: direct immersion in a temperature-controlled bath, or external circulation using the FTKY3 water jacket, across a stated range of -20°C to 180°C.

Direct bath immersion suits labs already running a compatible bath as part of the workflow. The FTKY3 water jacket option instead circulates temperature-controlled fluid externally around the sample chamber, which may suit setups where immersing the entire measuring head isn't practical. Both methods cover the same overall temperature range.

sections.tabSummary: Why having both modes on one instrument matters
body: Why having both modes on one instrument matters.

Some rheological questions are best answered by fixing the shear rate and observing how stress responds; others need the reverse — fixing shear stress and observing the resulting shear rate, particularly around yield behavior. RSX Cone Plate runs both: controlled shear rate (rpm) and controlled shear stress (torque), named explicitly as distinct operating modes rather than one general controlled-shear description.

That distinction matters for method design. A test protocol built around controlled stress — common for yield stress work — and one built around controlled rate — common for standard flow curve generation — can both run on the same instrument without switching hardware, only the operating mode.

paragraphs: Cone/plate rheometry depends on an accurate, consistent gap between the cone tip and the plate — get it wrong and the shear rate calculation the whole measurement rests on is wrong too. RSX Cone Plate automatically detects and adjusts that gap specifically with standard one-piece spindles, removing a manual step that's traditionally sensitive to operator technique.

Combined with auto spindle recognition via barcode, which automatically sets the correct spindle configuration, and the quick connect coupling system for physical attachment, the setup sequence from spindle selection to test-ready gap is largely automated rather than depending on a trained operator getting each step right by hand.

faqs.question: What is the RSX SST Rheometer used for?
faqs.answer: It's a Soft-Solids Tester for characterizing pastes, slurries, and soft solid materials, measuring creep, yield stress, and viscosity profile.

faqs.question: Why does it use vane and cross-hatch geometry instead of standard spindles?
faqs.answer: Standard smooth cone/plate or cylinder geometry can allow soft-solid or paste-like samples to slip at the measuring surface rather than shear internally, corrupting the measurement. Vane and cross-hatch geometry are used specifically to minimize that slippage.

faqs.question: What operating modes does it support?
faqs.answer: Controlled shear rate (rpm) and controlled shear stress (torque).

faqs.question: What are the core measurement types?
faqs.answer: Creep analysis, yield stress determination, and viscosity profiling.

faqs.question: How is the spindle gap set?
faqs.answer: Automatically, removing manual adjustment.

faqs.question: How are spindles recognized?
faqs.answer: Via barcode, automatically identifying and setting the correct spindle configuration.

faqs.question: What temperature control options are available?
faqs.answer: Peltier or fluid-heated.

faqs.question: Is it suitable for the production floor?
faqs.answer: Yes, described as rugged and built to withstand production floor demands while maintaining precision.

faqs.question: How much sample does a test require?
faqs.answer: A small sample volume, supporting rapid setup and cleanup.

faqs.question: How is RSX SST different from RSX Cone Plate or RSX Coaxial Cylinder?
faqs.answer: RSX SST uses vane and cross-hatch geometry specifically for soft solids, pastes, and slurries, where slippage is a problem on smooth cone/plate or cylinder geometry. RSX Cone Plate and RSX Coaxial Cylinder are built for standard flowable materials, with torque motors stated at 200 mNm and 200 Nm respectively.

faqs.question: How is RSX SST different from RSO Rheometer?
faqs.answer: RSO supports cone/plate and concentric cylinder geometry with stand-alone touchscreen operation, suited to standard-condition fluids. RSX SST is purpose-built with vane and cross-hatch geometry specifically for materials that slip on those standard geometries.

sections.title: Why Vane and Cross-Hatch Geometry
sections.tabSummary: The slippage problem this design solves
body: The slippage problem this design solves.

Standard cone/plate or smooth cylinder geometry works because the sample shears cleanly against the measuring surface. Pastes, slurries, and soft solids often don't behave that way — instead of shearing internally, the material slips at the surface of a smooth spindle or plate, which corrupts the measurement without necessarily looking wrong to the operator.

RSX SST addresses that specifically with vane and cross-hatch spindle geometries, described by Brookfield as used specifically to minimize slippage in soft-solid and paste-like samples. A vane geometry effectively traps material between its blades so the sample shears against itself rather than against a smooth surface; cross-hatch geometry provides a textured surface with the same intent.

rows: Shear happening within the sample, not at its surface
Purpose-built geometry rather than adapted smooth-surface spindles
Confidence the reading reflects the material, not an artifact
