body: The whole column body is UHMWPE, not just the piston seals the way it is on PC01 or PC02. Nothing in the flow path is metal, which is exactly what biochromatography and other sensitive applications require.

Piston actuation comes in two forms. Type A moves the input piston with flange bolts. Type B uses a central stainless steel threaded rod instead, which sits outside the mobile phase and doesn't compromise the non-metal contact claim.

Frits are polypropylene here, not stainless steel mesh, at 10 micron pore size, coarser than PC01's 3 microns or PC02's 5 microns. That coarser frit matches the lower pressure ceiling a plastic column is built to handle.
Pressure runs lower than either metal line. 16 bar down to 5 bar across the confirmed range, well below PC02's 15 to 50 bar and far below PC01's 80 to 200 bar.
One discrepancy in the source data is worth noting directly. The column labeled PC04-25/250 lists an inner diameter of 50 mm, not 25 mm, in its own configuration data.
Two related variants exist within the confirmed range. PC01 (high-pressure) and PC02 (medium-pressure), both cross-referenced directly by ECOM's own page.

sections.title: Fixed Flange Design and Frit Exchange
body: PC06 solves the packing problem differently than ECOM's piston-driven lines. Instead of a moving piston maintaining bed compression, the flanges stay fixed on both input and output, and the frit itself becomes the serviceable component.

Flange inserts allow the frit to be exchanged directly, connected to the same liquid distribution system that ensures even flow across the bed. This is a genuinely simpler mechanism than dynamic axial compression, matched to a pressure range where that simplicity doesn't cost you separation quality.

sections.title: Whole-Column Hydraulic Compression
body: PC08 solves bed compression differently than every other ECOM line. Instead of an internal piston moving inside a fixed tube, the hydraulics sit in the stand itself, and the whole column gets pressed upward against a fixed flange at the top of the system.

For the 150 and 200 millimeter columns, that pressing continues actively during use. A 40 ton hydraulic cylinder, double action with a 200 to 600 millimeter stroke, compensates for bed volume changes as separation runs, rather than only packing once at the start. The stand connects to the upper flange through five rods, robust enough to hold the whole assembly under that force, while still letting the column itself come out without taking the frame apart.

faqs.question: What is Separpress used for?

faqs.question: What's the difference between D and S cylinder types on Separpress?
faqs.answer: D refers to a double-action hydraulic cylinder, while S refers to a spring-return cylinder typically used on smaller systems. Smaller single-action cylinders rely on liquid pressure to retract the piston rather than pulling it out mechanically.

faqs.question: What does the MM or EE code mean in a Separpress model name?
faqs.answer: MM means a manual oil pump paired with a mechanical manometer, while EE means a motor-driven pump paired with an electronic pressure gauge. Larger cylinders, D30 and above, come only with motor-driven pumps due to the higher oil-flow rate required.

faqs.question: What power range does Separpress cover?

faqs.question: What piston stroke lengths are available?
faqs.answer: Piston stroke across the Separpress lineup ranges from 80mm to 500mm, depending on the system selected.

faqs.question: Can Separpress be used in hazardous environments?
faqs.answer: Yes, all EE-configured systems, those with a motor-driven pump and electronic gauge, can be modified for use in hazardous environments.

Larger cylinders, D30 and above, are only offered with a motor-driven pump, since the higher oil-flow rate they need isn't practical to deliver by hand.

The letter after the model name tells you the cylinder type, D for double-action, or S for a spring-return cylinder typically used on smaller systems. The two-letter code that follows covers the pump and gauge together: MM means a manual pump paired with a mechanical manometer, while EE means a motor-driven pump paired with an electronic pressure gauge. Smaller single-action cylinders rely on liquid pressure to retract the piston, since they can't pull it out mechanically on their own. Once you move into D30 and above, motor-driven pumps become the only option, simply because the oil-flow rate needed at that scale isn't practical to generate by hand.

Each is fully controlled through modified ECOMAC software, which sets separation parameters and monitors both detector signal and column pressure from a single PC.
HP 400 runs a 399mm ID, 1000mm long column packed with 15 µm spherical silica using a sedimentation packing procedure, at up to 80 bar.
800 FP steps up in column diameter to 799mm, at up to 50 bar, and adds a special floating piston along with an automatic bypass detection system, Separpass 03, positioned 10 meters from the column.

300 DS uses a narrower 299mm ID but a longer 1300mm column with full-length piston stroke, packed with finer 10 µm silica by a dynamic slurry method, running at up to 100 bar, the highest pressure rating of the three.

300 DS is the only configuration built with its own dedicated hydraulic system, a Separpress D100 EE 1300 rated for 100 tons of force and 1300mm of stroke, alongside a flow reversion block that lets flow direction in the column be changed.
Every system uses multiple Hydracell membrane pumps working together to handle mobile phase delivery, sample injection, and, on 800 FP and 300 DS, additional roles like piston actuation.
Pump motors across all three systems are powered through a remote switchboard using ABB frequency converters, allowing flow changes to be managed centrally.

Because these are examples of already-delivered units rather than fixed catalog products, Inkarp recommends working directly with ECOM's specialists to develop the right specification for your process.

sections.title: System Architecture and Pump Configuration
body: Each Separsys system routes mobile phase, sample, and pressure control a little differently, shaped by its column size and target application.

On HP 400, three Hydracell P3 pumps split the work cleanly: two run in parallel to supply the mobile phase, while the third delivers the sample mixture to be separated, all monitored through electronic pressure sensors on the delivery block. 800 FP scales that up, pairing a higher-capacity Hydracell G10 pump for mobile phase supply with multiple G3 pumps handling sample injection and, notably, moving the column's floating piston, all routed through air-controlled ball valves rather than manual ones. 300 DS takes a different approach entirely, using two Hydracell G04 pumps rated for higher pressure (120 bar each) to handle mobile phase and sample together, while a separate, purpose-built Separpress hydraulic system handles the piston stroke across the column's full 1300mm length, an approach that also enables its dedicated flow reversion block.

longForm.heroHook: The smallest roll-based slot-die coater footprint on the market, with 500 mm of deposition length behind it.
longForm.heroLead: Spin coating tells you a formulation works. It doesn't tell you whether that formulation will actually scale. FOM nanoRC closes that gap at the smallest possible footprint and cost. It's a benchtop slot-die coating machine that mimics the coating processes of large-scale roll-to-roll production, giving precise, reproducible, and scalable thin films from any solution or slurry precursor onto flexible substrates. A touch display controls drum speed, temperature, and rotation direction directly, a built-in drying system handles the film after deposition, and the whole unit stays portable and light enough to move around a lab, with no scheduled maintenance required to keep it running.

sections.title: Product Information
sections.description: FOM nanoRC product information: coating mechanics, control features, and lab-scale positioning.
body: The system deposits thin films from solution or slurry-based precursors onto flexible substrates, with a deposition length of 500 mm.
It's built to mimic the coating processes of large-scale roll-to-roll machines, giving a genuine miniaturized demonstration of industrial-scale slot-die coating rather than an approximation.

A touch display serves as the control panel, letting operators adjust drum speed, temperature, and rotation direction directly, with a physical power switch on the machine itself rather than a software-based one.
Key components include the touch display, a slot-die mounting gantry, adjustable feet, a removable drip tray, and a substrate support drum, with ventilation ducts and a power plug at the rear.
A drying system is built in, handling the deposited film as part of the coating process rather than requiring a separate step.
The machine doesn't come with an integrated syringe pump as standard, though FOM Technologies offers the option to combine the nanoRC with a compatible pump for precursor delivery.
Construction stays portable and compact, light enough to move around a lab, and the system is designed to run without scheduled maintenance or service.
It complies with the Machine Standards EN 60204-1 and ISO 13849-1 (CE), meeting the requirements of the 2006/42/EC Machinery Directive Annex II B.

sections.eyebrow: Replacing Spin Coating with Real Scalability
sections.title: Replacing Spin Coating with Real Scalability
sections.description: Spin coating is fast and familiar, but it answers a narrower question than most research programs actually need answered. Substrate size restraints, difficult batch processing, and a high percentage of material waste all limit how much a spin-coated result actually tells you about industrial viability. FOM nanoRC is built specifically to close that gap, replicating the coating process of large-scale roll-to-roll machines at laboratory scale, so results generated on the benchtop carry real, transferable relevance to pilot or production-scale coating lines. That makes it possible to develop or transfer thin-film knowledge directly into slot-die coating fabrication protocols, without the material consumption or hassle of a larger pilot line, while still supporting genuinely high-throughput experimental design.

sections.title: Machine Components and Control
sections.description: Every part of the coating process, from precursor delivery to the finished dried film, is handled through a small, purpose-built set of components.
body: The touch display sits at the center of daily operation, controlling drum speed, temperature, and rotation direction directly, with a physical power switch on the machine itself for turning the system on and off. The slot-die mounting gantry positions the coating head precisely over the substrate support drum, while a removable drip tray keeps runoff contained and cleanup simple between coating sessions. A built-in drying system processes the deposited film as part of the same workflow, and ventilation ducts at the rear manage airflow during operation. Because the system doesn't ship with an integrated syringe pump, FOM Technologies offers it as an optional combination, letting precursor delivery be matched to your specific formulation needs.

sections.title: Precision Coating and Web Handling
sections.description: Film uniformity depends on more than just the coating head itself. How the substrate moves and how precisely that head is positioned both matter just as much. Motorized height and tilt adjustment, accurate to +/- 1 µm, keeps the slot-die head positioned exactly where a formulation needs it, while an adjustable 0 to 90 degree coating angle gives control over deposition geometry beyond a single fixed setup. Bi-directional web handling with tension control manages how the substrate itself moves through the system, keeping tension consistent so the coated film doesn't distort or wrinkle during processing. Together, that combination is what delivers the uniform, reproducible dry film thickness the system is built around, from nanometers up through microns.

sections.title: Microporous Substrate Holding
sections.description: Sample flatness sounds like a small detail until it distorts an entire coating run, and most sheet coaters solve it with extra manual steps to fixate the substrate in place. FOM vectorSC's proprietary substrate holder takes a different approach, using a microporous structure that provides homogeneous suction across the substrate itself. That suction holds the sample flat directly, without needing the extra fixation steps typically required elsewhere, saving time on every single run rather than just occasionally. The result is excellent substrate flatness as a built-in property of the system, not something the operator has to work to achieve each time.

longForm.heroHook: Save a coating protocol once. Call it back and reproduce it exactly, every time.
longForm.heroLead: Every variable in a slot-die coating run, head position, pump timing, substrate fixation, is a chance for the next run to drift from the last one. FOM alphaSC is built to close that gap. A protocol library saves your deposition process in full, so recalling it reproduces the same run with high precision and gives you real insight into which variables actually moved between attempts. A microporous substrate holder provides homogeneous suction across flexible or rigid substrates, removing the manual fixation steps that usually eat into setup time between samples. The slot-die head itself moves on automated vertical and lateral axes, run through software-integrated pump control, for a systematic, accelerated workflow rather than manual positioning guesswork. Add post-deposition units, drying, annealing, compressed gas for quick-drying, and docking modules, and the standalone tool grows into a small-scale pilot processing line, built to carry your research from lab-scale proof of concept toward a higher technology readiness level.

body: Reproducibility in slot-die coating usually comes down to whether every variable in the process, substrate fixation, head position, pump timing, stayed identical between runs. FOM alphaSC is designed around removing the manual steps that normally introduce that drift.

A microporous substrate holder applies homogeneous suction across the substrate surface, holding flexible or rigid materials in place without the taping, clipping, or manual fixturing that typically adds setup time before a run can even start. The slot-die head itself moves on automated vertical and lateral axes, coordinated with software-integrated pump control, turning what would otherwise be manual positioning into a repeatable, systematic process.

Everything a given run needs, positions, timing, pump settings, saves into a protocol library, so calling that protocol back reproduces the exact same deposition conditions later, with visibility into which variables actually differ if a result doesn't match.

faqs.question: What is FOM SD 25 used for?
faqs.answer: FOM SD 25 is a PEEK slot-die coating head used for precise, uniform, non-contact thin-film deposition at coating widths up to 25 mm, built specifically for harsh chemical or high-temperature coating conditions.

faqs.question: Why choose PEEK over stainless steel for a slot-die head?
faqs.answer: PEEK offers exceptional thermal stability, broad chemical resistance, and low-friction wear reduction, making it better suited than steel for aggressive solvents or elevated process temperatures.

faqs.question: What coating width does FOM SD 25 support?
faqs.answer: It supports coating widths from 1 to 25 mm, the narrowest standard format in the PEEK series.

faqs.question: What flatness tolerance does FOM SD 25 hold?
faqs.answer: It holds a flatness tolerance of ≤ 5 µm across its entire surface.

faqs.question: What viscosity range can FOM SD 25 handle?
faqs.answer: It handles viscosities from 1 cPs up to over 100,000 cPs at 25°C.

faqs.question: Can FOM SD 25 be used for double-sided coating?
faqs.answer: Yes, double-sided coating applications are supported on the FOM moduloR2R machine.

faqs.question: Is FOM SD 25 easy to disassemble and clean?

faqs.question: Does FOM SD 25 work with a meniscus guide?
faqs.answer: Yes, the design works with or without a meniscus guide, adapting to different coating applications.

faqs.question: Are wider PEEK slot-die heads available?

longForm.heroHook: The same PEEK durability as SD 25 and SD 50, scaled to 100 mm.
longForm.heroLead: Wider formats put more surface area under the same demand for precision, and more chemistry exposure across that surface too. FOM SD 100 holds the line on both. Crafted from Polyetheretherketone for exceptional thermal stability, chemical resistance, and mechanical durability, it delivers ≤ 5 µm flatness tolerance across its entire surface at coating widths from 1 to 100 mm, handling viscosities from 1 cPs up to over 100,000 cPs at 25°C. Its low-friction characteristics reduce wear during coating, extending operational life while keeping maintenance requirements down.

sections.title: Product Information
sections.description: FOM SD 100 product information: PEEK construction, chemical resistance, and precision coating.
body: Constructed from Polyetheretherketone (PEEK), the head delivers exceptional thermal stability, chemical resistance, and mechanical durability suited to harsh coating environments.
Flatness tolerance holds at ≤ 5 µm across the entire surface, matching the precision of FOM's narrower PEEK heads despite the wider format.
Coating widths span 1 to 100 mm, double the range of the SD 50 head and four times that of SD 25, while keeping the same PEEK construction and precision.
Viscosity handling reaches from 1 cPs up to over 100,000 cPs at 25°C, covering thin, aggressive solvents through heavy formulations on the same head.
Exceptional thermal resistance lets the head withstand high temperatures encountered during coating without significant degradation.
High chemical resistance across a wide range of chemistries makes the head suitable for use with varied, aggressive coating materials.
Low friction characteristics reduce wear and frictional losses during coating, extending operational life and minimizing maintenance requirements.
A standard single manifold and a 1/2-20 UNF thread for tube connections come built into the head.
Lip protection on the slot-die supports a self-standing feature, aiding manufacturing processes.
The design works with or without a meniscus guide, adapting to different coating applications.
Custom shim and meniscus guide designs are supported, with precise FOM alignment design keeping shim and guide positioning reliable.
Double-sided coating applications are supported on the FOM moduloR2R machine.
A lightweight, high-quality protective flight case ships with the head for shipping and storage.

body: A slot-die head that's difficult to disassemble or clean adds friction to every changeover, and FOM SD 100 is engineered specifically to remove that friction, even at its larger format.

Lip protection on the slot-die supports a self-standing feature, making the head easier to handle and set down safely during manufacturing without needing a dedicated stand at every step. The design is engineered for effortless disassembly, assembly, and cleaning, and works with or without a meniscus guide depending on what a given coating application requires. A protective flight case ships with the head, keeping it protected during shipping and storage between uses, and an integrated pressure gauge enhances functionality directly on the unit.

faqs.question: What is the FOM SD 200 used for?
faqs.answer: It's a PEEK slot-die coating head for precision coating in harsh conditions, coating widths from 1 to 200 mm across applications including solar cells, OLEDs, batteries, membranes, and printed electronics.

faqs.question: What coating width does it support?
faqs.answer: 1 to 200 mm.

faqs.question: What viscosity range can it handle?
faqs.answer: From 1 cPs to more than 100,000 cPs at 25 °C — thin solutions through to highly viscous slurries.

faqs.question: What is the flatness tolerance?
faqs.answer: ≤ 5 µm, achieved over the entire inside plane surface of the slot-die.

faqs.question: Why is the head made from PEEK?
faqs.answer: Polyetheretherketone delivers exceptional thermal stability, high chemical resistance across a wide range of coating materials, mechanical durability, and low friction characteristics that reduce wear.

faqs.question: Can it be used with aggressive solvents?
faqs.answer: Yes. PEEK is highly resistant to a wide range of chemicals, making the slot-die suitable for use with varied and aggressive coating materials.

faqs.question: How does it handle high process temperatures?
faqs.answer: Exceptional thermal resistance allows it to withstand the high temperatures encountered during coating processes without significant degradation.

faqs.question: Are shims and meniscus guides customizable?
faqs.answer: Yes. Custom shim and meniscus guide designs are available, and the head works with or without a meniscus guide depending on the application.

faqs.question: How is the shim positioned accurately on reassembly?
faqs.answer: The FOM alignment design facilitates precise, reliable positioning of both the shim and the meniscus guide.

faqs.question: How easy is it to clean between formulations?
faqs.answer: The head is engineered specifically for effortless disassembly, assembly, and cleaning.

faqs.question: Does the head include pressure monitoring?
faqs.answer: Yes. An integrated pressure gauge is built into the head.

faqs.question: What tube connection does it use?
faqs.answer: A 1/2-20 UNF thread for connecting tubes.

faqs.question: Can it be used for double-sided coating?
faqs.answer: Yes, for double-sided coating applications on the FOM moduloR2R machine.

faqs.question: Does it stand on its own during handling?
faqs.answer: Yes. Lip protection on the slot-die supports a self-standing feature, aiding manufacturing and handling processes.

faqs.question: What is supplied with the head?
faqs.answer: A lightweight, high-quality protective flight case for shipping and storage.

faqs.question: How does FOM SD 200 differ from the other PEEK series heads?
faqs.answer: Width is the primary difference — SD 25, SD 50, SD 100, and SD 200 correspond to maximum coating widths of 25, 50, 100, and 200 mm. All share PEEK construction, custom shim and meniscus guide options, and the same design approach.

longForm.heroHook: 1 cPs to over 100,000 cPs. One head, five orders of magnitude.
longForm.heroLead: Formulation work rarely stays in one viscosity band. A dilute precursor solution today, a thick electrode slurry next month — and on most systems that means a second slot-die head, a second alignment procedure, and a second thing to maintain. FOM SD 200 handles the whole range: 1 cPs through more than 100,000 cPs at 25 °C, across coating widths from 1 to 200 mm. The precision behind that comes from manufacturing tolerance. Flatness on the inside planes holds to 5 µm or better across the entire surface — the specification that determines whether a coating bead stays uniform across the full width or thins toward the edges. Machined from PEEK, it brings three properties that matter in aggressive chemistry: thermal stability that withstands high coating temperatures without significant degradation, chemical resistance across a wide range of coating materials, and low friction that reduces wear and extends operational life. Designed for effortless disassembly, assembly, and cleaning, with custom shim and meniscus guide options and an integrated pressure gauge.

FOM SD 200 covers 1 cPs to more than 100,000 cPs at 25 °C on a single head, so dilute precursors and heavy slurries run through the same component without a second alignment or cleaning procedure.

sections.title: Precision Across the Widest Format
body: Holding tight flatness tolerance gets harder as coating width increases, since even small deviations across a wider surface compound into visible film non-uniformity.

FOM SD 500 holds ≤ 5 µm flatness across its entire surface despite being the largest standard-size head in the steel series, which is what keeps coatings uniform at the full 500 mm width rather than only at narrower settings. That precision pairs with a genuinely wide viscosity range, 1 cP up to over 100,000 cPs at 25°C, so the same head that coats a thin printed electronics ink can also handle a heavy battery slurry without needing separate hardware for each. Chemically passivated stainless steel 1.4404 construction keeps that precision intact over repeated use, resisting the corrosion that varied ink and slurry chemistries could otherwise introduce over time.

sections.eyebrow: Replacing Spin Coating with Real Scalability
sections.title: Replacing Spin Coating with Real Scalability
sections.description: Spin coating is fast and familiar, but it answers a narrower question than most research programs actually need answered. Substrate size restraints, difficult batch processing, and a high percentage of material waste all limit how much a spin-coated result actually tells you about industrial viability. FOM nanoRC is built specifically to close that gap, replicating the coating process of large-scale roll-to-roll machines at laboratory scale, so results generated on the benchtop carry real, transferable relevance to pilot or production-scale coating lines. That makes it possible to develop or transfer thin-film knowledge directly into slot-die coating fabrication protocols, without the material consumption or hassle of a larger pilot line, while still supporting genuinely high-throughput experimental design.

sections.title: Machine Components and Control
sections.description: Every part of the coating process, from precursor delivery to the finished dried film, is handled through a small, purpose-built set of components.
body: The touch display sits at the center of daily operation, controlling drum speed, temperature, and rotation direction directly, with a physical power switch on the machine itself for turning the system on and off. The slot-die mounting gantry positions the coating head precisely over the substrate support drum, while a removable drip tray keeps runoff contained and cleanup simple between coating sessions. A built-in drying system processes the deposited film as part of the same workflow, and ventilation ducts at the rear manage airflow during operation. Because the system doesn't ship with an integrated syringe pump, FOM Technologies offers it as an optional combination, letting precursor delivery be matched to your specific formulation needs.

The self-cleaning slot-die head removes that manual cleaning step between samples, keeping the system ready to move to the next material faster than a manual process would allow. Automatic ink-switching does the same for material changeovers, removing the manual handling that would otherwise interrupt a study's flow. Together with fully remote-optimized components and software, that means a researcher can spend allocated beam time watching material transitions unfold rather than managing the coating hardware itself.

sections.title: In-Situ Characterization with Synchrotron X-Rays
sections.description: Understanding how a thin film actually forms, not just what it looks like once finished, means watching the coating and drying process happen in real time under X-ray characterization. That's exactly the study FOM photonR2R is built to support.
body: Its compact footprint lets the coater sit directly inside a synchrotron beamline, rather than requiring samples to be coated elsewhere and transported in. That proximity is what makes true in-situ characterization possible, monitoring material transitions as they occur rather than only capturing a static end result. The system's versatility across roll-to-roll and sheet-based coating means the same platform adapts to whatever sample format a given beamline study calls for, without switching equipment mid-project.

sections.title: Precision Coating and Web Handling
sections.description: Film uniformity depends on more than just the coating head itself. How the substrate moves and how precisely that head is positioned both matter just as much. Motorized height and tilt adjustment, accurate to +/- 1 µm, keeps the slot-die head positioned exactly where a formulation needs it, while an adjustable 0 to 90 degree coating angle gives control over deposition geometry beyond a single fixed setup. Bi-directional web handling with tension control manages how the substrate itself moves through the system, keeping tension consistent so the coated film doesn't distort or wrinkle during processing. Together, that combination is what delivers the uniform, reproducible dry film thickness the system is built around, from nanometers up through microns.

sections.title: Controlling Shear and Gravity Effects
sections.description: The angle and position of a slot-die head relative to the coating roll changes how shear forces and gravity act on a wet film during deposition, and that's a variable most benchtop coaters don't give you access to. FOM arcRC's variable slot-die angles and positions around the coating roll put that control directly in your hands, letting you adjust for specific precursor rheology or film quality targets rather than working within a single fixed geometry. Paired with substrate heating up to 180°C, that gives genuine process-level control over how a film forms and dries, not just how much material gets deposited. This kind of control matters most for materials like perovskite formulations, where formation conditions directly affect final film performance.

sections.title: Building Your Production Line
sections.description: Industrial roll-to-roll equipment is usually built for one process and stays that way. FOM moduloR2R starts from the opposite assumption: that a research line needs to change as the research does. The base model, unwind, rewind, oven, and slot-die stations, handles simple pilot-scale thin film production immediately. From there, machine modules and process stations get added to customize and optimize the line for whatever coating process your work actually requires, including integrating entirely different deposition methods like flexographic, inkjet, or rotary screen printing alongside slot-die coating on the same frame. All-around web access keeps that expanded line maintainable and constantly monitorable, rather than becoming harder to service as it grows more complex.

sections.description: Sample flatness sounds like a small detail until it distorts an entire coating run, and most sheet coaters solve it with extra manual steps to fixate the substrate in place. FOM vectorSC's proprietary substrate holder takes a different approach, using a microporous structure that provides homogeneous suction across the substrate itself. The result is excellent substrate flatness as a built-in property of the system, not something the operator has to work to achieve each time.

body: Reproducibility in slot-die coating usually comes down to whether every variable in the process, substrate fixation, head position, pump timing, stayed identical between runs. FOM alphaSC is designed around removing the manual steps that normally introduce that drift.

A microporous substrate holder applies homogeneous suction across the substrate surface, holding flexible or rigid materials in place without the taping, clipping, or manual fixturing that typically adds setup time before a run can even start. The slot-die head itself moves on automated vertical and lateral axes, coordinated with software-integrated pump control, turning what would otherwise be manual positioning into a repeatable, systematic process.

Everything a given run needs, positions, timing, pump settings, saves into a protocol library, so calling that protocol back reproduces the exact same deposition conditions later, with visibility into which variables actually differ if a result doesn't match.

faqs.question: What is FOM SD 25 used for?
faqs.answer: FOM SD 25 is a PEEK slot-die coating head used for precise, uniform, non-contact thin-film deposition at coating widths up to 25 mm, built specifically for harsh chemical or high-temperature coating conditions.

faqs.question: Why choose PEEK over stainless steel for a slot-die head?
faqs.answer: PEEK offers exceptional thermal stability, broad chemical resistance, and low-friction wear reduction, making it better suited than steel for aggressive solvents or elevated process temperatures.

faqs.question: What coating width does FOM SD 25 support?
faqs.answer: It supports coating widths from 1 to 25 mm, the narrowest standard format in the PEEK series.

faqs.question: What flatness tolerance does FOM SD 25 hold?
faqs.answer: It holds a flatness tolerance of ≤ 5 µm across its entire surface.

faqs.question: What viscosity range can FOM SD 25 handle?
faqs.answer: It handles viscosities from 1 cPs up to over 100,000 cPs at 25°C.

faqs.question: Can FOM SD 25 be used for double-sided coating?
faqs.answer: Yes, double-sided coating applications are supported on the FOM moduloR2R machine.

faqs.question: Is FOM SD 25 easy to disassemble and clean?
faqs.answer: Yes, it's engineered specifically for effortless disassembly, assembly, and cleaning.

faqs.question: Does FOM SD 25 work with a meniscus guide?
faqs.answer: Yes, the design works with or without a meniscus guide, adapting to different coating applications.

faqs.question: Are wider PEEK slot-die heads available?
faqs.answer: Yes, FOM Technologies offers the PEEK Series in wider formats, including SD 50, SD 100, and SD 200, alongside the full Steel Series.

longForm.heroHook: 1 cPs to over 100,000 cPs. One head, five orders of magnitude.
longForm.heroLead: Formulation work rarely stays in one viscosity band. A dilute precursor solution today, a thick electrode slurry next month — and on most systems that means a second slot-die head, a second alignment procedure, and a second thing to maintain. FOM SD 200 handles the whole range: 1 cPs through more than 100,000 cPs at 25 °C, across coating widths from 1 to 200 mm. The precision behind that comes from manufacturing tolerance. Flatness on the inside planes holds to 5 µm or better across the entire surface — the specification that determines whether a coating bead stays uniform across the full width or thins toward the edges. Machined from PEEK, it brings three properties that matter in aggressive chemistry: thermal stability that withstands high coating temperatures without significant degradation, chemical resistance across a wide range of coating materials, and low friction that reduces wear and extends operational life. Designed for effortless disassembly, assembly, and cleaning, with custom shim and meniscus guide options and an integrated pressure gauge.

sections.title: Viscosity Range and Coating Precision
body: Formulation work rarely stays in one viscosity band, and most heads force a second purchase when it moves. FOM SD 200 covers 1 cPs to more than 100,000 cPs at 25 °C on a single head, so dilute precursors and heavy slurries run through the same component without a second alignment or cleaning procedure.

Precision comes from manufacturing tolerance. Flatness on the inside planes holds to 5 µm or better across the entire surface, not at selected measurement points, and that is what keeps the coating bead uniform across the full width rather than thinning toward the edges. Coating width runs from 1 mm for narrow trials up to 200 mm for pilot-relevant formats, with a standard single manifold distributing flow and an integrated pressure gauge showing what the head is actually experiencing during a run.

sections.title: Precision Across the Widest Format
body: Holding tight flatness tolerance gets harder as coating width increases, since even small deviations across a wider surface compound into visible film non-uniformity.

FOM SD 500 holds ≤ 5 µm flatness across its entire surface despite being the largest standard-size head in the steel series, which is what keeps coatings uniform at the full 500 mm width rather than only at narrower settings. That precision pairs with a genuinely wide viscosity range, 1 cP up to over 100,000 cPs at 25°C, so the same head that coats a thin printed electronics ink can also handle a heavy battery slurry without needing separate hardware for each. Chemically passivated stainless steel 1.4404 construction keeps that precision intact over repeated use, resisting the corrosion that varied ink and slurry chemistries could otherwise introduce over time.

sections.title: Choosing the Right Model
sections.description: Flow rate and operating pressure trade off directly across the Ariete® lineup, higher pressure settings reduce achievable flow rate on every model, so the right choice depends on which side of that trade-off the process actually needs. Smaller models like the Ariete 2006 and 3006 suit lower-volume production, topping out around 1,000 l/h at their lowest pressure setting. Mid-range models, the 3030 through 3160 series, scale up substantially, with the 3160 reaching 22,000 l/h at its lowest pressure point. The largest models, 5132 through 5400, are built for high-volume industrial lines, with the 5400 reaching up to 80,000 l/h. Every model in the range can be paired with the same customization options and high-efficiency add-ons, so scaling up in flow rate doesn't mean losing configuration flexibility.

sections.title: Choosing the Right Model
sections.description: Flow rate and operating pressure trade off directly across the Ariete® lineup, higher pressure settings reduce achievable flow rate on every model, so the right choice depends on which side of that trade-off the process actually needs. Smaller models like the Ariete 2006 and 3006 suit lower-volume production, topping out around 1,000 l/h at their lowest pressure setting. Mid-range models, the 3030 through 3160 series, scale up substantially, with the 3160 reaching 22,000 l/h at its lowest pressure point. The largest models, 5132 through 5400, are built for high-volume industrial lines, with the 5400 reaching up to 80,000 l/h. Every model in the range can be paired with the same customization options and high-efficiency add-ons, so scaling up in flow rate doesn't mean losing configuration flexibility.

Full traceability of parts, guaranteed by in-house manufacturing, supports audit and compliance needs beyond the certifications themselves.

body: Pharma Skid is an autonomous, turnkey system customized to specific production requirements, processing a wide range of applications up to a maximum pressure of 1500 bar.
Particle size reduction runs with maximum efficiency and optimal yield across cell rupture, nanoparticle, and nanoemulsion production, with meaningful energy savings built in.
The standard configuration includes a feed pump with by-pass system, the homogenizer itself, and an electrical power board, ready to connect into an existing production line.
A long list of options extends the base skid further: heat exchanger, dust release control system, and instrumentation for flow rate, temperature, conductivity, and turbidity measurement.
Skids are available across different sizes of the Ariete Series homogenizer range, matching capacity to the specific production requirement.
Aseptic operating conditions are supported, and every skid complies with pharmaceutical regulations, following cGMP and GAMP5 validation standards.
Beyond pharmaceutical and biotechnology, the same platform extends naturally into pharma food and nutraceutical applications.
Continuous or batch (collective) processing modes are both supported, including nanoemulsion and nanodispersion production with notable energy savings versus other cell disruption systems.

features: Clear Digital Display: The display shows actual values and set values, allowing users to monitor rotation speed and heating bath temperature during operation.
Separate Dynamic Control Knobs: Two dedicated control knobs make the system easy to operate. Fast turning supports larger value changes, while slow turning allows precise adjustment.
Lock Function: The lock function helps prevent accidental changes to selected values during operation, supporting better repeatability and safer use.
LED Ring Light System: The intuitive LED ring light system makes activated functions clearly visible, even from a distance.
Flexible Flask Positioning: The system allows easy adjustment of the immersion depth up to 155 mm and the inclination angle from 20° to 80°.
Standby Function: The standby function stops active operations. In motor lift versions, the standby button also lifts the evaporating flask from the heating bath.
Residual Heat Warning: The system provides a residual heat warning when the heating bath temperature is above 50°C, helping improve laboratory safety.

Hand Lift and Motor Lift Availability: The Hei-VAP Core is available as both hand lift and motor lift models, allowing laboratories to choose the lifting mechanism that best suits their operating style.

sections.title: The rotary evaporation cycle
sections.description: How the Hei-VAP Core gently removes solvent in a continuous loop of rotate, heat, evaporate, condense and collect.

steps.title: Rotate
steps.description: The flask spins (10–280 rpm), spreading a thin film for a large surface area.

steps.title: Heat
steps.description: The water/oil bath (20–210 °C) gently warms the sample.

steps.title: Evaporate
steps.description: Under vacuum, solvent boils off at low temperature, protecting the product.

steps.title: Condense
steps.description: Vapour cools on the G3 condenser (0.22 m² surface) back to liquid.

steps.title: Collect
steps.description: Recovered solvent drains into the receiving flask; product stays behind.

sections.disclaimer: This workflow explanation is illustrative. Real rates depend on solvent type, vacuum level, bath temperature, condenser setup, cooling efficiency and sample volume.

features: 5-Inch Touch Display: The central touch panel shows actual and set values and offers Basic and Advanced operating modes to match the process requirement.

Optional Vapor Temperature Display: The system can be configured to display vapor temperature for closer process visibility.
Upgrade-Ready Architecture: The Hei-VAP Expert can be upgraded to Hei-VAP Expert Control, adding vacuum and chiller control without replacing the core system.

longForm.heroHook: Precise, upgrade-ready rotary evaporation for laboratories that want more control.
longForm.heroLead: The Heidolph Hei-VAP Expert Rotary Evaporator is built for laboratories that need accurate, repeatable evaporation, distillation, sample concentration, and solvent recovery with clear process visibility and room to grow. A central 5-inch touch display and dedicated control knobs let users set values precisely or make quick changes during a run. An integrated solvent library, USB and Micro SD interfaces, and the option to upgrade to vacuum and chiller control make it suitable for both routine and more demanding evaporation work. It is available in hand lift and motor lift versions, with multiple glassware configurations to match different solvents, condensation needs, and laboratory setups.

sections.title: Hei-VAP Expert at a Glance
sections.description: Everything you need to evaluate the Hei-VAP Expert Rotary Evaporator: overview, features, applications, specifications, evaporation performance, configurations, documentation, and support.
body: The Hei-VAP Expert from Heidolph is built for laboratories that want more than basic solvent removal. It combines digital operation, accurate control of rotation and heating, and safety functions that support both routine work and more demanding evaporation tasks.

A central 5-inch touch display shows actual and set values, with Basic and Advanced modes to match the process requirement. Separate knobs for rotation and heating allow quick changes or precise fine adjustment, while the lock function helps prevent accidental changes during operation.

An integrated solvent library helps identify suitable vacuum settings when working with an external vacuum controller. USB and Micro SD interfaces support data handling, transfer of favorites, and updates.

The Hei-VAP Expert is upgrade-ready. It can be upgraded to Hei-VAP Expert Control, which adds vacuum and chiller control from the same display. This allows the setup to grow with the laboratory requirement without replacing the core system.

As a Heidolph Distributor and Service Provider in India, Inkarp supports laboratories with product consultation, application guidance, configuration assistance, installation, user training, and after-sales service.

steps.title: Rotate

steps.title: Heat
steps.description: The 6 L water or oil bath provides controlled heating from 20 to 210 deg C, depending on the medium.

steps.title: Evaporate
steps.description: Reduced pressure lowers the boiling point so solvent can evaporate gently from the sample.

steps.title: Condense
steps.description: Vapour reaches the selected condenser glassware and is cooled back into liquid.

steps.title: Collect
steps.description: Recovered solvent drains into the receiving flask while the concentrated sample remains in the evaporating flask.

longForm.heroLead: The Heidolph Hei-VAP Ultimate Rotary Evaporator is designed for laboratories that need controlled evaporation, distillation, sample concentration, and solvent recovery with larger process visibility and stronger connectivity. A central 7-inch touch display gives users access to operating values in Basic and Advanced modes. Dedicated knobs for rotation and heating allow quick adjustment during active operation, while the locking function helps prevent accidental changes. This page focuses on the Hei-VAP Ultimate Standard G3 vertical glassware Handlift, P/N 575-01300-00, with handlift operation, G3 vertical glassware, and no coated condenser or receiving flask. sections.subheading: Controlled rotary evaporation with larger visibility and Lab 4.0-ready connectivity
body: The Hei-VAP Ultimate from Heidolph is built for laboratories that need controlled rotary evaporation with larger process visibility, flexible operation, and digital connectivity.

The 7-inch touch display shows values clearly and supports Basic and Advanced modes. Users can manage rotation speed and heating bath temperature through the display or make quick changes during a run using the dedicated control knobs.

The system includes a timer, maximum temperature limitation, multilingual menu, text-based error messages, LED ring lights, pictogram status display, and a locking function to prevent accidental readjustment.

An integrated solvent library helps identify the required vacuum setting when working with an external vacuum controller. USB, Micro SD, LAN, and RS 232 interfaces support Lab 4.0-ready connectivity for laboratories that need stronger digital integration.

The Hei-VAP Ultimate can be upgraded to Hei-VAP Ultimate Control, including vacuum and chiller control. Inkarp supports laboratories in India with product consultation, configuration guidance, installation, user training, application support, genuine spares, and after-sales service.

steps.title: Rotate

steps.title: Condense
steps.description: Vapour cools across the condenser (0.22 m² surface) and returns to liquid.

steps.title: Collect
steps.description: Recovered solvent drains into the receiving flask while the sample stays behind.

longForm.heroHook: Integrated evaporation control with vacuum, cooling, saved methods, and automated process guidance.
longForm.heroLead: The Heidolph Hei-VAP Expert Control Rotary Evaporator is designed for laboratories that need more control over evaporation, distillation, sample concentration, and solvent recovery. A 5-inch touch display controls the complete evaporation system, including vacuum and cooling temperature. Separate quick-access knobs allow direct control of rotation and vacuum, while the display gives users an overview of all key parameters and the current process. This page focuses on the Hei-VAP Expert Control Standard Handlift, P/N 573-02300-00, with handlift operation, G3 vertical glassware, and no coated condenser or receiving flask. Other lift, glassware, coating, package, vacuum, and cooling configurations should be confirmed with Inkarp before quoting.

sections.description: Everything you need to evaluate the Hei-VAP Expert Control Rotary Evaporator: overview, features, applications, specifications, evaporation performance, configurations, automation, packages, documentation, and service support.
sections.subheading: Integrated control of evaporation, vacuum, and cooling from one display
body: The Hei-VAP Expert Control from Heidolph is built for laboratories that need integrated control of rotary evaporation parameters from one operating interface.

Unlike standard rotary evaporator setups where vacuum and cooling may be managed separately, the Expert Control version brings evaporation system control into the 5-inch touch display, including vacuum and cooling temperature.

The display gives users a clear overview of values and the current process. Active functions are shown through pictograms, while quick-access knobs support direct control of rotation and vacuum without navigating through multiple menu layers.

The system supports two favorites on the start screen, an expandable solvent library, user-defined evaporation ramps, and automated evaporation through the Dynamic AUTOaccurate Program, also called DAA. These functions help laboratories improve process repeatability and reduce manual intervention during evaporation work.

As a Heidolph Distributor and Service Provider in India, Inkarp supports laboratories with product consultation, configuration guidance, vacuum and cooling accessory selection, installation, user training, application support, and after-sales service.

faqs.question: What is the Hei-VAP Ultimate Control Rotary Evaporator?
faqs.answer: The Hei-VAP Ultimate Control is a Heidolph rotary evaporator designed for controlled solvent evaporation, vacuum distillation, sample concentration, and solvent recovery. It combines a 7-inch touch display, integrated vacuum and cooling temperature control, saved evaporation ramps, DAA automatic evaporation, and Lab 4.0-ready interfaces.

faqs.question: What is the exact Hei-VAP Ultimate Control model on this page?
faqs.answer: This page focuses on the Hei-VAP Ultimate Control hand lift model with G3 vertical glassware, P/N 575-02300-00. The confirmed configuration is handlift operation, G3 vertical glassware, and no coated condenser or receiving flask.

faqs.question: How is Hei-VAP Ultimate Control different from Hei-VAP Ultimate?
faqs.answer: Hei-VAP Ultimate Control adds integrated control of vacuum and cooling temperature from the 7-inch touch display. It also supports saved evaporation ramps, direct favorites, an expandable solvent library, and Dynamic AUTOaccurate Program for automatic evaporation.

faqs.question: How is Hei-VAP Ultimate Control different from Hei-VAP Expert Control?
faqs.answer: Both models support integrated vacuum and cooling temperature control, saved ramps, favorites, solvent library, and DAA. The main difference is that Hei-VAP Ultimate Control has a 7-inch touch display and USB, Micro SD, LAN, and RS 232 interfaces, making it Lab 4.0 ready.

faqs.question: What does the 7-inch touch display control?
faqs.answer: The 7-inch touch display controls the complete evaporation system, including rotation, vacuum, and cooling temperature. It also gives users an overview of all parameters and the current process.

faqs.question: Which quick-access knobs are available on Hei-VAP Ultimate Control?
faqs.answer: Hei-VAP Ultimate Control has separate quick-access knobs for vacuum and rotation. The right knob is used for direct vacuum control, and the left knob is used for rotation control.

faqs.question: What is Dynamic AUTOaccurate Program in Hei-VAP Ultimate Control?
faqs.answer: Dynamic AUTOaccurate Program, also called DAA, supports automatic evaporation with customizable control. It helps users manage evaporation behaviour, including foam avoidance and efficient evaporation.

faqs.question: Can users save evaporation processes on Hei-VAP Ultimate Control?
faqs.answer: Yes. Users can define and save their own evaporation processes as ramps. This helps laboratories repeat controlled evaporation processes with better consistency.

faqs.question: Can favorite methods be transferred between devices?
faqs.answer: Yes. The Hei-VAP Ultimate Control supports transfer of individual favorites to other devices using a USB stick. This is useful when laboratories want to standardize commonly used evaporation settings across similar systems.

faqs.question: Which interfaces are available on Hei-VAP Ultimate Control?
faqs.answer: Hei-VAP Ultimate Control includes USB, Micro SD, LAN, and RS 232 interfaces. These interfaces support Lab 4.0-ready connectivity and connection with compatible external systems.

faqs.question: What is the speed range of Hei-VAP Ultimate Control?
faqs.answer: The Hei-VAP Ultimate Control supports a rotation speed range of 10 to 280 rpm. This allows controlled rotation for routine evaporation, solvent recovery, distillation, and sample concentration workflows.

faqs.question: What is the heating bath volume and temperature range?
faqs.answer: The heating bath volume is 6 L. The heating bath temperature range is 20 to 100 °C with water and 20 to 210 °C with oil.

faqs.question: What evaporation rates are listed for Hei-VAP Ultimate Control?
faqs.answer: The listed evaporation rates at a temperature difference of 40 °C are 8.5 L/h for toluene, 5.8 L/h for acetone, 3.5 L/h for ethanol, and 1.2 L/h for water. Actual performance depends on solvent type, vacuum level, cooling efficiency, glassware, sample volume, and operating conditions.

faqs.question: Which packages are available for Hei-VAP Ultimate Control?
faqs.answer: The listed package directions for this product include University Research Package and University Research-Chill Package. Package availability, included accessories, and suitability should be confirmed with Inkarp before quoting.

faqs.question: What accessories may be required with Hei-VAP Ultimate Control?
faqs.answer: Accessory selection may include vacuum pumps, chillers or thermostats, glassware sets, flasks, tubing, receiving flasks, sensors, cables, and additional safety or process accessories. The final accessory set should be selected based on solvent, sample volume, cooling requirement, vacuum requirement, and workflow.

longForm.heroLead: Integrated evaporation control with 7-inch visibility, automation, and Lab 4.0-ready connectivity. The Heidolph Hei-VAP Ultimate Control Rotary Evaporator is designed for laboratories that need controlled evaporation, vacuum distillation, sample concentration, and solvent recovery with integrated process control. A 7-inch touch display controls the complete evaporation system, including vacuum and cooling temperature. Separate quick-access knobs allow direct control of vacuum and rotation, while the display gives users an overview of all parameters and the current process. This page focuses on the Hei-VAP Ultimate Control, hand lift model with G3 vertical glassware, P/N 575-02300-00, with handlift operation, G3 vertical glassware, and no coated condenser or receiving flask. Other lift, glassware, coating, package, vacuum, cooling, and accessory configurations should be confirmed with Inkarp before quoting.

sections.subheading: Integrated control of evaporation, vacuum, cooling, and connectivity from one display
body: The Hei-VAP Ultimate Control from Heidolph is built for laboratories that need integrated control of rotary evaporation parameters with larger process visibility, automation support, and digital connectivity.

The 7-inch touch display controls the complete system, including vacuum and cooling temperature. It gives users an overview of all parameters and the current process, while pictograms on the display show active functions for clear monitoring.

Separate quick-access knobs support direct operation during active use. The right knob provides direct vacuum control, while the left knob supports rotation control. Users can set values either through the touch display or through the quick-access knobs.

The system supports two favorites on the start screen, an expandable solvent library, USB transfer of favorites, user-defined evaporation ramps, and automatic evaporation through the Dynamic AUTOaccurate Program, also called DAA.
With USB, Micro SD, LAN, and RS 232 interfaces, the Hei-VAP Ultimate Control supports Lab 4.0-ready connectivity for laboratories that need connection with compatible external systems.

As a Heidolph Distributor and Service Provider in India, Inkarp supports laboratories with product consultation, configuration guidance, vacuum and cooling accessory selection, installation, user training, application support, genuine spares, and after-sales service.

faqs.question: What is the confirmed Hei-VAP Industrial configuration?
faqs.answer: The confirmed configuration is Hei-VAP Industrial with glassware A, P/N 518-13100-00.

faqs.question: What does Glassware A include?
faqs.answer: Glassware A includes one descending condenser, one expansion vessel, one 20 L evaporating flask, and one 10 L receiving flask.

faqs.question: What is the main difference between Hei-VAP Industrial and Hei-VAP Industrial Basic?
faqs.answer: The Hei-VAP Industrial includes a high-impact transparent PMMA door, non-fogging safety glass, metal-frame guard hood, receiver cassettes, and additional PMMA door housing. The Industrial Basic keeps the large-scale evaporation platform with reduced enclosure-based safety scope.

faqs.question: Is Hei-VAP Industrial suitable for foaming or splashing substances?
faqs.answer: Yes. Glassware A includes an expansion vessel and supports workflows where foaming or splashing behaviour may need to be managed.

faqs.question: What is the evaporating flask capacity?
faqs.answer: The evaporating flask capacity is 20 L.

faqs.question: What is the receiving flask capacity?
faqs.answer: The receiving flask capacity is 10 L.

faqs.question: What is the heating bath temperature range?
faqs.answer: The heating bath supports 20 to 100 deg C with water and 20 to 180 deg C with oil.

faqs.question: What pump capacity is required?
faqs.answer: The required pump capacity is 1.5 to 3 m3/h.

faqs.question: What cooling liquid consumption is required?
faqs.answer: The listed cooling liquid consumption is 150 to 250 L/h.

body: The Hei-VAP Industrial Basic Rotary Evaporator is designed for laboratories and pilot-scale facilities that need to process larger solvent volumes without moving directly into a fully enclosed industrial evaporation system.

This configuration, Hei-VAP Industrial B with glassware A, gives users a large-volume evaporation setup with a 20 L evaporating flask, 10 L receiving flask, descending condenser, expansion vessel, universal heating bath, receiver cassettes, programmable ramps, and a detachable 7-inch touch panel with control knobs.

The Basic version keeps the core industrial evaporation capability while reducing selected enclosure-based safety elements found in the full Hei-VAP Industrial model. This makes it suitable for labs that need scale, repeatability, and configuration flexibility, but also need to manage investment carefully.

products.overview: Your rotary evaporator stops every time someone has to refill a flask. This module means it does not have to.
features: Sensor or Time-Controlled Filling: Refilling the rotary flask is easy. Doing it every fifteen minutes is not. The module fills the flask either when a sensor detects that liquid is needed or at a time interval you program, so the distillation keeps moving without anyone returning to the bench.

Approx. 330 mL Coated Collector Vessel: A full collector is normally the point at which the process stops. The coated collector vessel holds approximately 330 mL and is emptied automatically on the schedule you set, so the next cycle starts without you.
Integrated Compressor: The compressor that empties the collector is built into the control box. There is no external compressed air line to source, plumb, or maintain.

Removable 7-Inch Touchscreen Control Panel: Filling parameters, collector emptying time, automatic cleaning, and manual operation are all entered on one removable 7 inch touchscreen. Automation should not add a second interface to learn.

Animated Process Display: The animated, easy-to-read screen shows which step is currently running, and a colour scheme tells you what is happening at any moment. You can see the state of the process before you decide whether it needs you.

Illuminated Control Knobs: The illuminated control knobs show from across the laboratory whether the system is being aerated, is under vacuum, or is under overpressure. Status you can read at a glance is status you will actually check.
Automatic Cleaning Mode: Preparing for the next process should not become another manual routine. Automatic cleaning is started directly from the touchscreen, which shortens turnaround between runs.
Manual Operation Mode: When a process needs direct control, manual operation is available from the same screen. Automation is the default, not the only option.

Chemical-Resistant Media Contact Parts: All parts that come into contact with the media, including the supplied tubing, are made of chemical-resistant materials. Your solvent list can change without the module becoming the limiting factor.

Direct Hei-VAP Benchtop Mounting: The control box with its integrated compressor mounts directly onto a Hei-VAP benchtop rotary evaporator using the bracket supplied. Adding automation does not mean redesigning the bench.
Compact Control Box: At 186 x 429 x 521 mm including the control panel and approximately 17 kg, the module keeps the automation close to the instrument instead of spreading it across the workspace.

Unattended Overnight and Weekend Operation: In combination with the corresponding evaporator system, the module enables efficient unattended operation. Solvents and solvent waste can be processed overnight and over the weekend, which is where the cost case usually lives.

Residue Drainage Configuration Choice: The module can be specified according to process need, including a version without automated residue drainage. The configuration follows your process rather than the other way round.

faqs.question: What is the Large Scale Hei-VOLUME Distimatic Pro used for?
faqs.answer: The Large Scale Hei-VOLUME Distimatic Pro is a Heidolph continuous automatic distillation module used to automate solvent recovery and continuous distillation on a compatible Hei-VAP benchtop rotary evaporator. It automatically fills the rotary flask, empties the collector vessel using an integrated compressor, and repeats the cycle, so long runs continue without an operator at the bench.

faqs.question: Which rotary evaporator is the Large Scale Hei-VOLUME Distimatic Pro compatible with?
faqs.answer: The Large Scale Hei-VOLUME Distimatic Pro is compatible with a Hei-VAP benchtop rotary evaporator, onto which the control box and its integrated compressor mount directly using the bracket supplied. Inkarp confirms compatibility against your existing Hei-VAP configuration before quotation.

faqs.question: What is the part number of the Large Scale Hei-VOLUME Distimatic Pro?
faqs.answer: The part number of the Large Scale Hei-VOLUME Distimatic Pro is 591-62230-00, supplied as the Hei-VOLUME Distimatic Pro Benchtop G9BXL. Inkarp is the authorized distributor for this Heidolph configuration in India.

faqs.question: How does the Large Scale Hei-VOLUME Distimatic Pro fill the rotary flask?
faqs.answer: The Large Scale Hei-VOLUME Distimatic Pro fills the rotary flask by either sensor-controlled or time-controlled filling, selected on the removable 7 inch touchscreen control panel. Sensor control responds to the actual flask level, while time control follows an interval you program.

faqs.question: What is the collector vessel capacity of the Large Scale Hei-VOLUME Distimatic Pro?
faqs.answer: The Large Scale Hei-VOLUME Distimatic Pro has a coated collector vessel of approximately 330 mL. The integrated compressor empties it on a time you program from the touchscreen, so the next distillation cycle begins without manual draining.

faqs.question: Does the Large Scale Hei-VOLUME Distimatic Pro need an external compressed air supply?
faqs.answer: No, the Large Scale Hei-VOLUME Distimatic Pro does not need an external compressed air supply, because the compressor that empties the collector vessel is integrated into the control box. This keeps the installation compact and removes the need to plumb a separate air line.

faqs.question: Can the Large Scale Hei-VOLUME Distimatic Pro run unattended overnight?
faqs.answer: Yes, the Large Scale Hei-VOLUME Distimatic Pro is designed for unattended operation, and in combination with the corresponding evaporator system it allows solvents and solvent waste to be processed overnight and over weekends. Automatic filling, automatic collector emptying, and repeat cycles remove the interventions that normally stop a run.

faqs.question: Is the Large Scale Hei-VOLUME Distimatic Pro suitable for aggressive solvents?
faqs.answer: The Large Scale Hei-VOLUME Distimatic Pro is built so that every part in contact with the media, including the supplied tubing, is made of chemical-resistant material, which supports a wide range of laboratory solvents. Share your solvent list with Inkarp to confirm suitability for your specific application.

faqs.question: Does the Large Scale Hei-VOLUME Distimatic Pro have an automatic cleaning mode?
faqs.answer: Yes, the Large Scale Hei-VOLUME Distimatic Pro has an automatic cleaning mode that is started directly from the removable 7 inch touchscreen, alongside automatic and manual operation. This shortens turnaround between distillation runs.

faqs.question: What power supply does the Large Scale Hei-VOLUME Distimatic Pro require?
faqs.answer: The Large Scale Hei-VOLUME Distimatic Pro requires 100 to 240 V AC at 50/60 Hz, with an L+N+PE connection, a maximum power input of 1,500 W, and a 15 A fuse. It carries IP42 protection to EN 60529.

faqs.question: What are the dimensions and weight of the Large Scale Hei-VOLUME Distimatic Pro?
faqs.answer: The Large Scale Hei-VOLUME Distimatic Pro measures 186 x 429 x 521 mm including the control panel and weighs approximately 17 kg. Confirm bench space next to your Hei-VAP rotary evaporator before installation.

longForm.heroLead: The Heidolph Large Scale Hei-VOLUME Distimatic Pro is a continuous automatic distillation module that turns a compatible Hei-VAP benchtop rotary evaporator into an unattended distillation system. It fills the rotary flask, empties the collector vessel, and repeats the cycle, so long solvent recovery runs no longer need someone standing beside the instrument. The confirmed configuration is the Hei-VOLUME Distimatic Pro Benchtop G9BXL, P/N 591-62230-00. It includes a removable 7 inch touchscreen control panel, an integrated compressor, a coated collector vessel of approximately 330 mL, and a mounting bracket that fixes the control box directly to the evaporator. Every part that touches your media, including the supplied tubing, is made of chemical-resistant material. Filling can be sensor-controlled or time-controlled. Cleaning has its own automatic mode. The workflow you already run does not change. The hours you spend supervising it do.

body: Continuous distillation is rarely limited by the evaporator. It is limited by the person standing next to it.
Automates the stops. Fills the rotary flask, empties the collector vessel, and repeats the cycle, without an operator at the bench.
Mounts directly to your Hei-VAP. The control box, with its integrated compressor, fixes onto a Hei-VAP benchtop rotary evaporator using the bracket supplied.

One screen runs everything. The removable 7 inch touchscreen sets sensor-controlled or time-controlled filling, programs the collector emptying time, and starts automatic cleaning or manual operation.
Coated collector vessel, approx. 330 mL. Emptied by the integrated compressor on the time you program, so the next cycle starts without you.
Runs overnight and over weekends. Solvents and solvent waste can be processed unattended, outside working hours.
Makes in-house reprocessing viable. Buy solvent at technical grade and reprocess it in-house, without the personnel cost that normally rules that out.
Chemical-resistant flow path. Every part in contact with the media, including the supplied tubing, is chemical-resistant, so your solvent list is not the limiting factor.

features: White PVDF Top Plate: The top plate is made of PVDF, a thermoplastic fluoropolymer, and it is white. In a titration, the endpoint is a colour change, and a white background is the difference between seeing it and guessing at it.

Stirring Volumes Up to 5 Litres: The Hei-Mix S handles stirring volumes up to 5 litres. That covers the working range of most titration setups, biochemical preparations, and small fermenters without over-specifying the instrument.

Speed Range of 0 to 2,200 rpm: The broad speed range allows quick mixing when a sample needs to homogenise fast, and gentle mixing when it does not. One instrument covers both ends of the same protocol.
104 mm Stirrer Plate: The 104 mm plate diameter is sized to the vessels the instrument is meant to carry, keeping the coupling to the stir bar reliable across the working volume range.

Built for Continuous Operation: The Hei-Mix S is constructed for continuous operation, which is what a small fermenter or an extended biochemical run actually demands. A certificate for continuous operation is available.
Robust Polyamide Housing: The polyamide housing is built to take the working life of a busy laboratory bench rather than a demonstration shelf.
Compact 126 x 80 x 140 mm Footprint: Bench space is the constraint nobody quotes for. At 126 x 80 x 140 mm and 1.1 kg, the Hei-Mix S adds a stirring station without taking a workstation away.
6 kg Maximum Permissible Load: The plate accepts a maximum permissible load of 6 kg, which comfortably covers filled vessels across the stirring range.
Shaded Pole Motor Drive: The shaded pole motor is a simple, proven drive with few points of failure, which is what continuous operation asks for.
Quiet Operation: Acoustic pressure is below 70 dB(A) in accordance with IEC 61010. In a laboratory running several stirrers at once, noise compounds.
IP21 Protection: The instrument carries IP21 protection to EN 60529 and is a Protection Class II device.
Stirring Only, No Heating: The Hei-Mix S does not heat. If your method needs a hot plate, this is the wrong model, and we would rather tell you that here than after delivery.

faqs.answer: The Hei-Mix S Magnetic Stirrer has a speed range of 0 to 2,200 rpm, driven by a shaded pole motor. The range covers both quick homogenisation and gentle mixing within the same method.

faqs.question: Why is the top plate of the Hei-Mix S Magnetic Stirrer white?
faqs.answer: The top plate of the Hei-Mix S Magnetic Stirrer is made of white PVDF, a thermoplastic fluoropolymer, so that colour changes during an application can be tracked precisely. In a titration, the endpoint is a colour change, and a white background makes it far easier to read.

faqs.question: Can the Hei-Mix S Magnetic Stirrer run continuously?

faqs.question: What is the maximum permissible load on the Hei-Mix S Magnetic Stirrer?

products.overview: Twenty litres, stirred gently, with no heat and no sudden start. Built for samples that cannot take either.
features: Gentle Stirring Without Heating: The Hei-Plate Mix 20 L was developed from Heidolph's stirring hotplate series and built deliberately without heating, for applications involving thermolabile substances. When your sample degrades with heat, the absence of a heater is not a missing feature, it is the specification.

Soft Start: The instrument accelerates gradually to the set speed. That gradual ramp prevents splashing, erratic starts, and the abrupt movement of the stirring rod that throws it out of coupling and can damage a delicate preparation.

Patented Kera-Disk Plate: The Kera-Disk plate is made of aluminium with a ceramic coating, and it is both chemical-resistant and scratch-resistant. Its distinctive composition and colour run across the Heidolph magnetic stirrer range, and it survives the spills that ruin a lesser plate.

Stirring Volumes Up to 20 Litres: The instrument handles solutions up to 20 litres, which covers preparation vessels well beyond the benchtop beaker range without asking you to stir them aggressively.
145 mm Plate Diameter: The 145 mm plate is compact for the volume it carries, which makes it workable with a range of accessories and vessels where bench space is tight.

Speed Range of 100 to 1,400 rpm: The range is tuned to gentle, controlled stirring of large volumes rather than fast homogenisation of small ones. Choosing this instrument means choosing control over speed.

25 kg Maximum Permissible Load: The plate carries up to 25 kg. This matters more here than on any small stirrer, because a filled large-volume vessel approaches that figure quickly. Check your filled weight before you order.
EC Motor Drive: The left-turning EC motor provides consistent torque across the speed range and is efficient, drawing 25 W in normal operation and 1.7 W in standby.
Quiet Operation: Acoustic pressure is below 50 dB(A). In a preparation laboratory running several stirrers at once, that is the difference between background noise and a nuisance.

10-Year Warranty: After registering the instrument, Heidolph warrants the magnetic stirrer for at least 10 years. The design has been refined over decades for dependable operation in demanding environmental conditions.
Built for Continuous Operation: A certificate for continuous operation is available for the Hei-PLATE range, which supports long, uninterrupted preparation and dissolution runs.
IP42 Protection: The instrument carries IP42 protection to EN 60529 and is a Protection Class I device.

faqs.question: What is the Hei-Plate Mix 20 L Magnetic Stirrer used for?
faqs.answer: The Hei-Plate Mix 20 L Magnetic Stirrer is a Heidolph large-volume magnetic stirrer used for gentle stirring of solutions up to 20 litres without heating. It was developed specifically for applications involving thermolabile substances, where heat would damage the sample.

faqs.question: Does the Hei-Plate Mix 20 L Magnetic Stirrer have a heating plate?
faqs.answer: No, the Hei-Plate Mix 20 L Magnetic Stirrer does not heat. It was developed from Heidolph's stirring hotplate series and built deliberately without heating, for thermolabile substances. If your method requires a heated plate, select from the Heidolph Hei-Plate Mix 'n' Heat range instead.

faqs.question: What is the maximum stirring volume of the Hei-Plate Mix 20 L Magnetic Stirrer?
faqs.answer: The Hei-Plate Mix 20 L Magnetic Stirrer stirs solutions of up to 20 litres. For volumes of 5 litres or less, the Hei-Mix S Magnetic Stirrer may be the more appropriate model.

faqs.question: What is the speed range of the Hei-Plate Mix 20 L Magnetic Stirrer?
faqs.answer: The Hei-Plate Mix 20 L Magnetic Stirrer has a speed range of 100 to 1,400 rpm, driven by a left-turning EC motor. The range is tuned for controlled, gentle stirring of large volumes rather than fast homogenisation.

faqs.question: What is the soft start on the Hei-Plate Mix 20 L Magnetic Stirrer?
faqs.answer: The soft start on the Hei-Plate Mix 20 L Magnetic Stirrer brings the stirring rod up to the set speed gradually. This prevents splashing, erratic starts, and the abrupt movement of the stirring rod that can throw it out of coupling and damage a delicate preparation.

faqs.question: What is the Kera-Disk plate on the Hei-Plate Mix 20 L Magnetic Stirrer?
faqs.answer: The Kera-Disk plate on the Hei-Plate Mix 20 L Magnetic Stirrer is a patented Heidolph plate made of aluminium with a ceramic coating, 145 mm in diameter. It is both chemical-resistant and scratch-resistant, which allows it to survive spills and aggressive media.

faqs.question: What is the maximum permissible load on the Hei-Plate Mix 20 L Magnetic Stirrer?
faqs.answer: The maximum permissible load on the Hei-Plate Mix 20 L Magnetic Stirrer is 25 kg. This matters in practice, because 20 litres of water alone weighs about 20 kg before the vessel is added, so weigh your filled vessel before selecting the instrument.

products.overview: Two knobs. Stir and heat. Everything else Heidolph put into the parts you do not touch.
features: Two Rotary Knobs, Direct Control: Speed and temperature are set on two rotary knobs against a scale. There is no menu, no display to read, and nothing between you and the two things you came to do.
Heating to 300 °C: The plate heats from 20 °C to 300 °C, which covers the great majority of heated stirring, dissolution, and reaction work carried out on a laboratory bench.
800 W Heating Power at 230 V: On an Indian 230 V supply the instrument delivers 800 W of heating output, which is what allows it to bring a liquid to temperature quickly rather than gradually.

PID Heating Control: The control algorithm holds the set temperature without overshooting past it. Overshoot is not a cosmetic problem, it is the difference between a controlled reaction and a spoiled one.

Separately Activated Heating: The heating function is switched on independently of stirring, and an LED in the button lights to show it is live. You cannot heat a plate by accident while reaching for the stirrer.

Optical Residual Heat Indicator: The indicator remains lit while the plate is above 50 °C. The most common burn on a hot plate stirrer happens after the heat has been switched off, and this is the feature that prevents it.
Large Safety Gap: The controls are separated from the heating plate by a large gap, so reaching for a knob does not mean reaching over a hot surface.
Die-Cast Aluminium Housing: The housing is die-cast aluminium: robust, durable, and chemical-resistant. The design is optimised to minimise operating errors as well as to survive spills.

Patented Kera-Disk Plate: The Kera-Disk surface is anodized aluminium, chemical-resistant and scratch-proof, and it transfers heat rapidly. Its distinctive colour and composition run across the Heidolph magnetic stirrer range.
25 kg Maximum Permissible Load: The plate carries up to 25 kg, including the vessel and its contents, which covers the vessel range this instrument is built for.

Temperature Probe Compatibility: With the EKT Hei-Con temperature control unit, the indication and measurement range extends from -80 °C to 350 °C. If your method needs the temperature of the medium rather than the plate, this is how you get it.
10-Year Warranty: After registering the instrument with Heidolph, the magnetic stirrer is warranted for at least 10 years, in a design refined over decades for demanding conditions.
