longForm.title: Hei-Plate Mix 'n' Heat Core Ultimate Magnetic Stirrer Product Information
longForm.description: The product information helps customers review connectivity, USB logging, e-Lift compatibility, heating modes, dual temperature sensing, specifications, accessories, documentation, and Inkarp support.
longForm.heroLead: The Heidolph Hei-Plate Mix 'n' Heat Ultimate is the connected, automated model in the Hei-PLATE range. RS232 and USB B ports allow control through the Hei-PROCESS solution, a front USB A port logs data straight to a USB stick, and a USB C port connects the electric Heidolph e-Lift lab jack. The confirmed configuration is the Hei-PLATE Mix 'n' Heat Ultimate (145 mm), P/N 506-41100-00. It heats to 350 °C, fifty degrees beyond the Core and Core+, with three selectable heating modules: FAST for speed, PRECISE and PRECISE+ for exact control without overshoot. It detects the stir bar automatically, spins clockwise or counterclockwise, resolves temperature to 0.1 K, and accepts a dual Pt1000 sensor so two temperature profiles can be run at once. With the e-Lift attached, it can lower the vessel out of the heat by itself on an overtemperature error or a timer expiry.

sections.title: Hei-Plate Mix 'n' Heat Core Ultimate Magnetic Stirrer at a Glance
sections.description: Everything you need to evaluate the Ultimate: connectivity, USB data logging, e-Lift compatibility, heating modes, dual temperature sensing, specifications, accessories, documentation, and Inkarp support.
body: The Ultimate is selected when the instrument must be integrated, logged, or connected to a larger workflow.
RS232, USB A, USB B and USB C interfaces support connection to software, process environments, USB storage, and e-Lift equipment.
Standalone data logging means run data can be stored to a USB stick without building a separate computer station around the instrument.
FAST, PRECISE and PRECISE+ heating modes allow the method to be configured around heat-up speed or sensitive sample control.
Configuration note: Confirmed model: Hei-PLATE Mix 'n' Heat Ultimate (145 mm), P/N 506-41100-00.
Four interfaces, not none. RS232 and USB B for control through Hei-PROCESS, a front USB A for logging to a stick, USB C for the e-Lift.
Three ways to reach temperature. FAST when speed matters, PRECISE and PRECISE+ when a degree of overshoot would ruin the sample.
It knows whether the stir bar is there. The automatic stir bar detector removes one of the commonest silent failures on a magnetic stirrer.
It can spin either way. Rotation direction is adjustable, and start-up behaviour has three stages.
It can get itself out of trouble. With the e-Lift, the vessel lowers automatically on an overtemperature error or when a timer expires.
More headroom than the rest of the range. It heats fifty degrees further than the Core and the Core+.
The Pt1000 and dual Pt1000 external sensors are separate items.
The e-Lift electric lab jack is a separate item and connects by USB C.
If you do not need interfaces, automation, or logging, the Hei-Plate Mix 'n' Heat Core + costs less and heats to 300 °C.
Product expert note: Tell our team what you need to automate, log, or integrate, and we will confirm the sensors, the e-Lift, and the interface before quotation.

faqs.question: What is the Hei-Plate Mix 'n' Heat Core Expert Magnetic Stirrer used for?
faqs.answer: The Hei-Plate Mix 'n' Heat Core Expert Magnetic Stirrer is Heidolph's safety and control hot plate magnetic stirrer, used for highly exothermic reactions, liquids with low ignition temperatures, materials with low melting points, and unsupervised heated runs. It heats to 350 °C with three selectable heating modes and two independent safety limits.

faqs.question: What is the settable ΔT on the Hei-Plate Mix 'n' Heat Core Expert Magnetic Stirrer?
faqs.answer: The settable ΔT on the Hei-Plate Mix 'n' Heat Core Expert Magnetic Stirrer is a user-defined maximum difference between the set temperature and the actual temperature. It provides additional safety during highly exothermic reactions and unsupervised operation, where the sample itself generates heat.

faqs.question: What is the digital plate temperature limitation on the Hei-Plate Mix 'n' Heat Core Expert Magnetic Stirrer?
faqs.answer: The digital plate temperature limitation on the Hei-Plate Mix 'n' Heat Core Expert Magnetic Stirrer is a user-set ceiling on the temperature of the heating plate itself. It provides additional safety for liquids with a low ignition temperature and for materials with a low melting point.

faqs.question: Does the Hei-Plate Mix 'n' Heat Core Expert Magnetic Stirrer protect against delayed boiling?
faqs.answer: Yes, the automatic stir bar detector on the Hei-Plate Mix 'n' Heat Core Expert Magnetic Stirrer confirms that the stir bar is turning, even when irregularities occur, which minimises the danger of delays in boiling.

faqs.question: What is the difference between the Hei-Plate Mix 'n' Heat Core Expert and the Core Ultimate?
faqs.answer: The two models share the same technical specification: 350 °C, 800 W at 230 V, 0.1 K resolution, two TFT displays, dual Pt1000 support, and bidirectional stirring. Heidolph documents the settable ΔT limit, the digital plate temperature limitation, separate timers, and programmable profiles on the Expert, and documents the RS232, USB A, USB B and USB C interfaces, standalone data logging, and e-Lift compatibility on the Ultimate.

faqs.question: What are the three heating modes on the Hei-Plate Mix 'n' Heat Core Expert Magnetic Stirrer?
faqs.answer: The Hei-Plate Mix 'n' Heat Core Expert Magnetic Stirrer has three selectable heating modes. FAST provides rapid heating. PRECISE and PRECISE+ provide exact temperature regulation without overshoot, protecting sensitive samples.

faqs.question: What does the dual Pt1000 sensor do on the Hei-Plate Mix 'n' Heat Core Expert Magnetic Stirrer?
faqs.answer: The dual Pt1000 sensor on the Hei-Plate Mix 'n' Heat Core Expert Magnetic Stirrer measures the temperature in the liquid and in the peripherals simultaneously, for example the sample and the bath liquid. When integrated into a process solution, control algorithms can be built between the two sensors interdependently.

faqs.question: What is the maximum temperature of the Hei-Plate Mix 'n' Heat Core Expert Magnetic Stirrer?
faqs.answer: The Hei-Plate Mix 'n' Heat Core Expert Magnetic Stirrer heats from 20 °C to 350 °C, with a setting accuracy of 1 K, at 800 W on a 230 V supply.

faqs.question: Does the Hei-Plate Mix 'n' Heat Core Expert Magnetic Stirrer have timers?
faqs.answer: Yes, the Hei-Plate Mix 'n' Heat Core Expert Magnetic Stirrer has separate timer functions for heating and for stirring. Together with programmable stirring and heating profiles, they allow reproducible, semi-automatic working.

sections.title: Safety limits and temperature control
sections.description: Safety limits and temperature control are delivered through a settable ΔT between set and actual temperature, a digital limitation of the plate temperature, three heating modes, an automatic stir bar detector, and dual Pt1000 sensing.
body: Two limits, and they guard against two different accidents.

The ΔT limit guards against the sample. In a highly exothermic reaction, the sample makes its own heat. You set the maximum allowable difference between the temperature you asked for and the temperature actually reached, and the instrument stops contributing to a runaway. This is the feature that makes unsupervised operation a considered decision rather than a gamble.

The digital plate limit guards against the plate. For a liquid with a low ignition temperature, or a material with a low melting point, the hazard is not the setpoint, it is the surface. A digital ceiling on the plate temperature caps it directly.

The stir bar detector guards against the bump. A stalled stir bar in a heated liquid leads to delayed boiling. The detector confirms the bar is turning even when irregularities occur, and minimises that danger.

faqs.question: What is the Hei-Torque Core with RS232 Overhead Stirrer used for?
faqs.answer: The Hei-Torque Core with RS232 Overhead Stirrer is Heidolph's lightest overhead stirrer, used for stirring media that a magnetic stirrer cannot turn. It delivers 65 Ncm of torque across 20 to 2,000 rpm, for viscosities up to 10,000 mPas or volumes up to 25 litres in water.

faqs.question: What is the maximum torque of the Hei-Torque Core with RS232 Overhead Stirrer?
faqs.answer: The maximum torque of the Hei-Torque Core with RS232 Overhead Stirrer is 65 Ncm. Torque, rather than speed, is the specification that determines whether an overhead stirrer can turn a given medium.

faqs.question: Can the Hei-Torque Core with RS232 Overhead Stirrer stir 25 litres of a viscous medium?
faqs.answer: No. The Hei-Torque Core with RS232 Overhead Stirrer handles viscosities up to 10,000 mPas or volumes up to 25 litres in water. These are two separate ceilings on the same 65 Ncm drive, not a combined capability.

faqs.question: What viscosity can the Hei-Torque Core with RS232 Overhead Stirrer handle?
faqs.answer: The Hei-Torque Core with RS232 Overhead Stirrer handles viscosities up to 10,000 mPas, at reduced volume. This is well beyond the point at which a magnetic stir bar decouples and stops turning.

faqs.question: What is included with the Hei-Torque Core with RS232 Overhead Stirrer?
faqs.answer: The Hei-Torque Core with RS232 Overhead Stirrer is supplied as a drive unit. The stand, boss head, stirring shaft, and stirring element are separate items and are not included.

faqs.question: What shaft diameters fit the Hei-Torque Core with RS232 Overhead Stirrer?
faqs.answer: The quick-action chuck on the Hei-Torque Core with RS232 Overhead Stirrer accepts stirring shafts from 0.5 mm to 10.5 mm in diameter. It is keyless, so no tool is needed to change a stirring element.

faqs.question: What is the Max button on the Hei-Torque Core with RS232 Overhead Stirrer?
faqs.answer: The Max button on the Hei-Torque Core with RS232 Overhead Stirrer takes the drive to its maximum speed of 2,000 rpm immediately. It is designed for short bursts, such as reslurrying a settled suspension or distributing a component that has just been added to the medium.

faqs.question: What happens if the Hei-Torque Core with RS232 Overhead Stirrer is overloaded?
faqs.answer: The Hei-Torque Core with RS232 Overhead Stirrer has automatic overload cut-out, which stops the motor rather than letting it stall under strain. The motor is also monitored in software, and a fault produces an error message.

faqs.question: What does the RS232 interface on the Hei-Torque Core do?
faqs.answer: This configuration of the Hei-Torque Core includes an RS232 interface, and a version without RS232 is also available. Heidolph does not publish the specific control or data capability the interface provides, so confirm your intended use with Inkarp before purchase.

faqs.answer: The Hei-Torque Core with RS232 Overhead Stirrer weighs 2.3 kg, which makes it the lightest overhead stirrer Heidolph produces. It can be mounted on a stand or in a closed system and set up or dismantled by one person.

products.overview:
The Hei-Torque Expert-100 Overhead Stirrer delivers 100 Ncm of torque with a live torque trend display, for viscosities to 60,000 mPas.
Most stirring is a black box. You set a speed, you come back later, and you hope the medium did what you expected.
The torque trend bar shows the load the drive is under, so a thickening reaction or a completing dissolution becomes visible while it happens rather than afterwards.
The stand, boss head, stirring shaft, and stirring element are NOT included.
features: Torque Trend Display: A bar indicator keeps the delivered torque visible for the whole run. Changes in the medium can be tracked as they happen, the speed adjusted in response, and the peak torque reliably monitored. This is the feature that turns a stirrer into an instrument that tells you something.
100 Ncm of Torque: Torque, not speed, decides whether an overhead stirrer can do your job. At 100 Ncm the Expert reaches media six times more viscous than the Hei-TORQUE Core.
Viscosity to 60,000 mPas: The drive handles media up to 60,000 mPas. That covers thick suspensions, gels, and viscous polymer solutions that a lighter drive would simply stall in.

Speed from 10 rpm: The range starts at 10 rpm, lower than the Core's 20 rpm. A viscous medium often needs to be brought up gently, and a drive that cannot go slow enough is as much a problem as one that cannot go fast enough.

Safety Start and Stop Touch Function: Starting or stopping is a swipe along the control panel. It works reliably through gloves, and it cannot be triggered accidentally by a knock, a sleeve, or a passing hand.
Quick-Action Chuck with Safety Ring: The chuck opens and closes by hand with no tools, and the safety ring holds the stirring tool securely once clamped.
2.4 Inch Display: Application parameters are set and the process controlled from a 2.4 inch display, including the torque trend bar.
Built for Fume Hoods and Reactor Superstructures: At IP54 and under 50 dB(A), the drive is sealed and quiet enough to work inside a fume hood, and it is rated as a drive for reactor superstructures.
Automatic Overload Cut-Out with Display: If the load exceeds what the drive can deliver, the motor cuts out automatically and the display tells you why.
KTY Motor Temperature Monitoring: The motor temperature is monitored directly, which protects the drive during long runs in demanding media.
90 W Power Input: Despite delivering more torque than the Hei-TORQUE Core, the Expert draws less power, at 90 W against the Core's 105 W.
Suitable for Continuous Operation: The duty cycle permits continuous operation, and a certificate for continuous operation is available for the Hei-TORQUE range.

body: Torque, viscosity and volume planning explains what 100 Ncm actually reaches, and why the viscosity and volume figures cannot be read together.
Read this before you read any other number on this page.
Heidolph states that the Expert 100 stirs viscosities up to 60,000 mPas or volumes up to 50 litres in water. Two separate ceilings on the same 100 Ncm drive. Not a combined specification.
Fifty litres is what 100 Ncm reaches when the medium behaves like water. Sixty thousand mPas is what 100 Ncm reaches when the volume is small. You do not get 50 litres of a 60,000 mPas medium.
The torque trend display is the honest answer to this problem. Instead of trusting a headline figure, you watch the actual torque the drive is delivering and see how much headroom is left.

products.overview:
The Hei-Torque Expert-200 Overhead Stirrer delivers 200 Ncm with a live torque trend display, for viscosities to 100,000 mPas.
Doubling the torque of the Expert 100 does not get you a bigger vessel. Both drives stop at the same volume. What the extra power buys is a medium that has stopped being pourable.
Viscosity, not volume. This is the drive you move to when the medium is too thick, not when the vessel is too large. The volume ceiling is unchanged from the Expert 100.
You can see what the medium is doing. The torque trend bar shows the load the drive is under, so a thickening reaction becomes visible while it happens.
Still not a complete instrument. The stand, the shaft, and the stirring element are separate items.
features: 200 Ncm of Torque: Torque, not speed, decides whether an overhead stirrer can do your job. At 200 Ncm the Expert 200 turns media that would stall a 100 Ncm drive, and it does so at the same working volume.
Viscosity to 100,000 mPas: The drive handles media up to 100,000 mPas. That is the territory of heavy gels, pastes, loaded slurries and viscous polymer solutions, where a lighter drive simply stops.

Torque Trend Display: A bar indicator keeps the delivered torque visible for the whole run. Changes in the medium can be tracked as they happen, the speed adjusted in response, and the peak torque monitored reliably. At this end of the viscosity range, headroom is what you are watching.

Speed from 10 rpm: The range starts at 10 rpm. A very viscous medium usually needs to be brought up slowly, and a drive that cannot go slow enough is as much of a problem as one that cannot go fast enough.

Safety Start and Stop Touch Function: Starting or stopping is a swipe along the control panel. It works reliably through gloves, and it cannot be triggered accidentally by a knock, a sleeve, or a passing hand.

Quick-Action Chuck with Safety Ring: The chuck opens and closes by hand with no tools, and the safety ring holds the stirring tool securely once clamped. At 200 Ncm, a tool that slips in the chuck is not a minor inconvenience.
2.4 Inch Display: Application parameters are set and the process controlled from a 2.4 inch display, including the torque trend bar.
Built for Fume Hoods and Reactor Superstructures: At IP54 and under 50 dB(A), the drive is sealed and quiet enough to work inside a fume hood, and it is rated as a drive for reactor superstructures.
Automatic Overload Cut-Out with Display: If the load exceeds what the drive can deliver, the motor cuts out automatically and the display tells you why.
KTY Motor Temperature Monitoring: The motor temperature is monitored directly, which protects the drive during long runs in demanding media.
Suitable for Continuous Operation: The duty cycle permits continuous operation, and a certificate for continuous operation is available for the Hei-TORQUE range.

faqs.question: What is the Hei-Torque Expert-200 Overhead Stirrer used for?
faqs.answer: The Hei-Torque Expert-200 Overhead Stirrer is a Heidolph overhead stirrer used for high-viscosity media and monitored reactions. It delivers 200 Ncm of torque across 10 to 2,000 rpm, for viscosities up to 100,000 mPas or volumes up to 50 litres in water, and displays the delivered torque live.

faqs.question: What is the maximum torque of the Hei-Torque Expert-200 Overhead Stirrer?
faqs.answer: The maximum torque of the Hei-Torque Expert-200 Overhead Stirrer is 200 Ncm. Torque, rather than speed, determines whether an overhead stirrer can turn a given medium.

faqs.question: What is the difference between the Hei-Torque Expert-100 and the Expert-200?
faqs.answer: The Hei-Torque Expert-200 delivers 200 Ncm against the Expert-100's 100 Ncm, and reaches 100,000 mPas against 60,000 mPas. The maximum volume is the same on both, at 50 litres in water. The extra torque buys a thicker medium, not a larger vessel.

faqs.question: Can the Hei-Torque Expert-200 Overhead Stirrer stir a larger volume than the Expert-100?
faqs.answer: No. Both the Hei-Torque Expert-200 and the Expert-100 have a maximum volume of 50 litres in water. Doubling the torque raises the viscosity ceiling, not the volume ceiling. If your constraint is vessel size rather than medium thickness, more torque will not solve it.

faqs.question: What viscosity can the Hei-Torque Expert-200 Overhead Stirrer handle?
faqs.answer: The Hei-Torque Expert-200 Overhead Stirrer handles viscosities up to 100,000 mPas, at reduced volume. That covers heavy gels, pastes, loaded slurries, and viscous polymer solutions.

faqs.question: Can the Hei-Torque Expert-200 Overhead Stirrer stir 50 litres of a viscous medium?
faqs.answer: No. The Hei-Torque Expert-200 Overhead Stirrer handles viscosities up to 100,000 mPas or volumes up to 50 litres in water. These are two separate ceilings on the same 200 Ncm drive, not a combined capability. As viscosity rises, the volume the drive can turn falls.

faqs.question: What is the torque trend display on the Hei-Torque Expert-200 Overhead Stirrer?
faqs.answer: The torque trend display on the Hei-Torque Expert-200 Overhead Stirrer is a bar indicator that keeps the delivered torque visible throughout the run. Changes in the medium can be tracked as they happen, the stirring speed adjusted in response, and the peak torque monitored reliably.

faqs.question: What shaft diameters fit the Hei-Torque Expert-200 Overhead Stirrer?
faqs.answer: The quick-action chuck on the Hei-Torque Expert-200 Overhead Stirrer accepts stirring shafts from 2.5 mm to 10.5 mm, and has a safety ring. For shafts thinner than 2.5 mm, the Hei-TORQUE Core goes down to 0.5 mm.

faqs.question: Can the Hei-Torque Expert-200 Overhead Stirrer be used in a fume hood?
faqs.answer: Yes. The Hei-Torque Expert-200 Overhead Stirrer carries IP54 protection and operates below 50 dB(A), and Heidolph rates it for use in fume hoods and as a drive for reactor superstructures.

faqs.question: What is included with the Hei-Torque Expert-200 Overhead Stirrer?
faqs.answer: The Hei-Torque Expert-200 Overhead Stirrer is supplied as a drive unit. The stand, boss head, stirring shaft, and stirring element are separate items and are not included. At 200 Ncm the stand and boss head must be rated to hold against the reaction torque, so Inkarp quotes a complete working setup rather than a drive alone.

products.overview:
The Hei-Torque Expert-400 Overhead Stirrer is the top of the Expert range, with a two-gear drive delivering 400 Ncm, for viscosities to 250,000 mPas and volumes to 100 litres in water.
The two lower Experts stall at the same 50 litre volume no matter how much torque you add. This one breaks that limit, because it does not just add torque. It adds a gearbox.
The only Expert with two gears. Gear I trades speed for torque and delivers full power below 400 rpm. Gear II opens up to 2,000 rpm for thinner media.
The stand, boss head, stirring shaft, and stirring element are NOT included.
features: Two-Gear Transmission: The Expert 400 is the only model in the Expert range with two gears. Gear I concentrates the drive's power in the speed range up to 400 rpm, which is where highly viscous media must be mixed. Gear II runs up to 2,000 rpm for lighter work. One drive covers both regimes, which a single-gear stirrer cannot.

400 Ncm of Torque: Torque, not speed, decides whether an overhead stirrer can do your job. At 400 Ncm this is the most powerful drive in the Expert range, built for media that stall everything below it.

Viscosity to 250,000 mPas: The drive handles media up to 250,000 mPas, more than double the Expert 200. This is the territory of stiff pastes, heavy adhesives, and loaded slurries that behave more like solids than liquids.

Volume to 100 Litres: The maximum volume is 100 litres in water, double the two lower Experts. This is the only model in the Expert range that raises the volume ceiling, not just the viscosity ceiling.

Torque Trend Display: A bar indicator keeps the delivered torque visible for the whole run, so changes in the medium can be tracked, the speed adjusted in response, and the peak torque monitored. At 400 Ncm, watching the headroom matters.

Safety Start and Stop Touch Function: Starting or stopping is a swipe along the control panel. It works reliably through gloves, and it cannot be triggered accidentally by a knock, a sleeve, or a passing hand.

Quick-Action Chuck with Safety Ring: The chuck opens and closes by hand with no tools, and the safety ring holds the stirring tool securely. At 400 Ncm, a tool that slips in the chuck is a serious hazard, and the safety ring is there to prevent it.
2.4 Inch Display: Application parameters are set and the process controlled from a 2.4 inch display, including the torque trend bar and the gear selection.
Built for Fume Hoods and Reactor Superstructures: At IP54 and under 50 dB(A), the drive is sealed and quiet enough to work inside a fume hood, and it is rated as a drive for reactor superstructures.
Automatic Overload Cut-Out with Display: If the load exceeds what the drive can deliver, the motor cuts out automatically and the display tells you why.
KTY Motor Temperature Monitoring: The motor temperature is monitored directly, which protects the drive during long runs in the demanding media this model is built for.
Suitable for Continuous Operation: The duty cycle permits continuous operation, and a certificate for continuous operation is available for the Hei-TORQUE range.

faqs.question: What is the Hei-Torque Expert-400 Overhead Stirrer used for?
faqs.answer: The Hei-Torque Expert-400 Overhead Stirrer is Heidolph's most powerful Expert overhead stirrer, used for very high-viscosity media, large volumes, and low-speed high-torque mixing. It delivers 400 Ncm through a two-gear drive, for viscosities up to 250,000 mPas or volumes up to 100 litres in water.

faqs.question: What is the maximum torque of the Hei-Torque Expert-400 Overhead Stirrer?
faqs.answer: The maximum torque of the Hei-Torque Expert-400 Overhead Stirrer is 400 Ncm, the highest in the Hei-TORQUE Expert range. Torque, rather than speed, determines whether an overhead stirrer can turn a given medium.

faqs.question: What is the two-gear design on the Hei-Torque Expert-400 Overhead Stirrer?
faqs.answer: The Hei-Torque Expert-400 Overhead Stirrer is the only Expert model with a two-gear drive. Gear I runs from 10 to 400 rpm and concentrates the full torque at low speed, where highly viscous media must be stirred. Gear II runs from 20 to 2,000 rpm for thinner media.

faqs.question: What is the difference between the Hei-Torque Expert-200 and the Expert-400?
faqs.answer: The Hei-Torque Expert-400 delivers 400 Ncm against the Expert-200's 200 Ncm, reaches 250,000 mPas against 100,000 mPas, and 100 litres against 50 litres in water. It is also the only Expert with a two-gear drive. Unlike the step from the 100 to the 200, the Expert-400 raises both the viscosity ceiling and the volume ceiling.

faqs.question: Can the Hei-Torque Expert-400 Overhead Stirrer handle larger volumes than the other Experts?
faqs.answer: Yes. The Hei-Torque Expert-400 Overhead Stirrer reaches 100 litres in water, double the 50 litre ceiling of the Expert-100 and Expert-200. It is the only model in the Expert range that raises the volume ceiling.

faqs.question: Can the Hei-Torque Expert-400 Overhead Stirrer stir 100 litres of a viscous medium?
faqs.answer: No. The Hei-Torque Expert-400 Overhead Stirrer handles viscosities up to 250,000 mPas or volumes up to 100 litres in water. These are two separate ceilings on the same 400 Ncm drive, not a combined capability. As viscosity rises, the volume the drive can turn falls.

faqs.question: What viscosity can the Hei-Torque Expert-400 Overhead Stirrer handle?
faqs.answer: The Hei-Torque Expert-400 Overhead Stirrer handles viscosities up to 250,000 mPas, at reduced volume. That covers stiff pastes, heavy adhesives, and loaded slurries.

faqs.question: What is the torque trend display on the Hei-Torque Expert-400 Overhead Stirrer?
faqs.answer: The torque trend display on the Hei-Torque Expert-400 Overhead Stirrer is a bar indicator that keeps the delivered torque visible throughout the run. Changes in the medium can be tracked as they happen, the stirring speed adjusted in response, and the peak torque monitored reliably.

faqs.question: What shaft diameters fit the Hei-Torque Expert-400 Overhead Stirrer?
faqs.answer: The quick-action chuck on the Hei-Torque Expert-400 Overhead Stirrer accepts stirring shafts from 2.5 mm to 10.5 mm, and has a safety ring. At 400 Ncm the shaft must also be rated for the torque.

faqs.question: Can the Hei-Torque Expert-400 Overhead Stirrer be used in a fume hood?
faqs.answer: Yes. The Hei-Torque Expert-400 Overhead Stirrer carries IP54 protection and operates below 50 dB(A), and Heidolph rates it for use in fume hoods and as a drive for reactor superstructures.

faqs.answer: The Hei-Torque Expert-400 Overhead Stirrer is supplied as a drive unit. The stand, boss head, stirring shaft, and stirring element are separate items and are not included. products.overview:
The Hei-Torque Ultimate-100 Overhead Stirrer is the connected, programmable Hei-TORQUE, delivering 100 Ncm with ramp programming, USB and RS232 interfaces, and free Hei-Control software.
The Ultimate 100 stirs exactly what the Expert 100 stirs: same torque, same viscosity, same volume. What you are buying is not more power. It is the ability to program, connect, and document.
Programmable methods. Ramp programming lets you define a stirring profile and repeat it exactly, run after run, operator after operator.
The stand, boss head, stirring shaft, and stirring element are NOT included.
features: Ramp Programming: Ramp programming lets you define a stirring profile and repeat it exactly. A method written into the drive is a method that runs the same way every time, regardless of who is operating it. This is the single feature that separates the Ultimate line from the Expert line.

USB and RS232 Interfaces: Two interfaces connect the drive to a PC, a programmable logic controller, or an automation system such as LabManager. This is what lets an overhead stirrer become a controlled step in an automated process rather than a manual interruption in one.

Free Hei-Control Software: The scope of delivery includes the free Hei-Control software, which remotely controls up to four devices from a single PC. Remote control and data logging are quick to set up, at no extra cost.

Process Monitoring and Documentation: The drive reads out the torque trend as a value and includes a timer function, giving you the equipment to document your application parameters. A number can be recorded and audited; a bar on a screen cannot.

Torque to 100 Ncm: Torque, not speed, decides whether an overhead stirrer can do your job. The Ultimate 100 delivers 100 Ncm, for viscosities up to 60,000 mPas, the same working envelope as the Expert 100.

Change of Rotational Direction: Rotation runs clockwise or counterclockwise. The flow variation makes it easier to stir up suspensions and accelerates dissolution processes, which a single-direction drive cannot do.

Controllable Start-Up: After switch-on, the start-up intensity is adjustable from soft to fast. That lets you choose the right ramp for the application and prevents liquid from splashing at the start.

Safety Start and Stop Touch Function: Starting or stopping is a swipe along the control panel. It works reliably through gloves, and it cannot be triggered accidentally by a knock, a sleeve, or a passing hand.
Quick-Action Chuck with Safety Ring: The chuck opens and closes by hand with no tools, and the safety ring holds the stirring tool securely once clamped.
Built for Fume Hoods and Reactor Superstructures: At IP54 and under 50 dB(A), the drive is sealed and quiet enough to work inside a fume hood, and it is rated as a drive for reactor superstructures.
Automatic Overload Cut-Out with Display: If the load exceeds what the drive can deliver, the motor cuts out automatically and the display tells you why.
KTY Motor Temperature Monitoring: The motor temperature is monitored directly, which protects the drive during long runs.
Suitable for Continuous Operation: The duty cycle permits continuous operation, and a certificate for continuous operation is available for the Hei-TORQUE range.

faqs.question: What is the Hei-Torque Ultimate-100 Overhead Stirrer used for?
faqs.answer: The Hei-Torque Ultimate-100 Overhead Stirrer is Heidolph's connected, programmable overhead stirrer, used for automated processes, documented methods, and reproducible stirring. It delivers 100 Ncm across 10 to 2,000 rpm, for viscosities up to 60,000 mPas or volumes up to 50 litres in water, with USB and RS232 interfaces and free Hei-Control software.

faqs.question: What is the difference between the Hei-Torque Expert-100 and the Ultimate-100?
faqs.answer: The Hei-Torque Ultimate-100 and the Expert-100 share the same drive: 100 Ncm, 60,000 mPas, 50 litres in water, and the same chassis. The Ultimate-100 adds ramp programming, USB and RS232 interfaces, free Hei-Control software for up to four devices, bidirectional rotation, and a torque trend read out as a documentable value. The Expert-100 has the same torque without the automation.

faqs.question: What interfaces does the Hei-Torque Ultimate-100 Overhead Stirrer have?
faqs.answer: The Hei-Torque Ultimate-100 Overhead Stirrer has two interfaces, USB and RS232. They connect the drive to a PC, a programmable logic controller, or an automation system such as LabManager.

faqs.question: What is the Hei-Control software included with the Hei-Torque Ultimate-100 Overhead Stirrer?
faqs.answer: Hei-Control is the free software included in the scope of delivery of the Hei-Torque Ultimate-100 Overhead Stirrer. It provides remote control and data logging, and can control up to four devices from a single PC.

faqs.question: Can the Hei-Torque Ultimate-100 Overhead Stirrer be programmed?
faqs.answer: Yes. The Hei-Torque Ultimate-100 Overhead Stirrer offers ramp programming, which lets you define a stirring profile and repeat it exactly. This is the main capability that distinguishes the Ultimate line from the Expert line.

faqs.question: What is the maximum torque of the Hei-Torque Ultimate-100 Overhead Stirrer?
faqs.answer: The maximum torque of the Hei-Torque Ultimate-100 Overhead Stirrer is 100 Ncm. Torque, rather than speed, determines whether an overhead stirrer can turn a given medium.

faqs.question: Can the Hei-Torque Ultimate-100 Overhead Stirrer stir 50 litres of a viscous medium?
faqs.answer: No. The Hei-Torque Ultimate-100 Overhead Stirrer handles viscosities up to 60,000 mPas or volumes up to 50 litres in water. These are two separate ceilings on the same 100 Ncm drive, not a combined capability. As viscosity rises, the volume the drive can turn falls.

faqs.question: Does the Hei-Torque Ultimate-100 Overhead Stirrer rotate in both directions?
faqs.answer: Yes. The Hei-Torque Ultimate-100 Overhead Stirrer rotates clockwise and counterclockwise. Reversing the flow makes it easier to stir up suspensions and accelerates dissolution processes.

faqs.question: What shaft diameters fit the Hei-Torque Ultimate-100 Overhead Stirrer?
faqs.answer: The quick-action chuck on the Hei-Torque Ultimate-100 Overhead Stirrer accepts stirring shafts from 2.5 mm to 10.5 mm, and has a safety ring. For shafts thinner than 2.5 mm, the Hei-TORQUE Core goes down to 0.5 mm.

faqs.question: What is included with the Hei-Torque Ultimate-100 Overhead Stirrer?
faqs.answer: The Hei-Torque Ultimate-100 Overhead Stirrer is supplied as a drive unit with the free Hei-Control software. The stand, boss head, stirring shaft, and stirring element are separate items and are not included. Inkarp quotes a complete working setup rather than a drive alone.

body: Torque, viscosity and volume planning explains what 100 Ncm reaches, and why the viscosity and volume figures cannot be read together.
Read this before you read any other number on this page.

Heidolph states that the Ultimate 100 stirs viscosities up to 60,000 mPas or volumes up to 50 litres in water. Two separate ceilings on the same 100 Ncm drive. Not a combined specification. Fifty litres is what 100 Ncm reaches when the medium behaves like water. Sixty thousand mPas is what it reaches when the volume is small.
The Ultimate 100 shares this envelope exactly with the Expert 100. The two drives have the same torque and the same limits. The Ultimate adds programming and connectivity, not stirring capacity.

products.overview:
The Hei-Torque Ultimate-200 Overhead Stirrer is a programmable, connected high-viscosity overhead stirrer, delivering 200 Ncm with ramp programming, USB and RS232 interfaces, and free Hei-Control software.
The Ultimate 200 stirs exactly what the Expert 200 stirs: same torque, same viscosity, same volume. What you are buying is not more power. It is the ability to program, connect, and document.
Programmable methods. Ramp programming stores a stirring profile and repeats it exactly, run after run, operator after operator.
The stand, boss head, stirring shaft, and stirring element are NOT included.
features: 200 Ncm of High-Viscosity Torque: Torque, not speed, decides whether an overhead stirrer can do your job. At 200 Ncm the Ultimate 200 turns media up to 100,000 mPas, reaching pastes, gels and loaded slurries that a lighter drive would stall in.

Ramp Programming: Ramp programming lets you define a stirring profile and repeat it exactly. A method stored in the drive runs the same way every time, regardless of who is operating it, which is what makes a result reproducible rather than dependent on the person at the bench.

USB and RS232 Interfaces: Two interfaces connect the drive to a PC, a programmable logic controller, or an automation system such as LabManager. This is what lets an overhead stirrer become a controlled step in an automated process rather than a manual interruption in one.

Free Hei-Control Software: The scope of delivery includes the free Hei-Control software, which controls and logs up to four devices from a single PC. Remote operation and data recording are quick to set up, at no added cost.

Process Monitoring and Documentation: The drive reads the torque trend out as a value and includes a timer, giving you the means to document each run. A recorded number can be audited in a way that an observed reading cannot.

Change of Rotational Direction: Rotation runs clockwise or counterclockwise. Varying the flow makes it easier to stir up suspensions and accelerates dissolution processes, which a single-direction drive cannot do.

Controllable Start-Up: After switch-on, the start-up intensity is adjustable from soft to fast. That lets you choose the right ramp for the application and prevents liquid from splashing at the start.

Safety Start and Stop Touch Function: Starting or stopping is a swipe along the control panel. It works reliably through gloves, and it cannot be triggered accidentally by a knock, a sleeve, or a passing hand.
Quick-Action Chuck with Safety Ring: The chuck opens and closes by hand with no tools, and the safety ring holds the stirring tool securely once clamped.
Built for Fume Hoods and Reactor Superstructures: At IP54 and under 50 dB(A), the drive is sealed and quiet enough to work inside a fume hood, and it is rated as a drive for reactor superstructures.
Automatic Overload Cut-Out with Display: If the load exceeds what the drive can deliver, the motor cuts out automatically and the display tells you why.
KTY Motor Temperature Monitoring: The motor temperature is monitored directly, which protects the drive during long runs in the demanding media this model handles.
Suitable for Continuous Operation: The duty cycle permits continuous operation, and a certificate for continuous operation is available for the Hei-TORQUE range.

faqs.question: What is the Hei-Torque Ultimate-200 Overhead Stirrer used for?
faqs.answer: The Hei-Torque Ultimate-200 Overhead Stirrer is a programmable, connected high-viscosity overhead stirrer, used for automated processes, documented methods, and reproducible stirring of viscous media. It delivers 200 Ncm across 10 to 2,000 rpm, for viscosities up to 100,000 mPas or volumes up to 50 litres in water, with USB and RS232 interfaces and free Hei-Control software.

faqs.question: What is the maximum torque of the Hei-Torque Ultimate-200 Overhead Stirrer?
faqs.answer: The maximum torque of the Hei-Torque Ultimate-200 Overhead Stirrer is 200 Ncm. Torque, rather than speed, determines whether an overhead stirrer can turn a given medium.

faqs.question: What viscosity can the Hei-Torque Ultimate-200 Overhead Stirrer handle?
faqs.answer: The Hei-Torque Ultimate-200 Overhead Stirrer handles viscosities up to 100,000 mPas, at reduced volume. That covers heavy gels, pastes, and loaded slurries. The 100,000 mPas and 50 litre figures are two ends of one working envelope, so a very viscous medium is turned in a smaller volume.

faqs.question: Can the Hei-Torque Ultimate-200 Overhead Stirrer be programmed?
faqs.answer: Yes. The Hei-Torque Ultimate-200 Overhead Stirrer offers ramp programming, which lets you define a stirring profile and repeat it exactly, run after run and operator after operator.

faqs.question: What interfaces does the Hei-Torque Ultimate-200 Overhead Stirrer have?
faqs.answer: The Hei-Torque Ultimate-200 Overhead Stirrer has two interfaces, USB and RS232, which connect the drive to a PC, a programmable logic controller, or an automation system such as LabManager.

faqs.question: What is the Hei-Control software included with the Hei-Torque Ultimate-200 Overhead Stirrer?
faqs.answer: Hei-Control is the free software included in the scope of delivery. It provides remote control and data logging, and can control up to four devices from a single PC.

faqs.question: What is the difference between the Hei-Torque Expert-200 and the Ultimate-200?
faqs.answer: Both use the same 200 Ncm drive, with the same 100,000 mPas and 50 litre limits. The Ultimate-200 adds ramp programming, USB and RS232 interfaces, free Hei-Control software for up to four devices, bidirectional rotation, and a torque trend read out as a documentable value. The Expert-200 offers the drive without the programming and connectivity, for processes run by hand.

faqs.question: Does the Hei-Torque Ultimate-200 Overhead Stirrer rotate in both directions?
faqs.answer: Yes. The Hei-Torque Ultimate-200 Overhead Stirrer rotates clockwise and counterclockwise. Varying the flow helps lift suspensions and accelerates dissolution.

faqs.question: What shaft diameters fit the Hei-Torque Ultimate-200 Overhead Stirrer?
faqs.answer: The quick-action chuck on the Hei-Torque Ultimate-200 Overhead Stirrer accepts stirring shafts from 2.5 mm to 10.5 mm, and has a safety ring.

sections.title: Torque, Viscosity and Volume Planning
body: Torque, viscosity and volume planning sets out what the Ultimate 200's 200 Ncm delivers, and how to size a viscous job against it.

The drive is rated to 100,000 mPas at reduced volume, or 50 litres when the medium is close to water. Picture these as two ends of one working envelope: the thicker the medium, the smaller the volume the drive will turn, and the thinner it is, the larger. A real job sits somewhere between those points, set by the medium, the volume and the impeller together.
The torque readout on the instrument shows, in real time, how much of the 200 Ncm a given setup is drawing, so headroom is visible rather than guessed.
Product expert note Share your medium, its viscosity, your working volume, and your vessel diameter, and our team will confirm whether 200 Ncm suits the job or whether a higher tier fits better.

products.overview:
The Hei-Torque Ultimate-400 Overhead Stirrer is the most powerful Hei-TORQUE, a programmable two-gear drive delivering 400 Ncm to 250,000 mPas and 100 litres in water, with ramp programming, USB and RS232 interfaces, and free Hei-Control software.
This is the drive for work that is both demanding and controlled: media too thick and batches too large for a single-gear stirrer, run to a stored method and recorded.
A two-gear drive. Gear I holds the full torque below 400 rpm, where a stiff medium must be turned slowly; Gear II runs to 2,000 rpm for thinner work.
The stand, boss head, stirring shaft, and stirring element are NOT included.
features: Two-Gear Transmission: The drive has two gears. Gear I concentrates the full 400 Ncm in the speed range up to 400 rpm, where highly viscous media must be mixed. Gear II runs up to 2,000 rpm for lighter work. One drive covers both regimes, which a single-gear stirrer cannot.

400 Ncm of Torque: Torque, not speed, decides whether an overhead stirrer can do your job. At 400 Ncm this is the most powerful drive in the Hei-TORQUE range, built for media that stall lighter models.

Viscosity to 250,000 mPas and Volume to 100 Litres: The drive reaches 250,000 mPas of viscosity and 100 litres in water, the highest ceilings in the range. This is the territory of stiff pastes, heavy adhesives, and large loaded batches.

Ramp Programming with Favourites Memory: Time-dependent ramps can be programmed and saved on the device, then loaded from a favourites memory and reused for a given application. A stored method runs the same way every time, regardless of who is at the bench.

USB and RS232 Interfaces: Two interfaces connect the drive to a PC, a programmable logic controller, or an automation system such as LabManager. This is what lets the stirrer become a controlled step in an automated process.

Free Hei-Control Software: The scope of delivery includes the free Hei-Control software, which controls and logs up to four devices from a single PC. Remote operation and data recording are quick to set up, at no added cost.

Process Monitoring and Documentation: The drive reads the torque trend out as a value and includes a timer, giving you the means to document each run and to hold reproducible process times without standing at the device.

Controllable Start-Up: After switch-on, the start-up intensity is adjustable from soft to fast. That lets you choose the right ramp for the application and prevents liquid from splashing at the start.

Safety Start and Stop Touch Function: Starting or stopping is a swipe along the control panel. It works reliably through gloves, and it cannot be triggered accidentally by a knock, a sleeve, or a passing hand.

Quick-Action Chuck with Safety Ring: The chuck opens and closes by hand with no tools, and the safety ring holds the stirring tool securely. At 400 Ncm, a tool that slips in the chuck is a serious hazard, and the safety ring is there to prevent it.
Built for Fume Hoods and Reactor Superstructures: At IP54 and under 50 dB(A), the drive is sealed and quiet enough to work inside a fume hood, and it is rated as a drive for reactor superstructures.
Automatic Overload Cut-Out with Display: If the load exceeds what the drive can deliver, the motor cuts out automatically and the display tells you why.
KTY Motor Temperature Monitoring: The motor temperature is monitored directly, which protects the drive during long runs in the demanding media this model is built for.
Suitable for Continuous Operation: The duty cycle permits continuous operation, and a certificate for continuous operation is available for the Hei-TORQUE range.

faqs.question: What is the Hei-Torque Ultimate-400 Overhead Stirrer used for?
faqs.answer: The Hei-Torque Ultimate-400 Overhead Stirrer is Heidolph's most powerful overhead stirrer, a programmable two-gear drive used for very high-viscosity media, large volumes, and automated documented processes. It delivers 400 Ncm for viscosities up to 250,000 mPas or volumes up to 100 litres in water, with USB and RS232 interfaces and free Hei-Control software.

faqs.question: What is the maximum torque of the Hei-Torque Ultimate-400 Overhead Stirrer?
faqs.answer: The maximum torque of the Hei-Torque Ultimate-400 Overhead Stirrer is 400 Ncm, the highest in the Hei-TORQUE range. Torque, rather than speed, determines whether an overhead stirrer can turn a given medium.

faqs.question: What is the two-gear design on the Hei-Torque Ultimate-400 Overhead Stirrer?
faqs.answer: The Hei-Torque Ultimate-400 Overhead Stirrer has a two-gear drive. Gear I runs from 10 to 400 rpm and concentrates the full torque at low speed, where highly viscous media must be stirred. Gear II runs from 20 to 2,000 rpm for thinner media.

faqs.question: What viscosity and volume can the Hei-Torque Ultimate-400 Overhead Stirrer handle?
faqs.answer: The Hei-Torque Ultimate-400 Overhead Stirrer reaches viscosities up to 250,000 mPas or volumes up to 100 litres in water, the highest figures in the range. These are two ends of one working envelope, so a very viscous medium is turned in a smaller volume.

faqs.question: Can the Hei-Torque Ultimate-400 Overhead Stirrer be programmed?
faqs.answer: Yes. The Hei-Torque Ultimate-400 Overhead Stirrer offers ramp programming with a favourites memory, letting you store time-dependent stirring profiles and rerun them exactly, along with a timer for reproducible process times.

faqs.question: What interfaces does the Hei-Torque Ultimate-400 Overhead Stirrer have?
faqs.answer: The Hei-Torque Ultimate-400 Overhead Stirrer has two interfaces, USB and RS232, which connect the drive to a PC, a programmable logic controller, or an automation system such as LabManager.

faqs.question: What is the Hei-Control software included with the Hei-Torque Ultimate-400 Overhead Stirrer?
faqs.answer: Hei-Control is the free software included in the scope of delivery. It provides remote control and data logging, and can control up to four devices from a single PC.

faqs.question: What is the difference between the Hei-Torque Expert-400 and the Ultimate-400?
faqs.answer: Both use the same two-gear 400 Ncm drive, with the same 250,000 mPas and 100 litre limits. The Ultimate-400 adds ramp programming, USB and RS232 interfaces, free Hei-Control software for up to four devices, and a torque trend read out as a documentable value. The Expert-400 offers the drive without the programming and connectivity, for processes run by hand.

faqs.question: What shaft diameters fit the Hei-Torque Ultimate-400 Overhead Stirrer?
faqs.answer: The quick-action chuck on the Hei-Torque Ultimate-400 Overhead Stirrer accepts stirring shafts from 2.5 mm to 10.5 mm, and has a safety ring. At 400 Ncm the shaft must also be rated for the torque.

The stand, boss head, stirring shaft, and stirring element are separate items and are not included. At 400 Ncm the stand, boss head, and shaft must all be rated for the reaction torque, so Inkarp quotes a complete working setup rated for the load.

sections.title: Torque, Viscosity and Volume Planning
body: Torque, viscosity and volume planning sets out what the Ultimate 400's two-gear drive delivers, and why the gearbox is what reaches both ceilings.

The drive reaches 250,000 mPas and 100 litres in water, the highest figures in the range, and the reason is the transmission rather than raw torque alone. Torque is hardest to deliver at low speed, and low speed is exactly where a very viscous medium has to be stirred. Gear I concentrates the full 400 Ncm below 400 rpm to meet that; Gear II opens up to 2,000 rpm once the work is thinner.

The viscosity and volume figures are the two ends of one envelope rather than a pair that holds at once: the full 250,000 mPas applies at reduced volume, the full 100 litres at low viscosity. The torque readout shows, in real time, where within that envelope a given setup is running.
Product expert note Share your medium, its viscosity, your working volume, and your vessel diameter, and our team will confirm the gear your process runs in and that 400 Ncm suits the job.

body: A complete Hei-Torque Ultimate-400 installation requires a drive, a heavy-duty stand and boss head, a shaft, and a stirring element.
The drive on its own cannot stir anything. It is a motor with a chuck. Below is what a working installation actually consists of.

At 400 Ncm the whole load path, from stand to boss head to shaft to vessel clamp, carries the highest reaction force in the range. An under-rated component is a hazard, not a compromise, so the assembly is specified against the torque, not just the vessel size.
Configuration note Inkarp quotes a complete working setup rated for the torque, integration included, not a drive unit in isolation.

products.overview: The Heidolph Multi Reax is a multi-tube vortex mixer for high-throughput sample preparation. It mixes up to 26 tubes together, runs from 150 to 2,000 rpm with digital speed indication, uses a stable 3 mm circular vibrating orbit, and includes a timer up to 999 minutes with automatic stop and signal tone.
features: Up to 26 Tubes in One Run: The platform takes 12 tubes at 16 to 32 mm diameter, or 26 tubes at 10 to 16 mm, so every tube in the rack gets the same speed for the same duration.
Timer to 999 Minutes with Automatic Stop: Set the time and the Multi Reax stops the shaking itself when it expires, then sounds a tone.
Digital Speed Indication: Speed runs from 150 to 2,000 rpm and is shown digitally, so the setting can be recorded and repeated.
Holds Falcon, Greiner and Snap-Lid Vessels: Falcon tubes, Greiner tubes, and reaction vessels with snap-on lids are all accommodated securely.
3 mm Shaking Orbit: A fixed 3 mm circular vibrating orbit drives mixing while keeping a loaded rack stable.
1.5 kg Load Limit: The platform is rated to 1.5 kg including tubes and contents, which should be checked for full racks of larger tubes.
Quiet Under Load: Under 45 dB(A) in accordance with IEC 61010, suited to long batch runs on a shared bench.
Self-Resetting Overheat Protection: If the motor runs hot during a long batch, protection acts and then recovers on its own.

faqs.question: What is the Multi Reax Vortex Mixer used for?
faqs.answer: The Multi Reax Vortex Mixer is a multi-tube vortexer used for high-throughput sample preparation, where several analyses have to be prepared at once. It mixes a full rack of tubes together at a set speed for a set time.

faqs.question: How many tubes does the Multi Reax Vortex Mixer hold?
faqs.answer: The Multi Reax holds 12 tubes of 16 to 32 mm diameter, or 26 tubes of 10 to 16 mm diameter. Falcon tubes, Greiner tubes, and reaction vessels with snap-on lids are all accommodated.

faqs.question: What is the speed range of the Multi Reax Vortex Mixer?
faqs.answer: The Multi Reax runs from 150 to 2,000 rpm, shown on a digital indicator so the setting can be recorded and repeated.

faqs.question: Does the Multi Reax Vortex Mixer have a timer?
faqs.answer: Yes. The integrated timer runs up to 999 minutes and terminates the shaking automatically when the time expires, then emits a signal tone. This lets a batch run unattended while you work on something else.

faqs.question: What is the shaking orbit of the Multi Reax Vortex Mixer?
faqs.answer: The Multi Reax has a fixed 3 mm shaking orbit with circular vibrating movement. The tighter orbit suits a fully loaded rack, where a wider throw would compromise stability.

faqs.question: What is the maximum load on the Multi Reax Vortex Mixer?
faqs.answer: The maximum permissible load is 1.5 kg, including the tubes and their contents. A full rack of larger tubes can approach this once filled, so it is worth checking the loaded weight.

faqs.question: Can the Multi Reax Vortex Mixer hold Eppendorf-type tubes?
faqs.answer: Yes. Reaction vessels with snap-on lids are held securely, alongside Falcon and Greiner tubes.

faqs.question: How loud is the Multi Reax Vortex Mixer?
faqs.answer: The Multi Reax runs under 45 dB(A) in accordance with IEC 61010, which is quieter than the single-tube models in the range and suits long batch runs on a shared bench.

faqs.question: What voltage variant should I order in India?
faqs.answer: The Multi Reax is available in 115 V and 220 V variants. Inkarp confirms the correct variant for your electrical supply before quoting, so the instrument arrives ready to run.

body: The Multi Reax Vortex Mixer is a multi-tube vortexer holding up to 26 tubes, with a 3 mm shaking orbit, 150 to 2,000 rpm digital speed control, and a 999-minute timer.
Analytical laboratories run batches, not single samples. The Multi Reax exists because preparing several analyses at once should not mean repeating the same operation twenty times over.
It mixes 12 tubes at 16 to 32 mm, or 26 at 10 to 16 mm, together under identical conditions.
Falcon tubes, Greiner tubes, and reaction vessels with snap-on lids are fixed securely.
The timer runs to 999 minutes, stops the shaking automatically, and sounds a tone when the batch is done.
Speed from 150 to 2,000 rpm is shown on a digital indicator, so a batch speed is a number, not a guess.
The 3 mm orbit is built for a loaded rack, giving a shorter, stable throw for parallel tube mixing.
The Multi Reax runs under 45 dB(A), which matters when a long batch is running on a shared bench.

body: The Titramax 101 Vibrating Shaker holds four multi-well plates on a 220 x 220 mm platform, with a 3 mm orbit and continuously variable speed from 150 to 1,350 rpm.
Mixing inside a microplate well is a different problem from mixing in a flask. The volume is tiny, the walls are close, and a wide slow orbit simply rocks the liquid rather than moving it.
The 3 mm throw is short and fast, generating real movement in a small cavity and making this model suited to distributing or dissolving solids in the wells.
Every plate on the 220 x 220 mm platform sees the same speed for the same duration.
Continuously variable speed from 150 to 1,350 rpm lets you tune to the plate rather than picking from fixed steps.
The timer runs to 120 minutes for a defined process, while continuous operation covers protocols that need longer.
The 2 kg maximum permissible load covers four standard filled plates, but heavier deep-well plates should be checked once filled.
Under 50 dB(A), the Titramax 101 stays quiet through long shared-bench runs.

sections.description: Speed, orbit and well mixing on the Titramax 101 comes down to one question: is the liquid inside the well actually moving?

sections.title: Titramax 100 Vibrating Shaker at a Glance
sections.description: The Titramax 100 is designed for laboratories that need gentle, reproducible agitation rather than aggressive mixing. Learn how the 1.5 mm orbit protects sensitive samples, how speed influences suspension quality, which vessels fit the platform, and how Inkarp supports installation and service across India.
sections.subheading: Gentle, reproducible agitation for biological samples
body: The Titramax 100 Vibrating Shaker is a laboratory shaker with a 1.5 mm circular vibrating orbit, continuously variable speeds from 150 to 1,350 rpm, a 220 x 220 mm platform, and both timed and continuous operating modes for gentle biological sample mixing.

Gentle mixing is often the difference between maintaining healthy cultures and damaging sensitive samples. Cell cultures, microorganisms and suspension samples need continuous movement to prevent settling, distribute nutrients evenly and improve oxygen transfer, but excessive agitation can expose them to unnecessary shear stress.
The compact 1.5 mm orbit produces smooth circular motion rather than vigorous agitation, making it suitable for workflows where sample integrity is more important than maximum mixing force.
Continuous circular movement keeps cells and suspended particles evenly distributed, reducing sedimentation during incubation and long-duration experiments.
The analogue speed control allows shaking intensity to be matched to vessel size, media viscosity and biological protocol instead of relying on fixed settings.
The 220 x 220 mm platform accommodates multiple culture vessels so every sample experiences identical shaking conditions throughout the experiment.
The integrated timer operates for up to 120 minutes, while continuous mode supports incubation protocols and long-running biological experiments.
Operating below 50 dB(A), the Titramax 100 is suitable for shared laboratory environments where equipment may run throughout the day.

Confirmed model: Heidolph Titramax 100, P/N 544-11200-00, with a fixed 1.5 mm circular vibrating orbit, continuously variable analogue speed control, 220 x 220 mm platform, 2 kg maximum permissible load, timer and continuous mode.

faqs.question: What is the Titramax 1000 Vibrating Shaker?
faqs.answer: The Heidolph Titramax 1000 Vibrating Shaker is a laboratory platform shaker designed for gentle mixing of biological samples, cell cultures, and multi-well plates. It combines a 1.5 mm shaking orbit, 150 to 1,350 rpm speed range, and a platform that holds up to six microplates for high-throughput laboratory workflows.

faqs.question: What is the Titramax 1000 Vibrating Shaker used for?
faqs.answer: The Titramax 1000 is used for cell culture, biological assays, microbial cultivation, immunoassays, and high-throughput plate-based sample preparation. Its gentle orbital motion keeps samples uniformly suspended while minimizing shear stress, making it ideal for sensitive biological applications.

faqs.question: How many microplates can the Titramax 1000 hold?
faqs.answer: The Titramax 1000 can hold up to six standard multi-well microplates on its 290 x 258 mm platform. This larger capacity enables laboratories to process more samples simultaneously while maintaining consistent shaking conditions across every plate.

faqs.question: What is the shaking orbit of the Titramax 1000?
faqs.answer: The Titramax 1000 uses a fixed 1.5 mm circular shaking orbit. This short orbit provides gentle, uniform agitation that distributes nutrients and maintains suspension without exposing sensitive biological samples to excessive mechanical stress.

faqs.question: What is the speed range of the Titramax 1000?
faqs.answer: The Titramax 1000 offers a continuously variable speed range of 150 to 1,350 rpm. Users can adjust the speed using the analogue control to match the requirements of different cell cultures, assays, and biological protocols.

faqs.question: Can the Titramax 1000 be used for temperature-controlled shaking?
faqs.answer: Yes. The Titramax 1000 is designed to integrate with Heidolph's modular incubation system, allowing laboratories to perform temperature-controlled shaking for applications such as cell culture, microbial growth, and biological incubation.

faqs.question: What is the maximum load capacity of the Titramax 1000?
faqs.answer: The Titramax 1000 supports a maximum permissible load of 5 kg, including plates, vessels, and sample contents. The higher load capacity allows multiple fully loaded microplates to be processed in a single run.

faqs.question: Does the Titramax 1000 have a timer?
faqs.answer: Yes. The Titramax 1000 includes an integrated timer adjustable up to 120 minutes. An acoustic signal indicates when the programmed shaking cycle has finished, and the shaker also supports continuous operation for longer experiments.

faqs.question: Can the Titramax 1000 operate continuously?
faqs.answer: Yes. The Titramax 1000 supports continuous operation, making it suitable for extended incubation, microbial cultivation, and long-duration biological experiments where uninterrupted shaking is required.

faqs.question: Is the Titramax 1000 suitable for cell culture applications?
faqs.answer: Yes. The Titramax 1000 is specifically designed for cell culture applications. Its gentle 1.5 mm orbit keeps cells in suspension while reducing shear forces, helping maintain cell viability during long incubation periods.

faqs.question: What are the dimensions and weight of the Titramax 1000?
faqs.answer: The Titramax 1000 measures 320 x 128 x 375 mm and weighs 8 kg. Its larger platform accommodates six microplates while maintaining a compact footprint suitable for laboratory benches.

faqs.question: What is the part number of the Titramax 1000 Vibrating Shaker?
faqs.answer: The official Heidolph part number for the Titramax 1000 Vibrating Shaker is 544-12200-00.

faqs.question: What is the Rotamax 120 Orbital Shaker?

faqs.question: What is the Rotamax 120 Orbital Shaker used for?
faqs.answer: The Rotamax 120 is used for solution preparation, culture media mixing, staining, destaining, sample extraction, washing procedures and general laboratory mixing. Its orbital motion creates continuous liquid circulation for homogeneous sample preparation.

faqs.question: What is the shaking orbit of the Rotamax 120?
faqs.answer: The Rotamax 120 has a fixed 20 mm orbital motion. This larger orbit moves the entire vessel in a circular path, creating effective liquid circulation and homogeneous mixing across a wide range of laboratory applications.

faqs.question: What is the speed range of the Rotamax 120?
faqs.answer: The Rotamax 120 offers a continuously variable speed range of 20 to 300 rpm. Users can adjust the speed using the analogue control to suit different vessel sizes, sample volumes and mixing requirements.

faqs.question: What is the maximum load capacity of the Rotamax 120?

faqs.question: Does the Rotamax 120 have a timer?

longForm.heroLead: Large orbital motion. Uniform mixing. Compact enough for every laboratory bench. Some applications need more than gentle vibration; they need liquid to travel through the vessel to create efficient mixing. The Heidolph Rotamax 120 uses a 20 mm orbital motion to generate strong, uniform circulation in flasks, bottles and laboratory vessels, making it ideal for culture media, staining, extraction, washing and general laboratory mixing. Its continuously variable speed from 20 to 300 rpm, 2 kg load capacity and 220 x 220 mm platform provide flexibility for everyday laboratory workflows. Whether running timed protocols or continuous mixing, the Rotamax 120 delivers reproducible orbital agitation while maintaining quiet operation and a compact footprint.

longForm.heroLead: Powerful reciprocating motion for separation, extraction and temperature-controlled shaking workflows. The Heidolph Promax 1020 is built for laboratories that need controlled back-and-forth motion instead of orbital mixing. Its 32 mm reciprocating stroke produces strong linear agitation, making it ideal for separation, extraction, staining, washing, protein purification and applications where directional movement delivers better results than circular motion. With a 30 to 250 rpm speed range, 5 kg load capacity and compatibility with the Heidolph modular incubation system, the Promax 1020 supports both ambient and temperature-controlled workflows. The large 290 x 258 mm platform accommodates a wide range of vessels, while dedicated holders allow secure mounting of up to four 50 to 1000 mL separatory funnels for extraction applications. The programmable timer enables unattended operation, while the quiet EC motor delivers reliable performance throughout long laboratory processes.

longForm.heroLead: Fast circular vibration for suspending particles, solubility studies and leaching applications with a 3 mm orbit and speeds up to 2,500 rpm. The Heidolph Vibramax 100 is designed for laboratory workflows where vigorous circular vibration delivers better sample suspension than gentle orbital motion. Its 3 mm orbit combined with speeds from 150 to 2,500 rpm creates rapid, uniform agitation for suspending solids, dissolving compounds and performing leaching studies. A 220 x 220 mm platform accommodates a wide range of laboratory vessels, while the optional tension roller attachment securely holds different container sizes. Together with the non-slip rubber mat, samples remain stable even during high-speed operation. The integrated 120-minute timer supports repeatable protocols, while continuous operation handles longer experiments. With a compact footprint, quiet operation and reliable performance, the Vibramax 100 fits naturally into research, analytical, environmental, pharmaceutical and academic laboratories.

longForm.heroLead: The full-power orbital drive, without the automation layer you may not need. The Hei-SHAKE Orbital Core delivers the core functions a laboratory needs for any shaking application, from a 1 to 530 rpm speed range to a 20 mm orbit that ensures homogeneous distribution across every vessel on the platform. Applications run in continuous operation or against a timer set from 1 minute to 999 hours 59 minutes, with an RS232 interface that connects the shaker to a PC or to server-based software such as Hei-PROCESS for semi-automated control. Automatic restart after a power failure is set through a straightforward menu structure, so unattended runs recover without manual intervention. The 294 x 263 mm platform, rated to 15 kg, accommodates a wide range of flasks, bottles and vessels for demanding batch work. Supplied with the Flat Rubber Mat 1000, the Orbital Core is ready for daily laboratory use from installation.

longForm.heroLead: Controlled 2D rocking motion for gentle and efficient sample processing. The Hei-SHAKE Rock Core Rocking Shaker is designed for laboratories requiring controlled rocking movement for biological samples, containers and sensitive mixing applications. The 5 degree tilt configuration supports gentle handling while reducing risks such as foaming, glass breakage and liquid spill-over. With 2D rocking motion, adjustable speed control from 0 to 80 rpm, 15 kg load capacity, timer-based operation and RS232 connectivity, the shaker supports reliable and repeatable laboratory workflows.

body: The Hei-SHAKE Rock Core uses a 2D rocking movement to provide continuous and uniform sample motion.
The rocking action enables efficient mixing while maintaining gentle handling conditions for sensitive samples.
The 5 degree tilt configuration helps minimize foaming and reduces the risk of glass breakage or liquid spill-over during operation.
The anti-slip rubber mat securely holds containers even at higher speeds.
Timer-controlled operation enables unattended processes, while RS232 connectivity supports remote operation and semi-automated workflows.
Automatic restart functionality helps maintain workflow continuity after power interruptions.
Confirmed model: Hei-SHAKE Rock Core (5 degree), P/N 546-13400-00, with 2D rocking movement, 5 degree tilt angle and flat rubber mat 1000 included.
The Rock Core is suitable for laboratories that require controlled rocking movement instead of orbital agitation.

faqs.question: What is the Hei-FLOW Ultimate 600 Single Channel Peristaltic Pump used for?
faqs.answer: The Hei-FLOW Ultimate 600 handles both precise reagent dosing and fast bulk fluid transfer, making it suited to reactor feed-batch dosing, chemostat operation, and rapid tank filling and emptying.

faqs.question: What flow rate does the Hei-FLOW Ultimate 600 deliver?
faqs.answer: In single-channel operation the pump delivers 2.0 to 4,056 mL/min, with the exact figure depending on the tubing bore fitted and the speed setting used.

faqs.question: How accurate is the dosing on the Hei-FLOW Ultimate 600?
faqs.answer: Control accuracy is +/-0.5% with a precision of +/-2%, and the retraction function further protects accuracy at small dosed volumes by preventing a drop from forming at the tube tip.

faqs.question: What is the retraction function?
faqs.answer: After each pumping run, the drive briefly reverses to pull the tube back and clear the last drop at the tip, which keeps microlitre-scale dosing accurate rather than letting a hanging drop register as an error.

faqs.question: Can the Hei-FLOW Ultimate 600 be automated?
faqs.answer: Yes. RS232 and analogue interfaces, 0 to 10 V or 4 to 20 mA, put speed, direction, and start and stop under external control from a PLC or process system.

faqs.question: Does the pump include the pump head and tubing?
faqs.answer: No. The pump drive is supplied on its own; the pump head and tubing are selected separately to match your flow rate and fluid chemistry, and Inkarp confirms this configuration before quotation.

faqs.question: What is interval dosing?
faqs.answer: Interval dosing lets you set a dosing volume together with a pause time, from 0.1 seconds to 750 hours, so a multi-step dosing sequence runs unattended exactly as programmed.

faqs.question: What is the difference between the Hei-FLOW Ultimate 600 and Ultimate 120?
faqs.answer: Both carry the same dosing accuracy, interval dosing, retraction function, and interfaces. The difference is the top-end speed: 600 rpm against a 120 rpm ceiling, which sets the maximum flow rate each variant reaches.

faqs.question: Can the Hei-FLOW Ultimate 600 run continuously?
faqs.answer: Yes. The pump is rated for continuous 24/7 operation, suited to chemostat feed and other processes that cannot pause.

faqs.question: What is the part number of the Hei-FLOW Ultimate 600?
faqs.answer: The part number is 523-52060-00. Inkarp is the authorized distributor for this configuration in India.

longForm.heroLead: Not every pumping application demands high flow. Some require precise, repeatable dosing, while others need rapid liquid transfer without changing equipment. The Hei-FLOW Ultimate 600 is designed to handle both, delivering 2.0 to 4,056 mL/min with +/-0.5% control accuracy across a 24 to 600 rpm speed range. Every parameter is programmable, with RS232 and analogue interfaces for process automation, and the retraction function prevents post-dosing drips for improved accuracy.

body: The Hei-FLOW Ultimate 600 is built around one problem: a reactor needs precise dosing while it runs, and fast bulk transfer when it does not.
One pump, two speeds of work. It delivers 2.0 to 4,056 mL/min in single-channel operation, covering microlitre dosing and rapid fill or empty work in the same drive.
Speed, tubing diameter, flow display, dosing volume, and interval pause times are stored as a profile you select instead of re-entering every parameter.
RS232 and analogue control let speed, direction, and start/stop run under a PLC or process controller through digital RS232 or analogue 0 to 10 V / 4 to 20 mA signals.
The retraction function briefly reverses after each run to pull the tube clear before a drop forms at the tip, keeping small-volume dosing cleaner and more repeatable.

sections.title: Flow rate and dosing accuracy
body: The number on the datasheet is a range; the number that matters is what your specific tubing bore delivers at your specific speed setting. Flow rate on a peristaltic pump is a function of speed and tubing internal diameter together, not speed alone.

At the low end of the 24 to 600 rpm range, a fine-bore tube delivers microlitre-scale dosing with room to spare. At 600 rpm with a wide-bore tube, the same drive moves toward its 4,056 mL/min ceiling for fast fill and empty work.

The +/-0.5% control accuracy holds the drive steady at whichever point on that curve the application sits, and the +/-2% precision figure describes how tightly repeat doses land relative to each other.

faqs.question: What is the Hei-FLOW Expert 600 Single Channel Peristaltic Pump used for?
faqs.answer: The Hei-FLOW Expert 600 is used for fast fluid transfer, tube draining, and process lines where an external controller sets the pump's speed and direction through a simple analogue signal.

faqs.question: What is the turbo button on the Hei-FLOW Expert 600?
faqs.answer: The turbo button takes the drive straight to full speed with one press, built for draining a tube or clearing the last of a fluid from a vessel quickly.

faqs.question: What flow rate does the Hei-FLOW Expert 600 deliver?
faqs.answer: In single-channel operation the pump delivers 2.0 to 4,056 mL/min, depending on the tubing bore fitted and the speed setting used.

faqs.question: Does the Hei-FLOW Expert 600 support programmed dosing?
faqs.answer: No. Volume dosing and interval dosing are not available on this model. For programmable dosing, the Hei-FLOW Ultimate 600 carries that functionality.

faqs.question: How is the Hei-FLOW Expert 600 controlled?
faqs.answer: Through a single analogue interface, 0 to 10 V or 4 to 20 mA, which sets speed, direction, and start/stop. It does not have an RS232 digital interface.

faqs.question: Does the pump include the pump head and tubing?
faqs.answer: No. The pump drive is supplied on its own; the pump head and tubing are selected separately to match your flow rate and fluid, and Inkarp confirms this configuration before quotation.

faqs.question: What is the precision of the Hei-FLOW Expert 600?
faqs.answer: Precision is +/-3.5%, with a control accuracy of +/-0.5% at the drive. For tighter precision, the Ultimate 600 is rated to +/-2%.

faqs.question: Can the Hei-FLOW Expert 600 run continuously?
faqs.answer: Yes. The pump is rated for continuous 24/7 operation.

faqs.question: What is the difference between the Hei-FLOW Expert 600 and Expert 120?
faqs.answer: Both share the same control and feature set. The difference is the top-end speed: 600 rpm against a 120 rpm ceiling, which sets the maximum flow rate each variant reaches.

faqs.question: What is the part number of the Hei-FLOW Expert 600?
faqs.answer: The part number is 523-51060-00. Inkarp is the authorized distributor for this configuration in India.

faqs.answer: The price depends on the pump head, tubing, and accessories your application needs. Contact Inkarp for a quotation once your flow rate and fluid are confirmed.

longForm.heroHook: One button for full speed. One signal for full control.
longForm.heroLead: Some pumping jobs don't need a program. They need a pump that moves fast when you ask it to, and takes commands from your control system the rest of the time. The Hei-FLOW Expert 600 runs 2.0 to 4,056 mL/min across 24 to 600 rpm, at +/-0.5% control accuracy, with a turbo button for instant full-speed draining and a single analogue interface for external control with reversible direction.

stats.label: Instant full-speed for draining and clearing

sections.title: Hei-FLOW Expert 600 at a glance
sections.description: Everything you need to evaluate the Expert 600: how the turbo button works, what the analogue interface controls, what pump head and tubing you still need, the full technical data, and Inkarp installation and service support.
sections.subheading: One pump for fast transfer and simple external control
body: Not every pump needs to remember a recipe. Some just need to run fast, run reliably, and answer to a signal from elsewhere in the process. The Hei-FLOW Expert 600 is built for that job: 2.0 to 4,056 mL/min across a 24 to 600 rpm range, at +/-0.5% control accuracy, without the programmable dosing layer that a reactor-dosing pump carries.

The turbo button is the feature this tier is built around. One press takes the drive straight to full speed, which is exactly what a tube needs when it's being drained or a vessel needs when the last of a residue has to come out. There's no menu to navigate and no parameter to set, press it, and the pump responds.

External control runs through a single analogue interface, 0 to 10 V or 4 to 20 mA, handling speed, direction, and start/stop. Wire it into a process controller and the pump takes its commands from the system rather than a person standing at the panel.
Direction reverses with a button press, and an optional foot switch frees both hands for the vessel, which matters most when you're filling something and changing containers often.
Confirmed model: Hei-FLOW Expert 600, P/N 523-51060-00. Pump head and tubing are selected separately to match your flow rate and fluid.

sections.title: Speed, flow and external control
body: Two things decide how this pump behaves in your process: the speed you set, and the signal your controller sends it.
Flow rate follows speed and tubing bore together, the same as any peristaltic drive, across 24 to 600 rpm and 2.0 to 4,056 mL/min. What's different here is how the drive is told what to do.

There's no stored program to select. The analogue interface takes a continuous voltage or current signal and translates it directly into speed, direction, and start/stop, so the pump does whatever the signal tells it to do, in real time.

faqs.question: What is the Hei-FLOW Core 120 Multi Channel Peristaltic Pump used for?
faqs.answer: The Core 120 Multi is used for general fluid transfer and multi-channel dispensing, with one drive accepting either a single-channel or multi-channel pump head.

faqs.question: Can the same pump run both single-channel and multi-channel heads?
