SD30's InLab 731-ISM sensor is built to cover medium and high conductivities across the full 0.001 μS/cm to 2000 mS/cm range on the same instrument, so switching between a low-conductivity water sample and a high-conductivity process solution doesn't mean switching hardware.

performance.title: Ion-Selective Electrode Measurement Explained
performance.description: What pX and ppm actually tell you, and why SD50 reports both.
body: Ion-selective electrodes measure the concentration of one specific ion in a sample, chloride, fluoride, sodium, and others, but the unit that concentration gets reported in depends on who's reading it. Chemists often work in pX, the negative logarithm of the ion's activity, the same style of unit as pH itself, while a QC report or regulatory spec is more likely to want a direct concentration in mg/L or ppm.
SD50 reports both, with auto-ranging 3- or 4-digit resolution, so a result doesn't need converting by hand to match whichever unit the lab's paperwork actually uses.

performance.description: What upgrading for more parameters, and a newer digital sensor platform, actually solve for a growing lab.
body: Buying a fixed, single-parameter meter is a fine choice on day one, but a lab's testing needs rarely stay fixed. Adding a second parameter later usually means buying a second meter entirely, doubling the calibration routines, the bench space, and the instruments to maintain. performance.title: Pure-Water Conductivity Sensors Explained
performance.description: Why a generalist conductivity probe isn't the right tool at the pure-water end of the scale.
body: A generalist conductivity sensor is built to handle a wide range reasonably well, but "reasonably well" at both ends of a range spanning 0.001 μS/cm to 2000 mS/cm usually means genuine compromises at the extremes. At the low end, in purified or ultra-pure water, a sensor not specifically designed for it can struggle to hold accuracy where the conductivity signal itself is faint.

NF3000's InLab 741 Pro-DES sensor is built specifically for pure water, rather than adapted from a generalist design, which matters most for pharmaceutical water systems, semiconductor rinse water, and any lab where the samples sit consistently at the low, sensitive end of the conductivity scale.

performance.title: LE703 Sensor Range Explained
performance.description: What "medium to high conductivities" actually means for choosing the right sensor.
body: Conductivity spans several orders of magnitude in practice, and no single sensor design covers the entire range equally well. LE703, the probe included with FP30-Std, is built specifically for the 10 μS/cm to 200 mS/cm range, medium to high conductivities, which covers most process solutions, buffers, and general laboratory samples.

For genuinely low-conductivity samples, purified or ultra-pure water in the low μS/cm range, a different sensor, such as the LE740 built for 0.01 μS/cm to 500 μS/cm, is the better fit. Choosing the right sensor for the sample's actual conductivity range matters more than the meter itself once the sample sits outside a probe's designed band.

performance.title: Internal Adjustment Explained
performance.description: What automatic calibration removes from daily operation on the Mettler Toledo MA204.

That matters most in a busy lab where the balance sees continuous use across multiple operators, adjustment happens reliably in the background, rather than depending on someone remembering to run it.

performance.title: Piece Counting and Dynamic Weighing Explained
performance.description: What LA204's two built-in apps take off a routine lab's plate.
body: Counting small components by hand is slow and error-prone past a handful of pieces, and weighing anything that shifts, settles, or breathes on the pan, powders, granules, or restless small samples, makes the reading drift before it stabilizes. LA204's two built-in apps are built around exactly those two everyday problems.

The piece counting app establishes an average unit weight from a reference sample, then converts any weighed batch into a piece count automatically. The dynamic weighing app takes repeated readings over a short window and calculates a stable average, so an unsettled sample still returns a trustworthy result instead of a fluctuating one.

performance.description: What FACT adjustment and leveling guidance actually remove from getting MR204 set up correctly.
body: An analytical balance that isn't level reads wrong before a single sample even touches the pan, and getting it level by eye, watching a bubble indicator and adjusting feet by feel, is easy to get slightly wrong without noticing. performance.title: GxP Compliance and LabX Connectivity Explained
performance.description: What a regulated lab actually needs from a balance, and where MX204 delivers it.
body: A weighing result in a GxP-regulated environment has to survive an audit, not just be accurate in the moment. That means the data trail matters as much as the number on the display: who weighed it, when, on what instrument, and whether the record can be tampered with after the fact. A balance that isn't built for that leaves the audit trail to manual logbooks and printouts, both easy to lose and easy to challenge.

MX204 is built GxP-compliant from the ground up, and connects directly to Mettler Toledo's LabX software, so weighing results move into a controlled, traceable record automatically rather than depending on someone transcribing a number correctly.

performance.title: IP43 and Passcode Protection Explained
performance.description: What durability and access control actually add in a lab that isn't a clean, controlled analytical bench.
body: A precision balance handling larger, everyday samples usually lives in a busier corner of the lab than an analytical balance: more dust in the air, more chance of a splash, more hands using it across a shift. Neither of those risks stops accurate weighing on their own, but together they wear down an instrument that isn't built for the environment, and they open the door to settings being changed by whoever's standing there.

MA1002's IP43 rating protects against dust ingress and splashing water, and passcode protection restricts who can access or change balance settings, so the instrument holds up physically and the configuration stays under control, regardless of how busy or shared the bench gets.

performance.title: Solid Base and Overload Protection Explained
performance.description: What a metal base and overload guard actually protect against on a busy bench.
body: A precision balance handling larger, heavier samples faces two everyday risks a lighter analytical balance rarely sees: the instrument itself shifting or tipping under an off-center load, and a sample or vessel accidentally set down too hard or too heavy for the pan. Either one can throw off a reading or damage the mechanism over time.

LA2002's solid metal base keeps the instrument planted regardless of how a sample is placed, and its overload protection guards the internal mechanism against a load beyond the 2.2 kg rating, absorbing the impact rather than passing it through.

performance.title: 21 CFR Part 11 Compliance and Automatic Doors Explained
performance.description: What full audit-trail compliance and touch-free handling actually protect at microgram precision.
body: At 0.1 µg readability, the smallest disturbance changes the result: a hand near the weighing chamber shifts air currents, a manually opened door introduces a draft, and body heat radiating toward the pan can measurably affect a reading this fine. XPR2U's automatic doors remove the operator's hand from that equation entirely, opening and closing without touch.

The same precision that makes the physical environment matter also makes the data trail matter more. XPR2U supports full 21 CFR Part 11 compliance, meaning every weighing result carries a complete, tamper-evident audit trail, who weighed it, when, and on what configuration, connected directly to LabX rather than depending on a manual record.

performance.title: Automated Workflows Explained
performance.description: What automation actually removes from a routine that repeats trace-level weighing many times a day.
body: Trace-level weighing at 1 µg readability is precise enough on a single measurement, but a routine that repeats the same weighing steps dozens of times a day introduces its own risk: a skipped step, an inconsistent sequence, or a small variation in how each sample is handled compounds across a batch. That's a harder problem to catch than a single bad reading.

XPR3's automated workflows guide the operator through a fixed, repeatable sequence, so every sample in a batch goes through the same steps in the same order, with the balance itself enforcing the routine rather than relying on the operator's memory of the process.

sections.title: Unattended Queueing and Throughput
body: Getting more out of an instrument usually means running it when nobody's watching, and that's exactly the gap AUTOsample-60 closes.

Setup starts with assigning an experiment to each tube through the onboard queueing software. Once that's done, the carousels take over, running through all 50 tubes in sequence without needing anyone at the bench. That means a queue can run overnight, over a lunch break, or in the background of a busy day, improving throughput without adding staff time. Data is acquired and saved automatically as each experiment finishes, so results are organized and waiting by the time you check back in.

sections.title: Structural Elucidation Routines
body: A single 1D spectrum doesn't always tell the full story. AUTOsample-60 is built to run the fuller picture automatically, one sample at a time.

That turns basic structural elucidation into something that runs unattended across an entire carousel, rather than requiring a researcher to set up and monitor each step by hand.

sections.title: Real-Time Reaction Monitoring
body: Sampling a reaction after the fact tells you where it ended up. Watching it in real time tells you how it got there, and that's the shift NMReady-Flow is built around.

Once installed, the flow-through cell turns the benchtop NMR into a continuous, online detector, letting you understand and optimize a chemical reaction as it actually progresses, rather than reconstructing it from periodic offline samples. That same setup extends naturally to automating repeated syntheses, since the instrument can monitor each run without needing manual sampling at every stage.

utilityChecklist.label: Protecting the reaction stream during monitoring

sections.disclaimer: Product expert note: Tell our team about the reaction or synthesis process you want to monitor, and Inkarp will confirm how NMReady-Flow fits into that workflow.

sections.title: Flexible Control and Lab Integration
body: A flow monitoring setup only helps if it fits how your lab actually operates, and NMReady-Flow is built to adapt to that rather than the other way around.

Experiments can be started directly at the instrument for hands-on control, remotely through NMReady-CONNECT for teams that need to check in from elsewhere, or through third-party software for labs that already run their own automation or control systems. That flexibility is also what makes it possible to integrate the benchtop NMR into a larger laboratory system, rather than keeping it as a standalone step disconnected from the rest of the process.

body: Running samples one at a time works fine for occasional use, but most labs eventually need more throughput than that allows. The AUTOsample-60 is built for that shift.

sections.title: Building a Custom Pulse Sequence
body: Writing a custom pulse sequence sounds like it should require a programming background. Experiment Designer is built specifically so it doesn't.

The workflow runs in three clear steps. First, the SeqDev platform opens for editing or creating a pulse sequence, with elements like channels, pulses, and delays added to the diagram with a double-click. Second, once the sequence is complete, it's exported as an application, carrying along any pre-acquisition settings such as automatic Receiver Gain calculation, so the experiment doesn't need to be reconfigured every time it runs. Third, that application loads directly into NMRGUI, the instrument's onboard software, ready to run. Acquisition parameters can be defined in advance for routine use, while still leaving room for fine-tuning when a specific run calls for it.

sections.title: Teaching NMR Fundamentals Through SeqDev
body: Understanding what a pulse sequence actually does is different from just running one. SeqDev's graphical design makes that understanding accessible without a coding prerequisite standing in the way.

Because sequence elements are placed visually, on a diagram, with a double-click, rather than typed as code, students can explore what each channel, pulse, and delay contributes to an experiment directly. That turns Experiment Designer into more than an expert tool. It becomes a way to teach the fundamental principles of NMR pulse sequence design hands-on, letting students build understanding piece by piece rather than treating the sequence as a black box.

sections.title: Real-Time Reaction Monitoring
body: Sampling a reaction after the fact tells you where it ended up. Watching it in real time tells you how it got there, and that's the shift NMReady-Flow is built around.

Once installed, the flow-through cell turns the benchtop NMR into a continuous, online detector, letting you understand and optimize a chemical reaction as it actually progresses, rather than reconstructing it from periodic offline samples. That same setup extends naturally to automating repeated syntheses, since the instrument can monitor each run without needing manual sampling at every stage.

sections.title: Flexible Control and Lab Integration

Experiments can be started directly at the instrument for hands-on control, remotely through NMReady-CONNECT for teams that need to check in from elsewhere, or through third-party software for labs that already run their own automation or control systems. That flexibility is also what makes it possible to integrate the benchtop NMR into a larger laboratory system, rather than keeping it as a standalone step disconnected from the rest of the process.

faqs.question: What is Experiment Designer used for?
faqs.answer: Experiment Designer is an advanced software module that lets expert users design and modify NMR pulse sequences on Nanalysis benchtop spectrometers. It's used for custom method development beyond the instrument's standard sequence library.

faqs.question: Do I need to know a programming language to use Experiment Designer?
faqs.answer: No, Experiment Designer uses a graphical interface built on the SeqDev platform, so pulse sequences are built visually without requiring a coding language.

faqs.question: What platform does Experiment Designer run on?
faqs.answer: Experiment Designer incorporates the Sequence Development (SeqDev) platform from Spinit, accessible directly through the instrument's onboard NMR software, NMRGUI.

faqs.question: How does the Experiment Designer workflow work?
faqs.answer: The workflow has three steps. You design or edit a pulse sequence in SeqDev, export it as an application with any pre-acquisition settings included, then load and run that application directly in NMRGUI.

faqs.question: Can I still adjust settings after exporting a sequence?
faqs.answer: Yes, acquisition parameters can be predefined for routine use, but fine-tuning remains available whenever a specific run needs it.

faqs.question: Can Experiment Designer be used for teaching?
faqs.answer: Yes, because the SeqDev interface is graphical, it works as a hands-on teaching tool, letting students explore pulse sequence fundamentals without needing to learn a coding language.

faqs.question: Which instruments is Experiment Designer compatible with?
faqs.answer: Experiment Designer is compatible with both the Nanalysis-60 and Nanalysis-100 benchtop NMR spectrometers.

faqs.question: What comes standard versus what requires Experiment Designer?
faqs.answer: Every Nanalysis benchtop NMR comes standard with basic pulse sequences like 1D, COSY, and HSQC. Experiment Designer is needed to modify those sequences or build new ones from scratch.

It runs on the graphical SeqDev platform from Spinit, so pulse sequences are built visually rather than written in a programming language.
Sequence elements including channels, pulses, and delays are added to the pulse sequence diagram with a simple double-click.

The workflow has three steps: open SeqDev to edit or create the sequence, export the completed application along with any pre-acquisition settings like automatic Receiver Gain calculation, then load and run it directly in the instrument's onboard software, NMRGUI.
Acquisition parameters can be defined in advance, so routine use doesn't require reconfiguring the experiment each time, though fine-tuning is still available when needed.

Because the interface is graphical, it also works as a genuine teaching tool, letting students explore the fundamental building blocks of pulse sequences without needing to learn a coding language first.
It's compatible with both the Nanalysis-60 and Nanalysis-100 benchtop NMR platforms.

sections.title: Building a Custom Pulse Sequence
body: Writing a custom pulse sequence sounds like it should require a programming background. Experiment Designer is built specifically so it doesn't.

The workflow runs in three clear steps. First, the SeqDev platform opens for editing or creating a pulse sequence, with elements like channels, pulses, and delays added to the diagram with a double-click. Second, once the sequence is complete, it's exported as an application, carrying along any pre-acquisition settings such as automatic Receiver Gain calculation, so the experiment doesn't need to be reconfigured every time it runs. Third, that application loads directly into NMRGUI, the instrument's onboard software, ready to run. Acquisition parameters can be defined in advance for routine use, while still leaving room for fine-tuning when a specific run calls for it.

sections.title: Teaching NMR Fundamentals Through SeqDev
body: Understanding what a pulse sequence actually does is different from just running one. SeqDev's graphical design makes that understanding accessible without a coding prerequisite standing in the way.

Because sequence elements are placed visually, on a diagram, with a double-click, rather than typed as code, students can explore what each channel, pulse, and delay contributes to an experiment directly. That turns Experiment Designer into more than an expert tool. It becomes a way to teach the fundamental principles of NMR pulse sequence design hands-on, letting students build understanding piece by piece rather than treating the sequence as a black box.

faqs.question: What is the NaioAFM used for?
faqs.answer: It's an all-in-one atomic force microscope built for nanoeducation and basic research on small samples, ideal for university courses, classroom settings, and entry-level research.

faqs.question: How long does it take to set up?
faqs.answer: Just a few minutes, with no laser alignment required.

faqs.question: How quickly can a new user get meaningful results?
faqs.answer: In as little as two hours, according to reported classroom experience.

faqs.question: What operating modes does it support?
faqs.answer: All standard imaging modes, static force, dynamic force, and phase imaging, plus magnetic force microscopy, conductive AFM, electrostatic force microscopy, force spectroscopy, force modulation, stiffness and modulus, adhesion, force mapping, and lithography/nanomanipulation.

faqs.question: Does it require laser alignment?
faqs.answer: No, laser alignment is not required at all.

faqs.question: Is it durable enough for student or first-time use?
faqs.answer: Yes, its robust design is specifically built to be insensitive to careless handling by novice users.

faqs.question: Does it include a camera for sample observation?
faqs.answer: Yes, an integrated high-resolution camera provides both top and side view observation.

faqs.question: What software does it run on?
faqs.answer: Nanosurf's shared control software, the same UI used across all Nanosurf AFM systems, with automatic frequency sweep, a spectroscopy wizard, and a scripting interface.

faqs.question: Can the software be scripted or automated?
faqs.answer: Yes, a powerful scripting interface is compatible with LabView, Python, MATLAB, C++, Java, and more.

body: STM has a reputation for demanding controlled environments, high voltage, and hazardous tip-etching chemistry. NaioSTM strips all three of those barriers away.
The system functions entirely without high voltage, making it genuinely safe to place in unexperienced hands, a real requirement for a classroom or teaching lab.
Scanning tips are simply cut from Pt/Ir wire, no etching chemicals, no hazardous substances, no specialized tip-prep station required before a measurement can even start.

A mechanical loop under 10 mm is what makes atomic resolution possible on HOPG in a standard classroom, not a dedicated vibration-isolated lab, backed further by passive isolation feet on a heavy stone table.

items: New STM users don't need a research-grade interface, they need to reach a real result fast, and then understand what they're looking at. NaioSTM's software is built around exactly that sequence.
Only a few clicks are needed per measurement, and helpful wizards guide the process of setting parameters for each measurement type, whether imaging, spectroscopy, or lithography.
Basic analysis tools let a user apply corrections, calculate roughness, and measure distances directly, so images can be evaluated on the spot rather than exported to a separate program first.
That combination is what lets even unexperienced users quickly learn to confidently perform measurements and get meaningful results, not just pretty pictures.

faqs.question: What is DriveAFM used for?
faqs.answer: It's Nanosurf's flagship research atomic force microscope, used across life science, materials research, semiconductors, and energy materials for high-resolution nanoscale imaging and property characterization.

faqs.question: What is CleanDrive?
faqs.answer: Photothermal cantilever excitation — the most stable way to drive a cantilever, maintaining performance in both air and the liquid environments biological samples require.

faqs.question: What is WaveMode?
faqs.answer: The fastest off-resonance imaging mode on the market, in which the cantilever acts as both sensor and actuator, offering the most gentle imaging available to date with directly adjustable interaction force.

faqs.question: Can DriveAFM image in liquid?
faqs.answer: Yes. CleanDrive photothermal excitation ensures reliable performance in the liquid conditions needed to maintain biological sample integrity.

faqs.question: What sample sizes can DriveAFM handle?
faqs.answer: The tip-scanning design accommodates samples of various sizes and shapes, including large and heavy samples, without compromising performance.

faqs.question: Can DriveAFM be combined with optical microscopy?
faqs.answer: Yes. The scan head integrates seamlessly with an inverted optical microscope, combining transmitted light and fluorescence microscopy with AFM imaging and force spectroscopy.

faqs.question: What is automated on the system?
faqs.answer: Full motorization automates laser alignment, spring constant and sensitivity calibration, approach, and data acquisition.

faqs.question: Can DriveAFM operate inside a glovebox?
faqs.answer: Yes. All mechanical adjustments are controlled via software, and magnetic cantilever holders allow operation while wearing thick gloves.

faqs.question: Which electrical modes are supported?
faqs.answer: C-AFM, SSRM, PFM, EFM, KPFM, SMM, and MFM.

faqs.question: Which mechanical characterization modes are available?
faqs.answer: Force spectroscopy including unfolding, stretching and adhesion, modular multi-segment spectroscopy, force modulation, and force mapping for stiffness, modulus, and adhesion.

faqs.question: What is FluidFM?
faqs.answer: Cantilever-based microfluidics for spotting and deposition, single-cell manipulation, and nanomechanics, available with a dedicated cantilever holder.

faqs.question: What is PicoBalance?
faqs.answer: A capability providing mass measurements and frequency-resolved nanomechanics for deeper sample characterization.

faqs.question: Can small cantilevers be used?
faqs.answer: Yes. DriveAFM is compatible with high-fidelity small cantilevers, delivering faster imaging than regular cantilevers.

faqs.question: Is the software suitable for inexperienced users?
faqs.answer: Nanosurf Studio is designed to be easy to learn for novice users while retaining full flexibility for experts, with a configurable GUI and automated setup.

faqs.question: Can instrument control be scripted?
faqs.answer: Yes. Instrument control is fully scriptable, and new software releases arrive quarterly.

faqs.question: Where can I find detailed technical specifications?
faqs.answer: Numeric system specifications are published in the DriveAFM brochure rather than on the product page — Inkarp can provide it on request.

faqs.question: What is the price of DriveAFM in India?
faqs.answer: Get in touch and Inkarp will put together a quote based on the setup configuration, operating modes, and accessories required.

faqs.question: Who is the authorized distributor of DriveAFM in India?
faqs.answer: Inkarp is the authorized distributor and service provider for the Nanosurf DriveAFM in India, providing demonstration, installation, training, AMC, spare parts, and technical support.

longForm.heroHook: See the DNA double helix. Then measure a semiconductor's dopant profile. Same instrument.
longForm.heroLead: Most AFMs are built around a compromise — resolution or sample flexibility, speed or gentleness, biology or materials. DriveAFM is Nanosurf's answer to labs that refuse to make the choice. CleanDrive photothermal cantilever excitation is what makes it possible: the most stable way to drive a cantilever, holding performance even in the liquid conditions biological samples demand. That stability unlocks WaveMode, the fastest off-resonance imaging mode on the market, where the cantilever becomes both sensor and actuator. The tip-scanning design accommodates samples of any size or shape without performance loss — large, heavy materials samples included. Full motorization automates laser alignment, calibration, and approach. And it runs stand-alone or integrated with an inverted optical microscope, so AFM sits alongside fluorescence and transmitted light in one correlative workflow.

faqs.question: What is FlexAFM used for?
faqs.answer: It's a versatile mid-range research atomic force microscope used across materials science, life science, semiconductor, and energy materials research for nanoscale imaging and property characterization.

faqs.question: Can FlexAFM handle large samples?
faqs.answer: Yes. The tip-scanning design handles large samples without compromising versatility, robustness, or the system's compact size.

faqs.question: What controller does FlexAFM use?
faqs.answer: A 24-bit C3000i controller, enabling high-resolution imaging of single atomic layers as well as topography spanning several micrometres. A CX controller upgrade is available.

faqs.question: What does the CX controller upgrade add?
faqs.answer: It allows the system to be integrated with external hardware for advanced applications, and is the first step on the upgrade path to DriveAFM.

faqs.question: Are FlexAFM accessories compatible with DriveAFM?
faqs.answer: Yes. Accessories and sample holders bought for FlexAFM work with DriveAFM, so upgrading the scan head leaves the surrounding hardware in place.

faqs.question: Which inverted optical microscopes can FlexAFM integrate with?
faqs.answer: Most inverted optical microscopes from leading manufacturers including Zeiss, Nikon, Olympus, and Leica.

faqs.question: Can FlexAFM operate inside a glovebox?
faqs.answer: Yes. Its light weight, compact design, and magnetic cantilever holder make it straightforward to operate inside any glovebox.

faqs.question: Can FlexAFM measure in liquid?
faqs.answer: Yes. Measurements can be made in liquid environments with the specimen held in near-physiological condition.

faqs.question: Which electrical modes does FlexAFM support?
faqs.answer: C-AFM, SSRM, PFM, EFM, KPFM, SMM, and MFM.

faqs.question: Which mechanical characterization modes are available?
faqs.answer: Force spectroscopy including unfolding, stretching and adhesion, force modulation, and force mapping for stiffness, modulus, and adhesion.

faqs.question: How difficult is cantilever mounting?
faqs.answer: Quick and simple — the intuitive alignment system uses grooves that precisely position the cantilever.

faqs.question: Does the system include sample navigation optics?
faqs.answer: Yes. An integrated camera provides top and side views of the sample for observation and navigation.

faqs.question: Can instrument control be scripted?
faqs.answer: Yes. Instrument control is fully scriptable, with Python scripting listed as a system feature.

faqs.question: Are software updates included?
faqs.answer: Nanosurf C3000 software includes free lifetime updates.

faqs.question: How is FlexAFM different from DriveAFM?
faqs.answer: DriveAFM adds CleanDrive photothermal excitation and WaveMode imaging, a 28-bit controller as standard, full motorization, small cantilever support, and PicoBalance. FlexAFM covers the same electrical mode set and setup configurations at mid-range cost, with accessories that transfer on upgrade.

faqs.question: Where can I find detailed technical specifications?
faqs.answer: Numeric system specifications are published in the FlexAFM brochure rather than on the product page — Inkarp can provide it on request.

faqs.question: What is the price of FlexAFM in India?
faqs.answer: Get in touch and Inkarp will put together a quote based on the setup configuration, operating modes, and accessories required.

faqs.question: Who is the authorized distributor of FlexAFM in India?
faqs.answer: Inkarp is the authorized distributor and service provider for the Nanosurf FlexAFM in India, providing demonstration, installation, training, AMC, spare parts, and technical support.

longForm.heroHook: Buy the mid-range AFM. Keep the accessories when you upgrade to the flagship.
longForm.heroLead: The usual problem with a mid-range instrument is that outgrowing it means starting over — new system, new sample holders, new accessories, the previous investment written off. Nanosurf built FlexAFM to avoid that. Its accessories and sample holders are compatible with DriveAFM, Nanosurf's most advanced research instrument, so upgrading the scan head later leaves everything else in place and working. The CX controller upgrade is the first deliberate step on that path. What sits underneath is a genuinely capable system in its own right. Tip-scanning design handles large samples without giving up compactness or robustness. A 24-bit C3000i controller resolves single atomic layers while still covering topography spanning several micrometres. It integrates with inverted optical microscopes from Zeiss, Nikon, Olympus, and Leica, or drops into a glovebox for sensitive 2D materials work — light enough to handle safely with one hand.

faqs.question: What is CoreAFM used for?
faqs.answer: It's an all-in-one research atomic force microscope used across nanoscience and nanotechnology — materials characterization, 2D materials, electrical property analysis, life science work, and teaching.

faqs.question: What is included in the all-in-one design?
faqs.answer: A modern flexure-guided scanner, XYZ sample stage, sample observation camera, active vibration table, and airflow shielding, all integrated into a single unit.

faqs.question: How difficult is the system to set up?
faqs.answer: Three cables — connect the controller, plug in power and USB, and the system is ready to go.

faqs.question: Does CoreAFM need a separate vibration isolation table?
faqs.answer: No. An active vibration table is integrated into the unit rather than being a separate purchase.

faqs.question: What controller does CoreAFM use?
faqs.answer: A specially designed 24-bit controller providing precise, reliable scan control alongside straightforward data acquisition and analysis.

faqs.question: How many operating modes are available?
faqs.answer: More than 30 optional modes and functions, spanning basic through advanced measurements.

faqs.question: Can CoreAFM measure in liquid?
faqs.answer: Yes. The system handles applications in both air and liquid environments.

faqs.question: Which electrical modes are supported?
faqs.answer: C-AFM, SSRM, PFM, EFM, KPFM, SMM, and MFM — the same seven modes as Nanosurf's higher-tier systems.

faqs.question: Is CoreAFM suitable for biological work?
faqs.answer: Yes. Nanosurf describes it as the only AFM in its class with versatility covering biological applications, with microscope integration available through DIMO.

faqs.question: What is DIMO?
faqs.answer: The Digital Inverted Microscope Option, providing the microscope integration life science AFM work generally requires.

faqs.question: Can CoreAFM run FluidFM?
faqs.answer: Yes — Nanosurf describes it as the most affordable path to FluidFM functionality.

faqs.question: What advanced options are available?
faqs.answer: Sample heating, environmental control, in-plane magnetic field control via a variable magnetic field generator, and scripting.

faqs.question: Can instrument control be scripted?
faqs.answer: Yes. Instrument control is fully scriptable, with Python scripting listed as a system feature.

faqs.question: Are software updates included?
faqs.answer: Nanosurf Core software includes free lifetime updates.

faqs.question: How is CoreAFM different from FlexAFM and DriveAFM?
faqs.answer: CoreAFM integrates everything including vibration isolation into one unit with three-cable setup. FlexAFM adds configurability across stand-alone, microscope, and glovebox setups plus large sample handling. DriveAFM adds CleanDrive photothermal excitation, WaveMode, a 28-bit controller, and full motorization. All three share the same seven electrical modes.

faqs.question: Where can I find detailed technical specifications?
faqs.answer: Numeric system specifications are published in the CoreAFM brochure rather than on the product page — Inkarp can provide it on request.

faqs.question: What is the price of CoreAFM in India?
faqs.answer: Get in touch and Inkarp will put together a quote based on the modes, options, and accessories required.

faqs.question: Who is the authorized distributor of CoreAFM in India?
faqs.answer: Inkarp is the authorized distributor and service provider for the Nanosurf CoreAFM in India, providing demonstration, installation, training, AMC, spare parts, and technical support.

longForm.heroHook: Three cables. That's the installation.
longForm.heroLead: An AFM is normally a project before it's an instrument. Scanner, sample stage, camera, vibration isolation table, environmental shielding — sourced separately, specified separately, assembled and commissioned before the first image. CoreAFM arrives with all of it inside one unit. Flexure-guided scanner, XYZ sample stage, sample observation camera, active vibration table, and airflow shielding, driven by a purpose-designed 24-bit controller. Connect the controller, plug in power and USB, and the system is ready. The vibration table is the detail worth pausing on — it's usually the separate purchase that decides whether an AFM performs or merely exists, and here it's part of the instrument. What that simplicity doesn't cost is capability. More than 30 optional modes and functions cover morphology, mechanical and electrical properties, in air and in liquid, with sample heating, environmental control, in-plane magnetic field generation, and scripting available. It's also the most affordable route to FluidFM functionality Nanosurf offers.

faqs.question: What is a Nanosurf Industrial Solution?
faqs.answer: It's a bespoke AFM system engineered specifically to an application — Nanosurf's engineering and development team designs the sample stage, scan head mount, and system geometry around the measurement requirement rather than supplying a catalogue product.

faqs.question: How large and heavy a sample can be measured?
faqs.answer: One documented implementation carries samples up to 500 kg, measuring up to 540 × 1500 × 210 mm on a 785 × 1950 mm platform. Nanosurf states virtually no restrictions on sample weight, size, and geometry.

faqs.question: What noise levels are achievable?
faqs.answer: Below 0.75 Å with the NaniteAFM 110 µm scan head on the extra-large stage, and below 0.40 Å with the Flex-Mount scan head on the XYZΦ stage, both in a quiet environment.

faqs.question: Which scan heads are used?
faqs.answer: Mountable versions of the FlexAFM and DriveAFM research-grade scan heads, with tip-scanner technology preserving scanner performance on heavy samples.

faqs.question: How many axes of movement are available?
faqs.answer: Up to 5 degrees of freedom, with the stage designed to reach any position on the sample.

faqs.question: Can curved surfaces be measured?
faqs.answer: Yes. A tiltable scan head combined with multi-axis stage freedom addresses highly polished concave and convex surfaces.

faqs.question: Are these systems cleanroom compatible?
faqs.answer: Yes. Systems are designed to ISO 6 cleanroom compliance, with all materials and components cleanroom certified and assembly carried out in a clean environment.

faqs.question: What safety systems are included?
faqs.answer: A programmable logic controller ensures safe operation, executing safe torque off if safe limited speed is exceeded, the emergency stop is pressed, or an AFM cantilever is lost.

faqs.question: Can the system integrate into factory processes?
faqs.answer: Yes. Automation solutions go beyond simple measurement series to factory-scale process integration, including MES.

faqs.question: How is performance guaranteed before delivery?
faqs.answer: Detailed system models and performance simulations including environmental factors — acoustic noise, temperature variation, and floor vibration — verify that requirements are met by the final system.

faqs.question: Which AFM modes are available?
faqs.answer: Static, lateral, dynamic, and phase imaging; C-AFM, SSRM, PFM, EFM, KPFM, SMM, and MFM for electrical properties; force spectroscopy, modulation, and mapping for mechanical properties.

faqs.question: What software runs these systems?
faqs.answer: Nanosurf C3000/CX control software, with a scripting interface handling everything from small measurement automation series to full-scale MES integration.

faqs.question: How does the engagement process work?
faqs.answer: It begins with an exploratory meeting to discuss the application. Nanosurf's engineering and development team then works iteratively with your team to design the system around the requirement.

faqs.question: How is this different from buying a Flex-Mount or NaniteAFM?
faqs.answer: Those are products configured to an application. An Industrial Solution is an engineering project — stage, mount, geometry, cleanroom compliance, safety systems, and automation all designed to a requirement no standard configuration meets.

faqs.question: What is the price of a Nanosurf Industrial Solution in India?
faqs.answer: Pricing follows the engineering scope. Get in touch and Inkarp will arrange the application scoping conversation that defines it.

faqs.question: Who is the authorized distributor of Nanosurf Industrial Solutions in India?
faqs.answer: Inkarp is the authorized distributor and service provider for Nanosurf in India, providing application scoping, engineering coordination, installation, training, AMC, spare parts, and technical support.

It exists because someone needed it. That's the proposition here: Nanosurf's engineering and development team works with yours to understand the requirement and iteratively design an AFM system around it — sample stage, scan head mount, and system geometry designed to the sample, regardless of size, weight, or curvature. Mountable versions of the FlexAFM and DriveAFM research scan heads supply the measurement performance, with tip-scanner technology preserving that performance even on heavy samples. Up to five axes of freedom reach any position on any sample. Before delivery, detailed system models and performance simulations account for acoustic noise, temperature variation, and floor vibration, so the requirements are met on arrival rather than discovered afterwards. ISO 6 cleanroom compliance and PLC-governed safety come as part of the design where the application demands them.

faqs.question: What is Alphacen 300 used for?
faqs.answer: It's a tip-scanning atomic force microscope for large and heavy samples, used in precision optics metrology, surface roughness measurement, industrial quality control, and large substrate characterization.

faqs.question: What sample size and weight can it handle?
faqs.answer: Samples up to 300 × 300 mm in size and up to 45 kg in weight, with a 50 mm z approach stage for thick samples.

faqs.question: Why does tip-scanning matter for large samples?
faqs.answer: The tip moves rather than the sample, so imaging quality holds regardless of sample size or weight — the sample's mass stops affecting scan performance.

faqs.question: What scan head does it use?
faqs.answer: The Flex-Mount scan head, based on proven research scan head technology from Nanosurf's FlexAFM, with a flexure-based tip design.

faqs.question: What scan range does it offer?
What controller does the system use?
faqs.answer: A 24-bit CX controller — Nanosurf's most advanced AFM controller, offering fast and precise control over the scan process.

faqs.question: Is vibration isolation included?
faqs.answer: Yes. A dedicated acoustic enclosure minimizes external noise and vibrations as part of the system.

faqs.question: Which AFM modes are available?
faqs.answer: Static, lateral, dynamic, and phase imaging; C-AFM, SSRM, PFM, EFM, KPFM, and MFM for electrical properties; force spectroscopy, modulation, and mapping for mechanical; plus lithography and nanomanipulation, EC-AFM, and SThM.

faqs.question: Is Scanning Microwave Microscopy available?
faqs.answer: SMM isn't listed in Nanosurf's published mode set for this system, though it appears on the Flex-Mount and Industrial Solutions pages. Confirm availability at configuration if SMM is required.

faqs.question: Can samples larger than 300 mm be measured?
faqs.answer: Yes, through customization — the Alphacen 300 Flex serves as the basis for custom-engineered solutions accommodating samples beyond 300 mm.

faqs.question: Can sample rotation be added?
faqs.answer: Yes. Rotation axes are customizable on both the sample positioning system and the scan head, useful where consistent feature alignment is needed.

faqs.question: Do cantilevers need manual alignment?
faqs.answer: No. Self-aligning cantilevers remove the manual alignment step.

faqs.question: Can measurements be automated?
faqs.answer: Yes. Automation scripts are customizable beyond the built-in options in the AFM software, and the system integrates into larger automation concepts with support from Nanosurf's Automation Software Solutions team.

faqs.question: How is Alphacen 300 different from Flex-Mount?
faqs.answer: Alphacen 300 Flex is a complete standard system — Flex-Mount scan head, CX controller, and acoustic enclosure, with a defined 300 × 300 mm and 45 kg sample capability. Flex-Mount is the scan head alone, requiring a stage to be specified or built around it.

faqs.question: How is it different from a full Industrial Solution?
faqs.answer: Alphacen 300 is a standard product deliverable without an engineering project. Industrial Solutions are bespoke systems engineered to requirements no standard configuration meets, including cleanroom compliance, PLC safety, and stages carrying up to 500 kg.

faqs.question: Where can I find detailed technical specifications?
faqs.answer: Numeric system specifications are published in the Alphacen 300 Flex brochure — Inkarp can provide it on request.

faqs.question: What is the price of Alphacen 300 in India?
faqs.answer: Get in touch and Inkarp will put together a quote based on the mode set, automation requirements, and any customization needed.

faqs.question: Who is the authorized distributor of Alphacen 300 in India?
faqs.answer: Inkarp is the authorized distributor and service provider for the Nanosurf Alphacen 300 in India, providing demonstration, installation, training, AMC, spare parts, and technical support.

longForm.heroHook: 45 kg on the stage, 300 × 300 mm of sample, and a standard system you can order today.
longForm.heroLead: Large-sample AFM usually means one of two things: a scan head that needs a stage designed around it, or a full bespoke engineering project with a scoping phase before anything is quoted. Alphacen 300 Flex is neither. It's a complete, standard system — Flex-Mount scan head, CX controller, dedicated acoustic enclosure — that handles samples up to 300 × 300 mm and 45 kg out of the box, with a 50 mm z approach stage so thick samples mount without difficulty. The performance comes from proven parts. The tip-scanner design means imaging quality holds regardless of sample size or weight, because the tip moves and the sample doesn't. The flexure-based scanner from Nanosurf's FlexAFM delivers flat, linear scanning at 100 µm range. The CX controller is Nanosurf's most advanced, giving fast and precise control over the scan process. The acoustic enclosure handles external noise and vibration as part of the system. And when the requirement outgrows it, the same system becomes the basis for a custom solution — additional translation or rotation axes on the sample positioning system and the scan head alike.

comparison.disclaimer: The trade is explicit and reasonable. LensAFM offers three electrical modes against seven on the standalone research systems, and no SMM, SThM, EC-AFM, or FluidFM. If the optical microscope is already the centre of the workflow, that trade favours LensAFM.

faqs.question: What is LensAFM used for?
faqs.answer: It's an atomic force microscope that mounts on an optical microscope or profilometer turret, extending resolution and measurement capability beyond the optical limit for surface inspection, defect analysis, and material property characterization.

faqs.question: How does LensAFM mount to a microscope?
faqs.answer: It mounts like a normal objective lens on the turret, using a quick-release kinematic mechanism, so switching to AFM is a matter of rotating the turret.

faqs.question: How accurately does it remount?
faqs.answer: Kinematic mounting guarantees replacement to better than 10 µm accuracy.

faqs.question: Can the same feature be found again after a cantilever change?
faqs.answer: Yes. Alignment grooves on the chip mount place the next cantilever's tip within 4 µm of the same position.

faqs.question: Does the cantilever need laser alignment?
faqs.answer: No. The alignment grooves remove the laser alignment step entirely, saving time on every cantilever change.

faqs.question: Which microscopes is LensAFM compatible with?
faqs.answer: Virtually any optical microscope or 3D optical profilometer, with eight mounting adapters covering Zeiss, Olympus, Leica, Nikon, and Mitutoyo thread standards and working distances.

faqs.question: How is the sample positioned?
faqs.answer: Using the optical microscope's own position manipulators, so no separate stage is required or needs learning.

faqs.question: Does LensAFM have its own optics?
faqs.answer: Yes. An integrated 8x objective lens provides a clear view of both the sample and the cantilever, and is used to relocate areas of interest before scanning.

faqs.question: How does the cantilever approach the sample?
faqs.answer: Automatically — bringing the sample into optical focus is all that's required, and the LensAFM completes the approach.

faqs.question: Can it measure tall surface structures?
faqs.answer: Yes. A large Z-range allows measurement of high structures.

faqs.question: Which properties can LensAFM measure beyond topography?
faqs.answer: Surface roughness, hardness variations, magnetism, and electrical conductance and resistance.

faqs.question: Which electrical modes are available?
faqs.answer: C-AFM, EFM, and MFM.

faqs.question: Can LensAFM characterize transparent samples?
faqs.answer: Yes. AFM overcomes the difficulty of characterizing transparent samples and others hard to assess optically.

faqs.question: How does LensAFM differ from a standalone Nanosurf AFM?
faqs.answer: LensAFM integrates natively with an existing optical microscope and is engineered for repositioning accuracy. Standalone systems like CoreAFM and FlexAFM offer a wider mode set including SMM, SThM, EC-AFM, and FluidFM, along with their own sample stages and vibration isolation.

faqs.question: Can instrument control be scripted?
faqs.answer: Yes. Nanosurf C3000 software offers fully scriptable instrument control, with a Python API available.

faqs.question: Where can I find detailed technical specifications?
faqs.answer: Numeric system specifications are published in the LensAFM brochure rather than on the product page — Inkarp can provide it on request.

faqs.question: What is the price of LensAFM in India?
faqs.answer: Get in touch and Inkarp will put together a quote based on the mounting adapter, modes, and accessories required.

faqs.question: Who is the authorized distributor of LensAFM in India?
faqs.answer: Inkarp is the authorized distributor and service provider for the Nanosurf LensAFM in India, providing demonstration, installation, training, AMC, spare parts, and technical support.

longForm.heroHook: Rotate the turret. The 100x objective just became an AFM.
longForm.heroLead: Optical microscopy stops at the wavelength of light. Everything smaller than that limit is a feature you know is there and cannot resolve — and the usual answer is a second instrument, a second bench, and a sample transferred between them with no certainty of finding the same spot twice. LensAFM mounts on the objective turret like a normal lens. Screen the sample optically, find the area of interest, rotate to the LensAFM position, and scan. The workflow doesn't change; the resolution does. The numbers behind it are what make that workflow trustworthy. Kinematic mounting guarantees remounting to better than 10 µm accuracy. Alignment grooves on the chip mount place the next cantilever's tip within 4 µm of the same position — so the feature found before a cantilever change is still findable after one. Those same grooves remove laser alignment from the process entirely. Beyond topography, it reads surface roughness, hardness variation, magnetism, and electrical conductance — and it characterizes transparent samples that defeat optical assessment altogether.

comparison.disclaimer: The trade is clear-eyed. Nanite carries the narrowest mode set in the Nanosurf range — three standard imaging modes without lateral force, three electrical modes, no SMM, SThM, EC-AFM, or FluidFM. What it uniquely offers is a form factor small enough to embed almost anywhere and the freedom to measure workpieces that cannot be sectioned or moved. Where the constraint is the sample or the system rather than the technique, that trade is the right one.

faqs.question: What is NaniteAFM used for?
faqs.answer: It's a compact, integratable atomic force microscope used for nanoscale surface analysis of workpieces of all shapes and sizes, across nanotechnology, data storage, precision optics, and industrial quality and process control.

faqs.question: How small is the scan head?
faqs.answer: Less than 48 × 87 × 61 mm — small enough to integrate into virtually any imaginable environment.

faqs.question: Is there a limit on sample size?
faqs.answer: No inherent limit. Large pieces and components that cannot be divided into smaller segments are measured as they are.

faqs.question: Does measurement damage or alter the sample?
faqs.answer: No. Samples remain intact and unaltered throughout the analysis process.

faqs.question: Can NaniteAFM measure curved surfaces?
faqs.answer: Yes. It is suited for concave surfaces and handles intricate curves.

faqs.question: What surface detail can it resolve?
faqs.answer: Features as small as a few nanometres, and surface roughness below one nanometre.

faqs.question: Can it be integrated into an existing system?
faqs.answer: Yes. It integrates into existing user systems or custom stages, often without significant modification.

faqs.question: What if no existing stage fits the application?
faqs.answer: Nanosurf's engineers design custom stages, along with automation features, around the specific application.

faqs.question: Is a stand-alone configuration available?
faqs.answer: Yes. Stand-alone solutions are offered alongside the integration configurations.

faqs.question: Can AFM control be built into an existing setup?
faqs.answer: Yes. The scripting interface allows AFM control to be integrated into existing system architectures.

faqs.question: Which programming environments are supported?
faqs.answer: LabVIEW, Python, MATLAB, C++, Java, and most other programming environments.

faqs.question: Which imaging modes are available?
faqs.answer: Static force, dynamic force (tapping), and phase imaging, plus C-AFM, EFM, and MFM for electrical properties and force modulation, spectroscopy, and mapping for mechanical properties.

faqs.question: Does the system include a camera?
faqs.answer: Yes. An integrated top and side view camera provides sample observation.

faqs.question: How is the cantilever set up before measurement?
faqs.answer: Select the cantilever in the software and the system automatically performs the frequency sweep before approach, with no manual parameter setting required.

faqs.question: How does NaniteAFM differ from LensAFM?
faqs.answer: LensAFM mounts on an optical microscope turret to extend an existing optical workflow. NaniteAFM is a scan head built to embed into systems or custom stages, with no inherent sample size limit and concave surface capability. LensAFM additionally offers lateral force mode.

faqs.question: Where can I find detailed technical specifications?
faqs.answer: Numeric system specifications are published in the Nanite brochure rather than on the product page — Inkarp can provide it on request.

longForm.heroLead: Most AFMs decide the shape of the workflow around them — the sample comes to the instrument, cut down to fit a stage, mounted flat, brought to the lab. For quality and process control on real components, that sequence often isn't available. NaniteAFM inverts it. At under 48 × 87 × 61 mm, the scan head integrates into existing user systems or custom stages, frequently without significant modification to either. The AFM goes to the workpiece. The consequence matters more than the dimension. Large pieces stay whole. Components that can't be sectioned are measured as they are. Concave and curved surfaces are accommodated. Samples come through the analysis intact and unaltered — which for a finished part or a costly component is the difference between measuring it and destroying it. Underneath, it delivers nanoscale precision: features a few nanometres across, surface roughness below one nanometre. A scripting interface compatible with LabVIEW, Python, MATLAB, C++, and Java brings AFM control into whatever system already runs the process.

faqs.answer: All standard imaging modes, static force, dynamic force, and phase imaging, plus magnetic force microscopy, conductive AFM, electrostatic force microscopy, force spectroscopy, force modulation, stiffness and modulus, adhesion, force mapping, and lithography/nanomanipulation.

faqs.question: Does it require laser alignment?

faqs.question: Is it durable enough for student or first-time use?

faqs.question: What software does it run on?

faqs.question: Can the software be scripted or automated?

faqs.question: Is high voltage required to operate it?

faqs.question: Does it need a specialized vibration-isolated lab?

faqs.question: What operating modes are available?

body.text: NaioSTM brings the scan head and controller together in a single instrument, simplifying installation, maximizing ease of use, and making the system genuinely easy to transport.
A very small mechanical loop, under 10 mm, provides the stability to achieve atomic resolution on a coffee table or in a classroom, not just in a vibration-controlled lab.
Passive vibration isolation feet on a heavy stone table protect measurements against disturbances, keeping the system robust during operation.
The system functions without high voltage, making it safe to operate in unexperienced hands.
Air-flow shielding, complete with a magnifying glass to aid the initial approach, integrates directly with the scan head, controller, and vibration isolation.
Setup requires connecting just two cables, power and USB, nothing more.
Scanning tips are simply cut from Pt/Ir wire, with no hazardous substances needed to etch them.
The full process from setup to seeing first successful images takes just a few minutes.
A 204 × 204 mm footprint means the system barely takes up workbench space.

body: STM has a reputation for demanding controlled environments, high voltage, and hazardous tip-etching chemistry. NaioSTM strips all three of those barriers away.
The system functions entirely without high voltage, making it genuinely safe to place in unexperienced hands, a real requirement for a classroom or teaching lab.
Scanning tips are simply cut from Pt/Ir wire, no etching chemicals, no hazardous substances, no specialized tip-prep station required before a measurement can even start.

A mechanical loop under 10 mm is what makes atomic resolution possible on HOPG in a standard classroom, not a dedicated vibration-isolated lab, backed further by passive isolation feet on a heavy stone table.

items: New STM users don't need a research-grade interface, they need to reach a real result fast, and then understand what they're looking at. NaioSTM's software is built around exactly that sequence.
Only a few clicks are needed per measurement, and helpful wizards guide the process of setting parameters for each measurement type, whether imaging, spectroscopy, or lithography.
Basic analysis tools let a user apply corrections, calculate roughness, and measure distances directly, so images can be evaluated on the spot rather than exported to a separate program first.
That combination is what lets even unexperienced users quickly learn to confidently perform measurements and get meaningful results, not just pretty pictures.

faqs.question: What is DriveAFM used for?
faqs.answer: It's Nanosurf's flagship research atomic force microscope, used across life science, materials research, semiconductors, and energy materials for high-resolution nanoscale imaging and property characterization.

faqs.question: What is CleanDrive?
faqs.answer: Photothermal cantilever excitation — the most stable way to drive a cantilever, maintaining performance in both air and the liquid environments biological samples require.

faqs.question: What is WaveMode?
faqs.answer: The fastest off-resonance imaging mode on the market, in which the cantilever acts as both sensor and actuator, offering the most gentle imaging available to date with directly adjustable interaction force.

faqs.question: Can DriveAFM image in liquid?
faqs.answer: Yes. CleanDrive photothermal excitation ensures reliable performance in the liquid conditions needed to maintain biological sample integrity.

faqs.question: What sample sizes can DriveAFM handle?
faqs.answer: The tip-scanning design accommodates samples of various sizes and shapes, including large and heavy samples, without compromising performance.

faqs.question: Can DriveAFM be combined with optical microscopy?
faqs.answer: Yes. The scan head integrates seamlessly with an inverted optical microscope, combining transmitted light and fluorescence microscopy with AFM imaging and force spectroscopy.

faqs.question: What is automated on the system?
faqs.answer: Full motorization automates laser alignment, spring constant and sensitivity calibration, approach, and data acquisition.

faqs.question: Can DriveAFM operate inside a glovebox?
faqs.answer: Yes. All mechanical adjustments are controlled via software, and magnetic cantilever holders allow operation while wearing thick gloves.

faqs.question: Which electrical modes are supported?
faqs.answer: C-AFM, SSRM, PFM, EFM, KPFM, SMM, and MFM.

faqs.question: Which mechanical characterization modes are available?
faqs.answer: Force spectroscopy including unfolding, stretching and adhesion, modular multi-segment spectroscopy, force modulation, and force mapping for stiffness, modulus, and adhesion.

faqs.question: What is FluidFM?
faqs.answer: Cantilever-based microfluidics for spotting and deposition, single-cell manipulation, and nanomechanics, available with a dedicated cantilever holder.

faqs.question: What is PicoBalance?
faqs.answer: A capability providing mass measurements and frequency-resolved nanomechanics for deeper sample characterization.

faqs.question: Can small cantilevers be used?
faqs.answer: Yes. DriveAFM is compatible with high-fidelity small cantilevers, delivering faster imaging than regular cantilevers.

faqs.question: Is the software suitable for inexperienced users?
faqs.answer: Nanosurf Studio is designed to be easy to learn for novice users while retaining full flexibility for experts, with a configurable GUI and automated setup.

faqs.question: Can instrument control be scripted?

faqs.question: What is FlexAFM used for?
faqs.answer: It's a versatile mid-range research atomic force microscope used across materials science, life science, semiconductor, and energy materials research for nanoscale imaging and property characterization.

faqs.question: Can FlexAFM handle large samples?
faqs.answer: Yes. The tip-scanning design handles large samples without compromising versatility, robustness, or the system's compact size.

faqs.question: What controller does FlexAFM use?
faqs.answer: A 24-bit C3000i controller, enabling high-resolution imaging of single atomic layers as well as topography spanning several micrometres. A CX controller upgrade is available.

faqs.question: What does the CX controller upgrade add?
faqs.answer: It allows the system to be integrated with external hardware for advanced applications, and is the first step on the upgrade path to DriveAFM.

faqs.question: Are FlexAFM accessories compatible with DriveAFM?
faqs.answer: Yes. Accessories and sample holders bought for FlexAFM work with DriveAFM, so upgrading the scan head leaves the surrounding hardware in place.

faqs.question: Which inverted optical microscopes can FlexAFM integrate with?
faqs.answer: Most inverted optical microscopes from leading manufacturers including Zeiss, Nikon, Olympus, and Leica.

faqs.question: Can FlexAFM operate inside a glovebox?
faqs.answer: Yes. Its light weight, compact design, and magnetic cantilever holder make it straightforward to operate inside any glovebox.

faqs.question: Can FlexAFM measure in liquid?
faqs.answer: Yes. Measurements can be made in liquid environments with the specimen held in near-physiological condition.

faqs.question: Which electrical modes does FlexAFM support?
faqs.answer: C-AFM, SSRM, PFM, EFM, KPFM, SMM, and MFM.

faqs.question: Which mechanical characterization modes are available?
faqs.answer: Force spectroscopy including unfolding, stretching and adhesion, force modulation, and force mapping for stiffness, modulus, and adhesion.

faqs.question: How difficult is cantilever mounting?
faqs.answer: Quick and simple — the intuitive alignment system uses grooves that precisely position the cantilever.

faqs.question: Does the system include sample navigation optics?
faqs.answer: Yes. An integrated camera provides top and side views of the sample for observation and navigation.

faqs.question: Can instrument control be scripted?
faqs.answer: Yes. Instrument control is fully scriptable, with Python scripting listed as a system feature.

faqs.question: Are software updates included?
faqs.answer: Nanosurf C3000 software includes free lifetime updates.

faqs.question: How is FlexAFM different from DriveAFM?
faqs.answer: DriveAFM adds CleanDrive photothermal excitation and WaveMode imaging, a 28-bit controller as standard, full motorization, small cantilever support, and PicoBalance. FlexAFM covers the same electrical mode set and setup configurations at mid-range cost, with accessories that transfer on upgrade.

faqs.question: Where can I find detailed technical specifications?
faqs.answer: Numeric system specifications are published in the FlexAFM brochure rather than on the product page — Inkarp can provide it on request.

The CX controller upgrade is the first deliberate step on that path. What sits underneath is a genuinely capable system in its own right. Tip-scanning design handles large samples without giving up compactness or robustness. faqs.question: What is CoreAFM used for?
faqs.answer: It's an all-in-one research atomic force microscope used across nanoscience and nanotechnology — materials characterization, 2D materials, electrical property analysis, life science work, and teaching.

faqs.question: What is included in the all-in-one design?
faqs.answer: A modern flexure-guided scanner, XYZ sample stage, sample observation camera, active vibration table, and airflow shielding, all integrated into a single unit.

faqs.question: How difficult is the system to set up?
faqs.answer: Three cables — connect the controller, plug in power and USB, and the system is ready to go.

faqs.question: Does CoreAFM need a separate vibration isolation table?
faqs.answer: No. An active vibration table is integrated into the unit rather than being a separate purchase.

faqs.question: What controller does CoreAFM use?
faqs.answer: A specially designed 24-bit controller providing precise, reliable scan control alongside straightforward data acquisition and analysis.

faqs.question: How many operating modes are available?
faqs.answer: More than 30 optional modes and functions, spanning basic through advanced measurements.

faqs.question: Can CoreAFM measure in liquid?
faqs.answer: Yes. The system handles applications in both air and liquid environments.

faqs.question: Which electrical modes are supported?
faqs.answer: C-AFM, SSRM, PFM, EFM, KPFM, SMM, and MFM — the same seven modes as Nanosurf's higher-tier systems.

faqs.question: Is CoreAFM suitable for biological work?
faqs.answer: Yes. Nanosurf describes it as the only AFM in its class with versatility covering biological applications, with microscope integration available through DIMO.

faqs.question: What is DIMO?
faqs.answer: The Digital Inverted Microscope Option, providing the microscope integration life science AFM work generally requires.

faqs.question: Can CoreAFM run FluidFM?
faqs.answer: Yes — Nanosurf describes it as the most affordable path to FluidFM functionality.

faqs.question: What advanced options are available?
faqs.answer: Sample heating, environmental control, in-plane magnetic field control via a variable magnetic field generator, and scripting.

faqs.question: Can instrument control be scripted?
faqs.answer: Yes. Instrument control is fully scriptable, with Python scripting listed as a system feature.

faqs.question: Are software updates included?
faqs.answer: Nanosurf Core software includes free lifetime updates.

faqs.question: How is CoreAFM different from FlexAFM and DriveAFM?
faqs.answer: CoreAFM integrates everything including vibration isolation into one unit with three-cable setup. FlexAFM adds configurability across stand-alone, microscope, and glovebox setups plus large sample handling. DriveAFM adds CleanDrive photothermal excitation, WaveMode, a 28-bit controller, and full motorization. All three share the same seven electrical modes.

faqs.answer: Numeric system specifications are published in the CoreAFM brochure rather than on the product page — Inkarp can provide it on request.

heroParagraphs: An AFM is normally a project before it's an instrument. Scanner, sample stage, camera, vibration isolation table, environmental shielding — sourced separately, specified separately, assembled and commissioned before the first image.

CoreAFM arrives with all of it inside one unit. Flexure-guided scanner, XYZ sample stage, sample observation camera, active vibration table, and airflow shielding, driven by a purpose-designed 24-bit controller. Connect the controller, plug in power and USB, and the system is ready.
The vibration table is the detail worth pausing on — it's usually the separate purchase that decides whether an AFM performs or merely exists, and here it's part of the instrument.

What that simplicity doesn't cost is capability. More than 30 optional modes and functions cover morphology, mechanical and electrical properties, in air and in liquid, with sample heating, environmental control, in-plane magnetic field generation, and scripting available. It's also the most affordable route to FluidFM functionality Nanosurf offers.

faqs.question: What is a Nanosurf Industrial Solution?
faqs.answer: It's a bespoke AFM system engineered specifically to an application — Nanosurf's engineering and development team designs the sample stage, scan head mount, and system geometry around the measurement requirement rather than supplying a catalogue product.

faqs.question: How large and heavy a sample can be measured?
faqs.answer: One documented implementation carries samples up to 500 kg, measuring up to 540 × 1500 × 210 mm on a 785 × 1950 mm platform. Nanosurf states virtually no restrictions on sample weight, size, and geometry.

faqs.question: What noise levels are achievable?
faqs.answer: Below 0.75 Å with the NaniteAFM 110 µm scan head on the extra-large stage, and below 0.40 Å with the Flex-Mount scan head on the XYZΦ stage, both in a quiet environment.

faqs.question: Which scan heads are used?
faqs.answer: Mountable versions of the FlexAFM and DriveAFM research-grade scan heads, with tip-scanner technology preserving scanner performance on heavy samples.

faqs.question: How many axes of movement are available?
faqs.answer: Up to 5 degrees of freedom, with the stage designed to reach any position on the sample.

faqs.question: Can curved surfaces be measured?
faqs.answer: Yes. A tiltable scan head combined with multi-axis stage freedom addresses highly polished concave and convex surfaces.

faqs.question: Are these systems cleanroom compatible?
faqs.answer: Yes. Systems are designed to ISO 6 cleanroom compliance, with all materials and components cleanroom certified and assembly carried out in a clean environment.

faqs.question: What safety systems are included?
faqs.answer: A programmable logic controller ensures safe operation, executing safe torque off if safe limited speed is exceeded, the emergency stop is pressed, or an AFM cantilever is lost.

faqs.question: Can the system integrate into factory processes?
faqs.answer: Yes. Automation solutions go beyond simple measurement series to factory-scale process integration, including MES.

faqs.question: How is performance guaranteed before delivery?
faqs.answer: Detailed system models and performance simulations including environmental factors — acoustic noise, temperature variation, and floor vibration — verify that requirements are met by the final system.

faqs.question: Which AFM modes are available?
faqs.answer: Static, lateral, dynamic, and phase imaging; C-AFM, SSRM, PFM, EFM, KPFM, SMM, and MFM for electrical properties; force spectroscopy, modulation, and mapping for mechanical properties.

faqs.question: What software runs these systems?
faqs.answer: Nanosurf C3000/CX control software, with a scripting interface handling everything from small measurement automation series to full-scale MES integration.

faqs.question: How does the engagement process work?
faqs.answer: It begins with an exploratory meeting to discuss the application. Nanosurf's engineering and development team then works iteratively with your team to design the system around the requirement.

faqs.question: How is this different from buying a Flex-Mount or NaniteAFM?
faqs.answer: Those are products configured to an application. An Industrial Solution is an engineering project — stage, mount, geometry, cleanroom compliance, safety systems, and automation all designed to a requirement no standard configuration meets.

faqs.question: What is the price of a Nanosurf Industrial Solution in India?
faqs.answer: Pricing follows the engineering scope. Get in touch and Inkarp will arrange the application scoping conversation that defines it.

It exists because someone needed it. That's the proposition here: Nanosurf's engineering and development team works with yours to understand the requirement and iteratively design an AFM system around it — sample stage, scan head mount, and system geometry designed to the sample, regardless of size, weight, or curvature. Mountable versions of the FlexAFM and DriveAFM research scan heads supply the measurement performance, with tip-scanner technology preserving that performance even on heavy samples. Up to five axes of freedom reach any position on any sample. Before delivery, detailed system models and performance simulations account for acoustic noise, temperature variation, and floor vibration, so the requirements are met on arrival rather than discovered afterwards. ISO 6 cleanroom compliance and PLC-governed safety come as part of the design where the application demands them.

heroParagraphs: That stage is real and it was built. Over 2 metres long, 1.45 metres wide, weighing more than 2 tonnes — one of the largest AFM stages ever constructed, on air bearings with drive belt and stepper motor positioning, carrying samples up to 500 kg while holding noise below 0.75 Å.

It exists because someone needed it. That's the proposition here: Nanosurf's engineering and development team works with yours to understand the requirement and iteratively design an AFM system around it — sample stage, scan head mount, and system geometry designed to the sample, regardless of size, weight, or curvature.

Mountable versions of the FlexAFM and DriveAFM research scan heads supply the measurement performance, with tip-scanner technology preserving that performance even on heavy samples. Up to five axes of freedom reach any position on any sample.

Before delivery, detailed system models and performance simulations account for acoustic noise, temperature variation, and floor vibration, so the requirements are met on arrival rather than discovered afterwards. ISO 6 cleanroom compliance and PLC-governed safety come as part of the design where the application demands them.

faqs.question: What is Alphacen 300 used for?
faqs.answer: It's a tip-scanning atomic force microscope for large and heavy samples, used in precision optics metrology, surface roughness measurement, industrial quality control, and large substrate characterization.

faqs.question: What sample size and weight can it handle?
faqs.answer: Samples up to 300 × 300 mm in size and up to 45 kg in weight, with a 50 mm z approach stage for thick samples.

faqs.question: Why does tip-scanning matter for large samples?
faqs.answer: The tip moves rather than the sample, so imaging quality holds regardless of sample size or weight — the sample's mass stops affecting scan performance.

faqs.question: What scan head does it use?
faqs.answer: The Flex-Mount scan head, based on proven research scan head technology from Nanosurf's FlexAFM, with a flexure-based tip design.

faqs.question: What scan range does it offer?
What controller does the system use?
faqs.answer: A 24-bit CX controller — Nanosurf's most advanced AFM controller, offering fast and precise control over the scan process.

faqs.question: Is vibration isolation included?
faqs.answer: Yes. A dedicated acoustic enclosure minimizes external noise and vibrations as part of the system.

faqs.question: Which AFM modes are available?
faqs.answer: Static, lateral, dynamic, and phase imaging; C-AFM, SSRM, PFM, EFM, KPFM, and MFM for electrical properties; force spectroscopy, modulation, and mapping for mechanical; plus lithography and nanomanipulation, EC-AFM, and SThM.

faqs.question: Is Scanning Microwave Microscopy available?
faqs.answer: SMM isn't listed in Nanosurf's published mode set for this system, though it appears on the Flex-Mount and Industrial Solutions pages. Confirm availability at configuration if SMM is required.

faqs.question: Can samples larger than 300 mm be measured?
faqs.answer: Yes, through customization — the Alphacen 300 Flex serves as the basis for custom-engineered solutions accommodating samples beyond 300 mm.

faqs.question: Can sample rotation be added?
faqs.answer: Yes. Rotation axes are customizable on both the sample positioning system and the scan head, useful where consistent feature alignment is needed.

faqs.question: Do cantilevers need manual alignment?
faqs.answer: No. Self-aligning cantilevers remove the manual alignment step.

faqs.question: Can measurements be automated?
faqs.answer: Yes. Automation scripts are customizable beyond the built-in options in the AFM software, and the system integrates into larger automation concepts with support from Nanosurf's Automation Software Solutions team.

faqs.question: How is Alphacen 300 different from Flex-Mount?
faqs.answer: Alphacen 300 Flex is a complete standard system — Flex-Mount scan head, CX controller, and acoustic enclosure, with a defined 300 × 300 mm and 45 kg sample capability. Flex-Mount is the scan head alone, requiring a stage to be specified or built around it.

faqs.question: How is it different from a full Industrial Solution?
faqs.answer: Alphacen 300 is a standard product deliverable without an engineering project. Industrial Solutions are bespoke systems engineered to requirements no standard configuration meets, including cleanroom compliance, PLC safety, and stages carrying up to 500 kg.

faqs.question: Where can I find detailed technical specifications?
faqs.answer: Numeric system specifications are published in the Alphacen 300 Flex brochure — Inkarp can provide it on request.

faqs.answer: Get in touch and Inkarp will put together a quote based on the mode set, automation requirements, and any customization needed.
