faqs.answer: Only if your protocols exceed 30 steps or 16 hours per step, or if you need to control external devices like pumps, balances, or sensors alongside the Mya 4.

faqs.question: How do I control a third-party device with the Mya 4?
faqs.answer: Upgrade to the PC Control Software, confirm your device is on the supported list (syringe pumps, pH sensors, peristaltic pumps, and others), and install the relevant device driver.

faqs.question: How do I try the software before buying it?
faqs.answer: Download the free demo version, which simulates device control and lets you build and test schedules without needing the physical Mya 4 connected.

faqs.question: Can I move my PC Software license to a different computer?
faqs.answer: No. Once the license is activated on a PC, it cannot be moved, so confirm your installation PC before activating.

faqs.question: What are the minimum PC requirements for the software?
faqs.answer: Windows 7, 8, 10, or 11, a dual-core 1.9 GHz processor, 2 GB RAM minimum (4 GB recommended), 30 GB hard disk at 5,400 rpm, and Intel HD Graphics.

faqs.question: Does the Control Pad support multi-user operation?
faqs.answer: Yes, this is included as standard, letting different users run experiments independently across the four zones.

faqs.question: Can I export reports from the Control Pad?
faqs.answer: Yes, in CSV format via USB memory stick; the PC Software additionally offers a Report Wizard for RTF reports.

faqs.answer: The price depends on your device integration needs. Contact Inkarp for a quotation once your protocol and device requirements are confirmed.

faqs.question: What vessel sizes are available for the Mya 4?
faqs.answer: Process reaction vessels from 50 to 400 mL, round bottom flasks from 25 to 250 mL, and vials and tubes across seven confirmed diameters.

faqs.question: Why does each vessel size get its own insert?
faqs.answer: Dedicated inserts give genuine heat transfer contact for each vessel size, avoiding the imprecise fit that comes from layering mismatched inserts together.

faqs.question: How do I set up overhead stirring for a very small sample volume?
faqs.answer: Use the Carousel 12 Plus reaction tube, which attaches to the Reflux or Manifold head and enables overhead stirring from as low as 5 mL.

faqs.question: How do I choose the right impeller for a scale-up study?
faqs.answer: Use the Retreat Curve Impeller, purpose-built to mirror the mixing conditions of a large-scale reaction during bench-scale work.

faqs.question: What impeller shapes are available?
faqs.answer: Turbine, anchor, U-shape, centrifugal, and flat, with custom impellers available on request.

faqs.question: Can I integrate a PAT probe with the Mya 4?
faqs.answer: Yes, using the dedicated Blaze Metrics probe lid, a 6-neck glass-filled PTFE lid for the 400 mL process vessel, which also works in standard operation without the probe fitted.

faqs.question: What is the difference between glass and PTFE lids?
faqs.answer: PTFE lids offer improved durability and safety, and are strong enough to support heavier probes and accessories, compared to standard glass lids.

faqs.question: Can I refresh a worn Mya 4 top cover without buying a new unit?
faqs.answer: Yes, the silicone top cover is designed as a low-cost way for existing users to rejuvenate a worn cover.

sections.title: Jacketed Filter Vessel Engineering
sections.tabSummary: What the flange, seal, and BOV design actually deliver
body: Every part of this vessel's design targets one of two problems: losing temperature control during filtration, or losing product to the equipment itself.

The jacket runs the full height down to the filter plate, not just around the reaction zone, which is what keeps temperature control consistent through both steps. The bottom outlet valve is built with zero dead space specifically to stop material collecting below the filter media, and it's removable for cleaning with a 15 mm bore for easy run-off. The seal between vessel and lid, an FEP-encapsulated O-ring with a PTFE collar on the DN100 flange, is what keeps the whole system leak-tight under those conditions.

faqs.question: What is the Reactor-Ready Duo Lab Reactor used for?
faqs.answer: It's a two-vessel jacketed lab reactor used for parallel synthesis, two-stage reactions, and comparative process optimisation, with each vessel independently exchangeable.

faqs.question: Can the two vessels run at different temperatures?
faqs.answer: Yes, with the double circulator manifold kit (RR121310), each vessel is controlled by its own thermoregulator independently.

faqs.question: Can I run Duo with just one vessel?
faqs.answer: Yes. The single circulator manifold kit (RR121305) ships with a blanking plug specifically for running one vessel only.

faqs.question: How do I order a complete Reactor-Ready Duo system?
faqs.answer: Start with the Core system (RR121300), choose a single or double circulator manifold kit, select your vessel kits and overhead stirrers, then add any circulators, hoses, or AVA automation you need.

faqs.question: How do I set up a two-stage reaction with automated fluid transfer?
faqs.answer: Configure AVA software to control fluid transfer between the two vessels via vacuum or pump, moving reactant from the first stage into the second without manual intervention.

faqs.question: Can the two vessels be different sizes?
faqs.answer: Yes. Vessel volumes from 100 mL to 5 L can be combined on the same Duo system.

faqs.question: What's included in the Core system?
faqs.answer: The stand and base, drip tray, support rods, clamps, hose tidies, stirrer guides and couplings, vessel lids with sealing caps, O-ring seals, and support collars.

faqs.question: Does Duo work with AVA software the same way as other Reactor-Ready systems?
faqs.answer: Yes, with one addition specific to Duo: AVA can control fluid transfer directly between the two vessels, not just log and control individual devices.

faqs.question: What is the price of the Reactor-Ready Duo Lab Reactor in India?
faqs.answer: The price depends on your manifold kit choice, vessel sizes, and whether you add AVA automation. Contact Inkarp for a quotation once your configuration is confirmed.

sections.title: Single vs Double Circulator Configuration
sections.tabSummary: Choosing shared or independent vessel temperatures
body: The manifold kit you choose decides whether your two vessels share a temperature or run apart, and that choice is worth making deliberately.

The single circulator kit (RR121305) routes one thermoregulator to both vessels, holding them at the same temperature, and includes a blanking plug for running just one vessel when the second isn't needed. The double circulator kit (RR121310) routes two independent thermoregulators to the vessels, letting each run its own temperature entirely. The hose lengths differ between the two kits, 70 cm on the single and 60 cm on the double, reflecting the different manifold layouts.

faqs.question: Does the Reactor-Ready Pilot work with stirrers I already own?
faqs.answer: Yes. It's compatible with Radleys stirrers and other leading brands, with tool-free, 4-axis alignment.

faqs.question: How do I choose between the vessel sizes?
faqs.answer: Match your target batch volume: 5 to 20 litres follow the standard 1.25:1 plant-scale ratio, while 30, 35, and 50 litre vessels are stated exceptions to that ratio and require the lower support plate.

faqs.question: How do I connect the Pilot framework to my thermoregulator?
faqs.answer: You'll need hoses with an M30x1.5 female connection, or appropriate adapters, since thermoregulator hoses aren't included in the core system.

faqs.question: How do I choose between a glass and PTFE lid?
faqs.answer: Choose glass for standard synthesis work, or PTFE if you're using PAT or test probes, since it supports up to 8 ports and is more robust than glass.

faqs.question: Does the Reactor-Ready Pilot include a drip tray?
faqs.answer: No. Drip trays are ordered separately, available in 7, 22, 45, and 55 litre capacities.

faqs.question: What is the V4 zero dead space stopcock?
faqs.answer: A drain stopcock design specifically built to prevent the over-tightening that commonly causes glass breakage on standard stopcocks.

faqs.question: Do the 30, 35, and 50 litre vessels need any additional support?
faqs.answer: Yes, they specifically require the lower support plate, which adjusts without tools.

faqs.question: Can the Reactor-Ready Pilot handle multiple vessel sizes on one framework?
faqs.answer: Yes. One compact framework accepts all vessel sizes from 5 to 50 litres, with vessel exchange in minutes.

faqs.question: What are Custom Jacketed Reaction Systems used for?
faqs.answer: They're bespoke jacketed reaction systems designed and built for requirements a standard configuration can't meet, covering vessels, multi-reactor rigs, fermenters, bioreactors, and photoreactors from 100 mL to 30 litres.

faqs.question: When should I choose custom instead of a standard Reactor-Ready system?
faqs.answer: Choose custom when your process needs a non-standard vessel geometry, special features like optical windows or split jackets, a system type like a fermenter or bioreactor, or a temperature and connection combination the standard range doesn't cover.

faqs.question: How do I scope a custom jacketed reaction system?
faqs.answer: Describe your volume, temperature, vessel geometry, and any special features or system-level requirements to Inkarp, who will work with Radleys' design team to confirm the build.

faqs.question: How do I decide between Reactor-Ready and traditional connections?
faqs.answer: Choose Reactor-Ready connections if you need to reach up to 230°C, or traditional connections if 200°C covers your process and a conventional setup is preferred.

faqs.question: What is the maximum volume for a custom system?
faqs.answer: 100 mL to 30 litres for single jacketed vessels; vacuum jacketed vessels are available up to 10 litres.

faqs.question: Can I get an air-powered stirrer for a hazardous atmosphere?
faqs.answer: Yes. Air-powered stirring is a confirmed option specifically for applications where an electrical motor poses an ignition risk.

faqs.question: Does Radleys build fermenters and bioreactors, not just standard reactors?
faqs.answer: Yes, this is confirmed within the scope of Custom Jacketed Reaction Systems, alongside photoreactors and multi-reactor parallel synthesis rigs.

faqs.question: Is training included with a custom system?
faqs.answer: Yes, installation and training are part of the confirmed scope of services.

faqs.question: What is the price of Custom Jacketed Reaction Systems in India?
faqs.answer: Pricing is fully specification-dependent. Contact Inkarp to scope your requirements and receive a custom quotation.

faqs.question: Who is the authorized distributor of Custom Jacketed Reaction Systems in India?
faqs.answer: Inkarp is the authorized distributor and service provider for Radleys Custom Jacketed Reaction Systems in India, providing demonstration, installation, training, AMC, spare parts, and technical support.

The scope runs from a small benchtop reactor to a complex multi-vessel parallel rig, 100 mL to 30 litres, built to your specification and budget. faqs.question: What is the Carousel 12 Plus Reaction Station used for?
faqs.answer: It's a patented 12-position station that simultaneously heats, stirs, and refluxes samples under an inert atmosphere, used for parallel reaction screening and solid supported reagent synthesis.

faqs.question: Do you offer a demo of the Carousel 12 Plus?
faqs.answer: Yes, Inkarp can arrange a demonstration on your own application.

faqs.question: How can I work with smaller volumes in my Carousel 12 Plus?
faqs.answer: Use reduced-volume tubes, which bring the reaction volume down to 1 to 5 mL, compared to the standard 5 to 20 mL tubes.

faqs.question: How do I purge my tubes for an inert atmosphere?
faqs.answer: Connect the central gas inlet via flexible tubing to a two-way stopcock, then alternate between vacuum and inert gas to quickly clear unwanted air from all 12 tubes.

faqs.question: How do I set up sub-ambient cooling for my reactions?
faqs.answer: Add the optional HDPE cooling reservoir, which brings the achievable temperature down to -78°C; the base configuration alone doesn't reach sub-ambient temperatures.

faqs.question: Does every tube really stir at the same speed?
faqs.answer: Yes. The patented design positions every tube and its stir bar equidistant from the hotplate's central magnet specifically to keep stirring speed identical across all 12 positions.

faqs.question: What tubing do I need for the reflux/inerting head?
faqs.answer: This is confirmed directly by Inkarp based on your specific installation.

faqs.question: How accurate is the temperature control?
faqs.answer: ±1°C, using the hotplate's digital control or an optional Pt1000 sensor for block or solution temperature.

faqs.question: Can I add reagents without breaking the inert atmosphere?
faqs.answer: Yes, through the replaceable Suba-Seal septum in each Easy-On cap, using a syringe.

faqs.question: What is the price of the Carousel 12 Plus Reaction Station in India?
faqs.answer: The price depends on your tube configuration and whether you need the cooling reservoir. Contact Inkarp for a quotation once your requirements are confirmed.

faqs.question: Who is the authorized distributor of the Carousel 12 Plus Reaction Station in India?
faqs.answer: Inkarp is the authorized distributor and service provider for the Radleys Carousel 12 Plus Reaction Station in India, providing demonstration, installation, training, AMC, spare parts, and technical support.

longForm.heroLead: Run 12 reactions on one stirring hotplate and it's easy for stirring speed to drift between positions, some tubes closer to the magnet than others. Carousel 12 Plus doesn't let that happen. Every tube and its stir bar sit equidistant from the hotplate's central magnet, patented specifically to keep stirring identical across all 12 positions, from 100 to 1,400 rpm. Heating reaches 180°C sustained, 220°C briefly, held to ±1°C, with the option to control block or solution temperature directly. Reflux runs through a water-cooled head that removes with the tubes still attached, and the whole system operates under a genuine inert atmosphere: individual gas-tight caps, a radial distribution system, and a two-way stopcock to purge each tube in seconds.

sections.tabSummary: What actually makes all 12 tubes behave identically
body: Twelve independent reactions running identically depends on three things behaving the same way across every position, not just one.

Stirring is uniform because of geometry: every tube and its stir bar sit equidistant from the hotplate's central magnet, which is the actual mechanism, not a side effect of the circular layout. Heating and cooling are uniform because the reaction tubes themselves are precision engineered from heavy-walled borosilicate glass specifically to maximise and equalize heat transfer. Reflux stays uniform because the water-cooled head creates the same cooling zone in the upper part of every tube simultaneously.

faqs.question: What is the Cooled Carousel 12 Plus Reaction Station used for?
faqs.answer: It's a cooling reservoir for parallel low-temperature synthesis, running up to 12 stirred reactions simultaneously down to -78°C.

faqs.question: What cooling mixtures does it use?
faqs.answer: A range of freezing mixtures, including dry ice/acetone, controlled manually from ambient down to -78°C.

faqs.question: How does the stirrer survive at -78°C?
faqs.answer: The insulated foam core is specifically built to protect the stirrer mechanism from freezing while holding the low temperature over long periods.

faqs.question: How do I switch between heating and cooling for the same reactions?
faqs.answer: Transfer the removable reflux/inerting head, with the tubes still attached, from the heated Carousel 12 Plus base to the Cooled Carousel 12 Plus reservoir, or back again.

faqs.question: Do I need a whole new system if I already own a standard Carousel 12 Plus?

faqs.answer: Match the mixture to how cold you need to go; dry ice/acetone reaches the full range down to -78°C, and Inkarp can confirm alternatives for less extreme temperatures.

faqs.question: Does the lid affect visibility of the reaction?
faqs.answer: No, it improves it. The HDPE lid minimizes ice formation on the tubes, keeping the contents visible, and prevents spitting from the cooling mixture.

faqs.question: Is the reservoir durable for routine lab use?

faqs.question: Why is vacuum-free design an advantage here?
faqs.answer: It removes taps, valves, and drip needles from the process entirely, which simplifies cleaning, cuts consumable costs, and specifically prevents columns from drying out the way a vacuum manifold can.

faqs.question: How do I speed up a work-up beyond gravity flow?
faqs.answer: Add the SpeediFlow Booster, a hand-held pressuriser that individually controls flow through a specific column, with a safety relief valve venting at 6 to 8 psi.

faqs.question: How do I set up a sequential, multi-step work-up?
faqs.answer: Add the optional third rack, stacked above the standard two-rack configuration, for staged processing.

faqs.question: How do I add a second rack to the station?
faqs.answer: Pull out the spring-loaded knob and rotate it 90 degrees to lock the second rack into place.

faqs.question: What column chemistries are available?
faqs.answer: 20 µm filtration, phase separation, silica, SCX, aminopropyl, and SAX acetate, all in the standard 70 mL format.

faqs.question: Can I use non-standard column sizes with SpeediFlow?
faqs.answer: Yes, using the optional SpeediFlow adapters, which cover 15, 25, 70, and 150 mL columns, plus the Whatman AutoCup.

faqs.question: Does this station work with my existing Carousel Reaction Tubes?
faqs.answer: Yes, the same Carousel Reaction Tubes used in Carousel 12 Plus and Cooled Carousel 12 Plus fit the lower collection rack directly.

faqs.question: Is the SpeediFlow Booster safe from over-pressurisation?
faqs.answer: Yes, it includes a safety relief valve that vents automatically at 6 to 8 psi.

longForm.heroHook: No vacuum, no valves, no drip needles. Twelve columns, still under precise control.
heroParagraphs: Post-synthesis work-up usually means a vacuum manifold, a set of valves, and columns that dry out the moment the vacuum pulls too hard. This station skips all of that.

Twelve columns run in parallel, gravity-fed by default, with no taps or drip needles to clean or replace. When you need more speed than gravity gives you, the hand-held SpeediFlow Booster pressurises each column individually, with a safety relief valve venting at 6 to 8 psi so pressure never gets away from you.

Two identical racks lock together, and a third stacks on top when the work-up needs a second step. The same Carousel Reaction Tubes from your Carousel 12 Plus system slot straight into the collection rack underneath.

faqs.question: What is the Carousel 6 Plus Reaction Station used for?
faqs.answer: It's a 6-position station that heats, stirs, and refluxes standard round bottom flasks simultaneously under an inert atmosphere, used for parallel synthesis and azeotropic distillation.

faqs.question: How fast does it heat?
faqs.answer: It boils six flasks of water in under 25 minutes, all together, ambient to 180°C.

faqs.question: How do I choose the right flask size?
faqs.answer: Match your reaction volume to one of seven confirmed sizes, 5 to 250 mL, with 1- or 2-sidearm versions where needed; a reducing insert lets a smaller flask sit in a larger well.

faqs.question: Can I remove a flask mid-run without disturbing the setup?
faqs.answer: Yes. The removable aluminium reflux insert maintains heat transfer, and a built-in spring clip retains the flask once the insert is out.

faqs.question: How do I set up azeotropic distillation?
faqs.answer: Use the 250 mL Dean-Stark azeotropic flask option, designed specifically for water removal during synthesis.

faqs.question: How do I extend the base unit for viscous samples or extended temperature control?
faqs.answer: Add the Tornado module for powerful stirring of viscous samples, or Breeze or Storm for controlled heating and cooling beyond the base configuration.

faqs.question: Can I run sub-ambient reactions on the Carousel 6 Plus?
faqs.answer: Yes, with the Cooled Carousel 6 option, performing up to six cooled reactions to -78°C.

faqs.question: What protects the user from the hot aluminium base?
faqs.answer: A PTFE heat protection ring, specifically included to guard against accidental contact.

faqs.question: What is the temperature accuracy?
faqs.answer: The source states ±1°C for heating performance and ±0.5°C under temperature control; Inkarp can confirm which applies to your specific configuration.

faqs.question: What is the price of the Carousel 6 Plus Reaction Station in India?
faqs.answer: The price depends on your flask configuration and any modular add-ons. Contact Inkarp for a quotation once your requirements are confirmed.

faqs.question: What is the Tornado Overhead Stirring System used for?

faqs.question: Does Tornado work as a standalone system?

faqs.question: How viscous a sample can Tornado handle?
faqs.answer: Up to 10,000 mPa·s at 500 rpm, with speeds up to 1,000 rpm available for lower-viscosity samples.

faqs.question: How do I choose between the 1:1 and 2:1 drive ratio?
faqs.answer: Use 1:1 for thin, free-flowing liquids at higher speed, or 2:1 when you need more torque for viscous samples, especially with a lower-powered stirrer.

faqs.question: How do I select the right stirrer shape for my sample?
faqs.answer: Choose centrifugal for high-shear dispersion, anchor or propeller for general viscous mixing, and confirm sizing with Inkarp based on your specific flask.

faqs.question: Can I use my existing overhead stirrer with Tornado?

faqs.question: Does adding Tornado increase my bench footprint?
faqs.answer: No. It integrates directly with an existing Carousel 6 Plus without adding footprint.

faqs.question: Is Tornado safe to operate around rotating parts?
faqs.answer: Yes, an integral polycarbonate guard prevents accidental contact with the rotating stirrer components.

faqs.question: Can Tornado run under an inert atmosphere?

sections.tabSummary: What the gear ratio actually changes for your stirrer
body: Handling a viscous sample usually means buying a more powerful, more expensive stirrer. The 2-speed drive is built specifically to avoid that.

Switching between the 1:1 and 2:1 gear ratios changes the torque delivered to the stirrer shaft without changing which physical stirrer motor you own, which is what lets a lower-torque unit still manage liquids up to 10,000 mPa·s at 500 rpm. At the low-viscosity end, speed reaches up to 1,000 rpm, giving genuine range across both thin and thick samples on the same system.

faqs.question: What is the GreenHouse Plus Parallel Synthesiser used for?
faqs.answer: It's a 24-position parallel synthesis platform for high-throughput reaction screening, built with an MTP-compatible footprint for pipettor or robotic sample handling.

faqs.question: Why does the MTP footprint matter?
faqs.answer: It lets samples transfer seamlessly via multi-channel pipettor or robotics, connecting a manual heating and stirring platform directly into an automated workflow without a custom transfer step.

faqs.question: How does V-Mag stirring differ from standard magnetic stirring?
faqs.answer: It positions the stir bar vertically within each tube specifically to maximise mixing uniformity, a different approach from horizontal, magnet-equidistant designs.

faqs.question: How do I add a reagent without breaking the inert atmosphere?
faqs.answer: Use the replaceable septum mats, which allow addition or retrieval from individual tubes while the system remains under reflux or inert conditions.

faqs.question: How do I set up GreenHouse Plus for automated liquid handling?
faqs.answer: Confirm your pipettor or robotic system's footprint requirements with Inkarp; the reaction block matches a standard MTP directly.

faqs.question: Why is GreenHouse Plus described as maintenance-free?
faqs.answer: The unit itself has no electrical or moving parts; it sits passively on the separately-powered Carousel Stirring Hotplate.

faqs.question: What temperature accuracy does GreenHouse Plus achieve?
faqs.answer: ±0.5°C, up to 150°C, tighter than the Carousel 12 Plus tube-based system's ±1°C.

faqs.question: Can GreenHouse Plus be converted for post-synthesis work-up?
faqs.answer: Yes, the same hardware can be converted into a GreenHouse Blowdown Evaporator for solvent removal after synthesis.

faqs.question: What is the price of the GreenHouse Plus Parallel Synthesiser in India?
faqs.answer: The price depends on your configuration and any conversion accessories. Contact Inkarp for a quotation once your workflow is confirmed.

faqs.question: What is the GreenHouse Blowdown Evaporator used for?
faqs.answer: It's a parallel evaporation system for post-synthesis work-up and HPLC fraction concentration, processing 8 or 24 samples simultaneously.

faqs.question: How does it prevent bumping during evaporation?
faqs.answer: It operates entirely without a vacuum, which is the mechanism that would otherwise cause bumping and sample loss.

faqs.question: How does solvent trapping work?
faqs.answer: The enclosed chamber routes evaporating solvent through a high-performance glass condenser, which captures and collects it instead of releasing it into the room.

faqs.question: Do I need to buy a whole new GreenHouse system?
faqs.answer: No, not necessarily. The Blowdown Adaptor upgrades an existing GreenHouse Plus base directly; the dedicated Blowdown Base runs entirely standalone if you don't already own one.

faqs.question: How do I switch between 8 and 24 sample positions?
faqs.answer: Exchange the interchangeable pin plate using the removable head's quick-release handles, no tools required.

faqs.question: What sample formats are compatible?
faqs.answer: GreenHouse tubes (0.5-7 mL), vial racks in 8 or 24 positions across 5 confirmed diameters, and 8 or 24-well microtiter plates.

faqs.question: Can I evaporate GreenHouse reaction tubes without moving them?
faqs.answer: Yes. They evaporate directly in the standard GreenHouse reaction block, without needing to load or reload it.

faqs.question: Is the evaporation rate controllable?
faqs.answer: Yes, through digital heating control from the shared hotplate, and an optional flowmeter for precise inert gas flow control.

faqs.question: What is the price of the GreenHouse Blowdown Evaporator in India?
faqs.answer: The price depends on whether you choose the adaptor or the standalone base, and your pin plate configuration. Contact Inkarp for a quotation once your setup is confirmed.

body: Two design decisions work together here: removing the vacuum, and containing the vapor that removal would otherwise release.

faqs.question: What is the GreenHouse Work-Up Station used for?
faqs.answer: It's a 24-position parallel purification station, using a stacked two-level column design to run sequential purification, like filtration into SPE, in a single pass.

faqs.question: How does sequential purification work without moving the sample?
faqs.answer: The upper column level handles the first step, and whatever passes through flows directly into the lower level's column for the second step, with no manual transfer in between.

faqs.question: Can I use this for single-step purification too?
faqs.answer: Yes, remove the upper support plate and the unit runs as a standard single-level purification station.

faqs.question: How do I speed up flow across all 24 positions?
faqs.answer: Use the clear acrylic gas cover, which applies slight positive pressure to boost flow rate across the whole unit at once.

faqs.question: How do I choose which columns go on which level?
faqs.answer: Match your purification sequence: filtration or phase separation typically goes on the upper level, with SPE chemistry (silica, SCX, aminopropyl, or SAX acetate) on the lower level.

faqs.question: What column formats are compatible?
faqs.answer: Standard 3 mL and 6 mL columns, tabbed or tabless, with no proprietary format required.

faqs.question: How does the recessed plate design help?
faqs.answer: It prevents standard column tabs from colliding with each other when packed into the tight microtiter plate footprint.

faqs.question: Where do purified fractions get collected?
faqs.answer: Into a standard 24-well microtiter plate, or directly into a GreenHouse reaction block for further synthesis.

faqs.question: What is the price of the GreenHouse Work-Up Station in India?
faqs.answer: The price depends on your column configuration and fraction collection format. Contact Inkarp for a quotation once your work-up sequence is confirmed.

faqs.question: Who is the authorized distributor of the GreenHouse Work-Up Station in India?
faqs.answer: Inkarp is the authorized distributor and service provider for the Radleys GreenHouse Work-Up Station in India, providing demonstration, installation, training, AMC, spare parts, and technical support.

The upper level handles the first step, filtration or phase separation, and the lower level handles the second, typically SPE, so the sample flows straight from one into the other. Remove the upper support plate and the same unit runs single-step purification just as easily. A clear acrylic gas cover applies slight positive pressure to speed up flow across all 24 positions, and recessed support plates keep standard column tabs from colliding with each other inside the tight microtiter plate footprint. faqs.question: What is the Storm Heating/Cooling Work Station used for?
faqs.answer: It's a steady-state heating and cooling module, built for reactions that need a stable temperature held over extended periods, from -65°C to +200°C.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Storm and Breeze?
faqs.answer: Storm is insulated with a sophisticated internal fluid path, giving it a wider -65°C to +200°C range with excellent stability for steady-state reactions; Breeze is smaller and uninsulated, giving it a faster response within a narrower -30°C to +165°C range, better suited to crystallisation and changing conditions.

faqs.question: Does Storm provide its own stirring?
faqs.answer: No. Storm contains no integral stirring at all; Tornado or a suitable overhead stirrer is a required part of the system.

faqs.question: How do I build a complete Storm-based system?
faqs.answer: You need Storm itself, a Carousel 6 Plus, Tornado or an overhead stirrer, and a compatible circulator, Huber, Julabo, Lauda, or another leading brand via M24 connections.

faqs.question: Is Storm compatible with my existing circulator?
faqs.answer: If it's Huber, Julabo, or Lauda, yes, directly confirmed; other leading brands are also compatible via M24 connections, with adapters available if needed.

faqs.question: How does Storm fit onto the Carousel 6 Plus?
faqs.answer: Its contoured inner surface accepts the Carousel 6 base precisely, and it locates tool-free.

faqs.question: Does the insulated case protect against burns?
faqs.answer: Yes, alongside reducing heat loss, the insulated outer case specifically prevents burns from contact with hot or cold thermofluid.

faqs.question: Can Storm reduce ice formation at low temperatures?
faqs.answer: Yes, with the optional PTFE insulating plate, which also improves energy efficiency.

faqs.question: What is the price of the Storm Heating/Cooling Work Station in India?
faqs.answer: The price depends on your circulator, stirrer, and Carousel 6 Plus configuration. Contact Inkarp for a quotation once your full system requirements are confirmed.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Breeze and Storm?

faqs.question: Why is the solution temperature range narrower than the thermofluid range?

faqs.question: How do I decide between Breeze and Storm for my application?
faqs.answer: Choose Breeze if your work needs fast, precise temperature changes, like crystallisation studies; choose Storm if your work needs a stable temperature held over an extended period.

faqs.question: Does Breeze provide stirring?
faqs.answer: No. Stirring comes from Tornado or a separate overhead stirrer; Breeze provides temperature control only.

faqs.question: What circulators are compatible with Breeze?
faqs.answer: M16 hose connections work with all popular circulator brands; the Huber Ministat 230 is confirmed as a working example.

faqs.question: How many flasks can Breeze heat or cool at once?

faqs.question: How do I clean or maintain the Breeze aluminium block?

sections.tabSummary: What the thermofluid-to-solution gap actually means
body: The thermofluid running through Breeze and the temperature your solution actually experiences are two different numbers, and the gap between them is real, not a rounding artifact.

Thermofluid reaches -85°C to +235°C, but by the time that heat or cold transfers through the plate to the solution, the achievable range narrows to -30°C to +165°C. What makes Breeze useful despite that narrower range is speed: its small internal volume means there's less thermal mass to bring along for the ride, so it catches up to a new setpoint faster than a larger, insulated system would.

longForm.heroHook: A small internal volume means a fast response. Built to follow a changing temperature, not just hold one.
heroParagraphs: Some reactions need a temperature held steady for hours. Others need it to actually move, precisely, on demand. Breeze is built for the second kind.

Its small internal volume is the whole design decision: less thermal mass to shift means faster response when the temperature setpoint changes, which is exactly what crystallisation studies need. Combine it with a circulator and you get a solution temperature of -30°C to +165°C, from a thermofluid range that runs much wider, -85°C to +235°C.

The 135 mm top plate fits the Carousel 6 Plus, Tornado, Heat-On, and other reaction blocks, heating or cooling multiple flasks up to 5 litres at once. Stirring comes from Tornado or a separate overhead stirrer; Breeze's job is temperature, precisely and quickly.

faqs.question: What makes the Kera-Disk plate different from a standard hotplate surface?

faqs.question: How do I set up precise solution temperature control?

faqs.question: How does the hotplate protect against overheating?

faqs.question: Can I use this hotplate on its own, without a Carousel or GreenHouse accessory?

faqs.question: How do I prevent my stir bar from decoupling at high speed?

sections.tabSummary: What the material and safety engineering actually deliver
body: (Section swapped. Replaces "Performance and Utility Planning".)

The plate's material choice and the safety system are engineered to solve two distinct problems: heating fast without damaging the surface, and protecting the user and sample without slowing anyone down.

The Kera-Disk plate uses aluminium specifically for its heat transfer speed, then adds a wafer-thin ceramic coating on top for chemical and scratch resistance, which is what allows the 35% faster heat-up without sacrificing durability. On the safety side, two independent circuits handle two separate failure modes: one shuts off heating if the set temperature is overshot by 25°C, and a completely separate one shuts off heating if the Pt1000 sensor isn't actually immersed in the liquid, since a dry sensor would otherwise let the plate keep heating well past a safe point.

faqs.question: What is the Findenser Super Air Condenser used for?
faqs.answer: It replaces water-cooled reflux condensers in over 95% of common chemistry applications, using a sealed water jacket instead of a running water supply.

faqs.question: Does Findenser actually contain water inside it?
faqs.answer: Yes, a small amount is permanently sealed between the glass condenser and the aluminium jacket, but no running water supply is ever needed.

faqs.question: How does Findenser compare to a standard air condenser?
faqs.answer: Significantly better with volatile solvents: acetone and DCM boiled completely dry using a standard air condenser, while Findenser retained 95% of the solvent under identical test conditions.

faqs.question: Can Findenser fully replace a water condenser?
faqs.answer: For most solvents, yes, with retention matching a water condenser within experimental error; diethyl ether is a confirmed exception where Findenser isn't recommended.

faqs.question: How do I choose between the Standard and Mini Findenser?
faqs.answer: Match your flask size: Standard covers up to 2 L flasks and 1 L of solvent, while Mini covers up to 250 mL flasks and 125 mL of solvent.

faqs.question: How do I estimate my water savings from switching to Findenser?
faqs.answer: Calculate your current tap flow rate and daily condenser run time; based on UK reference data, a single condenser running 4 hours daily can cost over £500 a year in water alone.

faqs.question: How do I mount Findenser in my fume hood?
faqs.answer: Use conventional laboratory clamps, or a dedicated clamping kit, on the standard ground glass fittings.

faqs.question: Is Findenser compatible with my existing glassware?
faqs.answer: Yes, the ground glass cone and socket fit standard tapered glass sockets, with a choice of 3 joint sizes and PTFE adapters available for broader compatibility.

sections.title: Performance Testing: Findenser vs Air and Water Condensers
sections.tabSummary: What the real comparison data actually shows
body: The test conditions were consistent and specific: 500 mL of solvent in a 1,000 mL flask, run for 16 hours, heated 10°C above each solvent's boiling point.

Against a standard air condenser, the difference was stark with low boiling point solvents. Acetone and DCM boiled completely dry using the air condenser, while Findenser retained 95% of the solvent under identical conditions. With medium boiling point solvents, Findenser still showed improved retention, particularly at larger volumes and higher temperatures. Against a water condenser, retention matched within experimental error across the range tested, with diethyl ether the one confirmed exception where Findenser isn't recommended.

groups.summary: What running water actually costs, and the payback period
groups.description: Running water for a condenser has a real, ongoing cost, even though it's easy to overlook once the tap is running.
body: Based on a single UK tap at 2.5 litres per minute, a water condenser running just 4 hours a day consumes 600 litres daily, working out to roughly £533 a year on that region's water tariff. Running 24 hours a day, that figure rises to over £3,000 annually, for one condenser. Against that basis, Findenser is stated to pay for itself in under 6 months. These are UK reference figures specifically; actual water and disposal costs in India will differ, but the underlying principle, that running water for reflux cooling carries a real recurring cost, applies regardless of region.

faqs.question: What is the Cool-It Insulated Bowl used for?
faqs.answer: It's a cooling bath system for round-bottom flasks, beakers, or test tubes, keeping samples below -70°C significantly longer than plastic bowls or glass dewars.

faqs.question: How much longer does Cool-It hold cold temperatures?
faqs.answer: Up to 5 times longer than a plastic bowl, and twice as long as a glass dewar, both measured as time spent below -70°C.

faqs.question: How do I choose between the Small and Large bowl?
faqs.answer: Match your flask size: Small covers up to 400 mL, Large covers up to 2 L.

faqs.question: How do I fit Cool-It onto my existing hotplate?
faqs.answer: It fits 145 mm top plates natively; for 135 mm plates, including the Carousel Stirring Hotplate, use the optional adapter.

faqs.question: How do I extend cooling time even further?
faqs.answer: Add the optional two-piece lid, which extends cooling time by 20% while also reducing ice formation and preventing spitting from the cooling mixture.

faqs.question: What safety equipment is available for handling cooling mixtures?
faqs.answer: Protective gloves, an apron, and a face shield are all confirmed accessories, alongside clamps, a stand, a digital thermometer, and a scoop.

faqs.question: Does Cool-It protect my stirrer from the cold?
faqs.answer: Yes, its design minimizes frost on the outer surface, which is what protects the stirrer underneath from moisture ingress.

faqs.question: Is Cool-It actually unbreakable, unlike a glass dewar?
faqs.answer: It's described as virtually unbreakable, built from a robust HDPE casing around an insulated foam core, specifically to avoid the fragility of glass dewars.

faqs.question: What is the Mya 4 Reaction Station used for?
faqs.answer: It's a 4-zone automated reaction station used for process development, Design of Experiment work, scale-up, and reaction screening, with each zone independently controlled.

faqs.question: How independent are the four zones really?
faqs.answer: Genuinely independent, with up to 200°C of temperature difference tolerated between adjacent zones, thanks to high-performance insulation.

faqs.question: How do I set up two reactions at very different temperatures side by side?
faqs.answer: Assign each reaction to a separate zone and set its temperature independently; as long as the difference between adjacent zones stays within 200°C, both run without interfering with each other.

faqs.question: How do I cool a reaction without a separate chiller?
faqs.answer: Use the built-in Peltier cooling, which reaches -25°C directly from a standard tap water supply, with no separate chiller unit required.

faqs.question: What vessels does the Mya 4 support?
faqs.answer: Vials and tubes from 2 to 20 mL, round bottom flasks from 25 to 250 mL, and process reaction vessels from 50 to 400 mL.

faqs.question: Can I mix magnetic and overhead stirring across zones?
faqs.answer: Yes. Magnetic stirring is standard on every zone, and the optional Mya Compact overhead stirrer can be used on adjacent zones alongside it.

faqs.question: What's the difference between the Control Pad and PC Control Software?
faqs.answer: The Control Pad is supplied as standard for manual or automated profile operation; the optional PC Control Software adds integration and control of third-party devices like pumps, balances, and pH sensors.

faqs.question: Does the Mya 4 support 24/7 unattended operation?
faqs.answer: Yes, this is a core design intent, with automated profiles and full data-logging supporting unattended runs.

faqs.question: Can the Mya 4 export reaction data?
faqs.answer: Yes, in CSV format, from either the Control Pad or the PC Control Software.

faqs.answer: The price depends on your vessel, stirring, and control configuration. Contact Inkarp for a quotation once your requirements are confirmed.

longForm.heroLead: Running four reactions at once usually means four separate setups, each fighting for bench space and each needing its own cooling. Mya 4 doesn't ask for that. Four fully independent zones sit close together, yet high-performance insulation holds up to a 200°C difference between adjacent zones, so a reflux at 150°C and a cryogenic reaction at -20°C can run side by side without interfering with each other. Cooling comes from Peltier technology and tap water, reaching -25°C with no separate chiller to plumb in. Heating runs from -30°C to +180°C at the block, built for genuine 24/7 unattended operation with full data-logging. Choose magnetic or overhead stirring per zone, mix both across adjacent positions, and run vessels from 2 mL vials up to 400 mL process vessels on the same station.

Mya 4 doesn't ask for that. Four fully independent zones sit close together, yet high-performance insulation holds up to a 200°C difference between adjacent zones, so a reflux at 150°C and a cryogenic reaction at -20°C can run side by side without interfering with each other.

Cooling comes from Peltier technology and tap water, reaching -25°C with no separate chiller to plumb in. Heating runs from -30°C to +180°C at the block, built for genuine 24/7 unattended operation with full data-logging.
Choose magnetic or overhead stirring per zone, mix both across adjacent positions, and run vessels from 2 mL vials up to 400 mL process vessels on the same station.

faqs.question: What is the difference between the Control Pad and the PC Control Software?
faqs.answer: The Control Pad, included as standard, caps experiments at 30 steps of up to 16 hours each with no third-party device control; the PC Software removes that step limit entirely and adds control of up to 16 third-party devices from one screen.

faqs.question: Do I need the PC Control Software?
faqs.answer: Only if your protocols exceed 30 steps or 16 hours per step, or if you need to control external devices like pumps, balances, or sensors alongside the Mya 4.

faqs.question: How do I control a third-party device with the Mya 4?
faqs.answer: Upgrade to the PC Control Software, confirm your device is on the supported list (syringe pumps, pH sensors, peristaltic pumps, and others), and install the relevant device driver.

faqs.question: How do I try the software before buying it?
faqs.answer: Download the free demo version, which simulates device control and lets you build and test schedules without needing the physical Mya 4 connected.

faqs.question: Can I move my PC Software license to a different computer?
faqs.answer: No. Once the license is activated on a PC, it cannot be moved, so confirm your installation PC before activating.

faqs.question: What are the minimum PC requirements for the software?
faqs.answer: Windows 7, 8, 10, or 11, a dual-core 1.9 GHz processor, 2 GB RAM minimum (4 GB recommended), 30 GB hard disk at 5,400 rpm, and Intel HD Graphics.

faqs.question: Does the Control Pad support multi-user operation?
faqs.answer: Yes, this is included as standard, letting different users run experiments independently across the four zones.

faqs.question: Can I export reports from the Control Pad?
faqs.answer: Yes, in CSV format via USB memory stick; the PC Software additionally offers a Report Wizard for RTF reports.

faqs.question: Why does each vessel size get its own insert?
faqs.answer: Dedicated inserts give genuine heat transfer contact for each vessel size, avoiding the imprecise fit that comes from layering mismatched inserts together.

faqs.question: How do I set up overhead stirring for a very small sample volume?
faqs.answer: Use the Carousel 12 Plus reaction tube, which attaches to the Reflux or Manifold head and enables overhead stirring from as low as 5 mL.

faqs.question: How do I choose the right impeller for a scale-up study?
faqs.answer: Use the Retreat Curve Impeller, purpose-built to mirror the mixing conditions of a large-scale reaction during bench-scale work.

faqs.question: What impeller shapes are available?
faqs.answer: Turbine, anchor, U-shape, centrifugal, and flat, with custom impellers available on request.

faqs.question: Can I integrate a PAT probe with the Mya 4?
faqs.answer: Yes, using the dedicated Blaze Metrics probe lid, a 6-neck glass-filled PTFE lid for the 400 mL process vessel, which also works in standard operation without the probe fitted.

faqs.question: What is the difference between glass and PTFE lids?
faqs.answer: PTFE lids offer improved durability and safety, and are strong enough to support heavier probes and accessories, compared to standard glass lids.

faqs.question: Can I refresh a worn Mya 4 top cover without buying a new unit?
faqs.answer: Yes, the silicone top cover is designed as a low-cost way for existing users to rejuvenate a worn cover.

body: Matching a vessel to its insert, and a tube to its diameter, is what actually determines fit and heat transfer performance, not just capacity.

Process vessels run 50 to 400 mL, shaped with straight sides and a dished base specifically to mimic a jacketed reactor's behavior. Round bottom flasks, drawn from the Carousel 6 Plus range, run 25 to 250 mL in standard or wide-neck versions. Vials and tubes span seven confirmed diameters, and every one of them, along with every vessel size, gets its own dedicated aluminium insert rather than a layered stack.

sections.tabSummary: What jacket design and vessel geometry actually deliver
body: Precise temperature control on a jacketed reactor comes down to how well the vessel and jacket actually fit together, not just how powerful the circulator running through them is.

Reactor-Ready Flex's vessel geometry and jacket design are optimised specifically to deliver accurate, consistent control across the full -70°C to +230°C range, rather than relying on raw circulator output to compensate for a loose thermal fit. That range is wider than Radleys' own Mya 4 reaction station line, which makes Flex the choice when a reaction genuinely needs to go colder or hotter than a multi-zone screening station reaches.

sections.title: Jacketed Filter Vessel Engineering
sections.tabSummary: What the flange, seal, and BOV design actually deliver
body: Every part of this vessel's design targets one of two problems: losing temperature control during filtration, or losing product to the equipment itself.

The jacket runs the full height down to the filter plate, not just around the reaction zone, which is what keeps temperature control consistent through both steps. The bottom outlet valve is built with zero dead space specifically to stop material collecting below the filter media, and it's removable for cleaning with a 15 mm bore for easy run-off. The seal between vessel and lid, an FEP-encapsulated O-ring with a PTFE collar on the DN100 flange, is what keeps the whole system leak-tight under those conditions.

faqs.question: What is the Reactor-Ready Duo Lab Reactor used for?
faqs.answer: It's a two-vessel jacketed lab reactor used for parallel synthesis, two-stage reactions, and comparative process optimisation, with each vessel independently exchangeable.

faqs.question: Can the two vessels run at different temperatures?
faqs.answer: Yes, with the double circulator manifold kit (RR121310), each vessel is controlled by its own thermoregulator independently.

faqs.question: Can I run Duo with just one vessel?
faqs.answer: Yes. The single circulator manifold kit (RR121305) ships with a blanking plug specifically for running one vessel only.

faqs.question: How do I order a complete Reactor-Ready Duo system?
faqs.answer: Start with the Core system (RR121300), choose a single or double circulator manifold kit, select your vessel kits and overhead stirrers, then add any circulators, hoses, or AVA automation you need.

faqs.question: How do I set up a two-stage reaction with automated fluid transfer?
faqs.answer: Configure AVA software to control fluid transfer between the two vessels via vacuum or pump, moving reactant from the first stage into the second without manual intervention.

faqs.question: Can the two vessels be different sizes?
faqs.answer: Yes. Vessel volumes from 100 mL to 5 L can be combined on the same Duo system.

faqs.question: What's included in the Core system?
faqs.answer: The stand and base, drip tray, support rods, clamps, hose tidies, stirrer guides and couplings, vessel lids with sealing caps, O-ring seals, and support collars.

faqs.question: Does Duo work with AVA software the same way as other Reactor-Ready systems?
faqs.answer: Yes, with one addition specific to Duo: AVA can control fluid transfer directly between the two vessels, not just log and control individual devices.

sections.title: Single vs Double Circulator Configuration
sections.tabSummary: Choosing shared or independent vessel temperatures
body: The manifold kit you choose decides whether your two vessels share a temperature or run apart, and that choice is worth making deliberately.

The single circulator kit (RR121305) routes one thermoregulator to both vessels, holding them at the same temperature, and includes a blanking plug for running just one vessel when the second isn't needed. The double circulator kit (RR121310) routes two independent thermoregulators to the vessels, letting each run its own temperature entirely. The hose lengths differ between the two kits, 70 cm on the single and 60 cm on the double, reflecting the different manifold layouts.

faqs.question: What is the Reactor-Ready Pilot Lab Reactor used for?
faqs.answer: It's a pilot-scale jacketed lab reactor used to replace multiple reactor setups with one universal system, covering 5 to 50 litres for process development and scale-up work.

faqs.question: Does the Reactor-Ready Pilot work with stirrers I already own?
faqs.answer: Yes. It's compatible with Radleys stirrers and other leading brands, with tool-free, 4-axis alignment.

faqs.question: How do I choose between the vessel sizes?
faqs.answer: Match your target batch volume: 5 to 20 litres follow the standard 1.25:1 plant-scale ratio, while 30, 35, and 50 litre vessels are stated exceptions to that ratio and require the lower support plate.

faqs.question: How do I connect the Pilot framework to my thermoregulator?
faqs.answer: You'll need hoses with an M30x1.5 female connection, or appropriate adapters, since thermoregulator hoses aren't included in the core system.

faqs.question: How do I choose between a glass and PTFE lid?
faqs.answer: Choose glass for standard synthesis work, or PTFE if you're using PAT or test probes, since it supports up to 8 ports and is more robust than glass.

faqs.question: Does the Reactor-Ready Pilot include a drip tray?
faqs.answer: No. Drip trays are ordered separately, available in 7, 22, 45, and 55 litre capacities.

faqs.question: What is the V4 zero dead space stopcock?
faqs.answer: A drain stopcock design specifically built to prevent the over-tightening that commonly causes glass breakage on standard stopcocks.

faqs.question: Do the 30, 35, and 50 litre vessels need any additional support?
faqs.answer: Yes, they specifically require the lower support plate, which adjusts without tools.

faqs.question: Can the Reactor-Ready Pilot handle multiple vessel sizes on one framework?
faqs.answer: Yes. One compact framework accepts all vessel sizes from 5 to 50 litres, with vessel exchange in minutes.

faqs.question: What is the price of the Reactor-Ready Pilot Lab Reactor in India?
faqs.answer: The price depends on your vessel size, lid type, and framework configuration. Contact Inkarp for a quotation once your requirements are confirmed.

faqs.answer: Inkarp is the authorized distributor and service provider for the Radleys Reactor-Ready Pilot Lab Reactor in India, providing demonstration, installation, training, AMC, spare parts, and technical support.

faqs.question: What are Custom Jacketed Reaction Systems used for?
faqs.answer: They're bespoke jacketed reaction systems designed and built for requirements a standard configuration can't meet, covering vessels, multi-reactor rigs, fermenters, bioreactors, and photoreactors from 100 mL to 30 litres.

faqs.question: When should I choose custom instead of a standard Reactor-Ready system?
faqs.answer: Choose custom when your process needs a non-standard vessel geometry, special features like optical windows or split jackets, a system type like a fermenter or bioreactor, or a temperature and connection combination the standard range doesn't cover.

faqs.question: How do I scope a custom jacketed reaction system?
faqs.answer: Describe your volume, temperature, vessel geometry, and any special features or system-level requirements to Inkarp, who will work with Radleys' design team to confirm the build.

faqs.question: How do I decide between Reactor-Ready and traditional connections?
faqs.answer: Choose Reactor-Ready connections if you need to reach up to 230°C, or traditional connections if 200°C covers your process and a conventional setup is preferred.

faqs.question: What is the maximum volume for a custom system?
faqs.answer: 100 mL to 30 litres for single jacketed vessels; vacuum jacketed vessels are available up to 10 litres.

faqs.question: Can I get an air-powered stirrer for a hazardous atmosphere?
faqs.answer: Yes. Air-powered stirring is a confirmed option specifically for applications where an electrical motor poses an ignition risk.

faqs.question: Does Radleys build fermenters and bioreactors, not just standard reactors?
faqs.answer: Yes, this is confirmed within the scope of Custom Jacketed Reaction Systems, alongside photoreactors and multi-reactor parallel synthesis rigs.

faqs.question: Is training included with a custom system?
faqs.answer: Yes, installation and training are part of the confirmed scope of services.

faqs.question: What is the price of Custom Jacketed Reaction Systems in India?
faqs.answer: Pricing is fully specification-dependent. Contact Inkarp to scope your requirements and receive a custom quotation.

faqs.question: Who is the authorized distributor of Custom Jacketed Reaction Systems in India?
faqs.answer: Inkarp is the authorized distributor and service provider for Radleys Custom Jacketed Reaction Systems in India, providing demonstration, installation, training, AMC, spare parts, and technical support.

This is where Radleys' own design engineers and scientific glassblowers take over, with over 50 years of experience building for industrial and academic research facilities worldwide. The scope runs from a small benchtop reactor to a complex multi-vessel parallel rig, 100 mL to 30 litres, built to your specification and budget. Cylindrical or spherical vessels, conical or dish or hemispherical bottoms, optical windows, split jackets, fixed or removable filters. Fermenters, bioreactors, photoreactors, distillation assemblies. Electrical or air-powered stirring, for atmospheres where an electrical motor isn't an option. Connection type genuinely changes what's achievable: Reactor-Ready connections reach 230°C; traditional connections cap at 200°C.

faqs.question: What is the Carousel 12 Plus Reaction Station used for?
faqs.answer: It's a patented 12-position station that simultaneously heats, stirs, and refluxes samples under an inert atmosphere, used for parallel reaction screening and solid supported reagent synthesis.

faqs.question: Do you offer a demo of the Carousel 12 Plus?
faqs.answer: Yes, Inkarp can arrange a demonstration on your own application.

faqs.question: How can I work with smaller volumes in my Carousel 12 Plus?
faqs.answer: Use reduced-volume tubes, which bring the reaction volume down to 1 to 5 mL, compared to the standard 5 to 20 mL tubes.

faqs.question: How do I purge my tubes for an inert atmosphere?
faqs.answer: Connect the central gas inlet via flexible tubing to a two-way stopcock, then alternate between vacuum and inert gas to quickly clear unwanted air from all 12 tubes.

faqs.question: How do I set up sub-ambient cooling for my reactions?
faqs.answer: Add the optional HDPE cooling reservoir, which brings the achievable temperature down to -78°C; the base configuration alone doesn't reach sub-ambient temperatures.

faqs.question: Does every tube really stir at the same speed?
faqs.answer: Yes. The patented design positions every tube and its stir bar equidistant from the hotplate's central magnet specifically to keep stirring speed identical across all 12 positions.

faqs.question: What tubing do I need for the reflux/inerting head?
faqs.answer: This is confirmed directly by Inkarp based on your specific installation.

faqs.question: How accurate is the temperature control?
faqs.answer: ±1°C, using the hotplate's digital control or an optional Pt1000 sensor for block or solution temperature.

faqs.question: Can I add reagents without breaking the inert atmosphere?
faqs.answer: Yes, through the replaceable Suba-Seal septum in each Easy-On cap, using a syringe.

longForm.heroLead: Run 12 reactions on one stirring hotplate and it's easy for stirring speed to drift between positions, some tubes closer to the magnet than others. Carousel 12 Plus doesn't let that happen. Every tube and its stir bar sit equidistant from the hotplate's central magnet, patented specifically to keep stirring identical across all 12 positions, from 100 to 1,400 rpm. Heating reaches 180°C sustained, 220°C briefly, held to ±1°C, with the option to control block or solution temperature directly. Reflux runs through a water-cooled head that removes with the tubes still attached, and the whole system operates under a genuine inert atmosphere: individual gas-tight caps, a radial distribution system, and a two-way stopcock to purge each tube in seconds.

sections.title: Uniform Heating, Stirring and Reflux Across 12 Positions
sections.tabSummary: What actually makes all 12 tubes behave identically
body: Twelve independent reactions running identically depends on three things behaving the same way across every position, not just one.

Stirring is uniform because of geometry: every tube and its stir bar sit equidistant from the hotplate's central magnet, which is the actual mechanism, not a side effect of the circular layout. Heating and cooling are uniform because the reaction tubes themselves are precision engineered from heavy-walled borosilicate glass specifically to maximise and equalize heat transfer. Reflux stays uniform because the water-cooled head creates the same cooling zone in the upper part of every tube simultaneously.

longForm.heroHook: 12 tubes, stirred at exactly the same speed. Patented, not left to chance.
heroParagraphs: Run 12 reactions on one stirring hotplate and it's easy for stirring speed to drift between positions, some tubes closer to the magnet than others. Carousel 12 Plus doesn't let that happen.

Every tube and its stir bar sit equidistant from the hotplate's central magnet, patented specifically to keep stirring identical across all 12 positions, from 100 to 1,400 rpm. Heating reaches 180°C sustained, 220°C briefly, held to ±1°C, with the option to control block or solution temperature directly.

Reflux runs through a water-cooled head that removes with the tubes still attached, and the whole system operates under a genuine inert atmosphere: individual gas-tight caps, a radial distribution system, and a two-way stopcock to purge each tube in seconds.

faqs.question: What is the Cooled Carousel 12 Plus Reaction Station used for?
faqs.answer: It's a cooling reservoir for parallel low-temperature synthesis, running up to 12 stirred reactions simultaneously down to -78°C.

faqs.question: What cooling mixtures does it use?
faqs.answer: A range of freezing mixtures, including dry ice/acetone, controlled manually from ambient down to -78°C.

faqs.question: How does the stirrer survive at -78°C?
faqs.answer: The insulated foam core is specifically built to protect the stirrer mechanism from freezing while holding the low temperature over long periods.

faqs.question: How do I switch between heating and cooling for the same reactions?
faqs.answer: Transfer the removable reflux/inerting head, with the tubes still attached, from the heated Carousel 12 Plus base to the Cooled Carousel 12 Plus reservoir, or back again.

faqs.question: Do I need a whole new system if I already own a standard Carousel 12 Plus?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily. The reservoir shares tubes, caps, and the hotplate with the standard unit, so confirm with Inkarp whether the reservoir alone covers your needs.

faqs.question: How do I choose the right cooling mixture for my target temperature?
faqs.answer: Match the mixture to how cold you need to go; dry ice/acetone reaches the full range down to -78°C, and Inkarp can confirm alternatives for less extreme temperatures.

faqs.question: Does the lid affect visibility of the reaction?
faqs.answer: No, it improves it. The HDPE lid minimizes ice formation on the tubes, keeping the contents visible, and prevents spitting from the cooling mixture.

faqs.question: Is the reservoir durable for routine lab use?
faqs.answer: Yes, the HDPE construction is stated as virtually unbreakable.

faqs.question: What is the Carousel Work-Up Station used for?
faqs.answer: It's a 12-position parallel work-up station used for filtration, phase separation, liquid/liquid extraction, and SPE, reducing post-synthesis processing bottlenecks.

faqs.question: Why is vacuum-free design an advantage here?
faqs.answer: It removes taps, valves, and drip needles from the process entirely, which simplifies cleaning, cuts consumable costs, and specifically prevents columns from drying out the way a vacuum manifold can.

faqs.question: How do I speed up a work-up beyond gravity flow?
faqs.answer: Add the SpeediFlow Booster, a hand-held pressuriser that individually controls flow through a specific column, with a safety relief valve venting at 6 to 8 psi.

faqs.question: How do I set up a sequential, multi-step work-up?
faqs.answer: Add the optional third rack, stacked above the standard two-rack configuration, for staged processing.

faqs.question: How do I add a second rack to the station?
faqs.answer: Pull out the spring-loaded knob and rotate it 90 degrees to lock the second rack into place.

faqs.question: What column chemistries are available?
faqs.answer: 20 µm filtration, phase separation, silica, SCX, aminopropyl, and SAX acetate, all in the standard 70 mL format.

faqs.question: Can I use non-standard column sizes with SpeediFlow?
faqs.answer: Yes, using the optional SpeediFlow adapters, which cover 15, 25, 70, and 150 mL columns, plus the Whatman AutoCup.

faqs.question: Does this station work with my existing Carousel Reaction Tubes?
faqs.answer: Yes, the same Carousel Reaction Tubes used in Carousel 12 Plus and Cooled Carousel 12 Plus fit the lower collection rack directly.

faqs.question: Is the SpeediFlow Booster safe from over-pressurisation?
faqs.answer: Yes, it includes a safety relief valve that vents automatically at 6 to 8 psi.

faqs.question: What is the price of the Carousel Work-Up Station in India?
faqs.answer: The price depends on your rack configuration and column chemistry needs. Contact Inkarp for a quotation once your work-up technique is confirmed.

faqs.question: Who is the authorized distributor of the Carousel Work-Up Station in India?
faqs.answer: Inkarp is the authorized distributor and service provider for the Radleys Carousel Work-Up Station in India, providing demonstration, installation, training, AMC, spare parts, and technical support.

body: Removing the vacuum manifold from a work-up station changes more than the assembly process.

faqs.question: What is the Carousel 6 Plus Reaction Station used for?
faqs.answer: It's a 6-position station that heats, stirs, and refluxes standard round bottom flasks simultaneously under an inert atmosphere, used for parallel synthesis and azeotropic distillation.

faqs.question: How fast does it heat?
faqs.answer: It boils six flasks of water in under 25 minutes, all together, ambient to 180°C.

faqs.question: How do I choose the right flask size?
faqs.answer: Match your reaction volume to one of seven confirmed sizes, 5 to 250 mL, with 1- or 2-sidearm versions where needed; a reducing insert lets a smaller flask sit in a larger well.

faqs.question: Can I remove a flask mid-run without disturbing the setup?
faqs.answer: Yes. The removable aluminium reflux insert maintains heat transfer, and a built-in spring clip retains the flask once the insert is out.

faqs.question: How do I set up azeotropic distillation?
faqs.answer: Use the 250 mL Dean-Stark azeotropic flask option, designed specifically for water removal during synthesis.

faqs.question: How do I extend the base unit for viscous samples or extended temperature control?
faqs.answer: Add the Tornado module for powerful stirring of viscous samples, or Breeze or Storm for controlled heating and cooling beyond the base configuration.

faqs.question: Can I run sub-ambient reactions on the Carousel 6 Plus?
faqs.answer: Yes, with the Cooled Carousel 6 option, performing up to six cooled reactions to -78°C.

faqs.question: What protects the user from the hot aluminium base?
faqs.answer: A PTFE heat protection ring, specifically included to guard against accidental contact.

faqs.question: What is the temperature accuracy?
faqs.answer: The source states ±1°C for heating performance and ±0.5°C under temperature control; Inkarp can confirm which applies to your specific configuration.

faqs.question: What is the price of the Carousel 6 Plus Reaction Station in India?
faqs.answer: The price depends on your flask configuration and any modular add-ons. Contact Inkarp for a quotation once your requirements are confirmed.

faqs.question: Who is the authorized distributor of the Carousel 6 Plus Reaction Station in India?

faqs.question: Does Tornado work as a standalone system?

faqs.question: How viscous a sample can Tornado handle?

faqs.question: How do I choose between the 1:1 and 2:1 drive ratio?
faqs.answer: Use 1:1 for thin, free-flowing liquids at higher speed, or 2:1 when you need more torque for viscous samples, especially with a lower-powered stirrer.

faqs.question: How do I select the right stirrer shape for my sample?

faqs.question: Can I use my existing overhead stirrer with Tornado?

faqs.question: Does adding Tornado increase my bench footprint?

faqs.question: Is Tornado safe to operate around rotating parts?
faqs.answer: Yes, an integral polycarbonate guard prevents accidental contact with the rotating stirrer components.

faqs.question: Can Tornado run under an inert atmosphere?
faqs.answer: Yes, the sealed Pinch-Grip stirrer shaft mechanism supports operation under inert atmosphere.

faqs.question: How does solvent trapping work?
faqs.answer: The enclosed chamber routes evaporating solvent through a high-performance glass condenser, which captures and collects it instead of releasing it into the room.

faqs.question: Do I need to buy a whole new GreenHouse system?

faqs.question: Can I evaporate GreenHouse reaction tubes without moving them?
faqs.answer: Yes. They evaporate directly in the standard GreenHouse reaction block, without needing to load or reload it.

faqs.question: Is the evaporation rate controllable?
faqs.answer: Yes, through digital heating control from the shared hotplate, and an optional flowmeter for precise inert gas flow control.

body: Two design decisions work together here: removing the vacuum, and containing the vapor that removal would otherwise release.

faqs.question: What is the GreenHouse Work-Up Station used for?
faqs.answer: It's a 24-position parallel purification station, using a stacked two-level column design to run sequential purification, like filtration into SPE, in a single pass.

faqs.question: How does sequential purification work without moving the sample?
faqs.answer: The upper column level handles the first step, and whatever passes through flows directly into the lower level's column for the second step, with no manual transfer in between.

faqs.question: Can I use this for single-step purification too?
faqs.answer: Yes, remove the upper support plate and the unit runs as a standard single-level purification station.

faqs.question: How do I speed up flow across all 24 positions?
faqs.answer: Use the clear acrylic gas cover, which applies slight positive pressure to boost flow rate across the whole unit at once.

faqs.question: How do I choose which columns go on which level?
faqs.answer: Match your purification sequence: filtration or phase separation typically goes on the upper level, with SPE chemistry (silica, SCX, aminopropyl, or SAX acetate) on the lower level.

faqs.question: What column formats are compatible?
faqs.answer: Standard 3 mL and 6 mL columns, tabbed or tabless, with no proprietary format required.

faqs.question: How does the recessed plate design help?
faqs.answer: It prevents standard column tabs from colliding with each other when packed into the tight microtiter plate footprint.

faqs.question: Where do purified fractions get collected?
faqs.answer: Into a standard 24-well microtiter plate, or directly into a GreenHouse reaction block for further synthesis.

faqs.question: What is the price of the GreenHouse Work-Up Station in India?

longForm.heroHook: Two purification steps, one pass. Filter straight into SPE below it, no plate swap needed.
heroParagraphs: Sequential purification usually means finishing one step, physically moving the sample, then starting the next. This station stacks both steps in the same unit instead.

The upper level handles the first step, filtration or phase separation, and the lower level handles the second, typically SPE, so the sample flows straight from one into the other. Remove the upper support plate and the same unit runs single-step purification just as easily.

A clear acrylic gas cover applies slight positive pressure to speed up flow across all 24 positions, and recessed support plates keep standard column tabs from colliding with each other inside the tight microtiter plate footprint. Collect fractions into a standard 24-well plate, or straight into a GreenHouse reaction block.

faqs.question: What is the Storm Heating/Cooling Work Station used for?
faqs.answer: It's a steady-state heating and cooling module, built for reactions that need a stable temperature held over extended periods, from -65°C to +200°C.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Storm and Breeze?
faqs.answer: Storm is insulated with a sophisticated internal fluid path, giving it a wider -65°C to +200°C range with excellent stability for steady-state reactions; Breeze is smaller and uninsulated, giving it a faster response within a narrower -30°C to +165°C range, better suited to crystallisation and changing conditions.

faqs.question: Does Storm provide its own stirring?
faqs.answer: No. Storm contains no integral stirring at all; Tornado or a suitable overhead stirrer is a required part of the system.

faqs.question: How do I build a complete Storm-based system?
faqs.answer: You need Storm itself, a Carousel 6 Plus, Tornado or an overhead stirrer, and a compatible circulator, Huber, Julabo, Lauda, or another leading brand via M24 connections.

faqs.question: Is Storm compatible with my existing circulator?
faqs.answer: If it's Huber, Julabo, or Lauda, yes, directly confirmed; other leading brands are also compatible via M24 connections, with adapters available if needed.

faqs.question: How does Storm fit onto the Carousel 6 Plus?
faqs.answer: Its contoured inner surface accepts the Carousel 6 base precisely, and it locates tool-free.

faqs.question: Does the insulated case protect against burns?
faqs.answer: Yes, alongside reducing heat loss, the insulated outer case specifically prevents burns from contact with hot or cold thermofluid.

faqs.question: Can Storm reduce ice formation at low temperatures?
faqs.answer: Yes, with the optional PTFE insulating plate, which also improves energy efficiency.

faqs.question: What is the price of the Storm Heating/Cooling Work Station in India?
faqs.answer: The price depends on your circulator, stirrer, and Carousel 6 Plus configuration. Contact Inkarp for a quotation once your full system requirements are confirmed.

body: Holding a temperature steady across hours, not just reaching it once, is what Storm's internal design is actually built around.

faqs.question: What is the Breeze™ Heating/Cooling Work Station used for?
faqs.answer: It's an add-on heating and cooling module for the Carousel 6 Plus and Tornado, used for applications needing fast, precise solution temperature control, such as crystallisation studies.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Breeze and Storm?
faqs.answer: Breeze is smaller and uninsulated, giving it a faster response time within a -30°C to +165°C solution range; Storm is insulated with a more sophisticated fluid path, giving it a wider -65°C to +200°C range with excellent stability for steady-state reactions.

faqs.question: Why is the solution temperature range narrower than the thermofluid range?
faqs.answer: Heat transfer from the thermofluid to the solution loses some range in the process; the thermofluid runs -85°C to +235°C, while the achievable solution temperature is -30°C to +165°C.

faqs.question: How do I decide between Breeze and Storm for my application?
faqs.answer: Choose Breeze if your work needs fast, precise temperature changes, like crystallisation studies; choose Storm if your work needs a stable temperature held over an extended period.

faqs.question: What reaction blocks does Breeze work with?
faqs.answer: The Carousel 6 Plus, Tornado, Heat-On, and other reaction blocks compatible with the 135 mm top plate.

faqs.question: Does Breeze provide stirring?
faqs.answer: No. Stirring comes from Tornado or a separate overhead stirrer; Breeze provides temperature control only.

faqs.question: What circulators are compatible with Breeze?
faqs.answer: M16 hose connections work with all popular circulator brands; the Huber Ministat 230 is confirmed as a working example.

faqs.question: How many flasks can Breeze heat or cool at once?
faqs.answer: Multiple or individual flasks, up to 5 litres total capacity; exact simultaneous count is confirmed by Inkarp based on flask size.

faqs.question: How do I clean or maintain the Breeze aluminium block?
faqs.answer: The block unscrews easily from the drip tray for cleaning or servicing.

faqs.question: What is the price of the Breeze™ Heating/Cooling Work Station in India?
faqs.answer: The price depends on your reaction block and circulator configuration. Contact Inkarp for a quotation once your requirements are confirmed.

faqs.answer: Inkarp is the authorized distributor and service provider for the Radleys Breeze™ Heating/Cooling Work Station in India, providing demonstration, installation, training, AMC, spare parts, and technical support.

sections.tabSummary: What the thermofluid-to-solution gap actually means
body: The thermofluid running through Breeze and the temperature your solution actually experiences are two different numbers, and the gap between them is real, not a rounding artifact.

Thermofluid reaches -85°C to +235°C, but by the time that heat or cold transfers through the plate to the solution, the achievable range narrows to -30°C to +165°C. What makes Breeze useful despite that narrower range is speed: its small internal volume means there's less thermal mass to bring along for the ride, so it catches up to a new setpoint faster than a larger, insulated system would.

faqs.answer: Add additional Data Hubs, which expand either platform up to a total of 16 controlled devices.

faqs.question: Can I try AVA before buying it?

faqs.question: Does AVA support unattended overnight reactions?
