sections.tabSummary: What the material and safety engineering actually deliver
body: (Section swapped. Replaces "Performance and Utility Planning".)

The plate's material choice and the safety system are engineered to solve two distinct problems: heating fast without damaging the surface, and protecting the user and sample without slowing anyone down.

The Kera-Disk plate uses aluminium specifically for its heat transfer speed, then adds a wafer-thin ceramic coating on top for chemical and scratch resistance, which is what allows the 35% faster heat-up without sacrificing durability. On the safety side, two independent circuits handle two separate failure modes: one shuts off heating if the set temperature is overshot by 25°C, and a completely separate one shuts off heating if the Pt1000 sensor isn't actually immersed in the liquid, since a dry sensor would otherwise let the plate keep heating well past a safe point.

faqs.question: What is the Findenser Super Air Condenser used for?
faqs.answer: It replaces water-cooled reflux condensers in over 95% of common chemistry applications, using a sealed water jacket instead of a running water supply.

faqs.question: Does Findenser actually contain water inside it?
faqs.answer: Yes, a small amount is permanently sealed between the glass condenser and the aluminium jacket, but no running water supply is ever needed.

faqs.question: How does Findenser compare to a standard air condenser?
faqs.answer: Significantly better with volatile solvents: acetone and DCM boiled completely dry using a standard air condenser, while Findenser retained 95% of the solvent under identical test conditions.

faqs.question: Can Findenser fully replace a water condenser?
faqs.answer: For most solvents, yes, with retention matching a water condenser within experimental error; diethyl ether is a confirmed exception where Findenser isn't recommended.

faqs.question: How do I choose between the Standard and Mini Findenser?
faqs.answer: Match your flask size: Standard covers up to 2 L flasks and 1 L of solvent, while Mini covers up to 250 mL flasks and 125 mL of solvent.

faqs.question: How do I estimate my water savings from switching to Findenser?
faqs.answer: Calculate your current tap flow rate and daily condenser run time; based on UK reference data, a single condenser running 4 hours daily can cost over £500 a year in water alone.

faqs.question: How do I mount Findenser in my fume hood?
faqs.answer: Use conventional laboratory clamps, or a dedicated clamping kit, on the standard ground glass fittings.

faqs.question: Is Findenser compatible with my existing glassware?
faqs.answer: Yes, the ground glass cone and socket fit standard tapered glass sockets, with a choice of 3 joint sizes and PTFE adapters available for broader compatibility.

body: The test conditions were consistent and specific: 500 mL of solvent in a 1,000 mL flask, run for 16 hours, heated 10°C above each solvent's boiling point.

Against a standard air condenser, the difference was stark with low boiling point solvents. Acetone and DCM boiled completely dry using the air condenser, while Findenser retained 95% of the solvent under identical conditions. With medium boiling point solvents, Findenser still showed improved retention, particularly at larger volumes and higher temperatures. Against a water condenser, retention matched within experimental error across the range tested, with diethyl ether the one confirmed exception where Findenser isn't recommended.

body: Based on a single UK tap at 2.5 litres per minute, a water condenser running just 4 hours a day consumes 600 litres daily, working out to roughly £533 a year on that region's water tariff. Running 24 hours a day, that figure rises to over £3,000 annually, for one condenser. Against that basis, Findenser is stated to pay for itself in under 6 months. These are UK reference figures specifically; actual water and disposal costs in India will differ, but the underlying principle, that running water for reflux cooling carries a real recurring cost, applies regardless of region.

longForm.heroHook: A standard air condenser lets acetone or DCM boil dry. Findenser keeps 95% of the solvent.
heroParagraphs: Air condensers are the obvious waterless choice, until the solvent is volatile enough to boil straight past them. Findenser is built for exactly that gap.

Under identical 16-hour reflux conditions, a standard air condenser let acetone and DCM boil completely dry. Findenser retained 95% of the solvent under the same test. Against a water condenser, it matched retention within experimental error across most solvents, with one confirmed exception: diethyl ether isn't recommended for use with Findenser.

No running water means no flooding risk, no water purchase or disposal cost, and no need to keep the setup near a water source at all. A patented sealed design, glass condenser plus a finned aluminium jacket, replaces water-cooled condensers in over 95% of common chemistry applications.

It keeps samples below -70°C up to five times longer than a plastic bowl, and twice as long as a glass dewar, in a virtually unbreakable HDPE casing wrapped around a high-quality insulated foam core. The optional two-piece lid extends that another 20%, while keeping the flask visible and stopping the cooling mixture from spitting. It fits standard stirring hotplates, 145 mm natively with an adapter for 135 mm plates, sits securely enough to prevent accidental knocks, and protects your stirrer from the moisture ingress that frost on an exposed bowl would otherwise cause.

faqs.question: What is the StarFish Work Station used for?
faqs.answer: It's a modular heating and stirring system for synthesis, distillation, and extraction, running individual or parallel vessels on your existing hotplate.

faqs.question: What's the difference between MonoBlocks and PolyBlocks?
faqs.answer: MonoBlocks hold multiple wells of the same size for uniform parallel runs; PolyBlocks use small mixable segments to accommodate any combination of vessel sizes.

faqs.question: Can I use the gas or water manifold without the rest of StarFish?
faqs.answer: Yes, both manifolds are designed to work independently of the StarFish blocks and clamps.

faqs.question: How do I set up multiple condensers with one water source?
faqs.answer: Use the Water Manifold, which distributes coolant from a single source to up to 5 condensers and recombines it to one outlet pipe, using two manifolds per set-up.

faqs.question: How does the clamp actually hold glassware in place?
faqs.answer: The lower clamp's rubber strap grips the flask neck for lifting, while the upper clamp's Velcro strap lets a condenser slide through it while still being safely restrained.

faqs.question: Can I use glassware I already own with StarFish?
faqs.answer: Yes, StarFish accommodates glassware from Carousel 12 Plus, Carousel 6 Plus, and GreenHouse directly, alongside standard laboratory glassware.

faqs.question: What hotplate does StarFish work with?
faqs.answer: All leading stirring hotplate brands, with base plates available for round or square top plates.

faqs.question: How hot can the blocks go?
faqs.answer: Up to 260°C, using chemical-resistant anodised aluminium construction.

faqs.question: What is the price of the StarFish Work Station in India?
faqs.answer: The price depends on your block type, manifold, and clamp configuration. Contact Inkarp for a quotation once your requirements are confirmed.

body: Four channels run up to three experiments at once, speeding up method development by testing different immobilization chemistries or regeneration schemes side by side.

Drift sits at an industry-leading 0.1 μRIU/min with noise as low as 0.05 μRIU rms, and baseline stabilizes 2 to 3x faster than competing systems thanks to streamlined fluidics.

Crude samples run directly, whole cells, viruses, lysates, serum, and aggregates, without a purification step first.

A full range of standard sensor chips ships alongside the system: carboxymethyl dextran, planar PEG/carboxyl, nickel NTA, hydrophobic planar alkyl, streptavidin/NeutrAvidin, protein A, and plain gold for custom chemistry.
No service contract is required to keep the system running. Accessible parts mean routine maintenance happens in-house, though a service contract remains available for labs that prefer it.

faqs.question: What is the Reichert 3SPR used for?
faqs.answer: It's a three-channel surface plasmon resonance system for real-time, label-free measurement of biomolecular binding kinetics and affinity, built to balance throughput and cost.

faqs.question: How sensitive is the Reichert 3SPR?
faqs.answer: It detects interactions with low molecular weight compounds under 100 Da, across an affinity range from 1 mM to 1 pM.

faqs.question: How much does the Reichert 3SPR save compared to competitors?
faqs.answer: It typically costs 20% less than a lower-throughput system from the leading competitor, and a typical lab saves around $20,000 per year per system, roughly $100,000 over five years.

faqs.question: Can the Reichert 3SPR run crude, unpurified samples?
faqs.answer: Yes, it runs whole cells, viruses, lysates, serum, and aggregates directly, without a purification step first.

faqs.question: How long does a tubing change take?
faqs.answer: About five minutes, using standard, off-the-shelf HPLC fittings, without needing a service call.

faqs.question: Do the flow cells need to be replaced regularly?

faqs.question: Is a service contract required?

faqs.question: What sensor chips are available?

longForm.heroHook: Three channels. Two experiments at once. The sweet spot between throughput and cost.
longForm.heroLead: Two channels can feel limiting. Four can feel like paying for capacity you don't need. Reichert 3SPR sits right in the middle: immobilize different molecules on two channels while a third stays as reference, maximizing data output without the price tag of a full four-channel system, all while costing 20% less than a lower-throughput system from the leading competitor. Sensitivity reaches below 100 Da, affinity measurement spans 1 mM to 1 pM, drift sits at an industry-leading 0.1 μRIU/min, and the same open, self-serviceable design that defines the Reichert line keeps ongoing costs low too.

sections.description: Reichert 3SPR product information: channel flexibility, sensitivity specs, and open-system serviceability.
body: Three channels run up to two experiments at once, letting different immobilization chemistries or regeneration schemes get tested in parallel instead of one after another.

Sensitivity reaches low molecular weight compounds under 100 Da, supporting high-quality kinetic analysis, affinity measurements from 1 mM to 1 pM, precise thermodynamic parameter determination, and accurate concentration analysis.
Drift sits at an industry-leading 0.1 μRIU/min with noise as low as 0.05 μRIU rms, and baseline stabilizes 2 to 3x faster than competing systems thanks to streamlined fluidics.
Sample capacity reaches up to 768 samples per run.
The system is fully open: tubing changes in five minutes using standard, off-the-shelf HPLC fittings, and flow cells clean or swap by hand rather than requiring a cartridge replacement.
Crude samples run directly, whole cells, viruses, lysates, serum, and aggregates, without a purification step first.

A full range of standard sensor chips ships alongside the system: carboxymethyl dextran, planar PEG/carboxyl, nickel NTA, hydrophobic planar alkyl, streptavidin/NeutrAvidin, protein A, and plain gold for custom chemistry.
No service contract is required to keep the system running. Accessible parts mean routine maintenance happens in-house, though a service contract remains available for labs that prefer it.

faqs.question: What is a safety barrel for in-plant use?
faqs.answer: It's a stainless steel container built primarily for storing bigger volumes of flammable liquid, with filling and metering available as a secondary capability, and removable flame traps and a pressure control valve for protection.

faqs.question: Can this barrel be used for off-site transport?
faqs.answer: No. This product is certified for in-plant use only; off-site transport requires a separately certified transportation barrel.

faqs.question: Which sizes are stackable?
faqs.answer: The 25 and 50-liter barrels specifically. This isn't stated for the 10-liter size or for the 100 and 200-liter sizes.

faqs.question: What is a safety collection barrel?
faqs.answer: A different barrel purpose entirely, built to receive liquid, such as waste or a contained spill, using a centered 2-inch plug rather than a dispensing mechanism.

faqs.question: How do I decide between a dispensing barrel and a collection barrel?
faqs.answer: Choose a dispensing barrel, with a screw cap, tap, or metering device, if you're storing and controlling liquid coming out; choose a collection barrel if you're receiving liquid, such as for waste or spill containment.

faqs.question: How do I find the exact order number for my requirement?
faqs.answer: Confirm your purpose (dispensing or collection), your size, and whether you need a content indicator; for example, a 25-liter barrel with a self-closing tap and content indicator is order number 25ZI.

faqs.question: Are 100 and 200-liter barrels available?
faqs.answer: Yes, across all barrel types, though specific order numbers for these sizes are confirmed directly by Inkarp rather than listed in the standard order table.

faqs.question: What is a content indicator?
faqs.answer: A feature that shows the fill level without needing to open the barrel, available on tap, metering device, and collection variants.

faqs.question: Can the flame traps be serviced?
faqs.answer: Yes. They're removable, supporting inspection and maintenance rather than replacing the entire barrel.

longForm.heroLead: Handling a flammable liquid safely comes down to two failure points: an open flame reaching the vapor inside, or pressure building until the can fails. This can is built against both. A flame trap stops external flame from reaching what's inside. A pressure control valve vents from around 0.3 bar, before pressure ever becomes a problem. The body is stainless steel, 0.6 mm thick, with PTFE gaskets that hold up against a wide range of chemicals. The handhold is powder-coated aluminum, shaped for a secure grip during pouring or metering. Choose a self-closing metering device for controlled dispensing, or a screw cap for straightforward access. Available in 1, 2, or 5 liters, polished or unpolished. This can is built for in-plant use. If you need to transport flammable liquid, that requires a separately certified product.

Two safety mechanisms work independently. The flame trap keeps external flame from reaching the liquid inside; the pressure control valve, venting from around 0.3 bar, keeps internal pressure from building to a dangerous point.
The materials are chosen for chemical exposure, not just strength. Stainless steel construction at 0.6 mm, with PTFE gaskets specifically for resistance across a wide range of chemicals.
Handling is built into the design. A powder-coated aluminum handhold, shaped ergonomically, supports safe pouring and metering rather than an afterthought grip.
Two dispensing types serve two different workflows. A self-closing metering device suits controlled, repeated dispensing; a screw cap suits straightforward fill-and-pour access.
Sizing is confirmed and specific. 1, 2, and 5-liter cans, each available in either dispensing type, with real order numbers for each combination.
A related product exists for wet-storage materials. Moistener cans, in 1 and 2 liters, are built for substances that need to be kept moistened for safe storage.

body: The technical specifications of the Safety Cans for In-Plant Use include stainless steel construction, a 0.3 bar pressure valve, and confirmed sizing from 1 to 5 liters.
A safety can earns its name from what happens when something goes wrong outside it, or builds up inside it.

The flame trap sits between the outside world and the liquid inside, physically stopping an open flame from reaching the vapor that could ignite. The pressure control valve handles the opposite risk: as pressure inside the can rises, it vents automatically from around 0.3 bar, before that pressure becomes a structural or safety problem. The two mechanisms don't depend on each other, which is what makes the can safe against both failure modes independently.

faqs.question: What is a safety funnel?
faqs.answer: It's a filling accessory that screws onto or plugs into a container, built with a flame trap, overfill protection, and a closure head to reduce vapor emission during filling of flammable liquids.

faqs.question: What is overfill protection?
faqs.answer: A built-in mechanism that stops filling before the container's capacity is exceeded, standard on every screw-on funnel.

faqs.question: How does grounding work on this funnel?
faqs.answer: Conductive containers ground through direct contact with the funnel; non-conductive containers, most plastics, use a dedicated grounding connection instead.

faqs.question: How do I choose the right funnel for my container?
faqs.answer: Match your container's opening: a standard DIN thread (50, 51, 61, or 71), a 2" thread, or a buttress thread uses a screw-on funnel, while a Rötzmeier safety can, canister, or barrel uses the matching plug-in funnel.

faqs.question: How do I find the plug-in funnel for my Rötzmeier can, canister, or barrel?
faqs.answer: Use TR1 for safety cans, TR2 or TR2V for safety canisters, and TR3 for safety barrels.

longForm.heroLead: Filling a flammable liquid container has two quiet risks: pouring past the top, and static building up until it discharges. This funnel is built against both. Overfill protection stops filling before the container overflows. Grounding handles the static risk directly, through contact for conductive containers, or through a dedicated grounding connection for containers that aren't. A flame trap sits underneath it all, and it unscrews for cleaning or replacement rather than being a fixed, disposable part. A closure head reduces the vapor that escapes while you're filling. Two families cover two different needs: screw-on funnels sized to standard DIN thread openings, or plug-in funnels matched exactly to the Safety Can, Safety Canister, or Safety Barrel you're already using.

sections.subheading: Filling has its own risks, separate from storage.
body: Overfilling and static discharge both happen during the filling moment itself, which is exactly what this funnel is built to address.
Overfill protection stops the problem before it starts. Rather than reacting to an overflow, the funnel is built to prevent it during filling.
Grounding depends on what you're filling into. Conductive containers ground through direct contact; non-conductive ones use a dedicated grounding connection instead.
The flame trap is serviceable, not disposable. It unscrews and removes for cleaning or exchange, consistent with the removable-flame-trap approach across Rötzmeier's whole range.

Two funnel families solve two different problems. Screw-on funnels fit standard DIN thread openings across a range of sizes; plug-in funnels are matched specifically to safety cans, canisters, and barrels.
If you already use a Rötzmeier can, canister, or barrel, there's a named funnel for it. TR1, TR2, TR2V, and TR3 map directly to those three product lines.
Not every funnel carries every feature. Screw-on funnels are consistently fully featured; the plug-in funnels are simpler, with overfill protection specifically called out only on the TR2V variant.

Configuration note: Confirmed line is Rötzmeier Safety Funnels. Screw-on funnels: DIN 50, 51, 61, 71, 2", and buttress thread S56x4, each in standard or flat profile. Plug-in funnels: TR1 (cans), TR2/TR2V (canisters), TR3 (barrels). faqs.question: What is a UN-approved transportation container?
faqs.answer: It's a stainless steel container, design-approved under ADR, RID, IMDG Code, ICAO-TI, and GGVSEB, for the safe and legally compliant transport of hazardous liquids by truck, train, ship, or airplane.

faqs.question: Is this different from the in-plant Safety Can, Canister, or Barrel?
faqs.answer: Yes, though it's the same form factor: these are the transport-certified versions of those exact products, approved for movement outside the plant, where the in-plant versions are not.

faqs.question: Which transport modes does this container cover?
faqs.answer: Road under ADR, rail under RID, sea under the IMDG Code, air under ICAO-TI, and German national transport under GGVSEB, all on the same approved design.

faqs.question: How do I find the transport-certified version of my in-plant container?
faqs.answer: Match your current container type and size: a 5-liter in-plant Safety Can corresponds to the 5-liter transportation can (order number 05T), and a 10-liter in-plant Canister corresponds to the 10-liter transportation canister (10KT).

faqs.question: Does the transport container include a pressure control valve?
faqs.answer: Not as standard. The base screw cap ships without a pressure control valve; a version with one is available separately.

faqs.question: Can I get a transport-certified version of a 50-liter or larger Barrel?
faqs.answer: Not in this confirmed range — the transportation barrel is only available at 10 and 25 liters. For larger volumes, confirm directly with Inkarp.

faqs.question: How do I know which certification applies to my shipment?
faqs.answer: Match your transport mode: ADR for road, RID for rail, IMDG Code for sea, ICAO-TI for air; a shipment using multiple modes is covered by all the relevant standards on the same container.

faqs.question: Is this container reusable?
faqs.answer: Yes. It's explicitly built to be reused across shipments, helping avoid one-way, non-returnable transport packaging.

faqs.question: What packaging group is this container licensed for?
faqs.answer: It's licensed for all types of hazardous goods under packaging group X, as specified in its approval.

longForm.heroLead: Most transport certifications cover one route. This one covers all of them. Design approved to ADR for road, RID for rail, the IMDG Code for sea, ICAO-TI for air, and GGVSEB for German national transport law — the same container is certified across trucks, trains, ships, and airplanes. It's built from stainless steel, 0.6 to 1.2 mm, chemically resistant, with a removable flame trap and PTFE gaskets. The screw cap ships without a pressure control valve as standard, with a pressure-valve version also available. This isn't a separate product line. It's the transport-certified version of the Safety Can, Safety Canister, and Safety Barrel already in your plant — same form factors, licensed for the road instead of confined to it. Reusable, rather than a one-way package you dispose of after a single trip.

body: ADR, RID, IMDG Code, ICAO-TI, and GGVSEB together cover road, rail, sea, air, and German national transport law, all on the same container.

This isn't a new product family. It's the same can, canister, and barrel form factors already in the Rötzmeier range, re-engineered and approved specifically for transport rather than confined to in-plant use.
The pressure valve is optional here, not default. The base screw cap ships without one; a pressure-control-valve version is available separately, a genuine difference from the in-plant lines.
It's built to be reused, not thrown away. Explicitly positioned to help avoid one-way, non-returnable transport packaging.

Sizing follows the in-plant lines, mostly. Cans run 1 to 5 liters, canisters 5 to 20 liters, matching their in-plant counterparts closely - but the transport barrel only reaches 25 liters, well short of the in-plant Barrel's 200-liter ceiling.

Construction stays consistent with the rest of the range. Chemically resistant stainless steel, PTFE gaskets, and a removable flame trap, the same core safety approach used across Cans, Canisters, and Barrels.

faqs.question: What is a safety barrel for in-plant use?
faqs.answer: It's a stainless steel container built primarily for storing bigger volumes of flammable liquid, with filling and metering available as a secondary capability, and removable flame traps and a pressure control valve for protection.

faqs.question: Can this barrel be used for off-site transport?
faqs.answer: No. This product is certified for in-plant use only; off-site transport requires a separately certified transportation barrel.

faqs.question: Which sizes are stackable?
faqs.answer: The 25 and 50-liter barrels specifically. This isn't stated for the 10-liter size or for the 100 and 200-liter sizes.

faqs.question: What is a safety collection barrel?
faqs.answer: A different barrel purpose entirely, built to receive liquid, such as waste or a contained spill, using a centered 2-inch plug rather than a dispensing mechanism.

faqs.question: How do I decide between a dispensing barrel and a collection barrel?
faqs.answer: Choose a dispensing barrel, with a screw cap, tap, or metering device, if you're storing and controlling liquid coming out; choose a collection barrel if you're receiving liquid, such as for waste or spill containment.

faqs.question: How do I find the exact order number for my requirement?
faqs.answer: Confirm your purpose (dispensing or collection), your size, and whether you need a content indicator; for example, a 25-liter barrel with a self-closing tap and content indicator is order number 25ZI.

faqs.question: Are 100 and 200-liter barrels available?
faqs.answer: Yes, across all barrel types, though specific order numbers for these sizes are confirmed directly by Inkarp rather than listed in the standard order table.

faqs.question: What is a content indicator?
faqs.answer: A feature that shows the fill level without needing to open the barrel, available on tap, metering device, and collection variants.

faqs.question: Can the flame traps be serviced?
faqs.answer: Yes. They're removable, supporting inspection and maintenance rather than replacing the entire barrel.

longForm.heroLead: Some flammable liquids need to be dispensed carefully. Others just need to be stored in bulk, safely, without eating up warehouse floor space. This barrel is built for the second job first. Stainless steel from 0.8 to 1.5 mm, scaled to the size, with removable flame traps and a pressure control valve venting from around 0.3 bar. The 25 and 50-liter sizes stack, so bulk storage doesn't mean spreading out. It still dispenses when you need it to, with a screw cap, a self-closing tap, or a metering device with separate ventilation. Content indicators let you check the fill level without opening the barrel at all. There's also a genuinely different variant: the safety collection barrel, built to receive liquid rather than dispense it, for waste or spill containment. This barrel is for in-plant use. Off-site transport needs a certified transportation barrel instead.

body: This line is built primarily for storing bigger volumes of flammable liquid, with filling and metering as a secondary, still-fully-usable capability.
Stacking is real, and it's specific. The 25 and 50-liter barrels are stackable; that claim isn't made for the 10-liter size or for the 100 and 200-liter sizes.
The size range goes further than the order number table shows. All barrel types are also available in 100 and 200 liters, though specific order numbers for those sizes aren't listed here.
Two barrels do two different jobs. A dispensing barrel controls how liquid comes out; a collection barrel is built to receive liquid, for waste or spill containment, a genuinely different purpose.
You can check the level without opening it. Content indicators are available on the tap, metering device, and collection barrel variants.
Construction scales with size. Stainless steel thickness runs 0.8 to 1.5 mm, with removable flame traps for inspection and service.
This is an in-plant product, and that boundary holds here too. Off-site transport requires a certified transportation barrel, a separate Rötzmeier line.

Configuration note: Confirmed line is the Rötzmeier Safety Barrels - for in-plant use. Confirmed sizes with order numbers are 10, 25 and 50 liters. Also available: 100 and 200 liters, with specific order numbers confirmed by Inkarp. Stackable: 25 and 50-liter sizes specifically. Not certified for off-site transport - a separate product line covers that requirement. Full specifications (exact dimensions, weight, additional certification detail) are available on request from Inkarp.

sections.title: Technical Specifications
body: The technical specifications of the Safety Barrels for In-Plant Use include 0.8 to 1.5 mm stainless steel construction, size-specific stackability, and seven distinct configurations.
Storing a bigger volume safely is a different problem from dispensing a smaller one carefully, and this line is built around that first.

Stacking is the clearest example. At 25 and 50 liters, barrels stack, which turns a warehouse floor space problem into a vertical one instead. That claim doesn't extend to the 10-liter size, which doesn't need it as much, or to the 100 and 200-liter sizes, which are confirmed available but not confirmed stackable. Content indicators solve a related problem: knowing how much is left without opening a barrel that's specifically built to stay sealed.
Product expert note: Tell our team your storage volume and warehouse layout, and Inkarp will confirm whether stacking applies to your size and what floor space it actually saves.

sections.title: Dispensing, Collection and Order Numbers
body: The first decision isn't size. It's whether you're dispensing liquid out of the barrel, or collecting liquid into it.

For bulk storage with occasional simple access, specify the screw cap variant. For controlled, repeated dispensing, specify a self-closing tap or metering device. To check fill level without opening, add a content indicator variant. For collecting waste or spill liquid rather than dispensing, specify the collection barrel, with or without a level indicator. For larger-volume dispensing beyond 10 liters, use the screw cap or tap variants at 25 or 50 liters.
Product expert note: Send our team whether you're dispensing or collecting, your required volume, and whether you need a content indicator, and Inkarp will confirm the exact order number.

longForm.heroLead: A glass bottle takes up the space it takes up, standing upright, every time. This canister doesn't have to. Its self-closing tap versions are built for horizontal storage and filling, and the canister shape itself saves real space in a safety cabinet, laboratory cupboard, or shelf, specifically compared to bottles. Stainless steel at 0.8 mm, thicker than a standard safety can, with a solid stainless steel handhold built for repeated handling. The flame traps are removable, so they can be inspected and serviced rather than replaced as a whole unit. Four dispensing mechanisms cover different needs: a self-closing metering device for controlled dosing, the same device with separate ventilation at 20 liters, a screw cap for simple access, or a self-closing tap with separate ventilation for horizontal use. This canister is built for in-plant use. Off-site transport requires a certified transportation container instead.

longForm.heroLead: Handling a flammable liquid safely comes down to two failure points: an open flame reaching the vapor inside, or pressure building until the can fails. This can is built against both. A flame trap stops external flame from reaching what's inside. A pressure control valve vents from around 0.3 bar, before pressure ever becomes a problem. The body is stainless steel, 0.6 mm thick, with PTFE gaskets that hold up against a wide range of chemicals. The handhold is powder-coated aluminum, shaped for a secure grip during pouring or metering. Choose a self-closing metering device for controlled dispensing, or a screw cap for straightforward access. Available in 1, 2, or 5 liters, polished or unpolished. This can is built for in-plant use. If you need to transport flammable liquid, that requires a separately certified product.

sections.title: Technical Specifications
body: The technical specifications of the Safety Cans for In-Plant Use include stainless steel construction, a 0.3 bar pressure valve, and confirmed sizing from 1 to 5 liters.
A safety can earns its name from what happens when something goes wrong outside it, or builds up inside it.

The flame trap sits between the outside world and the liquid inside, physically stopping an open flame from reaching the vapor that could ignite. The pressure control valve handles the opposite risk: as pressure inside the can rises, it vents automatically from around 0.3 bar, before that pressure becomes a structural or safety problem. The two mechanisms don't depend on each other, which is what makes the can safe against both failure modes independently.
Product expert note: Tell our team what liquid you're handling and how it's typically stored, and Inkarp will confirm this can suits your safety requirements.

For a material requiring moistened storage, specify the Moistener can, in 1 or 2 liters.

faqs.question: What is a safety funnel?
faqs.answer: It's a filling accessory that screws onto or plugs into a container, built with a flame trap, overfill protection, and a closure head to reduce vapor emission during filling of flammable liquids.

faqs.question: What is overfill protection?
faqs.answer: A built-in mechanism that stops filling before the container's capacity is exceeded, standard on every screw-on funnel.

faqs.question: How does grounding work on this funnel?
faqs.answer: Conductive containers ground through direct contact with the funnel; non-conductive containers, most plastics, use a dedicated grounding connection instead.

faqs.question: How do I choose the right funnel for my container?
faqs.answer: Match your container's opening: a standard DIN thread (50, 51, 61, or 71), a 2" thread, or a buttress thread uses a screw-on funnel, while a Rötzmeier safety can, canister, or barrel uses the matching plug-in funnel.

faqs.question: How do I find the plug-in funnel for my Rötzmeier can, canister, or barrel?
faqs.answer: Use TR1 for safety cans, TR2 or TR2V for safety canisters, and TR3 for safety barrels.

faqs.question: Can the flame trap be cleaned or replaced?
faqs.answer: Yes. It unscrews and removes for cleaning or exchange, rather than requiring the whole funnel to be replaced.

faqs.question: Do the plug-in funnels have overfill protection?
faqs.answer: Overfill protection is explicitly stated only for the TR2V variant; confirm feature details with Inkarp for TR1, TR2, and TR3.

faqs.question: What is the closure head for?
faqs.answer: It reduces the vapor that escapes into the surrounding air while the container is being filled.

faqs.question: What is the difference between the standard and flat ("-180") funnel versions?
faqs.answer: The flat version has a lower profile, useful where clearance above the container is limited; both carry the same core safety features.

longForm.heroLead: Filling a flammable liquid container has two quiet risks: pouring past the top, and static building up until it discharges. This funnel is built against both. Overfill protection stops filling before the container overflows. Grounding handles the static risk directly, through contact for conductive containers, or through a dedicated grounding connection for containers that aren't. A flame trap sits underneath it all, and it unscrews for cleaning or replacement rather than being a fixed, disposable part. A closure head reduces the vapor that escapes while you're filling. Two families cover two different needs: screw-on funnels sized to standard DIN thread openings, or plug-in funnels matched exactly to the Safety Can, Safety Canister, or Safety Barrel you're already using.

sections.subheading: Filling has its own risks, separate from storage.
body: Overfilling and static discharge both happen during the filling moment itself, which is exactly what this funnel is built to address.
Overfill protection stops the problem before it starts. Rather than reacting to an overflow, the funnel is built to prevent it during filling.
Grounding depends on what you're filling into. Conductive containers ground through direct contact; non-conductive ones use a dedicated grounding connection instead.
The flame trap is serviceable, not disposable. It unscrews and removes for cleaning or exchange, consistent with the removable-flame-trap approach across Rötzmeier's whole range.

Two funnel families solve two different problems. Screw-on funnels fit standard DIN thread openings across a range of sizes; plug-in funnels are matched specifically to safety cans, canisters, and barrels.
If you already use a Rötzmeier can, canister, or barrel, there's a named funnel for it. TR1, TR2, TR2V, and TR3 map directly to those three product lines.
Not every funnel carries every feature. Screw-on funnels are consistently fully featured; the plug-in funnels are simpler, with overfill protection specifically called out only on the TR2V variant.

Configuration note: Confirmed line is Rötzmeier Safety Funnels. Screw-on funnels: DIN 50, 51, 61, 71, 2", and buttress thread S56x4, each in standard or flat profile. Plug-in funnels: TR1 (cans), TR2/TR2V (canisters), TR3 (barrels). faqs.answer: It's a stainless steel container, design-approved under ADR, RID, IMDG Code, ICAO-TI, and GGVSEB, for the safe and legally compliant transport of hazardous liquids by truck, train, ship, or airplane.

faqs.question: Is this different from the in-plant Safety Can, Canister, or Barrel?
faqs.answer: Yes, though it's the same form factor: these are the transport-certified versions of those exact products, approved for movement outside the plant, where the in-plant versions are not.

faqs.question: Which transport modes does this container cover?
faqs.answer: Road under ADR, rail under RID, sea under the IMDG Code, air under ICAO-TI, and German national transport under GGVSEB, all on the same approved design.

faqs.question: How do I find the transport-certified version of my in-plant container?
faqs.answer: Match your current container type and size: a 5-liter in-plant Safety Can corresponds to the 5-liter transportation can (order number 05T), and a 10-liter in-plant Canister corresponds to the 10-liter transportation canister (10KT).

faqs.question: Does the transport container include a pressure control valve?
faqs.answer: Not as standard. The base screw cap ships without a pressure control valve; a version with one is available separately.

faqs.question: Can I get a transport-certified version of a 50-liter or larger Barrel?
faqs.answer: Not in this confirmed range — the transportation barrel is only available at 10 and 25 liters. For larger volumes, confirm directly with Inkarp.

faqs.question: How do I know which certification applies to my shipment?
faqs.answer: Match your transport mode: ADR for road, RID for rail, IMDG Code for sea, ICAO-TI for air; a shipment using multiple modes is covered by all the relevant standards on the same container.

faqs.question: Is this container reusable?
faqs.answer: Yes. It's explicitly built to be reused across shipments, helping avoid one-way, non-returnable transport packaging.

faqs.question: What packaging group is this container licensed for?
faqs.answer: It's licensed for all types of hazardous goods under packaging group X, as specified in its approval.

faqs.question: What is the price of the Transportation Containers with UN-Approval in India?
faqs.answer: The price depends on the form factor, size, and whether you need the pressure valve version. Contact Inkarp for a quotation once your shipment requirements are confirmed.

faqs.answer: Inkarp is the authorized distributor and service provider for Rötzmeier Transportation Containers in India, providing demonstration, installation, training, AMC, spare parts, and technical support.

longForm.heroLead: Most transport certifications cover one route. This one covers all of them. Design approved to ADR for road, RID for rail, the IMDG Code for sea, ICAO-TI for air, and GGVSEB for German national transport law — the same container is certified across trucks, trains, ships, and airplanes. It's built from stainless steel, 0.6 to 1.2 mm, chemically resistant, with a removable flame trap and PTFE gaskets. The screw cap ships without a pressure control valve as standard, with a pressure-valve version also available. This isn't a separate product line. It's the transport-certified version of the Safety Can, Safety Canister, and Safety Barrel already in your plant — same form factors, licensed for the road instead of confined to it. Reusable, rather than a one-way package you dispose of after a single trip.

sections.title: Transportation Containers with UN-Approval at a Glance
sections.description: Everything you need to evaluate these containers: which international standards they're approved to, how they map to your existing in-plant containers, what sizes and order numbers exist, and Inkarp installation and service support.
body: ADR, RID, IMDG Code, ICAO-TI, and GGVSEB together cover road, rail, sea, air, and German national transport law, all on the same container.

This isn't a new product family. It's the same can, canister, and barrel form factors already in the Rötzmeier range, re-engineered and approved specifically for transport rather than confined to in-plant use.
The pressure valve is optional here, not default. The base screw cap ships without one; a pressure-control-valve version is available separately, a genuine difference from the in-plant lines.
It's built to be reused, not thrown away. Explicitly positioned to help avoid one-way, non-returnable transport packaging.

Sizing follows the in-plant lines, mostly. Cans run 1 to 5 liters, canisters 5 to 20 liters, matching their in-plant counterparts closely - but the transport barrel only reaches 25 liters, well short of the in-plant Barrel's 200-liter ceiling.

Construction stays consistent with the rest of the range. Chemically resistant stainless steel, PTFE gaskets, and a removable flame trap, the same core safety approach used across Cans, Canisters, and Barrels.

Configuration note: Confirmed line is Rötzmeier Safety Transportation Containers, UN-approved. Approved to: ADR, RID, IMDG Code, ICAO-TI, GGVSEB. Available as transportation cans (1-5 L), canisters (5-20 L), and barrels (10-25 L). Screw cap standard, without pressure control valve; pressure-valve version also available. Full specifications (exact dimensions, weight, further certification detail) are available on request from Inkarp.

body.text: Arium Comfort I produces both ASTM Type 1 ultrapure water and Type 3 pure water from a single system, connected directly to a potable feed water source.
Type 1 water dispenses at rates up to 2 L/min, with quality that exceeds ASTM Type 1 specifications, not just meets them.
Type 3 pure water production runs at either 8 or 16 L/h, depending on the RO module configuration selected.
The system uses the latest reverse osmosis technology alongside a unique ion-exchange cartridge, consistently delivering purified water of the highest reproducible quality.
Intelligent iJust software makes the best use of water resources: enhancing purified water quality, reducing overall water usage, and calculating optimal cleaning cycles automatically.
Purified water is stored in the unique, closed Arium Bagtank system, reliably protecting it from secondary contamination and ensuring consistently reproducible results.

A 185/254 nm UV lamp, available as an option, prevents microbiological growth and minimizes TOC, bringing levels under 2 ppb; an optional TOC monitor checks and displays readings continuously in real time.
A touch-function display with clearly structured menu navigation ensures error-free control with a light touch, even while wearing lab gloves.
Installation adapts to available lab space: benchtop, wall-mounted, or built-in configurations are all supported.

body.text: Arium Comfort II connects directly to a potable feed water source and produces ASTM Type 1 ultrapure and Type 2 pure water from that single connection.
Three technologies work in sequence: advanced reverse osmosis membranes, Sartorius's patented electrodeionization (EDI), and a cartridge with highly efficient ion-exchange resin.
Type 1 water dispenses at 2 L/min; Type 2 production runs at 5 L/h or 10 L/h depending on the configuration selected.
The optional integrated 185 | 254 nm UV lamp does two jobs at once — suppressing microbiological growth and reducing total organic carbon, bringing TOC below 2 ppb.
An optional TOC monitor, developed specifically for this system, displays readings continuously in real time rather than requiring a separate offline check.
Purified water is stored in the closed arium® bagtank system, which protects it from secondary contamination between production and use.
iJust software enhances purified water quality, reduces overall water consumption, and calculates optimal cleaning cycles rather than running them on a fixed schedule.
The touch-active display responds through gloves, so navigating the menu doesn't mean breaking sterile technique or stopping to de-glove.
Installation works three ways — benchtop, wall-mounted, or built-in — so the system fits the bench space that exists rather than requiring a bench to be cleared for it.
Feeding downstream instruments and ultrapure systems with Type 2 water extends their service life by keeping feed water quality consistent.

body: Reverse osmosis handles the bulk removal first, taking dissolved salts, organics, and particulates out of the potable feed before anything downstream has to deal with them.
Patented electrodeionization then polishes continuously without regeneration chemicals, holding purity steady rather than degrading between service intervals the way a resin-only system does.
The ion-exchange cartridge with highly efficient resin provides the final polish that takes water to ASTM Type 1 rather than stopping at Type 2.

Because the stages run in sequence rather than as separate machines, Type 2 water is available at 5 or 10 L/h for bulk work while Type 1 dispenses at 2 L/min for analytical work — from the same unit, on the same feed line.
Adding the 185 | 254 nm UV lamp puts organic reduction and microbial control into the same step: 185 nm breaks organics down to bring TOC below 2 ppb, 254 nm suppresses microbiological growth.
Feeding autoclaves, glassware washers, and downstream ultrapure systems with this Type 2 water extends their working life, since scale and fouling are what usually shorten it.

items: A purification system that runs fixed cleaning cycles rejects water on a schedule, whether or not the membrane condition actually calls for it. That reject water is a real, recurring operating cost.
iJust calculates optimal cleaning cycles from actual system condition instead, so cleaning happens when it's needed rather than when a timer says so.
The same software reduces overall water usage compared with conventional systems, which matters most where feed water is metered, restricted, or expensive.
Product water quality improves alongside that economy — iJust enhances purified water quality rather than trading purity for consumption savings.
Downstream ultrapure systems fed by this water are guaranteed longer life, because consistent feed quality is what determines how hard their own consumables have to work.
The closed bagtank protects that carefully produced water after the fact, so quality achieved at production isn't lost to airborne contamination in storage.

body.text: Arium Mini Plus provides ASTM Type 1/ultrapure water from Sartorius's innovative Bagtank storage, purified from pretreated water held in an internal storage bag.
Daily output covers up to approximately 10 liters of Type 1 water, suited to general and analytical lab applications.
The unit measures just 28 centimeters (11 inches) wide, a compact design with minimal footprint that integrates easily into any lab environment.
A touch-activated color display works seamlessly with laboratory gloves, showing the last volume dispensed, purified water quality, and water temperature directly.
Dispensing runs manually or in 50 mL increments, adding flexibility for different sample prep needs.
The 5-liter bag requires no chemical cleaning, lowering contamination risk, and swaps out easily via a leak-tight quick-connect coupling that preserves the closed system.

Purification runs through multiple stages: a pretreatment cartridge using high-quality carbon for effective absorption, reverse osmosis to retain impurities, and optional point-of-use filters, Arium Sterile Plus for bacteria removal down to 0.001 CFU/mL via a 0.22 μm membrane, and Arium Cell Plus for endotoxins, RNase, DNase, microorganisms, and particles.
The unit is available with or without an integrated UV lamp, depending on application needs.
Bagtank technology maintains a closed system throughout, automatically regulating pressure so no CO2 penetrates, preserving low conductivity and preventing biofilm formation.

body: Open water storage systems are vulnerable to secondary contamination the moment they're exposed to air. Arium Mini Plus avoids that risk entirely with a closed Bagtank system.
Pressure inside the system regulates automatically, keeping CO2 from penetrating the stored water, which directly preserves low conductivity readings over time.
That same closed environment prevents biofilm formation, a common failure point in lab water systems that rely on open reservoirs or infrequently cleaned tanks.
The bag itself needs replacing roughly every six months depending on lab requirements, a predictable, low-effort maintenance cycle rather than an open-ended cleaning routine.

faqs.question: What is Arium Advance EDI used for?
faqs.answer: It's a Type 2 pure water system used for microbiological media and reagent preparation, chemical analysis and synthesis solutions, histology, ELISA and RIA, buffer and pH solution preparation, and feeding laboratory instruments.

faqs.question: What water quality does Arium Advance EDI produce?
faqs.answer: Type 2 pure water with a resistivity of 5 to 15 MΩ·cm, delivered consistently at rates up to 10 L/h.

faqs.question: What is electrodeionization and why does it matter?
faqs.answer: EDI removes ions continuously using an electrical field rather than a depleting exchange capacity, which is what allows water quality to stay consistent instead of declining across a service interval.

faqs.question: What contaminants does the system remove?
faqs.answer: Oxidants, heavy metal ions, and particulates are reliably removed from the potable feed water, with the highest ion retention rates alongside optimum purified water yield.

faqs.question: Does Arium Advance EDI produce Type 1 ultrapure water?
faqs.answer: No. It produces Type 2 pure water. Where Type 1 is also needed, this system can feed a downstream ultrapure polisher, or a combined system covering both grades may be the better fit.

faqs.question: What is iJust?
faqs.answer: It's the system's intelligent software — it makes the best use of the initial feed water conditions, enhances purified water quality, reduces water usage, and calculates optimal cleaning cycles.

faqs.question: How is purified water stored?
faqs.answer: In the closed arium® bagtank system, which protects the water from secondary contamination after production.

faqs.question: Can the display be operated while wearing gloves?
faqs.answer: Yes. The touch-function display responds to a light touch through gloves, with clearly structured menu navigation.

faqs.question: How can the system be installed?
faqs.answer: Three ways — benchtop, wall-mounted, or built-in — so it fits the space actually available rather than requiring space to be cleared.

faqs.question: Does it extend the life of downstream systems?
faqs.answer: Yes. Feeding downstream ultrapure water systems with consistent Type 2 water gives them a guaranteed longer service life.

faqs.question: What production rates are available?
faqs.answer: 5 L/h and 10 L/h, depending on the configuration selected.

longForm.heroHook: 5 to 15 MΩ·cm, held steady. No resin swap, no purity drift between services.
longForm.heroLead: Cartridge-based deionizers start strong and decline. Resistivity drops as the resin exhausts, and the water feeding a media prep or an autoclave in week six isn't the water that fed it in week one — which is exactly the kind of variable that quietly undermines reproducibility. Arium Advance EDI works differently. Patented electrodeionization runs continuously, holding Type 2 pure water at 5 to 15 MΩ·cm at production rates up to 10 L/h, connected straight to the potable feed. Oxidants, heavy metal ions, and particulates come out reliably, with the highest ion retention rates alongside optimum purified water yield. iJust software reads the actual feed water condition and adapts to it, tuning water usage and calculating cleaning cycles rather than running fixed intervals. Purified water then sits in the closed arium® bagtank, protected from the airborne contamination an open reservoir invites.

body.text: Arium Advance EDI connects directly to a potable feed water source and produces Type 2 pure water at rates up to 10 L/h.
Resistivity holds between 5 and 15 MΩ·cm, delivered consistently rather than declining across a service interval.
Proprietary, patented electrodeionization sits at the core, achieving the highest ion retention rates while maintaining an optimum yield of purified water.
Oxidants, heavy metal ions, and particulates are reliably removed from the incoming feed water.
iJust software makes the best use of the initial feed water condition specifically, adapting to what's actually coming in rather than assuming a fixed input quality.
The same software enhances purified water quality, reduces water usage compared with conventional systems, and calculates optimal cleaning cycles.
Purified water is stored in the closed arium® bagtank system, which protects it from secondary contamination between production and point of use.
The touch-function display responds through gloves, with structured menu navigation that removes guesswork from routine operation.
Installation works three ways — benchtop, wall-mounted, or built-in — so the system fits the space the lab has rather than requiring space to be made.
Feeding downstream ultrapure water systems with this Type 2 water gives them a guaranteed longer service life.

sections.tabSummary: What holding 5–15 MΩ·cm actually delivers

items: Electrodeionization removes ions continuously using an electrical field rather than depleting a fixed pool of exchange capacity, which is why purity holds instead of declining as a cartridge would.
That continuity is what makes 5 to 15 MΩ·cm a working range rather than a peak figure — the water produced late in a service interval matches the water produced early in it.
The highest ion retention rates come alongside an optimum yield of purified water, so purity isn't achieved by rejecting an unreasonable proportion of the feed.
Oxidants, heavy metal ions, and particulates are all removed reliably, covering the contaminant classes that most commonly compromise media preparation and analytical solution work.
Downstream ultrapure systems fed with this water get a guaranteed longer life, because their own polishing consumables aren't compensating for an inconsistent input.
The closed bagtank protects that consistency after production — quality achieved at the membrane isn't given back to airborne contamination in an open storage vessel.

cards.title: Cleaning based on need, not a timer

body: Feed water quality isn't uniform. It varies by site, by season, and sometimes by day, and a system that assumes a fixed input either over-treats or under-performs.
iJust makes the best use of the initial feed water conditions specifically, adapting operation to what's actually arriving rather than to an assumed baseline.
Cleaning cycles are calculated from that real condition instead of running to a fixed timer, so the system cleans when it needs to and not on a schedule that ignores it.
Water usage drops compared with conventional systems, which matters directly wherever feed water is metered, restricted, or carries real cost.
Purified water quality improves alongside that economy — iJust enhances quality rather than trading purity for lower consumption.
The touch-function display keeps all of it accessible: a light touch works through gloves, and structured menu navigation means routine control doesn't require interpreting the system.

faqs.question: What is Arium Advance RO used for?
faqs.answer: It's a Type 3 reverse osmosis water system used to supply feed water to ultrapure water systems, rinse glassware and laboratory vessels, and feed instruments such as autoclaves, glassware dishwashers, and humidifiers.

faqs.question: What water grade does Arium Advance RO produce?
faqs.answer: Type 3 reverse osmosis water, with the highest ion retention in its class at rates up to 24 L/h.

faqs.question: What flow rates are available?
faqs.answer: Constant flow rates of 8, 16, and 24 L/h, selected to match actual daily demand.

faqs.question: What is automatic membrane backflushing?
faqs.answer: The system periodically reverses flow across the RO membrane using purified water, lifting accumulated fouling off the surface without any operator step or service visit.

faqs.question: Why does backflushing use purified water rather than feed water?
faqs.answer: Cleaning with purified water avoids reintroducing the salts, particulates, and organics the membrane is there to remove in the first place.

faqs.question: How is Arium Advance RO different from Arium Advance EDI?
faqs.answer: RO produces Type 3 water at 8 to 24 L/h for feed, rinsing, and instrument supply. EDI produces Type 2 water at 5 to 15 MΩ·cm up to 10 L/h for media, reagent, and analytical solution preparation.

faqs.question: Can Arium Advance RO feed an ultrapure water system?
faqs.answer: Yes. Supplying downstream ultrapure systems is a primary application, and consistent Type 3 feed gives them a guaranteed longer working life.

faqs.question: What is iJust?
faqs.answer: It's the system's intelligent software — it makes the best use of available water resources, enhances purified water quality, reduces water usage, and calculates optimal cleaning cycles.

faqs.question: How is purified water stored?
faqs.answer: In the closed arium® bagtank system, which protects the water from secondary contamination after production.

faqs.question: Can the display be operated while wearing gloves?
faqs.answer: Yes. The touch-function display responds to a light touch through gloves, with clearly structured menu navigation.

faqs.question: How can the system be installed?
faqs.answer: Three ways — benchtop, wall-mounted, or built-in — so it fits the space actually available in the lab.

sections.title: Automatic Backflushing and Membrane Life
sections.tabSummary: What self-cleaning membranes change day to day

items: RO membranes foul. Rejected salts, particulates, and organics accumulate on the membrane surface, and left alone that layer reduces both flux and retention performance over time.
Arium Advance RO backflushes the membrane automatically using purified water, reversing flow to lift that accumulation off the surface before it consolidates.
Because the backflush uses purified water rather than raw feed, the cleaning step doesn't reintroduce the contaminants it's meant to be removing.
Automatic means it happens on the system's schedule, not the lab's — no operator step, no reminder, no dependence on someone remembering during a busy week.
The practical result is retention performance held closer to specification across the membrane's life, and a membrane that reaches its replacement point later rather than sooner.
iJust sits alongside it, calculating optimal cleaning cycles from actual system condition rather than running fixed intervals that ignore what's really happening at the membrane.

body: Under-sizing a Type 3 system turns it into a bottleneck: glassware waits, autoclaves wait, and the downstream ultrapure polisher runs short. Over-sizing pays for capacity that never gets used.
Three constant flow rates — 8, 16, and 24 L/h — let the system be matched to real daily demand instead of forcing a compromise in either direction.
Constant flow matters as much as the number itself: output stays predictable, so the volume available in an hour is the volume planned for.
The same flexibility runs through installation. Benchtop, wall-mounted, and built-in formats all work, so a lab short on bench space isn't excluded from the system.
iJust makes the best use of available water resources across whichever rate is selected, reducing consumption without giving up product water quality.
The closed bagtank protects produced water regardless of rate, so a higher-throughput configuration doesn't mean more water sitting exposed to airborne contamination.

longForm.heroLead: Most labs end up running two water systems: one producing Type 2 for autoclaves, dishwashers and media prep, another polishing to Type 1 for HPLC and ion chromatography. Two footprints, two consumable schedules, two things to service. Arium Comfort II produces both from a single unit connected directly to potable feed water. Reverse osmosis membranes, patented electrodeionization, and a high-efficiency ion-exchange cartridge work in sequence, so ASTM Type 1 ultrapure dispenses at 2 L/min while Type 2 pure water is produced continuously at 5 or 10 L/h depending on configuration. Purified water is held in the closed arium® bagtank, which keeps it away from the airborne contamination an open reservoir invites. And iJust software runs underneath all of it, tuning water usage and calculating cleaning cycles rather than running fixed intervals regardless of what the system actually needs.

body.text: Arium Comfort II connects directly to a potable feed water source and produces ASTM Type 1 ultrapure and Type 2 pure water from that single connection.
Three technologies work in sequence: advanced reverse osmosis membranes, Sartorius's patented electrodeionization (EDI), and a cartridge with highly efficient ion-exchange resin.
Type 1 water dispenses at 2 L/min; Type 2 production runs at 5 L/h or 10 L/h depending on the configuration selected.
The optional integrated 185 | 254 nm UV lamp does two jobs at once — suppressing microbiological growth and reducing total organic carbon, bringing TOC below 2 ppb.
An optional TOC monitor, developed specifically for this system, displays readings continuously in real time rather than requiring a separate offline check.
Purified water is stored in the closed arium® bagtank system, which protects it from secondary contamination between production and use.
iJust software enhances purified water quality, reduces overall water consumption, and calculates optimal cleaning cycles rather than running them on a fixed schedule.
The touch-active display responds through gloves, so navigating the menu doesn't mean breaking sterile technique or stopping to de-glove.
Installation works three ways — benchtop, wall-mounted, or built-in — so the system fits the bench space that exists rather than requiring a bench to be cleared for it.
Feeding downstream instruments and ultrapure systems with Type 2 water extends their service life by keeping feed water quality consistent.

body: Reverse osmosis handles the bulk removal first, taking dissolved salts, organics, and particulates out of the potable feed before anything downstream has to deal with them.
Patented electrodeionization then polishes continuously without regeneration chemicals, holding purity steady rather than degrading between service intervals the way a resin-only system does.
The ion-exchange cartridge with highly efficient resin provides the final polish that takes water to ASTM Type 1 rather than stopping at Type 2.

Because the stages run in sequence rather than as separate machines, Type 2 water is available at 5 or 10 L/h for bulk work while Type 1 dispenses at 2 L/min for analytical work — from the same unit, on the same feed line.
Adding the 185 | 254 nm UV lamp puts organic reduction and microbial control into the same step: 185 nm breaks organics down to bring TOC below 2 ppb, 254 nm suppresses microbiological growth.
Feeding autoclaves, glassware washers, and downstream ultrapure systems with this Type 2 water extends their working life, since scale and fouling are what usually shorten it.

items: A purification system that runs fixed cleaning cycles rejects water on a schedule, whether or not the membrane condition actually calls for it. That reject water is a real, recurring operating cost.
iJust calculates optimal cleaning cycles from actual system condition instead, so cleaning happens when it's needed rather than when a timer says so.
The same software reduces overall water usage compared with conventional systems, which matters most where feed water is metered, restricted, or expensive.
Product water quality improves alongside that economy — iJust enhances purified water quality rather than trading purity for consumption savings.
Downstream ultrapure systems fed by this water are guaranteed longer life, because consistent feed quality is what determines how hard their own consumables have to work.
The closed bagtank protects that carefully produced water after the fact, so quality achieved at production isn't lost to airborne contamination in storage.

body.text: Arium Mini Plus provides ASTM Type 1/ultrapure water from Sartorius's innovative Bagtank storage, purified from pretreated water held in an internal storage bag.
Daily output covers up to approximately 10 liters of Type 1 water, suited to general and analytical lab applications.
The unit measures just 28 centimeters (11 inches) wide, a compact design with minimal footprint that integrates easily into any lab environment.
A touch-activated color display works seamlessly with laboratory gloves, showing the last volume dispensed, purified water quality, and water temperature directly.
Dispensing runs manually or in 50 mL increments, adding flexibility for different sample prep needs.
The 5-liter bag requires no chemical cleaning, lowering contamination risk, and swaps out easily via a leak-tight quick-connect coupling that preserves the closed system.

Purification runs through multiple stages: a pretreatment cartridge using high-quality carbon for effective absorption, reverse osmosis to retain impurities, and optional point-of-use filters, Arium Sterile Plus for bacteria removal down to 0.001 CFU/mL via a 0.22 μm membrane, and Arium Cell Plus for endotoxins, RNase, DNase, microorganisms, and particles.
The unit is available with or without an integrated UV lamp, depending on application needs.
Bagtank technology maintains a closed system throughout, automatically regulating pressure so no CO2 penetrates, preserving low conductivity and preventing biofilm formation.

body: Open water storage systems are vulnerable to secondary contamination the moment they're exposed to air. Arium Mini Plus avoids that risk entirely with a closed Bagtank system.
Pressure inside the system regulates automatically, keeping CO2 from penetrating the stored water, which directly preserves low conductivity readings over time.
That same closed environment prevents biofilm formation, a common failure point in lab water systems that rely on open reservoirs or infrequently cleaned tanks.
The bag itself needs replacing roughly every six months depending on lab requirements, a predictable, low-effort maintenance cycle rather than an open-ended cleaning routine.

body: Reproducibility in analytical work depends directly on water purity, and total organic carbon is one of the most sensitive variables to get wrong.
The 185/254 nm UV lamp does double duty: preventing microbiological growth in the system while actively minimizing TOC in the purified water, bringing it down to under 2 ppb.
That low TOC level directly supports reproducibility and reliability across lab results, not just a specification on paper.
The optional TOC monitor closes the loop, checking and displaying TOC readings continuously in real time, so water quality is confirmed at the point of use rather than assumed.

arium® pro UV adds the 185/254 nm UV lamp instead, bringing TOC down to under 2 ppb and preventing microbial growth, suited to analytical work where organic carbon content matters most.
arium® pro VF combines both, UV lamp and ultrafilter together, for applications demanding the lowest TOC and the most thorough biological contaminant removal in one system.
A TOC monitor can be added to either the UV or VF configuration for continuous, real-time verification of water quality.

faqs.question: What is Arium Advance EDI used for?
faqs.answer: It's a Type 2 pure water system used for microbiological media and reagent preparation, chemical analysis and synthesis solutions, histology, ELISA and RIA, buffer and pH solution preparation, and feeding laboratory instruments.

faqs.question: What water quality does Arium Advance EDI produce?
faqs.answer: Type 2 pure water with a resistivity of 5 to 15 MΩ·cm, delivered consistently at rates up to 10 L/h.

faqs.question: What is electrodeionization and why does it matter?
faqs.answer: EDI removes ions continuously using an electrical field rather than a depleting exchange capacity, which is what allows water quality to stay consistent instead of declining across a service interval.

faqs.question: What contaminants does the system remove?
faqs.answer: Oxidants, heavy metal ions, and particulates are reliably removed from the potable feed water, with the highest ion retention rates alongside optimum purified water yield.

faqs.question: Does Arium Advance EDI produce Type 1 ultrapure water?
faqs.answer: No. It produces Type 2 pure water. Where Type 1 is also needed, this system can feed a downstream ultrapure polisher, or a combined system covering both grades may be the better fit.

faqs.question: What is iJust?
faqs.answer: It's the system's intelligent software — it makes the best use of the initial feed water conditions, enhances purified water quality, reduces water usage, and calculates optimal cleaning cycles.

faqs.question: How is purified water stored?
faqs.answer: In the closed arium® bagtank system, which protects the water from secondary contamination after production.

faqs.question: Can the display be operated while wearing gloves?
faqs.answer: Yes. The touch-function display responds to a light touch through gloves, with clearly structured menu navigation.

faqs.question: How can the system be installed?
faqs.answer: Three ways — benchtop, wall-mounted, or built-in — so it fits the space actually available rather than requiring space to be cleared.

faqs.question: Does it extend the life of downstream systems?
faqs.answer: Yes. Feeding downstream ultrapure water systems with consistent Type 2 water gives them a guaranteed longer service life.

faqs.question: What production rates are available?
faqs.answer: 5 L/h and 10 L/h, depending on the configuration selected.

longForm.heroHook: 5 to 15 MΩ·cm, held steady. No resin swap, no purity drift between services.
longForm.heroLead: Cartridge-based deionizers start strong and decline. Resistivity drops as the resin exhausts, and the water feeding a media prep or an autoclave in week six isn't the water that fed it in week one — which is exactly the kind of variable that quietly undermines reproducibility. Arium Advance EDI works differently. Patented electrodeionization runs continuously, holding Type 2 pure water at 5 to 15 MΩ·cm at production rates up to 10 L/h, connected straight to the potable feed. Oxidants, heavy metal ions, and particulates come out reliably, with the highest ion retention rates alongside optimum purified water yield. iJust software reads the actual feed water condition and adapts to it, tuning water usage and calculating cleaning cycles rather than running fixed intervals. Purified water then sits in the closed arium® bagtank, protected from the airborne contamination an open reservoir invites.

body.text: Arium Advance EDI connects directly to a potable feed water source and produces Type 2 pure water at rates up to 10 L/h.
Resistivity holds between 5 and 15 MΩ·cm, delivered consistently rather than declining across a service interval.
Proprietary, patented electrodeionization sits at the core, achieving the highest ion retention rates while maintaining an optimum yield of purified water.
Oxidants, heavy metal ions, and particulates are reliably removed from the incoming feed water.
iJust software makes the best use of the initial feed water condition specifically, adapting to what's actually coming in rather than assuming a fixed input quality.
The same software enhances purified water quality, reduces water usage compared with conventional systems, and calculates optimal cleaning cycles.
Purified water is stored in the closed arium® bagtank system, which protects it from secondary contamination between production and point of use.
The touch-function display responds through gloves, with structured menu navigation that removes guesswork from routine operation.
Installation works three ways — benchtop, wall-mounted, or built-in — so the system fits the space the lab has rather than requiring space to be made.
Feeding downstream ultrapure water systems with this Type 2 water gives them a guaranteed longer service life.

sections.tabSummary: What holding 5–15 MΩ·cm actually delivers

items: Electrodeionization removes ions continuously using an electrical field rather than depleting a fixed pool of exchange capacity, which is why purity holds instead of declining as a cartridge would.
That continuity is what makes 5 to 15 MΩ·cm a working range rather than a peak figure — the water produced late in a service interval matches the water produced early in it.
The highest ion retention rates come alongside an optimum yield of purified water, so purity isn't achieved by rejecting an unreasonable proportion of the feed.
Oxidants, heavy metal ions, and particulates are all removed reliably, covering the contaminant classes that most commonly compromise media preparation and analytical solution work.
Downstream ultrapure systems fed with this water get a guaranteed longer life, because their own polishing consumables aren't compensating for an inconsistent input.
The closed bagtank protects that consistency after production — quality achieved at the membrane isn't given back to airborne contamination in an open storage vessel.

body: Feed water quality isn't uniform. It varies by site, by season, and sometimes by day, and a system that assumes a fixed input either over-treats or under-performs.
iJust makes the best use of the initial feed water conditions specifically, adapting operation to what's actually arriving rather than to an assumed baseline.
Cleaning cycles are calculated from that real condition instead of running to a fixed timer, so the system cleans when it needs to and not on a schedule that ignores it.
Water usage drops compared with conventional systems, which matters directly wherever feed water is metered, restricted, or carries real cost.
Purified water quality improves alongside that economy — iJust enhances quality rather than trading purity for lower consumption.
The touch-function display keeps all of it accessible: a light touch works through gloves, and structured menu navigation means routine control doesn't require interpreting the system.

sections.title: Automatic Backflushing and Membrane Life
sections.tabSummary: What self-cleaning membranes change day to day

items: RO membranes foul. Rejected salts, particulates, and organics accumulate on the membrane surface, and left alone that layer reduces both flux and retention performance over time.
Arium Advance RO backflushes the membrane automatically using purified water, reversing flow to lift that accumulation off the surface before it consolidates.
Because the backflush uses purified water rather than raw feed, the cleaning step doesn't reintroduce the contaminants it's meant to be removing.
Automatic means it happens on the system's schedule, not the lab's — no operator step, no reminder, no dependence on someone remembering during a busy week.
The practical result is retention performance held closer to specification across the membrane's life, and a membrane that reaches its replacement point later rather than sooner.
iJust sits alongside it, calculating optimal cleaning cycles from actual system condition rather than running fixed intervals that ignore what's really happening at the membrane.

body: Under-sizing a Type 3 system turns it into a bottleneck: glassware waits, autoclaves wait, and the downstream ultrapure polisher runs short. Over-sizing pays for capacity that never gets used.
Three constant flow rates — 8, 16, and 24 L/h — let the system be matched to real daily demand instead of forcing a compromise in either direction.
Constant flow matters as much as the number itself: output stays predictable, so the volume available in an hour is the volume planned for.
The same flexibility runs through installation. Benchtop, wall-mounted, and built-in formats all work, so a lab short on bench space isn't excluded from the system.
iJust makes the best use of available water resources across whichever rate is selected, reducing consumption without giving up product water quality.
The closed bagtank protects produced water regardless of rate, so a higher-throughput configuration doesn't mean more water sitting exposed to airborne contamination.

sections.title: How Impedance Flow Cytometry Works
sections.description: Most bacterial concentration methods measure something correlated with cell count, like light absorbance, and infer the actual number from there. BactoBox measures the cells themselves. As bacterial cells pass individually through a microfluidic channel, they're counted electrically, based on the impedance each cell creates as it moves through. That's what makes the result a direct count rather than an inferred estimate. The full workflow takes three steps: sample your culture, dilute it to fall within BactoBox's working range, and insert it for a roughly two-minute measurement. Because the measurement is direct and fast, it's practical to sample repeatedly through a culture's growth, building an actual growth curve from real data points rather than a handful of widely spaced estimates.
