sections.title: How Impedance Flow Cytometry Works
sections.description: Most bacterial concentration methods measure something correlated with cell count, like light absorbance, and infer the actual number from there. BactoBox measures the cells themselves. As bacterial cells pass individually through a microfluidic channel, they're counted electrically, based on the impedance each cell creates as it moves through. That's what makes the result a direct count rather than an inferred estimate. The full workflow takes three steps: sample your culture, dilute it to fall within BactoBox's working range, and insert it for a roughly two-minute measurement. Because the measurement is direct and fast, it's practical to sample repeatedly through a culture's growth, building an actual growth curve from real data points rather than a handful of widely spaced estimates.

sections.title: Visualizing Real Growth Kinetics
sections.description: A growth curve built from absorbance readings shows you a proxy signal changing over time. A growth curve built from BactoBox shows you the actual population.
body: Every measurement feeds directly into a live growth curve, plotting cell concentration in actual cells/mL rather than arbitrary absorbance units. That distinction matters directly for identifying lag, exponential, and stationary phases with certainty, since you're reading the real population dynamics rather than inferring them through an indirect signal. Runs can be overlaid to compare strains, media formulations, or process conditions side by side, and the underlying data exports cleanly for further analysis in whatever tools your team already uses.

sections.title: Energy Monitoring and Precision Control
sections.description: A small-volume sonicator lives or dies on precision, since there's far less margin for error in a 150 µL sample than in a full-liter batch. The digital wattmeter and energy monitor track power and delivered energy continuously during a run, so exactly how much energy a sample received is never a guess. Automatic tuning and amplitude compensation adjust output on the fly as sample viscosity, temperature, or composition shifts mid-process, keeping delivered energy consistent even when the sample itself isn't perfectly uniform. The independent ON/OFF pulser, adjustable in 1-second increments from 1 to 59 seconds, gives fine control over intermittent cycling for samples sensitive to continuous sonication.

sections.title: Probe and Volume Range
sections.description: The standard probe covers a solid working range on its own, and accessories extend that range further in either direction depending on what your samples actually need.
body: The included ¼" (6mm) titanium alloy probe handles 10 to 50 mL directly, autoclavable for workflows that require repeated sterilization between samples. For volumes below that range, down toward 150 µL, dedicated microtip and smaller-diameter probe accessories are available, suited to precious or limited-quantity samples. On the higher end, up to 150 mL, alternative probe configurations extend coverage without stepping up to a higher-power VCX model. An air-cooled converter option is also available for labs running longer or more frequent processing cycles where heat buildup in the converter itself becomes a factor.

longForm.heroHook: 750 watts of programmable ultrasonic power, from 200 µL microsamples up to 2 L batches.
longForm.heroLead: Cell lysis, homogenization, emulsification, or nanoparticle dispersion all demand different amounts of ultrasonic energy delivered precisely, not just applied longer or shorter. VCX-750 gives you that precision directly. A 750 W, 20 kHz microprocessor-based system, it's fully programmable through intuitive, easy-to-navigate screens, with energy setpoint and temperature monitoring built in for reproducible results across every run. A standard ½" diameter titanium alloy probe with a replaceable tip ships with the system, and a wide range of horns and accessories extends processing across 200 µL to 2 L, depending on the probe or accessory selected.

Control is fully programmable through a microprocessor-based interface, with intuitive, easy-to-navigate screens rather than a fixed dial or switch setup.

Wattage and energy are both displayed directly during operation, giving real-time visibility into exactly how much energy a sample has received.

sections.eyebrow: Reproducible Sonication Through Energy Setpoint Control
sections.title: Reproducible Sonication Through Energy Setpoint Control
sections.description: Timing a sonication run by seconds alone assumes every sample absorbs energy at the same rate, and that assumption rarely holds across different batches, viscosities, or sample volumes. VCX-750's energy setpoint control sidesteps that problem entirely by dosing sonication in Joules delivered rather than time elapsed. Two samples that process at different rates still receive the same total energy input, keeping results comparable across a study or production run. Temperature monitoring runs in parallel, so a run that's delivering energy efficiently and heating a sample faster than expected can be caught and managed before it affects results. Wattage and energy both display in real time, so the actual dose delivered is always visible, not just the setpoint targeted.

The standard ½" diameter probe, built from Ti6Al4V titanium alloy with a replaceable tip, ships with the base VCX-750 configuration and covers general-purpose sonication work directly. Optional additions, a stand with clamp for hands-free operation, a sound enclosure for noise containment, and a dedicated temperature probe, round out the system for labs running it as a fixed workstation rather than a bench-to-bench tool.

sections.title: Energy Monitoring and Precision Control
sections.description: A small-volume sonicator lives or dies on precision, since there's far less margin for error in a 150 µL sample than in a full-liter batch. The digital wattmeter and energy monitor track power and delivered energy continuously during a run, so exactly how much energy a sample received is never a guess. Automatic tuning and amplitude compensation adjust output on the fly as sample viscosity, temperature, or composition shifts mid-process, keeping delivered energy consistent even when the sample itself isn't perfectly uniform. The independent ON/OFF pulser, adjustable in 1-second increments from 1 to 59 seconds, gives fine control over intermittent cycling for samples sensitive to continuous sonication.

sections.title: Probe and Volume Range
sections.description: The standard probe covers a solid working range on its own, and accessories extend that range further in either direction depending on what your samples actually need.
body: The included ¼" (6mm) titanium alloy probe handles 10 to 50 mL directly, autoclavable for workflows that require repeated sterilization between samples. For volumes below that range, down toward 150 µL, dedicated microtip and smaller-diameter probe accessories are available, suited to precious or limited-quantity samples. On the higher end, up to 150 mL, alternative probe configurations extend coverage without stepping up to a higher-power VCX model. An air-cooled converter option is also available for labs running longer or more frequent processing cycles where heat buildup in the converter itself becomes a factor.

sections.eyebrow: Reproducible Sonication Through Energy Setpoint Control
sections.title: Reproducible Sonication Through Energy Setpoint Control
sections.description: Timing a sonication run by seconds alone assumes every sample absorbs energy at the same rate, and that assumption rarely holds across different batches, viscosities, or sample volumes. VCX-750's energy setpoint control sidesteps that problem entirely by dosing sonication in Joules delivered rather than time elapsed. Two samples that process at different rates still receive the same total energy input, keeping results comparable across a study or production run. Temperature monitoring runs in parallel, so a run that's delivering energy efficiently and heating a sample faster than expected can be caught and managed before it affects results. Wattage and energy both display in real time, so the actual dose delivered is always visible, not just the setpoint targeted.

sections.eyebrow: Sample Protection: Dri-Pure and eXalt Technology
sections.title: Sample Protection: Dri-Pure and eXalt Technology
body: Two named technologies handle two different risks during evaporation: violent bumping that can damage or lose a sample, and uncontrolled crystallization that ruins a polymorph study before it starts.

Dri-Pure anti-bumping technology works alongside advanced temperature control to keep the evaporation process gentle and predictable, protecting the sample itself rather than just monitoring the process. eXalt technology takes the opposite approach for crystallization work, using controlled evaporation deliberately to produce usable crystals for polymorph screening and related studies, rather than treating crystallization as something to avoid.

sections.title: Steam Heating and Sample Recovery
body: Two things usually cost you time and sample after evaporation: waiting for a slow heating method, and transferring the concentrated sample somewhere else afterward. Rocket Synergy 2 addresses both directly.

Low-pressure steam heating maximizes drying efficiency, and the chamber design is specifically built to keep moisture from reaching the sample during the process. On the recovery side, Flip-Flop and SampleGenie let concentration or drying happen directly in the storage or autosampler vial the sample is going to live in anyway, which is what actually improves recovery and keeps results consistent from one sample to the next, rather than losing material in a transfer step.

sections.title: SpeedTrap Condenser and Freeze-Drying Capability
body: Removing trace water from a sample usually means switching to a separate freeze dryer. The SpeedTrap condenser is built to avoid that step for low-volume work.

Reaching an ultimate low temperature of -50°C, it freeze-dries very low volumes of water directly within the same evaporation workflow. That matters most for the DNA model's core job, clearing the trace water and volatile solvents that would otherwise interfere with PCR and NGS, but it's a capability available across the line where freeze-drying is selected as an option.

sections.eyebrow: Sample Protection: Dri-Pure and eXalt Technology
sections.title: Sample Protection: Dri-Pure and eXalt Technology
body: Two named technologies handle two different risks during evaporation: violent bumping that can damage or lose a sample, and uncontrolled crystallization that ruins a polymorph study before it starts.

Dri-Pure anti-bumping technology works alongside advanced temperature control to keep the evaporation process gentle and predictable, protecting the sample itself rather than just monitoring the process. eXalt technology takes the opposite approach for crystallization work, using controlled evaporation deliberately to produce usable crystals for polymorph screening and related studies, rather than treating crystallization as something to avoid.

sections.title: How Continuous Flow Hydrogenation Works
sections.tabSummary: The real six-step reaction mechanism
body: The whole process runs as a continuous flow, not a batch reaction sitting in a flask.

Hydrogen is generated on demand by electrolysis of water, right inside the system. An HPLC pump brings in pure solvent, which mixes with that hydrogen through a mixing valve, and the resulting gas-liquid mixture runs through the reaction zone while the system stabilizes at your chosen pressure, temperature, and flow rate. Once those conditions are reached, you switch the input from solvent to your actual reactant solution. The reaction happens as the mixture passes through the packed CatCart column, where the solid catalyst stays behind while the product moves on to the collection vial.

longForm.heroHook: Runs on hydrogen, or any of 13 other gases. Same mass flow controller.
heroParagraphs: Most flow hydrogenation systems do one thing well: hydrogen, in-situ, and that's it. This one doesn't stop there.

A built-in mass flow controller doses in-situ hydrogen at 99.9% purity, or switches to any of 13 external gases, from oxygen and carbon monoxide to argon and ethylene, through the same external gas inlet.
The water reservoir is external and detachable, so refilling and cleaning don't mean opening the system up. A next-generation single-cell electrolysis design extends cell life and cuts maintenance.

It runs from 0°C to 150°C, atmospheric pressure to 100 bar, and connects to a full fleet: a high-temperature Reactor Module, the 450°C/200 bar Phoenix Flow Reactor, and a Brooks Autosampler for fully automated catalyst screening, all coordinated from one screen.

faqs.question: What is the H-Genie® Lite used for?
faqs.answer: It's a standalone hydrogen gas generator, used to replace a hydrogen cylinder by producing hydrogen from water on demand, up to 50 bar.

faqs.question: What quality water does the H-Genie Lite need?
faqs.answer: Deionized water with a recommended conductivity below 1 µS/cm.

faqs.question: Where should the H-Genie Lite be used?
faqs.answer: In a ventilated laboratory fume hood, which it's specifically sized to fit, and it can be relocated to wherever hydrogen is needed next.

faqs.question: How do I set up the H-Genie Lite for a run?
faqs.answer: Set the required pressure or time on the touchscreen, then press start; the workflow is stated to be learnable in about one minute.

faqs.question: How do I extend runtime for longer or unattended operation?
faqs.answer: Add the Automatic Water Filler accessory, which detects a low tank and refills automatically from a built-in or external water source, monitoring Millipore Milli-Q water quality throughout.

faqs.question: Can the H-Genie Lite perform reactions like deuteration?
faqs.answer: No. It generates hydrogen gas; it doesn't run chemical reactions itself. Reactions like deuteration are performed by systems such as the H-Cube, which this generator could potentially supply.

faqs.question: Can generated hydrogen be stored?
faqs.answer: The system is built for on-demand generation and use; storage isn't described in the confirmed materials, and this is worth confirming directly with Inkarp for your specific setup.

faqs.question: Is the H-Genie Lite compatible with ThalesNano's fleet systems?
faqs.answer: Yes, via the Automatic Water Filler accessory, which connects to the Phoenix – H-Genie platform or the broader Instrument Fleet through the same THS System Controller used with H-Cube Advance.

faqs.question: What is the difference between the H-Genie Lite and the full H-Genie?
faqs.answer: The Lite is a streamlined, more affordable version focused on essential features; full comparison detail against the H-Genie II is confirmed by Inkarp.

faqs.question: What is the price of the H-Genie® Lite in India?
faqs.answer: The price depends on whether you add the Automatic Water Filler or fleet integration. Contact Inkarp for a quotation once your requirements are confirmed.

faqs.question: Who is the authorized distributor of the H-Genie® Lite in India?
faqs.answer: Inkarp is the authorized distributor and service provider for the ThalesNano H-Genie® Lite in India, providing demonstration, installation, training, AMC, spare parts, and technical support.

sections.tabSummary: What leak detection and water quality actually protect
body: Replacing a hydrogen cylinder only works if the replacement is genuinely safer, and that comes down to continuous monitoring, not just a different generation method.

Internal hydrogen leak detectors run throughout operation, alongside whatever other safety features the system carries. Water quality has its own requirement too: deionized water below 1 µS/cm conductivity, consumed at 200 mL/hr from a 3-liter reservoir, which gives a working runtime before a refill is needed. The recommended installation, a ventilated fume hood, is stated directly rather than left implicit.

faqs.question: What is the H-Genie® II used for?
faqs.answer: It's an award-winning standalone hydrogen gas generator, used to replace hydrogen cylinders while producing hydrogen from water at up to 100 bar and 99.99% purity.

faqs.question: What quality water does the H-Genie II need?
faqs.answer: Deionized water with a recommended conductivity below 1 µS/cm.

faqs.question: Where should the H-Genie II be used?
faqs.answer: In a ventilated laboratory fume hood, and it's suitable for use in any laboratory setting.

faqs.question: How do I check if my reactor is compatible with H-Genie II?
faqs.answer: Confirm your setup type: CatCarts, MidiCarts, coiled reactors, metal-metal sealed catalyst columns, and standard balloon setups are all confirmed compatible.

faqs.question: How do I access exported consumption data?
faqs.answer: The system monitors hydrogen consumption automatically during each run, with data export functionality built in for documentation and process records.

faqs.question: Can the H-Genie II perform reactions like deuteration?
faqs.answer: No. It generates hydrogen gas; it doesn't run chemical reactions itself. Reactions like deuteration are performed by a connected reactor system, which this generator can supply.

faqs.question: Can generated hydrogen be stored?
faqs.answer: The system is built for on-demand generation and use; storage isn't described in the confirmed materials, and this is worth confirming directly with Inkarp.

faqs.question: What is the Phoenix platform, and does it work with H-Genie II?
faqs.answer: Yes. Paired with the Phoenix Flow Reactor, the combined platform reaches 450°C and 200 bar, combining high-pressure hydrogen generation with high-temperature reactor capability.

faqs.question: What is the difference between H-Genie II and H-Genie Lite?
faqs.answer: H-Genie II reaches double the pressure (100 bar versus 50 bar), a full purity grade higher (99.99% versus 99.9%), and adds consumption data export that Lite doesn't offer.

faqs.question: What is the price of the H-Genie® II in India?
faqs.answer: The price depends on whether you add the Phoenix Flow Reactor or Automatic Water Filler. Contact Inkarp for a quotation once your requirements are confirmed.

faqs.question: Who is the authorized distributor of the H-Genie® II in India?
faqs.answer: Inkarp is the authorized distributor and service provider for the ThalesNano H-Genie® II in India, providing demonstration, installation, training, AMC, spare parts, and technical support.

faqs.question: What is the Phoenix™ II Flow Reactor used for?
faqs.answer: It's a high-temperature, high-pressure flow reactor used for novel compound synthesis, reaching 450°C and 200 bar for both homogeneous and heterogeneous chemistry.

faqs.question: Can I purchase only the Phoenix Flow Reactor, without other modules?
faqs.answer: Yes. The base system covers reactions like SNAr, Boc-removal, and alkylations on its own; modules are added when your application needs hydrogenation, gas dosing, or fleet integration.

faqs.question: Can I use the Phoenix Flow Reactor without connecting it to other devices?
faqs.answer: Yes, for base-configuration applications. Modules like H-Genie or the Gas Module extend it into hydrogenation, oxidation, and other gas-based chemistry when needed.

faqs.question: How do I choose the right heated element for my reaction?
faqs.answer: Match your chemistry type: PTFE, stainless steel, or Hastelloy loops for homogeneous reactions, or CatCarts, MidiCarts, and metal-metal sealed cartridges for heterogeneous catalyst-based reactions.

faqs.question: How do I add hydrogenation capability to the Phoenix Flow Reactor?
faqs.answer: Add the H-Genie module for up to 100 bar at 99.99% purity, or H-Genie Lite for up to 50 bar at 99.9% purity, depending on your pressure requirement.

faqs.question: What types of chemical reactions can be performed with the Phoenix Flow Reactor?
faqs.answer: SNAr reactions, Boc-removal, Claisen rearrangement, C- and N-alkylation, supercritical reactions, and heterocycle synthesis in the base configuration, with hydrogenation, oxidation, and carbonylation available through additional modules.

faqs.question: Is gas phase catalytic reaction possible on the Phoenix Flow Reactor?
faqs.answer: The Gas Module and Gas Module Plus support precise dosing of 14 different gases, which supports gas-based catalytic work; confirm your specific reaction with Inkarp.

faqs.question: Can I select only the elements or modules I actually need?
faqs.answer: Yes. The modular design is built specifically for this, letting you build and customize the system around your application rather than take a fixed configuration.

faqs.question: What is the difference between the Phoenix II and the Phoenix – H-Genie Platform?
faqs.answer: The Phoenix II is the standalone reactor, with hydrogen generation added separately via the H-Genie module. The Phoenix – H-Genie Platform is a combined, pre-integrated system; full comparison detail is confirmed by Inkarp.

faqs.question: What is the price of the Phoenix™ II Flow Reactor in India?
faqs.answer: The price depends on the heated elements and modules your application needs. Contact Inkarp for a quotation once your target reactions are confirmed.

faqs.answer: Inkarp is the authorized distributor and service provider for the ThalesNano Phoenix™ II Flow Reactor in India, providing demonstration, installation, training, AMC, spare parts, and technical support.

faqs.question: What is the Phoenix – H-Genie® Platform used for?
faqs.answer: It's a combined high-temperature reactor and on-demand hydrogen generation system, used for hydrogenation and related synthetic chemistry from milligram screening to kilogram-scale production.

faqs.question: What is the maximum pressure this platform reaches for hydrogenation?
faqs.answer: Up to 100 bar, which is the ceiling set by the H-Genie hydrogen generator's own output; the Phoenix reactor hardware itself supports up to 200 bar with an alternative gas source.

faqs.question: How does this differ from the standalone Phoenix II Flow Reactor?
faqs.answer: Hydrogenation is included as standard here, while the standalone Phoenix II requires adding H-Genie or H-Genie Lite separately as a module.

faqs.question: How do I scale a reaction from screening to production on this platform?
faqs.answer: Start with self-fillable cartridges at milligram scale for catalyst optimization, then move to larger CatCart or cartridge configurations as the reaction scales toward kilogram quantities, without changing platforms.

faqs.question: How do I integrate my existing HPLC pump or mass flow controller?
faqs.answer: Confirm your equipment brand: Bronkhorst mass flow controllers, Knauer or Eldex Optos HPLC pumps, and Vici selector valves are all confirmed compatible, with custom integrations available for other equipment.

faqs.question: Can this platform run multiple experiments or devices at once?
faqs.answer: Yes. THS ReAction Software supports consecutive, parallel, and failover fleet operation, built for laboratory optimization and scale-up work specifically.

faqs.question: Can parameters be changed during a running experiment?
faqs.answer: Yes. Temperature, hydrogen pressure, and flow rate all adjust on the fly, without stopping the run.

faqs.question: Is data from each run exportable?
faqs.answer: Yes. The built-in mass flow controller monitors and exports hydrogen pressure and flow data for analysis and record-keeping.

faqs.question: What chemistry does this platform support?
faqs.answer: Hydrogenation, oxidation, carbonylation, SNAr reactions, Boc-removal, Claisen rearrangement, C- and N-alkylation, supercritical reactions, and heterocycle synthesis.

faqs.question: What is the price of the Phoenix – H-Genie® Platform in India?
faqs.answer: The price depends on your scale requirements and any third-party equipment integration needed. Contact Inkarp for a quotation once your application is confirmed.

products.overview: Four wavelengths at full intensity, at once. The original managed one. Running multiple light wavelengths together used to mean turning the intensity down. PhotoCube Plus doesn't make that trade. It runs four wavelengths simultaneously, at full intensity, where the original PhotoCube could only manage one before intensity had to drop. Any commercially available wavelength from 257 to 650 nm is usable, not a fixed set. An optional cooler module holds vials at 10–15°C at maximum LED power; without it, that same power runs at 40–50°C. The choice is real and it matters for reaction control. It's the first ThalesNano system built for both batch and flow. Four vials in batch mode, or an 8 mL loop in continuous flow, at 0.1 to 10 mL/min, on the same device.

faqs.question: What is the PhotoCube™ Plus used for?
faqs.answer: It's an LED photochemistry reactor used for reactions including bromination, C-C coupling, the Minisci reaction, and thiol-ene click chemistry, in both batch and continuous flow.

faqs.question: How many wavelengths can run at once?
faqs.answer: Up to four, at full intensity, a genuine improvement over the original PhotoCube's limit of one wavelength at high intensity.

faqs.question: How do I choose between batch and flow mode?
faqs.answer: Use batch mode with 4x4 mL or 4x30 mL vials for screening and method development, or flow mode with an 8 mL loop at 0.1 to 10 mL/min for continuous, scaled-up production.

faqs.question: How do I set up cooling for a temperature-sensitive reaction?
faqs.answer: Add the optional cooler module, which uses cold finger technology to hold vials at 10 to 15°C at maximum LED power, compared to 40 to 50°C without it.

faqs.question: What wavelength range is available?
faqs.answer: Any commercially available wavelength from 257 to 650 nm, with a basic configuration of 365, 457, 523, and 625 nm, and custom wavelengths available on request.

faqs.question: Is the PhotoCube Plus safe to open while running?
faqs.answer: Yes. Opening the device door triggers an automatic lighting shutdown.

faqs.question: What pumps are compatible with the PhotoCube Plus?
faqs.answer: Knauer HPLC pumps (10 or 50 mL/min) and Eldex Optos HPLC pumps (up to 80 mL/min) are both confirmed compatible.

faqs.question: Can the PhotoCube Plus connect to ThalesNano's fleet system?
faqs.answer: Yes, through the THS System Controller and THS RS232-CAN Converter, using THS ReAction Software for remote and automated control.

faqs.question: What is the difference between PhotoCube Plus and the original PhotoCube?
faqs.answer: PhotoCube Plus runs four wavelengths at full intensity simultaneously versus the original's one, covers an open 257-650 nm range instead of a fixed set, and adds a proper cooler module and fleet compatibility the original didn't have.

faqs.question: What is the price of the PhotoCube™ Plus in India?
faqs.answer: The price depends on whether you include the cooler module and any custom wavelength requirements. Contact Inkarp for a quotation once your application is confirmed.

faqs.question: Who is the authorized distributor of the PhotoCube™ Plus in India?
faqs.answer: Inkarp is the authorized distributor and service provider for the ThalesNano PhotoCube™ Plus in India, providing demonstration, installation, training, AMC, spare parts, and technical support.

sections.title: How Continuous Flow Hydrogenation Works
sections.tabSummary: The real six-step reaction mechanism
body: The whole process runs as a continuous flow, not a batch reaction sitting in a flask.

Hydrogen is generated on demand by electrolysis of water, right inside the system. An HPLC pump brings in pure solvent, which mixes with that hydrogen through a mixing valve, and the resulting gas-liquid mixture runs through the reaction zone while the system stabilizes at your chosen pressure, temperature, and flow rate. Once those conditions are reached, you switch the input from solvent to your actual reactant solution. The reaction happens as the mixture passes through the packed CatCart column, where the solid catalyst stays behind while the product moves on to the collection vial.

faqs.question: What is the H-Cube® Advance used for?
faqs.answer: It's a continuous flow reactor used for catalytic hydrogenation, catalyst screening, and related reactions, running on in-situ hydrogen or any of 13 external gas types.

faqs.question: What gases can the H-Cube Advance run besides hydrogen?
faqs.answer: Oxygen, nitrogen, carbon monoxide, carbon dioxide, air, argon, ethylene, ethane, methane, helium, nitrous oxide, nitrogen monoxide, and external hydrogen, all through the built-in mass flow controller.

faqs.question: How do I set up the H-Cube Advance for a reaction requiring an external gas?
faqs.answer: Confirm your required gas is on the supported list, connect it through the external gas inlet, and the built-in mass flow controller doses it precisely alongside your solvent and reactant stream.

faqs.question: How do I automate catalyst screening on the H-Cube Advance?
faqs.answer: Connect the Brooks AIM3300 Autosampler via the THS System Controller, which automates continuous liquid sample handling for unattended optimization studies or catalyst screening.

faqs.question: What is the difference between the H-Cube Advance and the H-Cube Mini Plus?
faqs.answer: The Advance supports 13 external gas types beyond hydrogen, reaches a wider temperature range (0 to 150°C versus ambient to 100°C), and connects to fleet modules the Mini Plus doesn't support; the Mini Plus is a more compact, standard-hydrogenation-only system.

faqs.question: What is the Phoenix Flow Reactor?
faqs.answer: An optional add-on module with an extended parameter window, up to 450°C and 200 bar, for synthesizing novel compounds beyond the base system's range.

faqs.question: Is the H-Cube Advance compatible with an autosampler?
faqs.answer: Yes, with the Brooks AIM3300 Autosampler, connected via the THS System Controller for fully automated liquid sample handling.

faqs.question: What is the purity of the hydrogen produced in-situ?
faqs.answer: 3.0 grade, 99.9% purity.

faqs.question: Does the H-Cube Advance need external equipment to run?
faqs.answer: Only an external ThalesNano HPLC or Knauer pump; the system valve, pressure sensor, and mixer module are all built in.

faqs.question: What is the price of the H-Cube® Advance in India?
faqs.answer: The price depends on the gas configuration and fleet modules your application needs. Contact Inkarp for a quotation once your requirements are confirmed.

faqs.question: Who is the authorized distributor of the H-Cube® Advance in India?
faqs.answer: Inkarp is the authorized distributor and service provider for the ThalesNano H-Cube® Advance in India, providing demonstration, installation, training, AMC, spare parts, and technical support.

faqs.question: What is the H-Genie® Lite used for?
faqs.answer: It's a standalone hydrogen gas generator, used to replace a hydrogen cylinder by producing hydrogen from water on demand, up to 50 bar.

faqs.question: What quality water does the H-Genie Lite need?
faqs.answer: Deionized water with a recommended conductivity below 1 µS/cm.

faqs.question: Where should the H-Genie Lite be used?
faqs.answer: In a ventilated laboratory fume hood, which it's specifically sized to fit, and it can be relocated to wherever hydrogen is needed next.

faqs.question: How do I set up the H-Genie Lite for a run?
faqs.answer: Set the required pressure or time on the touchscreen, then press start; the workflow is stated to be learnable in about one minute.

faqs.question: How do I extend runtime for longer or unattended operation?

faqs.question: What is the H-Genie® II used for?
faqs.answer: It's an award-winning standalone hydrogen gas generator, used to replace hydrogen cylinders while producing hydrogen from water at up to 100 bar and 99.99% purity.

faqs.question: What quality water does the H-Genie II need?
faqs.answer: Deionized water with a recommended conductivity below 1 µS/cm.

faqs.question: Where should the H-Genie II be used?
faqs.answer: In a ventilated laboratory fume hood, and it's suitable for use in any laboratory setting.

faqs.question: How do I check if my reactor is compatible with H-Genie II?
faqs.answer: Confirm your setup type: CatCarts, MidiCarts, coiled reactors, metal-metal sealed catalyst columns, and standard balloon setups are all confirmed compatible.

faqs.question: How do I access exported consumption data?
faqs.answer: The system monitors hydrogen consumption automatically during each run, with data export functionality built in for documentation and process records.

faqs.question: Can the H-Genie II perform reactions like deuteration?
faqs.answer: No. It generates hydrogen gas; it doesn't run chemical reactions itself. Reactions like deuteration are performed by a connected reactor system, which this generator can supply.

faqs.question: Can generated hydrogen be stored?
faqs.answer: The system is built for on-demand generation and use; storage isn't described in the confirmed materials, and this is worth confirming directly with Inkarp.

faqs.question: What is the Phoenix platform, and does it work with H-Genie II?
faqs.answer: Yes. Paired with the Phoenix Flow Reactor, the combined platform reaches 450°C and 200 bar, combining high-pressure hydrogen generation with high-temperature reactor capability.

faqs.question: What is the difference between H-Genie II and H-Genie Lite?
faqs.answer: H-Genie II reaches double the pressure (100 bar versus 50 bar), a full purity grade higher (99.99% versus 99.9%), and adds consumption data export that Lite doesn't offer.

faqs.question: What is the Phoenix™ II Flow Reactor used for?
faqs.answer: It's a high-temperature, high-pressure flow reactor used for novel compound synthesis, reaching 450°C and 200 bar for both homogeneous and heterogeneous chemistry.

faqs.question: Can I purchase only the Phoenix Flow Reactor, without other modules?
faqs.answer: Yes. The base system covers reactions like SNAr, Boc-removal, and alkylations on its own; modules are added when your application needs hydrogenation, gas dosing, or fleet integration.

faqs.question: Can I use the Phoenix Flow Reactor without connecting it to other devices?
faqs.answer: Yes, for base-configuration applications. Modules like H-Genie or the Gas Module extend it into hydrogenation, oxidation, and other gas-based chemistry when needed.

faqs.question: How do I choose the right heated element for my reaction?
faqs.answer: Match your chemistry type: PTFE, stainless steel, or Hastelloy loops for homogeneous reactions, or CatCarts, MidiCarts, and metal-metal sealed cartridges for heterogeneous catalyst-based reactions.

faqs.question: How do I add hydrogenation capability to the Phoenix Flow Reactor?
faqs.answer: Add the H-Genie module for up to 100 bar at 99.99% purity, or H-Genie Lite for up to 50 bar at 99.9% purity, depending on your pressure requirement.

faqs.question: What types of chemical reactions can be performed with the Phoenix Flow Reactor?
faqs.answer: SNAr reactions, Boc-removal, Claisen rearrangement, C- and N-alkylation, supercritical reactions, and heterocycle synthesis in the base configuration, with hydrogenation, oxidation, and carbonylation available through additional modules.

faqs.question: Is gas phase catalytic reaction possible on the Phoenix Flow Reactor?
faqs.answer: The Gas Module and Gas Module Plus support precise dosing of 14 different gases, which supports gas-based catalytic work; confirm your specific reaction with Inkarp.

faqs.question: Can I select only the elements or modules I actually need?
faqs.answer: Yes. The modular design is built specifically for this, letting you build and customize the system around your application rather than take a fixed configuration.

faqs.question: What is the difference between the Phoenix II and the Phoenix – H-Genie Platform?
faqs.answer: The Phoenix II is the standalone reactor, with hydrogen generation added separately via the H-Genie module. The Phoenix – H-Genie Platform is a combined, pre-integrated system; full comparison detail is confirmed by Inkarp.

faqs.question: What is the price of the Phoenix™ II Flow Reactor in India?
faqs.answer: The price depends on the heated elements and modules your application needs. Contact Inkarp for a quotation once your target reactions are confirmed.

faqs.question: Who is the authorized distributor of the Phoenix™ II Flow Reactor in India?
faqs.answer: Inkarp is the authorized distributor and service provider for the ThalesNano Phoenix™ II Flow Reactor in India, providing demonstration, installation, training, AMC, spare parts, and technical support.

faqs.question: What is the Phoenix – H-Genie® Platform used for?
faqs.answer: It's a combined high-temperature reactor and on-demand hydrogen generation system, used for hydrogenation and related synthetic chemistry from milligram screening to kilogram-scale production.

faqs.question: What is the maximum pressure this platform reaches for hydrogenation?
faqs.answer: Up to 100 bar, which is the ceiling set by the H-Genie hydrogen generator's own output; the Phoenix reactor hardware itself supports up to 200 bar with an alternative gas source.

faqs.question: How does this differ from the standalone Phoenix II Flow Reactor?
faqs.answer: Hydrogenation is included as standard here, while the standalone Phoenix II requires adding H-Genie or H-Genie Lite separately as a module.

faqs.question: How do I scale a reaction from screening to production on this platform?
faqs.answer: Start with self-fillable cartridges at milligram scale for catalyst optimization, then move to larger CatCart or cartridge configurations as the reaction scales toward kilogram quantities, without changing platforms.

faqs.question: How do I integrate my existing HPLC pump or mass flow controller?
faqs.answer: Confirm your equipment brand: Bronkhorst mass flow controllers, Knauer or Eldex Optos HPLC pumps, and Vici selector valves are all confirmed compatible, with custom integrations available for other equipment.

faqs.question: Can this platform run multiple experiments or devices at once?
faqs.answer: Yes. THS ReAction Software supports consecutive, parallel, and failover fleet operation, built for laboratory optimization and scale-up work specifically.

faqs.question: Can parameters be changed during a running experiment?
faqs.answer: Yes. Temperature, hydrogen pressure, and flow rate all adjust on the fly, without stopping the run.

faqs.question: Is data from each run exportable?
faqs.answer: Yes. The built-in mass flow controller monitors and exports hydrogen pressure and flow data for analysis and record-keeping.

faqs.question: What chemistry does this platform support?
faqs.answer: Hydrogenation, oxidation, carbonylation, SNAr reactions, Boc-removal, Claisen rearrangement, C- and N-alkylation, supercritical reactions, and heterocycle synthesis.

Phoenix's high-temperature reactor pairs directly with H-Genie's on-demand hydrogen generation, reaching 450°C and up to 100 bar, without a hydrogen cylinder anywhere in the lab. Self-fillable cartridges and CatCarts scale the same chemistry from milligrams up to kilograms.

faqs.question: What is the PhotoCube™ Plus used for?
faqs.answer: It's an LED photochemistry reactor used for reactions including bromination, C-C coupling, the Minisci reaction, and thiol-ene click chemistry, in both batch and continuous flow.

faqs.question: How many wavelengths can run at once?
faqs.answer: Up to four, at full intensity, a genuine improvement over the original PhotoCube's limit of one wavelength at high intensity.

faqs.question: How do I choose between batch and flow mode?
faqs.answer: Use batch mode with 4x4 mL or 4x30 mL vials for screening and method development, or flow mode with an 8 mL loop at 0.1 to 10 mL/min for continuous, scaled-up production.

faqs.question: How do I set up cooling for a temperature-sensitive reaction?
faqs.answer: Add the optional cooler module, which uses cold finger technology to hold vials at 10 to 15°C at maximum LED power, compared to 40 to 50°C without it.

faqs.question: What wavelength range is available?
faqs.answer: Any commercially available wavelength from 257 to 650 nm, with a basic configuration of 365, 457, 523, and 625 nm, and custom wavelengths available on request.

faqs.question: Is the PhotoCube Plus safe to open while running?
faqs.answer: Yes. Opening the device door triggers an automatic lighting shutdown.

faqs.question: What pumps are compatible with the PhotoCube Plus?
faqs.answer: Knauer HPLC pumps (10 or 50 mL/min) and Eldex Optos HPLC pumps (up to 80 mL/min) are both confirmed compatible.

faqs.question: Can the PhotoCube Plus connect to ThalesNano's fleet system?
faqs.answer: Yes, through the THS System Controller and THS RS232-CAN Converter, using THS ReAction Software for remote and automated control.

faqs.question: What is the difference between PhotoCube Plus and the original PhotoCube?
faqs.answer: PhotoCube Plus runs four wavelengths at full intensity simultaneously versus the original's one, covers an open 257-650 nm range instead of a fixed set, and adds a proper cooler module and fleet compatibility the original didn't have.

faqs.question: What is the price of the PhotoCube™ Plus in India?
faqs.answer: The price depends on whether you include the cooler module and any custom wavelength requirements. Contact Inkarp for a quotation once your application is confirmed.

faqs.question: Who is the authorized distributor of the PhotoCube™ Plus in India?
faqs.answer: Inkarp is the authorized distributor and service provider for the ThalesNano PhotoCube™ Plus in India, providing demonstration, installation, training, AMC, spare parts, and technical support.

sections.title: Wavelength Control and Cooling Performance
sections.tabSummary: What the cooler module actually changes
body: Running photochemistry at real intensity, across multiple wavelengths, generates real heat, and that's exactly what the cooler module is built to manage.

At maximum LED power, an uncooled vial sits at 40 to 50°C. With the cooler module's cold finger technology engaged, the same power holds the vial at 10 to 15°C, a genuinely different reaction environment for temperature-sensitive photochemistry. Wavelength control runs independently of that, with up to four wavelengths operable at once, at full intensity, across the open 257–650 nm range.

sections.title: Product Information
sections.description: HAAKE Falling Ball Viscometer C product information: measurement principle, standards compliance, and included components.
body: Measuring accuracy ranks among the highest available in any type of viscometer, particularly when paired with the precise temperature control of a circulator.
The instrument measures the viscosity of transparent Newtonian liquids and gases directly, using the falling ball principle rather than powered rotational or electronic sensing.
It meets the requirements of German DIN 53015 and ISO 12058 standards, and is accepted as an official reference instrument, used to validate other viscometers rather than needing validation itself.
Viscosity range covers 0.5 to 1,000,000 cSt, across a temperature range of -20°C to +150°C.
Reproducibility stays under 0.5%, a tight tolerance for a fully manual instrument.
The falling tube and balls 1, 2, and G are borosilicate glass; balls 3, 4, 5, and 6 are nickel iron alloy, giving a range of ball densities to match different sample viscosities.
A stopwatch is required to operate the instrument; it is not included.
Applications span the chemical industry (polymer solutions, solvents), pharmaceutical industry (raw materials, glycerine), food industry (sugar solutions), and mineral oil industry (oils).

faqs.question: What is the HAAKE Falling Ball Viscometer C used for?

faqs.question: Does this instrument need a power connection?

faqs.question: Is this instrument recognized as a reference standard?

sections.title: Product Information
sections.description: HAAKE Falling Ball Viscometer C product information: measurement principle, standards compliance, and included components.
body: Measuring accuracy ranks among the highest available in any type of viscometer, particularly when paired with the precise temperature control of a circulator.
The instrument measures the viscosity of transparent Newtonian liquids and gases directly, using the falling ball principle rather than powered rotational or electronic sensing.
It meets the requirements of German DIN 53015 and ISO 12058 standards, and is accepted as an official reference instrument, used to validate other viscometers rather than needing validation itself.
Viscosity range covers 0.5 to 1,000,000 cSt, across a temperature range of -20°C to +150°C.
Reproducibility stays under 0.5%, a tight tolerance for a fully manual instrument.
The falling tube and balls 1, 2, and G are borosilicate glass; balls 3, 4, 5, and 6 are nickel iron alloy, giving a range of ball densities to match different sample viscosities.
A stopwatch is required to operate the instrument; it is not included.
Applications span the chemical industry (polymer solutions, solvents), pharmaceutical industry (raw materials, glycerine), food industry (sugar solutions), and mineral oil industry (oils).

faqs.question: What is the Arc HPLC System used for?
faqs.answer: It's a versatile HPLC system for routine regulated analysis, built to receive transferred methods from other HPLC platforms and to modernize existing methods without redeveloping them.

faqs.question: Can existing methods transfer to Arc HPLC without changes?
faqs.answer: Waters states that transferred methods achieve equivalent test results while preserving analyte retention time and reproducibility, without compromising method integrity or changing validated gradient tables. Regulatory change control requirements remain the lab's own determination.

faqs.question: What is Gradient SmartStart?
faqs.answer: A tool that compensates for dwell volume differences between the sending and receiving systems during method transfer, adjusting at the system level rather than requiring the method to be rewritten.

faqs.question: What is the maximum operating pressure?
faqs.answer: 9,500 psi, across an operating flow rate range up to 5.000 mL/min.

faqs.question: How does Arc HPLC perform on USP assays?
faqs.answer: On the USP-NF assay for losartan potassium it met all system suitability requirements including injection precision below 0.5%, and led competitive HPLC systems on USP efficiency, USP tailing, and injection precision — with all comparison data generated concurrently in the same laboratory.

faqs.question: Does a quaternary pump compromise gradient performance?
faqs.answer: Waters' side-by-side testing on a challenging high-flow separation showed similar retention time stability and superior peak area repeatability compared with a competitive binary system.

faqs.question: Can Arc HPLC run smaller particle columns?
faqs.answer: Yes. The 9,500 psi limit allows high flow rates with smaller particle columns, so scaling from 5 µm to 3.5 µm gains resolution while reducing run time and mobile phase consumption.

faqs.question: What is the sample carryover specification?
faqs.answer: ≤0.002% for caffeine under UV conditions, on a stainless steel sample flow path.

faqs.question: How many samples can the system hold?
faqs.answer: Up to 768 positions using two 384-well plates, or 96 positions using 2 mL vial holders, in a 4–40 °C sample compartment.

faqs.question: How many columns can be installed?
faqs.answer: 1 to 3 columns, up to 7.8 mm internal diameter and 300 mm length.

faqs.question: Which detectors are available?
faqs.answer: Tunable UV, photodiode array, fluorescence, charged aerosol, refractive index, evaporative light scattering, conductivity, electrochemical, and the ACQUITY QDa mass detector.

faqs.question: How is column usage tracked?
faqs.answer: eCord Technology tracks column usage and history automatically, supporting replacement decisions and batch investigations.

faqs.question: What software controls the Arc HPLC System?
faqs.answer: The Empower Chromatography Data System.

faqs.question: How is Arc HPLC different from Alliance HPLC and Alliance iS?
faqs.answer: Arc offers more pressure headroom than Alliance HPLC (9,500 versus 5,000 psi) for method scaling, and broader detection and multi-column capability than Alliance iS. Alliance iS leads on error prevention and guided operation.

faqs.question: How much bench space does the system need?
faqs.answer: 57.4 cm wide, 57.1 cm high, and 62.8 cm deep in the QSM-R, SM-FTN-R, 30 cm column heater configuration.

faqs.question: What is the price of the Arc HPLC System in India?
faqs.answer: Get in touch and Inkarp will put together a quote based on the pump, column, sample manager, and detector configuration required.

faqs.question: Who is the authorized distributor of the Arc HPLC System in India?
faqs.answer: Inkarp is the authorized distributor and service provider for the Waters Arc HPLC System in India, providing demonstration, installation, training, AMC, spare parts, and technical support.

longForm.heroHook: Receives the method as validated. Gradient tables unchanged.
longForm.heroLead: Method transfer is where instrument replacement projects stall. A validated method developed on one platform arrives on another, retention times shift, and what should have been an installation becomes months of adjustment work with a compliance file attached to it. Arc HPLC is built to receive methods as they are. Transferred methods preserve analyte retention time and reproducibility, achieving equivalent test results without compromising method integrity or changing validated gradient tables. Where dwell volume differs between the sending and receiving system, Gradient SmartStart makes the adjustment rather than the method. Performance backs it. On the USP-NF assay for losartan potassium, Arc met all system suitability requirements including injection precision below 0.5%, and led competitive HPLC systems on USP efficiency, USP tailing, and injection precision — with all comparison data generated concurrently in the same laboratory. Then there's headroom: 9,500 psi means the same system can scale a 5 µm method to 3.5 µm columns, gaining resolution and cutting run time and solvent consumption when the lab is ready.

body: Reliable HPLC for regulated QC — designed for high efficiency separations and consistent data quality in regulated product quality control environments.
Replicate existing methods — established LC methods can be transferred and improved without compromising method integrity or requiring complete redevelopment.
Seamless method transfer — methods transferred from other HPLC platforms can maintain analyte retention time and reproducibility without changing validated gradient tables.
Gradient SmartStart compensates for dwell volume differences when transferring methods between LC systems.
High pressure performance — supports pressures up to 9,500 psi with flow rates up to 5.000 mL/min.
Wide operating pH range — supports an operating pH range of 1 to 12.5 under specified conditions.
Consistent system suitability — demonstrated compliance with USP system suitability requirements for losartan potassium, including injection precision below 0.5%.
High efficiency and precision — demonstrated strong performance in USP efficiency, USP tailing and injection precision against competitive HPLC systems.
Quaternary gradient performance — comparable with many binary HPLC systems, including stable retention times and strong peak area repeatability.

Higher efficiency with smaller particles — the 9,500 psi pressure capability supports higher flow rates with smaller particle columns, enabling methods to scale from 5 µm to 3.5 µm for improved resolution and shorter runtimes.
Low carryover — ≤0.002% for caffeine under UV conditions.
Flexible sample capacity — up to 768 samples using two 384-well plates, or 96 samples using 2 mL vial holders.
Controlled sample temperature — the sample compartment operates from 4 to 40 °C.
Flexible column capacity — 1 to 3 columns, with column dimensions up to 7.8 mm I.D. and 300 mm length.
eCord column tracking automatically records column usage and history for improved column management.
Controlled solvent conditioning — supports both passive and active solvent preheating.

Broad detection options — compatible with tunable UV, photodiode array, fluorescence, charged aerosol, refractive index, evaporative light scattering, conductivity, electrochemical and ACQUITY QDa mass detection.
Empower integration — external system control is provided through the Empower Chromatography Data System.

faqs.question: What is the Alliance HPLC System used for?
faqs.answer: It's an analytical HPLC system for methods development and routine analysis, built for standard HPLC workflows where consistency and compliance are the highest priorities — particularly regulated pharmaceutical QC.

faqs.question: How consistent is Alliance HPLC between systems and over time?
faqs.answer: Waters compared a carbamate separation run on two Alliance systems manufactured seven years apart and the results were equivalent, demonstrating both system-to-system and year-to-year consistency.

faqs.question: What is the maximum operating pressure?
faqs.answer: 5,000 psi, with a flow rate range up to 10 mL/min.

faqs.question: How many solvents can Alliance HPLC blend?
faqs.answer: Up to four, in any proportion, using Auto-Blend Technology, with 11 unique gradient profile curves for isocratic and gradient methods.

faqs.question: What is the sample carryover specification?
faqs.answer: ≤0.0025% for caffeine under specified conditions, and typically below 0.005% in routine operation, supported by active user-programmable needle wash.

faqs.question: What injection volumes are supported?
faqs.answer: 0.1 to 100 µL as standard, extending to 2 mL as an option.

faqs.question: How many samples can the system hold?
faqs.answer: Up to 120 vials, in an optional temperature-controlled environment running 4–40 °C, with STAT sample support and auto-addition.

faqs.question: Which detectors can be used with Alliance HPLC?
faqs.answer: Tunable UV, photodiode array, fluorescence, charged aerosol, refractive index, evaporative light scattering, electrochemical, conductivity, and mass spectrometry.

faqs.question: Can mass detection be added to an existing Alliance workflow?
faqs.answer: Yes. The ACQUITY QDa Detector integrates into the existing workflow, and Empower 3 combines UV/Vis and MS data to give mass information for each peak in the separation.

faqs.question: Can Alliance HPLC run sub-3 µm columns?
faqs.answer: Yes. CORTECS 2.7 µm solid-core columns improve resolution and reduce run times when transferring methods from 5 µm chemistries.

faqs.question: Which mobile phase chemistries are supported?
faqs.answer: Reversed-phase, normal-phase, GPC, SEC, and IEX, all on the same system.

faqs.question: What software controls the Alliance HPLC System?
faqs.answer: Empower Software and MassLynx Software, with third-party software packages also supported.

faqs.question: Is Alliance HPLC suitable for GMP laboratories?
faqs.answer: Yes. It supports Waters' Empower-based automated System Qualification Tool, which minimizes the time and cost of annual qualification against GMP, GLP, ISO 17025, and USP <1058>.

faqs.question: How much bench space does the system need?
faqs.answer: 45.7 cm wide (58.4 cm with column heater), 57.1 cm high, and 57.1 cm deep (64.8 cm with sample heater/cooler).

faqs.answer: Get in touch and Inkarp will put together a quote based on the pump, sample manager, column, and detector configuration required.

longForm.heroHook: Two systems built seven years apart. Equivalent separations. That's the whole argument.
longForm.heroLead: In a regulated QC lab, the instrument isn't the deliverable — the data is, and it has to hold up under audit years after it was generated. A system that drifts between units, or between its own first year and its fifth, turns every method transfer into a revalidation exercise. Waters ran the carbamate separation on two Alliance HPLC Systems manufactured seven years apart. The results were equivalent. That system-to-system and year-to-year consistency is what makes Alliance the industry's analytical HPLC of choice for methods development and routine analysis. Underneath it: quaternary solvent blending with Auto-Blend Technology across four solvents, a fixed delay volume that keeps results predictable regardless of back pressure, pulse-free serial-flow delivery without dampeners, and carryover at ≤0.0025% under specified conditions. Empower-based automated system qualification supports GMP, GLP, ISO 17025, and USP <1058> without the annual qualification burden that usually comes with them.

sections.title: Product Information
sections.description: Alliance HPLC System product information: solvent delivery, sample management, detection, and compliance.
body: Alliance HPLC is a time-tested, dependable workhorse for HPLC separations, built for standard workflows where consistency and compliance are the highest priorities.
Waters demonstrated system-to-system and year-to-year consistency directly: a carbamate separation run on two Alliance systems manufactured seven years apart produced equivalent results.
Maximum operating pressure is 5,000 psi with a flow rate range up to 10 mL/min, covering standard analytical HPLC methods.
The quaternary pump blends up to four solvents in any proportion using Auto-Blend Technology, supporting both isocratic and gradient work with 11 unique gradient profile curves.
Solvent compatibility spans reversed-phase, normal-phase, GPC, SEC, and IEX chemistries on the same system.

Solvent delivery runs on a serial flow path with pulse-free delivery achieved without dampeners, alongside online vacuum degassing and automated solvent compressibility compensation for accurate flow.
A fixed delay volume in the integrated solvent delivery system keeps results consistent and predictable regardless of system back pressure.
Integrated seal wash is standard, supporting robust operation across all solvent types.
Sample capacity reaches 120 vials in an optional temperature-controlled environment running 4–40 °C, with active, user-programmable needle wash for low carryover.
Injection volumes run 0.1 to 100 µL as standard and up to 2 mL optionally, with STAT sample support and auto-addition.
Carryover is ≤0.0025% for caffeine under specified conditions, and typically below 0.005% in routine operation.
Column capacity is up to 3 columns as standard, with optional column heating, heating/cooling, or column switching.
Detection options cover tunable UV, photodiode array, fluorescence, charged aerosol, refractive index, evaporative light scattering, electrochemical, conductivity, and mass spectrometry.
CORTECS 2.7 µm solid-core columns can be used to gain resolution and cut run times when transferring methods from 5 µm chemistries.
Adding the ACQUITY QDa Detector brings mass confirmation into the existing workflow, with Empower 3 combining UV/Vis and MS peak data to assign mass information to each peak.
External control runs through Empower Software or MassLynx Software, with third-party software packages also supported.
Waters' Empower-based automated System Qualification Tool (SQT) minimizes the time and cost of annual qualification against GMP, GLP, ISO 17025, and USP <1058>.

sections.title: Consistency Across Systems and Years
sections.description: The hardest question in a multi-instrument QC lab isn't whether one system performs — it's whether system four gives the same answer as system one, and whether either still matches what they produced three years ago.
body: Waters answered it directly: a carbamate separation run on two Alliance HPLC Systems manufactured seven years apart produced equivalent results.
That equivalence is what makes a method transferable across a fleet without revalidating each unit, and what keeps historical data comparable to current data during a trend review.
A newly manufactured Alliance and one several years into service behave as the same instrument, so age in the fleet isn't a variable that has to be tracked and compensated for.

High injection precision, repeatable and accurate flow rates, and exceptional retention time repeatability are the mechanisms underneath it — easy peak identification and precise quantification follow from them.
The fixed delay volume in the solvent delivery system holds gradient behaviour consistent regardless of system back pressure, so a column change or an aging frit doesn't shift the separation.

faqs.answer: It's a quadrupole time-of-flight mass spectrometer for both detailed characterization and accurate quantitation, covering challenging small molecules through to complex biotherapeutics on one system.

faqs.question: What mass range does the Xevo G3 QTof cover?
faqs.answer: The calibration range extends to m/z 16,000, which is what brings complex biologics into scope alongside small molecule work.

faqs.question: What is StepWave XS?
faqs.answer: An ion transmission technology that efficiently transmits low mass, labile species, increasing compound coverage and analytical fidelity for analytes that are otherwise easily lost.

faqs.question: What dynamic range does the system offer?
faqs.answer: Up to 5 orders of linear dynamic range for targeted analysis, and up to a 4× increase in in-spectrum dynamic range for untargeted and screening experiments.

faqs.question: What is the difference between linear and in-spectrum dynamic range?
faqs.answer: Linear dynamic range describes the concentration span over which a known analyte quantifies reliably. In-spectrum dynamic range describes how large an abundance difference can be resolved within a single spectrum, which matters when low-abundance components sit alongside high-abundance ones.

faqs.question: Can one instrument really handle both qualitative and quantitative work?
faqs.answer: That's the design intent — Waters positions it as a flexible multifunctional instrument delivering high-quality quantitative and qualitative data sets, maximizing system usage across both workflow types.

faqs.question: What is waters_connect?
faqs.answer: An informatics ecosystem harmonizing workflows across development, manufacturing, and QC, offering compliance-ready workflows with security-controlled access, full data traceability, and networked deployment.

faqs.question: How does the system support the transition from development to QC?
faqs.answer: Biomolecules and processes are characterized on the Xevo G3 QTof first, then transition to dedicated attribute monitoring assays either on the same system or on the BioAccord System with ACQUITY Premier, with waters_connect carrying the workflow.

faqs.question: What software controls the instrument?
faqs.answer: MassLynx for acquiring, analyzing, managing, and sharing nominal and exact mass MS and MS/MS data, and the waters_connect ecosystem for connected, compliance-ready workflows.

faqs.question: How robust is the instrument for high-throughput use?
faqs.answer: Updated ion optics design and optimized ion beam conditioning are engineered specifically to deliver consistent robustness and reproducibility, maintaining performance and productivity over a longer time period.

faqs.question: Which LC systems pair with the Xevo G3 QTof?
faqs.answer: Waters pairs it with ACQUITY Premier in its own materials, and it has been applied with ACQUITY UPLC I-Class PLUS and M-Class in published application work.

faqs.question: What is the Xevo TQ-S cronos used for?
faqs.answer: It's a tandem quadrupole mass spectrometer for routine quantitative LC-MS/MS analysis, applied to food safety, pesticide residues, nitrosamine quantitation in drug products, and other regulated quantitative testing where sample clean-up is part of the workflow.

faqs.question: How reliable is the instrument over a long run?
faqs.answer: A Waters mycotoxin study in wheat flour — a matrix that can contaminate LC-MS instrumentation — showed consistent performance across 5 days of continuous use and 1,000 injections, with peak area RSD of only 3–8%.

faqs.question: How often does the detector need replacing?
faqs.answer: Fewer than 1% of Waters' tandem quadrupole mass spectrometers launched between 2006 and 2022 require a detector replacement annually, based on their internal service history data.

faqs.question: What is the mass range and MRM speed?
faqs.answer: 2 to 2048 m/z, at 555 MRM/sec — which is faster than both the Xevo TQ-XS and Xevo TQ Absolute XR, each at 500 MRM/sec.

faqs.question: Where does cronos sit in the Xevo TQ line?
faqs.answer: It's the entry point on sensitivity, rated ★★ on Waters' five-point scale, below TQ-S micro (★★★), TQ-XS (★★★★), and TQ Absolute XR (★★★★★). Waters recommends it for accessible routine quantitative analysis with sample clean-up where capital expenditure is limited.

faqs.question: How is cronos different from the Xevo TQ-S micro?
faqs.answer: They share identical dimensions, mass range, MRM speed, StepWave optics, and acquisition modes. TQ-S micro is rated one step higher on sensitivity and adds APGC, ionKey, and nanoflow source compatibility; cronos uniquely adds ACQUITY Arc chromatographic compatibility.

faqs.question: Which ion sources are compatible?
faqs.answer: APCI, ASAP, ESCi, ESI as standard, and UniSpray. Sources can be changed to extend analytical capacity as demands shift.

faqs.question: Which LC systems can it pair with?
faqs.answer: ACQUITY Arc, ACQUITY Premier, ACQUITY UPC2, ACQUITY UPLC, and ACQUITY UPLC M-Class.

faqs.question: What acquisition modes are available?
faqs.answer: Full scan, product scan, precursor ion scan, constant neutral loss scan, multiple reaction monitoring (MRM), and RADAR — simultaneous full scan and MRM in one acquisition.

faqs.question: What software options are available?
faqs.answer: waters_connect for Quantitation and MassLynx v4.2, with LIMS and MassLynx SkyLine interfaces and MassLynx security supported.

faqs.question: What is Exception Focused Review?
faqs.answer: A waters_connect capability that focuses review on results needing attention rather than requiring equal review of everything, which Waters states can save up to 50% of data review time.

faqs.question: Are there compatibility restrictions with waters_connect?
faqs.answer: Yes. ACQUITY Arc, ACQUITY UPC2, ACQUITY UPLC M-Class, ASAP, and ESCi are marked by Waters as not available with waters_connect, so confirm the inlet and source combination against the software choice.

faqs.question: How much bench space does the instrument need?
faqs.answer: 35.6 x 60 x 93 cm (w x h x d), which Waters describes as 2–3× narrower than most other instruments in its class.

faqs.question: What are the power and heat requirements?
faqs.answer: Up to 35% lower electrical power consumption and up to 35% less heat produced than equivalent competitor products, reducing both utility cost and cooling load.

faqs.question: Is the instrument approved for regulated environments?
faqs.answer: Regulatory approval marks include CE, CB, NRTL (Canada/USA), and RCM, with MassLynx security supported for regulated data control.

sections.title: Reliability Across a Full Campaign
sections.description: Peak sensitivity on a clean standard tells you what an instrument can do once. A quantitative lab needs to know what it does on injection 900, in a matrix that has been depositing residue since injection one.
body: Waters answered that specifically. A mycotoxin study in wheat flour — a matrix they explicitly name as one that can contaminate LC-MS instrumentation — ran 1,000 injections across 5 days of continuous use.
Peak area RSD held between 3 and 8% across that campaign, meaning the instrument's response didn't drift meaningfully as the source accumulated matrix.
Proven ion guide technology is what Waters credits for maintaining uptime as standard, and the Xevo family's inherent robustness is the design lineage behind it.

The detector data carries real provenance rather than being a general claim: fewer than 1% of Waters' tandem quadrupole mass spectrometers launched between 2006 and 2022 require a detector replacement on an annual basis, from their own service history.

A low noise, off-axis photomultiplier is the design choice behind that longevity — off-axis geometry keeps neutrals and photons off the detector surface, which is what shortens detector life on in-line designs.
sections.disclaimer: Share the matrix and the typical campaign length between maintenance windows, and expected performance gets discussed against the published mycotoxin study conditions.

faqs.question: What is the Xevo TQ-S micro used for?
faqs.answer: It's a compact tandem quadrupole mass spectrometer for routine quantitative LC-MS/MS, applied across food testing, PFAS and environmental analysis, clinical research, cannabis testing, and pharmaceutical quantitation.

faqs.question: How often will the instrument need unplanned service?
faqs.answer: Waters' internal global service data shows customers on average need no unplanned service visit during the warranty period and for 3 years after. Planned scheduled Performance Maintenance visits are still recommended for trouble-free operation.

faqs.question: How reliable is performance over a long campaign?
faqs.answer: A mycotoxin study in wheat flour — a matrix that can contaminate LC-MS instrumentation — showed consistent performance across 5 days of continuous use and 1,000 injections, with peak area RSD of 5–9%.

faqs.question: How is Xevo TQ-S micro different from the Xevo TQ-S cronos?
faqs.answer: They share identical dimensions, mass range, MRM speed, StepWave optics, acquisition modes, and detector. TQ-S micro rates one step higher on sensitivity (★★★ versus ★★) and adds APGC, ionKey, and nanoflow ion sources plus APGC chromatographic compatibility. cronos uniquely adds ACQUITY Arc compatibility.

faqs.question: What is the mass range and MRM speed?
faqs.answer: 2 to 2048 m/z, at 555 MRM/sec — matching cronos and faster than both TQ-XS and TQ Absolute XR, each at 500 MRM/sec.

faqs.question: Where does TQ-S micro sit in the Xevo TQ line?
faqs.answer: Second on sensitivity, rated ★★★ on Waters' five-point scale, above cronos (★★) and below TQ-XS (★★★★) and TQ Absolute XR (★★★★★).

faqs.question: Which ion sources are compatible?
faqs.answer: APCI, APGC, ASAP, ESCi, ESI as standard, ionKey, nanoflow, and UniSpray.

faqs.question: Can the instrument do GC-MS work?
faqs.answer: Yes. The Atmospheric Pressure GC (APGC) source is a field upgrade that extends the platform to AP GC-MS, bringing GC-amenable compounds onto the same mass spectrometer.

faqs.question: Which LC systems can it pair with?
faqs.answer: ACQUITY Premier, ACQUITY UPC2, ACQUITY UPLC, ACQUITY UPLC M-Class, and APGC.

faqs.question: What acquisition modes are available?
faqs.answer: Full scan, product scan, precursor ion scan, constant neutral loss scan, MRM, and RADAR — simultaneous full scan and MRM in one acquisition.

faqs.question: What software options are available?
faqs.answer: waters_connect for Quantitation and MassLynx v4.2, with LIMS and MassLynx SkyLine interfaces and MassLynx security supported.

faqs.question: Are there compatibility restrictions with waters_connect?
faqs.answer: Yes. ACQUITY UPC2, ACQUITY UPLC M-Class, ASAP, ESCi, ionKey, and nanoflow are marked by Waters as not available with waters_connect, so confirm the source and inlet combination against the software choice.

faqs.question: How much bench space does the instrument need?
faqs.answer: 35.6 x 60 x 93 cm (w x h x d), which Waters describes as 2–3× narrower than other instruments in its class — identical to the Xevo TQ-S cronos.

faqs.question: What are the power and heat requirements?
faqs.answer: Up to 34% lower electricity consumption and associated heat production than other instruments in its class.

faqs.question: How often does the detector need replacing?
faqs.answer: Fewer than 1% of Waters' tandem quadrupole mass spectrometers launched between 2006 and 2022 require a detector replacement annually, based on their internal service history data.

faqs.question: Is the instrument approved for regulated environments?
faqs.answer: Regulatory approval marks include CE, CB, NRTL (Canada/USA), and RCM, with MassLynx security supported for regulated data control.

longForm.heroHook: The next step in sensitivity for demanding quantitative work, injection after injection.
longForm.heroLead: Reaching part-per-trillion concentrations reliably takes more than a sensitive detector alone. Xevo TQ-XS is built to hold that sensitivity consistently across an entire batch. Coupled with ACQUITY UPLC, Xevo TQ-XS delivers a mass range of 2 to 2048 m/z, MRM speed of 500 transitions per second, and StepWave XS ion source transfer optics purpose-built for the sensitivity this tier demands. In direct comparison, average analyte area counts for vancomycin came in over 10 times higher on Xevo TQ-XS than on Xevo TQ-S, and it supports the full range of acquisition modes from full scan through simultaneous full scan and MRM (RADAR).

sections.title: Product Information
sections.description: Xevo TQ-XS product information: sensitivity performance, software ecosystem, and regulatory readiness.
body: Coupled with ACQUITY UPLC, Xevo TQ-XS is built for routine quantitative workflows that need superior sensitivity, adaptability, and flexibility as analytical demands evolve.

StepWave XS ion source transfer optics sit specifically at this tier, positioned between the standard StepWave design on the TQ-S cronos and TQ-S micro, and the StepWave XR optics used on TQ Absolute XR.
Mass range covers 2 to 2048 m/z, with MRM speed reaching 500 transitions per second, supported by a low-noise, off-axis, long-life photomultiplier detector.
Six acquisition modes are available: full scan, product scan, precursor ion scan, constant neutral loss scan, multiple reaction monitoring (MRM), and simultaneous full scan and MRM (RADAR).

Ion source compatibility spans APCI, APGC, ASAP, ESCi, ESI, ionKey, Nanoflow, and UniSpray, matched to a chromatographic configuration compatibility list including ACQUITY Premier, ACQUITY UPC2, ACQUITY UPLC, ACQUITY UPLC M-Class, and APGC.
In a direct vancomycin comparison, average analyte area counts on Xevo TQ-XS came in more than 10 times higher than on Xevo TQ-S.
A representative liraglutide LLOQ chromatogram at 0.5 ng/mL, extracted from plasma, demonstrates the sensitivity and selectivity available at this tier.

Detector reliability runs high across the installed base, with less than 1% of Waters' tandem quadrupole mass spectrometers requiring a detector replacement annually, based on internal service data from units launched between 2006 and 2022.
Software options include MassLynx v4.2 and waters_connect for Quantitation, both supporting LIMS interfaces and MassLynx SkyLine interfaces, with MassLynx security included as standard.
Regulatory approval marks include CE, CB, NRTL (Canada/USA), and RCM.

sections.title: Sensitivity Where It Matters Most
sections.description: A sensitivity claim means more with a direct comparison behind it than a general performance statement alone.
body: For vancomycin, average analyte area counts on Xevo TQ-XS measured more than 10 times higher than on Xevo TQ-S, a direct, quantified sensitivity gain rather than an approximate improvement.

On the low-concentration end, a representative liraglutide LLOQ chromatogram at 0.5 ng/mL, extracted from plasma, shows both the sensitivity and the selectivity available at this concentration, relevant for bioanalytical work operating near a method's detection limit.

Behind both results sits the StepWave XS ion source transfer optics, purpose-built for this sensitivity tier within the Xevo TQ family, positioned above the standard StepWave design and below the StepWave XR optics on TQ Absolute XR.

Set against what the analysis needs: confidence at trace-level concentrations comes from the demonstrated 0.5 ng/mL LLOQ performance on liraglutide; measurable sensitivity gains over standard TQ systems come from the >10x area counts versus Xevo TQ-S on vancomycin; reliable detection at the needed sensitivity tier comes from the purpose-built StepWave XS optics; and high-throughput analysis without losing sensitivity comes from the 500 MRM/sec speed.
