faqs.question: What is the ACQUITY UPLC M-Class System used for?
faqs.answer: It's a nano- to microscale UPLC system for sample-limited LC-MS work, used primarily in proteomics, biomarker discovery, protein conformation analysis, and other applications where sample material is severely limited.

faqs.question: What flow rate range does M-Class cover?
faqs.answer: 200 nL/min to 100 µL/min, delivered without flow splitting.

faqs.question: Why does flow splitting matter?
faqs.answer: Splitting produces low flow by diverting most of an analytical pump's output, which makes the flow reaching the column dependent on restrictor and back pressure conditions. Direct, non-split delivery with pulse-less flow control gives increased retention time reproducibility instead.

faqs.question: What column inner diameters does the system support?
faqs.answer: Waters' body copy states 75 µm to 1.0 mm and the specification table states 75 µm to 4.6 mm. Confirm the exact range against the intended column set at configuration.

faqs.question: Can optical detection be used at all column sizes?
faqs.answer: Mass spectrometry supports the full column inner diameter range; optical detection applies to 300 µm to 1 mm I.D. columns.

faqs.question: Why does low flow increase sensitivity?
faqs.answer: Delivering the same quantity of analyte in less volume raises concentration at the source, improving sensitivity for any mass spectrometer without changing the instrument.

faqs.question: What is the sample flow path made from?
faqs.answer: The flow path is non-ferrous, with non-reactive surfaces maintaining sample integrity through the system.

faqs.question: What is the HDX Technology configuration for?
faqs.answer: Quantifying small changes in protein conformation, with an extended pressure range for higher efficiency separation and DynamX HDX Data Analysis Software integrating sample prep through sequence determination, D2 uptake curves, and comparison plots.

faqs.question: What is the 2D Technology configuration for?
faqs.answer: Expanding dynamic range and throughput through reversed-phase/reversed-phase 2D-LC, running the first dimension at pH 10 and the second at pH 2 with MS-compatible eluents.

faqs.question: What injection volumes does the system accept?
faqs.answer: 0.1 µL to 100.0 µL.

faqs.question: Does M-Class include column tracking?
faqs.answer: No. Column tracking is not provided on this system, unlike the analytical-scale ACQUITY systems that carry eCord Technology.

faqs.question: What is the operating pH range?
faqs.answer: 2 to 10 — narrower than the analytical-scale ACQUITY systems, which is worth checking against the intended mobile phase chemistry.

faqs.question: What software controls the system?
faqs.answer: MassLynx Software per the specification, with new drivers integrating the system into existing MassLynx workflows. Waters also publishes Empower and third-party driver pack certificates for the platform, so confirm the software scope at configuration.

faqs.question: What is the maximum sample capacity?
faqs.answer: Up to 21 plates with the Sample Organizer.

faqs.question: How much bench space does the system need?
faqs.answer: 34.3 cm wide, 69.7 cm high, and 71.2 cm deep in the µBSM, µSM-FL, TVM configuration.

longForm.heroHook: 200 nL/min to 100 µL/min. No flow splitting anywhere in it.
longForm.heroLead: The usual route to nanoflow is splitting an analytical-scale pump's output down. It works, and it costs reproducibility and reliability — which is precisely the trade-off that stops labs from adopting low-flow LC-MS despite the sensitivity waiting on the other side. ACQUITY UPLC M-Class delivers 200 nL/min through 100 µL/min directly, without splitting. Automatic solvent flow control algorithms provide pulse-less flow, and retention time reproducibility follows from that rather than being fought for. Every part of the system was designed and tested to deliver the right flow for the right column, across inner diameters from 75 µm upward. For samples that are severely limited in amount or availability, that combination is the whole argument: higher sensitivity from any mass spectrometer, less sample volume consumed, increased dynamic range, and non-reactive surfaces that keep the sample intact on the way to the source.

comparison.disclaimer: These are specialists, not tiers. I-Class PLUS trades column capacity and multi-solvent blending for the lowest dispersion and carryover in the series — the right choice when the mass spectrometer or the separation is the binding constraint. faqs.question: What is the ACQUITY UPLC I-Class PLUS System used for?
faqs.answer: It's a high-performance binary UPLC system built for maximum resolution and sensitivity, used particularly as an LC-MS front end in bioanalysis, impurity profiling, peptide characterization, and clinical research.

faqs.question: What is system band spread and why does 4 µL matter?
faqs.answer: System band spread is how much the flow path broadens a peak after the column has separated it. Waters compared a tetracaine impurity analysis on I-Class PLUS at 4 µL against a UHPLC system at 20 µL under identical conditions, achieving significantly better resolution on I-Class PLUS.

faqs.question: What is the maximum operating pressure?
faqs.answer: 18,000 psi, the highest in the ACQUITY UPLC PLUS Series, with a flow rate range up to 2.0 mL/min.

faqs.question: What is the sample carryover specification?
faqs.answer: Below 0.001% for caffeine under UV conditions, and manageable through programmable method settings for compatibility with the most sensitive mass spectrometers.

faqs.question: Why is I-Class PLUS recommended as a mass spectrometry inlet?
faqs.answer: Narrow peak widths improve both resolution and ionization efficiency, enhancing MS sensitivity, while high resolution minimizes interference from co-elutions and industry-leading carryover protects trace-level detection.

faqs.question: How many columns can the system hold?
faqs.answer: Up to two columns of 150 mm length and up to 4.6 mm internal diameter, with accurate temperature control across the entire column and active preheating.

faqs.question: What pump configuration does I-Class PLUS use?
faqs.answer: A Binary Solvent Manager delivering precise, accurate blending for up to four solvents with an integrated solvent-select valve.

faqs.question: What injector options are available?
faqs.answer: Flow-through needle and fixed loop, giving sample injection versatility depending on the application.

faqs.question: What are CORTECS columns and why pair them with this system?
faqs.answer: CORTECS 1.6 µm solid-core columns deliver exceptional efficiency and narrower peaks; paired with the system's ultra-low dispersion and 18,000 psi headroom, they produce higher peak capacity for the toughest samples.

faqs.question: How is I-Class PLUS different from H-Class PLUS?
faqs.answer: I-Class PLUS offers higher pressure (18,000 versus 15,000 psi) and lower carryover with the lowest dispersion in the series, but takes two columns and is binary only. H-Class PLUS offers up to six columns, nine-solvent quaternary blending, and automated method screening.

faqs.question: Does the system support annual qualification?
faqs.answer: Yes. The Waters Empower-based automated System Qualification Tool (SQT) minimizes the time and cost associated with annual qualification.

faqs.question: What software controls the system?
faqs.answer: Empower, MassLynx, waters_connect, the UNIFI Scientific Information System, and several third-party software packages.

faqs.question: Does the system handle metal-sensitive analytes?
faqs.answer: The sample flow path is stainless steel, so metal-sensitive analytes may require passivation. Where that's a recurring issue, the ACQUITY Premier System's inert MaxPeak HPS flow path is designed for exactly that problem.

faqs.question: What is multidimensional UPLC?
faqs.answer: A configuration allowing selective isolation across more than one separation dimension, improving characterization where a single dimension cannot resolve everything of interest.

faqs.question: What is the maximum sample capacity?
faqs.answer: Up to 20 plates with the Sample Organizer.

faqs.question: How much bench space does the system need?
faqs.answer: 34.3 cm wide, 71.1 cm high, and 71.2 cm deep in the QSM or BSM, SM-FTN, CHA configuration.

longForm.heroHook: 4 µL of band spread against 20 µL. Same sample, same conditions, different answer.
longForm.heroLead: Waters ran a tetracaine impurity analysis twice under identical conditions — once on ACQUITY UPLC I-Class PLUS with a system band spread of 4 µL, once on a UHPLC system with 20 µL. The resolution difference was significant, and it came entirely from the system, not the chemistry. That's the point of I-Class PLUS. Industry-leading ultra-low dispersion and delay volume produce narrow, ultra-efficient peaks — which is why it works as an inlet that improves the performance of any mass spectrometer. Narrow peaks mean better ionization efficiency, and carryover below 0.001% means the sensitivity a modern tandem quad or QTof is capable of doesn't get spent on baseline noise. 18,000 psi of pressure headroom pairs it with CORTECS 1.6 µm solid-core columns for peak capacity beyond what conventional UHPLC reaches. And Waters' Empower-based automated System Qualification Tool keeps annual qualification time and cost down in regulated environments.

faqs.question: What is the ACQUITY UPLC H-Class PLUS System used for?
faqs.answer: It's a UPLC system for method development and routine analysis, built to decrease time to result while increasing the depth and quality of information from sample analysis.

faqs.question: How much can scaling a method to UPLC save?
faqs.answer: Waters scaled the USP analysis of diclazuril and organic impurities from HPLC to UPLC, achieving a 4× reduction in run time and a 10× reduction in solvent consumption.

faqs.question: What is the difference between the Quaternary and Binary configurations?
faqs.answer: Quaternary blends up to nine solvents and automatically screens column and eluent combinations, built for method development. Binary offers the lowest system volume with high-pressure mixing, built for reproducible routine LC-MS.

faqs.question: Why does low dispersion matter if the system already runs at 15,000 psi?
faqs.answer: High pressure alone doesn't produce sharp peaks. System dispersion has to be matched to the narrow peak widths that sub-2 µm columns generate, or the resolution the chemistry provides is lost in the system.

faqs.question: What is Auto•Blend Plus Technology?
faqs.answer: It automates mobile phase formulation and allows pH and ionic strength to be screened as method parameters, significantly reducing time spent preparing mobile phases in the prep lab.

faqs.question: How many columns can be screened at once?
faqs.answer: Up to six columns of 150 mm length and up to 4.6 mm internal diameter, in independently temperature-controlled compartments with active preheating.

faqs.question: How many solvents can the system blend?
faqs.answer: Up to nine on the Quaternary Solvent Manager with the integrated solvent-select valve, or up to four on the Binary Solvent Manager.

faqs.question: Can methods be transferred from another LC system?
faqs.answer: Yes. Gradient SmartStart adjusts for system volume differences when transferring from an alternative LC system, without altering the method table.

faqs.question: What is the maximum operating pressure and flow rate?
faqs.answer: 15,000 psi, with an operating flow rate range up to 2.2 mL/min.

faqs.question: Which columns does the system support?
faqs.answer: Any analytical LC column, with particle sizes from sub-2 µm to 5 µm.

faqs.question: What is the sample carryover specification?
faqs.answer: ≤0.002% for caffeine under UV conditions, with direct inject sampling using a needle-in-flow-path design for an accurate seal at high pressure.

faqs.question: Does H-Class PLUS work with mass spectrometry?
faqs.answer: Yes. The Binary configuration is built for reproducible everyday LC-MS with any tandem quad or Q-ToF, and pairs with Waters tandem quadrupole technology for routine quantitative UPLC-MS/MS.

faqs.question: Does the system need passivation for metal-sensitive analytes?
faqs.answer: The sample flow path is stainless steel, so metal-sensitive analytes may require passivation. Where that's a recurring problem, the ACQUITY Premier System's inert MaxPeak HPS flow path is designed to remove the need entirely.

faqs.question: What software controls the system?
faqs.answer: Empower, MassLynx, waters_connect, the UNIFI Scientific Information System, and several third-party software packages.

faqs.question: What is the maximum sample capacity?
faqs.answer: Up to 20 plates with the Sample Organizer.

faqs.question: How much bench space does the system need?
faqs.answer: 34.3 cm wide, 71.1 cm high, and 71.2 cm deep in the QSM or BSM, SM-FTN, CHA configuration.

longForm.heroHook: Four times faster. Ten times less solvent. Same USP analysis.
longForm.heroLead: Waters scaled the USP analysis of diclazuril and its organic impurities from HPLC through UHPLC to UPLC. The UPLC method cut run time by a factor of four and solvent consumption by a factor of ten — throughput up, cost per analysis down, on the same separation. That's what UPLC delivers when the system is actually built for it. High pressure alone doesn't produce sharp peaks; system dispersion has to be matched to the narrow peak widths that sub-2 µm columns generate. ACQUITY UPLC H-Class PLUS is engineered for that match, which is why the same method on the same column resolves better here than on a higher-dispersion UHPLC system. It comes two ways. The Quaternary system screens up to six columns and nine solvents automatically to find the best separation conditions — built for method development. The Binary system brings the lowest system volume and high-pressure gradient formation for reproducible everyday LC-MS with any tandem quad or Q-ToF.

sections.title: UPLC Performance and Method Scaling
sections.description: High pressure and UPLC performance are not the same thing. A system rated to 15,000 psi can still produce broad peaks if its extra-column dispersion is wider than the peaks the column is generating.
body: True UPLC requires system dispersion matched to the peak widths associated with narrow-bore columns packed with sub-2 µm particles — that matching is the design premise here.

Waters showed the difference directly: the same method, the same column, run on a low-dispersion H-Class PLUS versus a higher-dispersion UHPLC system, with the resolution difference visible in the chromatogram.

The productivity case is quantified. Scaling the USP diclazuril and organic impurity analysis from HPLC through UHPLC to UPLC gave a 4× reduction in run time and a 10× reduction in solvent consumption.
Those two numbers move different budget lines: run time reduction increases sample throughput per instrument, solvent reduction cuts consumables spend and waste disposal cost per analysis.
Existing HPLC methods run on the system now, so the transition is gradual rather than a cliff — the lab keeps its validated work while modernizing selectively.
A separate transfer example showed analysis time going from 5 minutes to 3 through direct transfer without gradient delay, a 40% runtime reduction.
Gradient SmartStart handles system volume differences when methods arrive from another LC platform, without requiring the method table to be altered.

Binary or Quaternary Pump Options: Configuration flexibility to match the separation chemistry in use.
Flow-Through Needle and Fixed Loop Injection: Two injector options for sample injection versatility across applications.
Direct Inject Sampling: Delivers high-precision injections where accuracy is the constraint.
Six-Column Capacity With eCord Tracking: Up to six columns up to 150 mm, with usage tracked and archived automatically.

Seven Detection Options: TUV, PDA eλ, FLR, charged aerosol, RI, ELS, and mass spectrometers.
Holistic System and Column Design: ACQUITY Premier Columns designed alongside the system to reduce analyte losses across the whole flow path.
ACT® Certified Sustainable Design: Renewable-powered manufacturing, 25–40% recycled content, and sustainable packaging.

faqs.question: What is the ACQUITY Premier System used for?
faqs.answer: It's a UPLC system built to improve peak shape, recovery, and reproducibility for metal-sensitive compounds, used across peptide therapeutics, oligonucleotide and mRNA analysis, targeted metabolomics, and pharmaceutical QC.

faqs.question: What is MaxPeak HPS Technology?
faqs.answer: MaxPeak High Performance Surfaces Technology gives the system an inert sample flow path, preventing the non-specific adsorption that causes metal-sensitive analytes to bind to conventional stainless steel surfaces.

faqs.question: Which analytes are affected by metal adsorption?
faqs.answer: Metal-sensitive compounds including phosphopeptides, oligonucleotides, organic acids, phosphates, and chelators — classes where conventional LC produces broad peaks, large RSDs, and undetected analytes.

faqs.question: How much does ACQUITY Premier improve peak shape?
faqs.answer: Waters measured a 54% reduction in peak tailing on the T37 peptide, leading to better detection of deamidation impurities.

faqs.question: Does the system still need passivation?
faqs.answer: No. Time-consuming system and column passivation is eliminated, with Waters demonstrating reproducible performance from the first injection.

faqs.question: What is the maximum operating pressure?
faqs.answer: 15,000 psi, across an operating flow rate range of 0.001 to 2.000 mL/min.

faqs.question: What pump and injection options are available?
faqs.answer: Binary and quaternary pump options, with flow-through needle and fixed loop injection, plus direct inject sampling for high-precision injections.

faqs.question: How many columns can the system hold?
faqs.answer: Six columns up to 150 mm length and 4.6 mm internal diameter, with eCord Technology tracking and archiving column usage.

faqs.question: What is the maximum sample capacity?
faqs.answer: 8,064 samples with the Sample Organizer.

faqs.question: Which detectors are available?
faqs.answer: TUV, PDA eλ, FLR, charged aerosol, refractive index, evaporative light scattering, and mass spectrometers.

faqs.question: Which software controls the system?
faqs.answer: Empower, MassLynx, and waters_connect are listed in the system specification; Waters also cites UNIFI in its platform support summary. Confirm the exact software requirement at configuration.

faqs.question: Can existing HPLC methods be scaled onto ACQUITY Premier?
faqs.answer: Yes. The system supports scaling HPLC methods to UPLC to gain increased resolution, sensitivity, and speed from modern small-particle chemistries.

faqs.question: Do ACQUITY Premier Columns need to be used with the system?
faqs.answer: The system and ACQUITY Premier Columns are holistically designed together to reduce analyte losses across the full flow path, so pairing them is how the full benefit is realized.

faqs.question: Is the system environmentally certified?
faqs.answer: Yes. It carries an ACT® label for environmentally responsible design, manufactured in a renewable-powered facility with 25–40% recycled content and sustainable packaging.

faqs.question: How much bench space does the system need?
faqs.answer: 34.3 cm wide, 71.1 cm high, and 71.2 cm deep in the QSM or BSM, SM-FTN, CH-A configuration.

longForm.heroHook: The peak you couldn't see wasn't absent. It was stuck to the flow path.
longForm.heroLead: Metal-sensitive compounds — phosphopeptides, nucleotides, organic acids, chelators — adsorb onto stainless steel surfaces inside a conventional LC. The result is broad peaks, large RSDs, and analytes that go undetected entirely. The usual remedy is passivation: hours of system conditioning before a run, repeated whenever the system sits idle. ACQUITY Premier removes the cause. MaxPeak High Performance Surfaces Technology makes the sample flow path inert, so metal-sensitive analytes stay in the mobile phase instead of binding to the hardware. Waters measured a 54% reduction in peak tailing on a deamidation impurity peptide, and reduced adsorption of a doubly phosphorylated insulin receptor peptide against conventional LC technology. The chromatography underneath is true UPLC — 15,000 psi, ultra-low dispersion, high resolution, on the ACQUITY UPLC PLUS Series platform. And with passivation eliminated, the first injection is usable rather than being the first of several conditioning runs.

body: Advanced Performance LC System — builds on the reliability, ruggedness and configuration flexibility of the ACQUITY UPLC H Class PLUS and I Class PLUS systems.

Improved peak shape — Waters reports a 54% reduction in peak tailing for T37 peptide analysis, supporting improved detection of deamidation impurities.

First injection performance — designed to provide reproducible performance from the first injection, reducing the need for time consuming system and column passivation.
High pressure operation — supports pressures up to 15,000 psi across a flow rate range of 0.001 to 2.000 mL/min.
Wide operating pH range — supports an operating pH range of 1 to 12.5.
Binary and Quaternary configurations — available with both binary and quaternary pump options to suit different LC workflows.
Controlled solvent conditioning — active preheating is provided as standard for consistent solvent conditioning.
Flexible injection options — supports flow through needle and fixed loop injection, along with direct inject sampling for high precision applications.
Low carryover — provides sample carryover of ≤0.002%, supporting sensitive analytical workflows.
Controlled sample temperature — the sample compartment operates from 4 to 40 °C.
Flexible column capacity — supports up to six columns with lengths up to 150 mm and internal diameters up to 4.6 mm.
eCord column tracking — tracks and archives column usage to support method management and column history.
High sample capacity — the Sample Organizer supports up to 8,064 samples.
Multiple detection options — compatible with TUV, PDA eλ, FLR, charged aerosol, refractive index, evaporative light scattering and mass spectrometer detection.
Designed for metal sensitive analytes — the ACQUITY Premier System and ACQUITY Premier Columns are designed together to reduce analyte losses and improve repeatability.
LC MS compatibility — when paired with a Waters mass spectrometer, the system supports identification and quantification of unknown compounds and detection of trace components in complex samples.
Sustainable system design — the system carries an ACT label and incorporates renewable powered manufacturing, recycled content, responsible chemical management and sustainable packaging.

faqs.question: What is the Arc HPLC System used for?

faqs.question: Can existing methods transfer to Arc HPLC without changes?
faqs.answer: Waters states that transferred methods achieve equivalent test results while preserving analyte retention time and reproducibility, without compromising method integrity or changing validated gradient tables. Regulatory change control requirements remain the lab's own determination.

faqs.question: What is Gradient SmartStart?
faqs.answer: A tool that compensates for dwell volume differences between the sending and receiving systems during method transfer, adjusting at the system level rather than requiring the method to be rewritten.

faqs.question: What is the maximum operating pressure?
faqs.answer: 9,500 psi, across an operating flow rate range up to 5.000 mL/min.

faqs.question: How does Arc HPLC perform on USP assays?
faqs.answer: On the USP-NF assay for losartan potassium it met all system suitability requirements including injection precision below 0.5%, and led competitive HPLC systems on USP efficiency, USP tailing, and injection precision — with all comparison data generated concurrently in the same laboratory.

faqs.question: Does a quaternary pump compromise gradient performance?
faqs.answer: Waters' side-by-side testing on a challenging high-flow separation showed similar retention time stability and superior peak area repeatability compared with a competitive binary system.

faqs.question: Can Arc HPLC run smaller particle columns?
faqs.answer: Yes. The 9,500 psi limit allows high flow rates with smaller particle columns, so scaling from 5 µm to 3.5 µm gains resolution while reducing run time and mobile phase consumption.

faqs.question: What is the sample carryover specification?
faqs.answer: ≤0.002% for caffeine under UV conditions, on a stainless steel sample flow path.

faqs.question: How many samples can the system hold?
faqs.answer: Up to 768 positions using two 384-well plates, or 96 positions using 2 mL vial holders, in a 4–40 °C sample compartment.

faqs.question: How many columns can be installed?
faqs.answer: 1 to 3 columns, up to 7.8 mm internal diameter and 300 mm length.

faqs.question: Which detectors are available?
faqs.answer: Tunable UV, photodiode array, fluorescence, charged aerosol, refractive index, evaporative light scattering, conductivity, electrochemical, and the ACQUITY QDa mass detector.

faqs.question: How is column usage tracked?
faqs.answer: eCord Technology tracks column usage and history automatically, supporting replacement decisions and batch investigations.

faqs.question: What software controls the Arc HPLC System?
faqs.answer: The Empower Chromatography Data System.

faqs.question: How is Arc HPLC different from Alliance HPLC and Alliance iS?
faqs.answer: Arc offers more pressure headroom than Alliance HPLC (9,500 versus 5,000 psi) for method scaling, and broader detection and multi-column capability than Alliance iS. Alliance iS leads on error prevention and guided operation.

faqs.question: How much bench space does the system need?
faqs.answer: 57.4 cm wide, 57.1 cm high, and 62.8 cm deep in the QSM-R, SM-FTN-R, 30 cm column heater configuration.

faqs.question: What is the Alliance iS HPLC System used for?
faqs.answer: It's an HPLC system built specifically for QC laboratories, aimed at first-time-right results, shortened release cycles, and fewer investigations through error prevention and guided operation.

faqs.question: How much does Alliance iS reduce human errors?
faqs.answer: Waters reports a reduction of up to 40%, based on their 2022 market research surveying 56 global pharma QC labs each running more than 25 systems.

faqs.question: What does the system check before a run starts?
faqs.answer: Pre-run verification confirms the correct column, the expected vials and plates, solvent levels, and solvent expiration dates before an unacceptable run can begin.

faqs.question: How does column tracking work?
faqs.answer: RFID-enabled eConnect Waters Columns are auto-recognized by the system, giving automated column history tracking for replacement decisions and batch investigations.

faqs.question: What is the maximum operating pressure?
faqs.answer: 12,000 psi, across an operating flow rate range of 0.001 to 10.000 mL/min.

faqs.question: What is the sample carryover specification?
faqs.answer: ≤0.002% for caffeine under UV conditions, using flow-through needle injection on a stainless steel sample flow path.

faqs.question: How many columns and which detectors does Alliance iS support?
faqs.answer: One column up to 300 mm length and 8 mm internal diameter, with PDA and TUV detector options.

faqs.question: What sample formats can the system hold?
faqs.answer: Any three holders from: 48- and 54-position 2.00 mL vial holders, 96-well plates, 384-well plates, 48-position 0.65 mL micro-centrifuge tube plates, and 24-position 1.50 mL micro-centrifuge plates.

faqs.question: Does Alliance iS require Empower software?
faqs.answer: Yes. Informatics compatibility is Empower Chromatography Data System, Feature Release 4 with Windows 10 and later, and several features including pre-run verification and Method Matching depend on it.

faqs.question: Can existing methods be migrated onto Alliance iS?
faqs.answer: Yes. The Intelligent Method Translator App (iMTA) assists with migrating methods from other systems, and hardware compatibility with legacy methods preserves existing validated work.

faqs.question: What happens if an unsupported method is loaded?
faqs.answer: Method Matching warns the user at the point of attempting to run it, rather than letting the mismatch surface later during data review.

faqs.question: How does the system help when something goes wrong?
faqs.answer: Guided troubleshooting and guided maintenance run on the instrument touchscreen, with enhanced access to serviceable components and direct access to the Waters Help Center.

faqs.question: How is Alliance iS different from the Alliance HPLC System?
faqs.answer: Alliance iS adds 12,000 psi pressure, pre-run error verification, RFID column tracking, and guided workflows. Alliance HPLC retains a wider detection range, up to three columns, and broader software compatibility including MassLynx and third-party packages.

faqs.question: How much bench space and weight capacity does it need?
faqs.answer: 74.2 cm high, 49.9 cm wide, 63.5 cm deep, weighing 72.5 kg.

faqs.answer: Get in touch and Inkarp will put together a quote based on the detector, sample holder, and column configuration required.

sections.title: Product Information
sections.description: Alliance iS HPLC System product information: error reduction, guided workflows, and Empower integration.
body: Built for QC laboratories — designed to support first time right results, shorter release cycles and fewer investigations in routine quality control workflows.
Intelligent error prevention — system intelligence helps identify potential setup and operational errors before an unacceptable run begins.
Pre run verification — checks columns, vials, plates, solvent levels and expiration dates before analysis starts.
Automated column tracking — eConnect Waters Columns are recognized through RFID, enabling automatic column identification and usage history without manual records.
Simplified system setup — tool free fittings and clearly labelled solvent lines help reduce leaks and setup related errors.
Guided operation — the touchscreen provides guided workflows for system start up, shutdown and priming, helping users follow consistent procedures.
High pressure operation — supports pressures up to 12,000 psi with flow rates from 0.001 to 10.000 mL/min.
Wide operating pH range — supports an operating pH range of 1 to 13.
Low carryover — provides carryover of ≤0.002% for caffeine under UV conditions.
Flexible sample capacity — supports multiple holder configurations, including 48 and 54 position 2.00 mL vial holders, 96 and 384 well plates, and 48 and 24 position micro centrifuge plates.
Controlled column environment — supports one column up to 300 mm length and 8 mm I.D. with enhanced temperature stability.
Integrated system monitoring — status lights, touchscreen controls, Empower Software and waters_connect System Monitoring provide visibility into system operation.
Automated system health monitoring — monitors key performance parameters to help identify maintenance and service requirements earlier.
Guided troubleshooting and maintenance — touchscreen guidance supports troubleshooting and maintenance, with enhanced component serviceability and access to the Waters Help Center.
Enhanced reliability — updates to the injector, mixer, column manager, check valves and detectors are designed to improve system reliability.
Consistent temperature control — enhanced temperature management across the sample manager, column manager and detector supports repeatable method performance.
Method migration support — the Intelligent Method Translator App helps migrate methods from other systems, while Method Matching identifies unsupported methods before execution.
Complete audit trail — Empower System Audit Trail automatically records system and software installation and modification activities for traceability.
Detection options — available with PDA and TUV detectors.
Informatics compatibility — compatible with Empower Chromatography Data System Feature Release 4, with Windows 10 and later support.

faqs.question: What is the Alliance HPLC System used for?
faqs.answer: It's an analytical HPLC system for methods development and routine analysis, built for standard HPLC workflows where consistency and compliance are the highest priorities — particularly regulated pharmaceutical QC.

faqs.question: How consistent is Alliance HPLC between systems and over time?
faqs.answer: Waters compared a carbamate separation run on two Alliance systems manufactured seven years apart and the results were equivalent, demonstrating both system-to-system and year-to-year consistency.

faqs.question: What is the maximum operating pressure?
faqs.answer: 5,000 psi, with a flow rate range up to 10 mL/min.

faqs.question: How many solvents can Alliance HPLC blend?
faqs.answer: Up to four, in any proportion, using Auto-Blend Technology, with 11 unique gradient profile curves for isocratic and gradient methods.

faqs.question: What is the sample carryover specification?
faqs.answer: ≤0.0025% for caffeine under specified conditions, and typically below 0.005% in routine operation, supported by active user-programmable needle wash.

faqs.question: What injection volumes are supported?
faqs.answer: 0.1 to 100 µL as standard, extending to 2 mL as an option.

faqs.question: How many samples can the system hold?
faqs.answer: Up to 120 vials, in an optional temperature-controlled environment running 4–40 °C, with STAT sample support and auto-addition.

faqs.question: Which detectors can be used with Alliance HPLC?
faqs.answer: Tunable UV, photodiode array, fluorescence, charged aerosol, refractive index, evaporative light scattering, electrochemical, conductivity, and mass spectrometry.

faqs.question: Can mass detection be added to an existing Alliance workflow?
faqs.answer: Yes. The ACQUITY QDa Detector integrates into the existing workflow, and Empower 3 combines UV/Vis and MS data to give mass information for each peak in the separation.

faqs.question: Can Alliance HPLC run sub-3 µm columns?
faqs.answer: Yes. CORTECS 2.7 µm solid-core columns improve resolution and reduce run times when transferring methods from 5 µm chemistries.

faqs.question: Which mobile phase chemistries are supported?
faqs.answer: Reversed-phase, normal-phase, GPC, SEC, and IEX, all on the same system.

faqs.question: What software controls the Alliance HPLC System?
faqs.answer: Empower Software and MassLynx Software, with third-party software packages also supported.

faqs.question: Is Alliance HPLC suitable for GMP laboratories?
faqs.answer: Yes. It supports Waters' Empower-based automated System Qualification Tool, which minimizes the time and cost of annual qualification against GMP, GLP, ISO 17025, and USP <1058>.

faqs.question: How much bench space does the system need?
faqs.answer: 45.7 cm wide (58.4 cm with column heater), 57.1 cm high, and 57.1 cm deep (64.8 cm with sample heater/cooler).

sections.description: The hardest question in a multi-instrument QC lab isn't whether one system performs — it's whether system four gives the same answer as system one, and whether either still matches what they produced three years ago.
body: Waters answered it directly: a carbamate separation run on two Alliance HPLC Systems manufactured seven years apart produced equivalent results.
That equivalence is what makes a method transferable across a fleet without revalidating each unit, and what keeps historical data comparable to current data during a trend review.
A newly manufactured Alliance and one several years into service behave as the same instrument, so age in the fleet isn't a variable that has to be tracked and compensated for.

High injection precision, repeatable and accurate flow rates, and exceptional retention time repeatability are the mechanisms underneath it — easy peak identification and precise quantification follow from them.

faqs.question: What mass range does the Xevo G3 QTof cover?
faqs.answer: The calibration range extends to m/z 16,000, which is what brings complex biologics into scope alongside small molecule work.

faqs.question: What is StepWave XS?
faqs.answer: An ion transmission technology that efficiently transmits low mass, labile species, increasing compound coverage and analytical fidelity for analytes that are otherwise easily lost.

faqs.question: What dynamic range does the system offer?
faqs.answer: Up to 5 orders of linear dynamic range for targeted analysis, and up to a 4× increase in in-spectrum dynamic range for untargeted and screening experiments.

faqs.question: What is the difference between linear and in-spectrum dynamic range?
faqs.answer: Linear dynamic range describes the concentration span over which a known analyte quantifies reliably. In-spectrum dynamic range describes how large an abundance difference can be resolved within a single spectrum, which matters when low-abundance components sit alongside high-abundance ones.

faqs.question: Can one instrument really handle both qualitative and quantitative work?
faqs.answer: That's the design intent — Waters positions it as a flexible multifunctional instrument delivering high-quality quantitative and qualitative data sets, maximizing system usage across both workflow types.

faqs.question: What is waters_connect?
faqs.answer: An informatics ecosystem harmonizing workflows across development, manufacturing, and QC, offering compliance-ready workflows with security-controlled access, full data traceability, and networked deployment.

faqs.question: How does the system support the transition from development to QC?
faqs.answer: Biomolecules and processes are characterized on the Xevo G3 QTof first, then transition to dedicated attribute monitoring assays either on the same system or on the BioAccord System with ACQUITY Premier, with waters_connect carrying the workflow.

faqs.question: What software controls the instrument?
faqs.answer: MassLynx for acquiring, analyzing, managing, and sharing nominal and exact mass MS and MS/MS data, and the waters_connect ecosystem for connected, compliance-ready workflows.

faqs.question: How robust is the instrument for high-throughput use?
faqs.answer: Updated ion optics design and optimized ion beam conditioning are engineered specifically to deliver consistent robustness and reproducibility, maintaining performance and productivity over a longer time period.

faqs.question: Which LC systems pair with the Xevo G3 QTof?
faqs.answer: Waters pairs it with ACQUITY Premier in its own materials, and it has been applied with ACQUITY UPLC I-Class PLUS and M-Class in published application work.

faqs.question: What is the Xevo TQ-S cronos used for?
faqs.answer: It's a tandem quadrupole mass spectrometer for routine quantitative LC-MS/MS analysis, applied to food safety, pesticide residues, nitrosamine quantitation in drug products, and other regulated quantitative testing where sample clean-up is part of the workflow.

faqs.question: How reliable is the instrument over a long run?
faqs.answer: A Waters mycotoxin study in wheat flour — a matrix that can contaminate LC-MS instrumentation — showed consistent performance across 5 days of continuous use and 1,000 injections, with peak area RSD of only 3–8%.

faqs.question: How often does the detector need replacing?
faqs.answer: Fewer than 1% of Waters' tandem quadrupole mass spectrometers launched between 2006 and 2022 require a detector replacement annually, based on their internal service history data.

faqs.question: What is the mass range and MRM speed?
faqs.answer: 2 to 2048 m/z, at 555 MRM/sec — which is faster than both the Xevo TQ-XS and Xevo TQ Absolute XR, each at 500 MRM/sec.

faqs.question: Where does cronos sit in the Xevo TQ line?
faqs.answer: It's the entry point on sensitivity, rated ★★ on Waters' five-point scale, below TQ-S micro (★★★), TQ-XS (★★★★), and TQ Absolute XR (★★★★★). Waters recommends it for accessible routine quantitative analysis with sample clean-up where capital expenditure is limited.

faqs.question: How is cronos different from the Xevo TQ-S micro?
faqs.answer: They share identical dimensions, mass range, MRM speed, StepWave optics, and acquisition modes. TQ-S micro is rated one step higher on sensitivity and adds APGC, ionKey, and nanoflow source compatibility; cronos uniquely adds ACQUITY Arc chromatographic compatibility.

faqs.question: Which ion sources are compatible?
faqs.answer: APCI, ASAP, ESCi, ESI as standard, and UniSpray. Sources can be changed to extend analytical capacity as demands shift.

faqs.question: Which LC systems can it pair with?
faqs.answer: ACQUITY Arc, ACQUITY Premier, ACQUITY UPC2, ACQUITY UPLC, and ACQUITY UPLC M-Class.

faqs.question: What acquisition modes are available?
faqs.answer: Full scan, product scan, precursor ion scan, constant neutral loss scan, multiple reaction monitoring (MRM), and RADAR — simultaneous full scan and MRM in one acquisition.

faqs.question: What software options are available?
faqs.answer: waters_connect for Quantitation and MassLynx v4.2, with LIMS and MassLynx SkyLine interfaces and MassLynx security supported.

faqs.question: What is Exception Focused Review?
faqs.answer: A waters_connect capability that focuses review on results needing attention rather than requiring equal review of everything, which Waters states can save up to 50% of data review time.

faqs.question: Are there compatibility restrictions with waters_connect?
faqs.answer: Yes. ACQUITY Arc, ACQUITY UPC2, ACQUITY UPLC M-Class, ASAP, and ESCi are marked by Waters as not available with waters_connect, so confirm the inlet and source combination against the software choice.

faqs.question: How much bench space does the instrument need?
faqs.answer: 35.6 x 60 x 93 cm (w x h x d), which Waters describes as 2–3× narrower than most other instruments in its class.

faqs.question: What are the power and heat requirements?
faqs.answer: Up to 35% lower electrical power consumption and up to 35% less heat produced than equivalent competitor products, reducing both utility cost and cooling load.

faqs.question: Is the instrument approved for regulated environments?
faqs.answer: Regulatory approval marks include CE, CB, NRTL (Canada/USA), and RCM, with MassLynx security supported for regulated data control.

sections.title: Product Information
sections.description: Xevo TQ-S cronos product information: quantitative performance, footprint efficiency, and software options.
body: Xevo TQ-S cronos is a tandem quadrupole mass spectrometer from the Xevo family, built around dependable performance with proven ion guide technology maintaining uptime as standard.

Waters recommends it for accessible routine quantitative analysis with sample clean-up, where capital expenditure is limited — the entry point of the Xevo TQ line rather than its sensitivity flagship.

A mycotoxin study in wheat flour, a complex matrix Waters identifies as one that can contaminate LC-MS instrumentation, showed consistent performance across 5 days of continuous use and 1,000 injections at only 3–8% RSD for peak areas.
Mass range is 2 to 2048 m/z, matching every other system in the Xevo TQ line.
MRM speed is 555 MRM/sec — higher than both the Xevo TQ-XS and Xevo TQ Absolute XR, which run at 500 MRM/sec.
Sensitivity is rated ★★ on Waters' five-point comparison scale, below TQ-S micro (★★★), TQ-XS (★★★★), and TQ Absolute XR (★★★★★).
Ion source transfer optics use StepWave, the same technology found on the TQ-S micro.
Six acquisition modes are supported: full scan, product scan, precursor ion scan, constant neutral loss scan, multiple reaction monitoring (MRM), and simultaneous full scan and MRM (RADAR).

Detection uses a low noise, off-axis, long life photomultiplier; Waters' internal service data on tandem quadrupoles launched between 2006 and 2022 shows fewer than 1% require an annual detector replacement.
Five ion sources are compatible: APCI, ASAP, ESCi, ESI, and UniSpray, with ESI as standard.
Chromatographic compatibility covers ACQUITY Arc, ACQUITY Premier, ACQUITY UPC2, ACQUITY UPLC, and ACQUITY UPLC M-Class.
Dimensions are 35.6 x 60 x 93 cm, which Waters describes as 2–3× narrower than most other instruments in its class.
Electrical power consumption is up to 35% lower and heat output up to 35% less than equivalent competitor products.
Two software platforms are available: waters_connect for Quantitation and MassLynx v4.2, with MassLynx security supported.
waters_connect includes Exception Focused Review (XFR), which Waters states can save up to 50% of data review time.
Third-party interfaces include LIMS and the MassLynx SkyLine interface.
Regulatory approval marks include CE, CB, NRTL (Canada/USA), and RCM.
Note that ACQUITY Arc, ACQUITY UPC2, ACQUITY UPLC M-Class, ASAP, and ESCi are marked by Waters as not available with waters_connect.

sections.title: Reliability Across a Full Campaign
sections.description: Peak sensitivity on a clean standard tells you what an instrument can do once. A quantitative lab needs to know what it does on injection 900, in a matrix that has been depositing residue since injection one.
body: Waters answered that specifically. A mycotoxin study in wheat flour — a matrix they explicitly name as one that can contaminate LC-MS instrumentation — ran 1,000 injections across 5 days of continuous use.
Peak area RSD held between 3 and 8% across that campaign, meaning the instrument's response didn't drift meaningfully as the source accumulated matrix.
Proven ion guide technology is what Waters credits for maintaining uptime as standard, and the Xevo family's inherent robustness is the design lineage behind it.

The detector data carries real provenance rather than being a general claim: fewer than 1% of Waters' tandem quadrupole mass spectrometers launched between 2006 and 2022 require a detector replacement on an annual basis, from their own service history.

A low noise, off-axis photomultiplier is the design choice behind that longevity — off-axis geometry keeps neutrals and photons off the detector surface, which is what shortens detector life on in-line designs.
sections.disclaimer: Share the matrix and the typical campaign length between maintenance windows, and expected performance gets discussed against the published mycotoxin study conditions.

sections.description: Acquisition time is only part of a quantitative workflow's cost. Data review is where analyst hours actually accumulate, particularly in regulated environments where every result needs looking at.

faqs.question: What is the Xevo TQ-S micro used for?
faqs.answer: It's a compact tandem quadrupole mass spectrometer for routine quantitative LC-MS/MS, applied across food testing, PFAS and environmental analysis, clinical research, cannabis testing, and pharmaceutical quantitation.

faqs.question: How often will the instrument need unplanned service?
faqs.answer: Waters' internal global service data shows customers on average need no unplanned service visit during the warranty period and for 3 years after. Planned scheduled Performance Maintenance visits are still recommended for trouble-free operation.

faqs.question: How reliable is performance over a long campaign?
faqs.answer: A mycotoxin study in wheat flour — a matrix that can contaminate LC-MS instrumentation — showed consistent performance across 5 days of continuous use and 1,000 injections, with peak area RSD of 5–9%.

faqs.question: How is Xevo TQ-S micro different from the Xevo TQ-S cronos?
faqs.answer: They share identical dimensions, mass range, MRM speed, StepWave optics, acquisition modes, and detector. TQ-S micro rates one step higher on sensitivity (★★★ versus ★★) and adds APGC, ionKey, and nanoflow ion sources plus APGC chromatographic compatibility. cronos uniquely adds ACQUITY Arc compatibility.

faqs.question: What is the mass range and MRM speed?
faqs.answer: 2 to 2048 m/z, at 555 MRM/sec — matching cronos and faster than both TQ-XS and TQ Absolute XR, each at 500 MRM/sec.

faqs.question: Where does TQ-S micro sit in the Xevo TQ line?
faqs.answer: Second on sensitivity, rated ★★★ on Waters' five-point scale, above cronos (★★) and below TQ-XS (★★★★) and TQ Absolute XR (★★★★★).

faqs.question: Which ion sources are compatible?
faqs.answer: APCI, APGC, ASAP, ESCi, ESI as standard, ionKey, nanoflow, and UniSpray.

faqs.question: Can the instrument do GC-MS work?
faqs.answer: Yes. The Atmospheric Pressure GC (APGC) source is a field upgrade that extends the platform to AP GC-MS, bringing GC-amenable compounds onto the same mass spectrometer.

faqs.question: Which LC systems can it pair with?
faqs.answer: ACQUITY Premier, ACQUITY UPC2, ACQUITY UPLC, ACQUITY UPLC M-Class, and APGC.

faqs.question: What acquisition modes are available?
faqs.answer: Full scan, product scan, precursor ion scan, constant neutral loss scan, MRM, and RADAR — simultaneous full scan and MRM in one acquisition.

faqs.question: What software options are available?
faqs.answer: waters_connect for Quantitation and MassLynx v4.2, with LIMS and MassLynx SkyLine interfaces and MassLynx security supported.

faqs.question: Are there compatibility restrictions with waters_connect?
faqs.answer: Yes. ACQUITY UPC2, ACQUITY UPLC M-Class, ASAP, ESCi, ionKey, and nanoflow are marked by Waters as not available with waters_connect, so confirm the source and inlet combination against the software choice.

faqs.question: How much bench space does the instrument need?
faqs.answer: 35.6 x 60 x 93 cm (w x h x d), which Waters describes as 2–3× narrower than other instruments in its class — identical to the Xevo TQ-S cronos.

faqs.question: What are the power and heat requirements?
faqs.answer: Up to 34% lower electricity consumption and associated heat production than other instruments in its class.

faqs.question: How often does the detector need replacing?
faqs.answer: Fewer than 1% of Waters' tandem quadrupole mass spectrometers launched between 2006 and 2022 require a detector replacement annually, based on their internal service history data.

faqs.question: Is the instrument approved for regulated environments?
faqs.answer: Regulatory approval marks include CE, CB, NRTL (Canada/USA), and RCM, with MassLynx security supported for regulated data control.

longForm.heroLead: That's not a design goal. It's what Waters' global service data shows customers using the Xevo TQ-S micro actually experience on average — through the warranty period and for three years beyond it. Scheduled Performance Maintenance still applies, but the unplanned call-out that stops a run mid-campaign is the exception rather than the pattern. Reliability under load backs it up. A mycotoxin study in wheat flour — a matrix Waters names outright as one that contaminates LC-MS instrumentation — ran 1,000 injections across five days of continuous use at 5–9% peak area RSD. What makes it a workhorse rather than just a dependable box is the range packed into 35.6 cm of bench. Rated one step above the cronos on sensitivity while occupying identical space, with APGC, ionKey, and nanoflow sources available alongside the standard five, and 555 MRM/sec for large panels. Waters calls it best value performance per square inch, and the specification supports the claim.

sections.title: Product Information
sections.description: Xevo TQ-S micro product information: sensitivity, uptime record, source flexibility, and software options.
body: Xevo TQ-S micro is a compact tandem quadrupole mass spectrometer from the inherently robust Xevo family, providing superior performance per square inch alongside exceptional analytical flexibility.
Waters positions it as a laboratory workhorse, offering best value performance per square inch of bench space with unrivalled flexibility to meet changing, growing, or unexpected analytical demands.

Waters' internal global service data shows customers using the instrument will on average not need an unplanned service visit during the warranty period and for 3 years after — with planned scheduled Performance Maintenance visits still recommended for trouble-free operation.

A mycotoxin study in wheat flour, a complex matrix Waters identifies as one that can contaminate LC-MS instrumentation, showed consistent performance across 5 days of continuous use and 1,000 injections at 5–9% RSD for peak areas.
Sensitivity is rated ★★★ on Waters' five-point scale — above Xevo TQ-S cronos (★★), below TQ-XS (★★★★) and TQ Absolute XR (★★★★★).
Mass range is 2 to 2048 m/z, and MRM speed is 555 MRM/sec, matching cronos and exceeding both TQ-XS and TQ Absolute XR at 500 MRM/sec.
Ion source transfer optics use StepWave, the same as cronos.
Eight ion sources are compatible: APCI, APGC, ASAP, ESCi, ESI as standard, ionKey, nanoflow, and UniSpray — three more than cronos, adding APGC, ionKey, and nanoflow.
Six acquisition modes are supported: full scan, product scan, precursor ion scan, constant neutral loss scan, MRM, and simultaneous full scan and MRM (RADAR).
Detection uses a low noise, off-axis, long life photomultiplier; fewer than 1% of Waters' tandem quadrupoles launched between 2006 and 2022 require an annual detector replacement.
Chromatographic compatibility covers ACQUITY Premier, ACQUITY UPC2, ACQUITY UPLC, ACQUITY UPLC M-Class, and APGC.
Dimensions are 35.6 x 60 x 93 cm — identical to cronos, and 2–3× narrower than other instruments in its class.
Electricity consumption and associated heat production are up to 34% lower than other instruments in its class.
Two software platforms are available: waters_connect for Quantitation and MassLynx v4.2, with MassLynx security supported.
waters_connect includes Exception Focused Review (XFR), which Waters states can save up to 50% of data review time.
Third-party interfaces include LIMS and the MassLynx SkyLine interface.
Regulatory approval marks include CE, CB, NRTL (Canada/USA), and RCM.
Note that ACQUITY UPC2, ACQUITY UPLC M-Class, ASAP, ESCi, ionKey, and nanoflow are marked by Waters as not available with waters_connect.

sections.title: Uptime and Reliability Under Load
sections.description: Instrument downtime in a quantitative lab is rarely just the repair. It's the requalification afterwards, the backlog that built during it, and the questions about whether data either side of the fault is comparable.
body: Waters makes a specific, checkable claim: customers using the Xevo TQ-S micro will on average not need an unplanned service visit during the warranty period and for 3 years after, sourced to their internal global service data on unplanned visits.

Their own caveat travels with it and matters — planned visits for regular scheduled Performance Maintenance are recommended to ensure trouble-free operation. The claim is about unplanned interruptions, not maintenance-free running.
Performance under matrix load is separately evidenced. The mycotoxin study in wheat flour ran 1,000 injections across 5 days of continuous use, holding peak area RSD between 5 and 9%.

Worth noting for anyone comparing directly: Xevo TQ-S cronos returned 3–8% RSD on the equivalent study. TQ-S micro's advantage over cronos sits in sensitivity, source range, and this uptime record rather than in campaign precision.

Detector longevity carries the same provenance as across the Xevo TQ line — fewer than 1% of Waters' tandem quadrupoles launched between 2006 and 2022 require an annual detector replacement. The off-axis photomultiplier geometry is the design reason: keeping neutrals and photons off the detector surface is what extends life relative to in-line arrangements.

Against the higher-sensitivity systems, the footprint gap is substantial — TQ-XS is 61 cm wide and TQ Absolute XR is 43 cm, against 35.6 cm here. These footprint and efficiency claims are stated against "other instruments in its class" without named comparators, so they read as directional rather than benchmarked.

sections.description: Xevo TQ-XS product information: sensitivity performance, software ecosystem, and regulatory readiness.
body: Coupled with ACQUITY UPLC, Xevo TQ-XS is built for routine quantitative workflows that need superior sensitivity, adaptability, and flexibility as analytical demands evolve.

StepWave XS ion source transfer optics sit specifically at this tier, positioned between the standard StepWave design on the TQ-S cronos and TQ-S micro, and the StepWave XR optics used on TQ Absolute XR.
Mass range covers 2 to 2048 m/z, with MRM speed reaching 500 transitions per second, supported by a low-noise, off-axis, long-life photomultiplier detector.
Six acquisition modes are available: full scan, product scan, precursor ion scan, constant neutral loss scan, multiple reaction monitoring (MRM), and simultaneous full scan and MRM (RADAR).

Ion source compatibility spans APCI, APGC, ASAP, ESCi, ESI, ionKey, Nanoflow, and UniSpray, matched to a chromatographic configuration compatibility list including ACQUITY Premier, ACQUITY UPC2, ACQUITY UPLC, ACQUITY UPLC M-Class, and APGC.
In a direct vancomycin comparison, average analyte area counts on Xevo TQ-XS came in more than 10 times higher than on Xevo TQ-S.
A representative liraglutide LLOQ chromatogram at 0.5 ng/mL, extracted from plasma, demonstrates the sensitivity and selectivity available at this tier.

Detector reliability runs high across the installed base, with less than 1% of Waters' tandem quadrupole mass spectrometers requiring a detector replacement annually, based on internal service data from units launched between 2006 and 2022.
Software options include MassLynx v4.2 and waters_connect for Quantitation, both supporting LIMS interfaces and MassLynx SkyLine interfaces, with MassLynx security included as standard.
Regulatory approval marks include CE, CB, NRTL (Canada/USA), and RCM.

faqs.question: What is the ACQUITY UPLC M-Class System used for?
faqs.answer: It's a nano- to microscale UPLC system for sample-limited LC-MS work, used primarily in proteomics, biomarker discovery, protein conformation analysis, and other applications where sample material is severely limited.

faqs.question: What flow rate range does M-Class cover?
faqs.answer: 200 nL/min to 100 µL/min, delivered without flow splitting.

faqs.question: Why does flow splitting matter?
faqs.answer: Splitting produces low flow by diverting most of an analytical pump's output, which makes the flow reaching the column dependent on restrictor and back pressure conditions. Direct, non-split delivery with pulse-less flow control gives increased retention time reproducibility instead.

faqs.question: What column inner diameters does the system support?
faqs.answer: Waters' body copy states 75 µm to 1.0 mm and the specification table states 75 µm to 4.6 mm. Confirm the exact range against the intended column set at configuration.

faqs.question: Can optical detection be used at all column sizes?
faqs.answer: Mass spectrometry supports the full column inner diameter range; optical detection applies to 300 µm to 1 mm I.D. columns.

faqs.question: Why does low flow increase sensitivity?
faqs.answer: Delivering the same quantity of analyte in less volume raises concentration at the source, improving sensitivity for any mass spectrometer without changing the instrument.

faqs.question: What is the sample flow path made from?
faqs.answer: The flow path is non-ferrous, with non-reactive surfaces maintaining sample integrity through the system.

faqs.question: What is the HDX Technology configuration for?
faqs.answer: Quantifying small changes in protein conformation, with an extended pressure range for higher efficiency separation and DynamX HDX Data Analysis Software integrating sample prep through sequence determination, D2 uptake curves, and comparison plots.

faqs.question: What is the 2D Technology configuration for?
faqs.answer: Expanding dynamic range and throughput through reversed-phase/reversed-phase 2D-LC, running the first dimension at pH 10 and the second at pH 2 with MS-compatible eluents.

faqs.question: What injection volumes does the system accept?
faqs.answer: 0.1 µL to 100.0 µL.

faqs.question: Does M-Class include column tracking?
faqs.answer: No. Column tracking is not provided on this system, unlike the analytical-scale ACQUITY systems that carry eCord Technology.

faqs.question: What is the operating pH range?
faqs.answer: 2 to 10 — narrower than the analytical-scale ACQUITY systems, which is worth checking against the intended mobile phase chemistry.

faqs.question: What software controls the system?
faqs.answer: MassLynx Software per the specification, with new drivers integrating the system into existing MassLynx workflows. Waters also publishes Empower and third-party driver pack certificates for the platform, so confirm the software scope at configuration.

faqs.question: What is the maximum sample capacity?
faqs.answer: Up to 21 plates with the Sample Organizer.

faqs.question: How much bench space does the system need?
faqs.answer: 34.3 cm wide, 69.7 cm high, and 71.2 cm deep in the µBSM, µSM-FL, TVM configuration.

longForm.heroLead: The usual route to nanoflow is splitting an analytical-scale pump's output down. It works, and it costs reproducibility and reliability — which is precisely the trade-off that stops labs from adopting low-flow LC-MS despite the sensitivity waiting on the other side. ACQUITY UPLC M-Class delivers 200 nL/min through 100 µL/min directly, without splitting. Automatic solvent flow control algorithms provide pulse-less flow, and retention time reproducibility follows from that rather than being fought for. Every part of the system was designed and tested to deliver the right flow for the right column, across inner diameters from 75 µm upward. For samples that are severely limited in amount or availability, that combination is the whole argument: higher sensitivity from any mass spectrometer, less sample volume consumed, increased dynamic range, and non-reactive surfaces that keep the sample intact on the way to the source.

comparison.disclaimer: These are specialists, not tiers. I-Class PLUS trades column capacity and multi-solvent blending for the lowest dispersion and carryover in the series — the right choice when the mass spectrometer or the separation is the binding constraint. H-Class PLUS trades some of that performance for six-column screening and nine-solvent blending, which is what method development needs. ACQUITY Premier addresses a different problem entirely: metal-sensitive analytes adsorbing to a stainless steel flow path, which neither H-Class nor I-Class resolves.

faqs.question: What is the ACQUITY UPLC I-Class PLUS System used for?
faqs.answer: It's a high-performance binary UPLC system built for maximum resolution and sensitivity, used particularly as an LC-MS front end in bioanalysis, impurity profiling, peptide characterization, and clinical research.

faqs.question: What is system band spread and why does 4 µL matter?
faqs.answer: System band spread is how much the flow path broadens a peak after the column has separated it. Waters compared a tetracaine impurity analysis on I-Class PLUS at 4 µL against a UHPLC system at 20 µL under identical conditions, achieving significantly better resolution on I-Class PLUS.

faqs.question: What is the maximum operating pressure?
faqs.answer: 18,000 psi, the highest in the ACQUITY UPLC PLUS Series, with a flow rate range up to 2.0 mL/min.

faqs.question: What is the sample carryover specification?
faqs.answer: Below 0.001% for caffeine under UV conditions, and manageable through programmable method settings for compatibility with the most sensitive mass spectrometers.

faqs.question: Why is I-Class PLUS recommended as a mass spectrometry inlet?
faqs.answer: Narrow peak widths improve both resolution and ionization efficiency, enhancing MS sensitivity, while high resolution minimizes interference from co-elutions and industry-leading carryover protects trace-level detection.

faqs.question: How many columns can the system hold?
faqs.answer: Up to two columns of 150 mm length and up to 4.6 mm internal diameter, with accurate temperature control across the entire column and active preheating.

faqs.question: What pump configuration does I-Class PLUS use?
faqs.answer: A Binary Solvent Manager delivering precise, accurate blending for up to four solvents with an integrated solvent-select valve.

faqs.question: What injector options are available?
faqs.answer: Flow-through needle and fixed loop, giving sample injection versatility depending on the application.

faqs.question: What are CORTECS columns and why pair them with this system?
faqs.answer: CORTECS 1.6 µm solid-core columns deliver exceptional efficiency and narrower peaks; paired with the system's ultra-low dispersion and 18,000 psi headroom, they produce higher peak capacity for the toughest samples.

faqs.question: How is I-Class PLUS different from H-Class PLUS?
faqs.answer: I-Class PLUS offers higher pressure (18,000 versus 15,000 psi) and lower carryover with the lowest dispersion in the series, but takes two columns and is binary only. H-Class PLUS offers up to six columns, nine-solvent quaternary blending, and automated method screening.

faqs.question: Does the system support annual qualification?
faqs.answer: Yes. The Waters Empower-based automated System Qualification Tool (SQT) minimizes the time and cost associated with annual qualification.

faqs.question: What software controls the system?
faqs.answer: Empower, MassLynx, waters_connect, the UNIFI Scientific Information System, and several third-party software packages.

faqs.question: Does the system handle metal-sensitive analytes?
faqs.answer: The sample flow path is stainless steel, so metal-sensitive analytes may require passivation. Where that's a recurring issue, the ACQUITY Premier System's inert MaxPeak HPS flow path is designed for exactly that problem.

faqs.question: What is multidimensional UPLC?
faqs.answer: A configuration allowing selective isolation across more than one separation dimension, improving characterization where a single dimension cannot resolve everything of interest.

faqs.question: What is the maximum sample capacity?
faqs.answer: Up to 20 plates with the Sample Organizer.

faqs.question: How much bench space does the system need?
faqs.answer: 34.3 cm wide, 71.1 cm high, and 71.2 cm deep in the QSM or BSM, SM-FTN, CHA configuration.

longForm.heroHook: 4 µL of band spread against 20 µL. Same sample, same conditions, different answer.
longForm.heroLead: Waters ran a tetracaine impurity analysis twice under identical conditions — once on ACQUITY UPLC I-Class PLUS with a system band spread of 4 µL, once on a UHPLC system with 20 µL. The resolution difference was significant, and it came entirely from the system, not the chemistry. That's the point of I-Class PLUS. Industry-leading ultra-low dispersion and delay volume produce narrow, ultra-efficient peaks — which is why it works as an inlet that improves the performance of any mass spectrometer. Narrow peaks mean better ionization efficiency, and carryover below 0.001% means the sensitivity a modern tandem quad or QTof is capable of doesn't get spent on baseline noise. 18,000 psi of pressure headroom pairs it with CORTECS 1.6 µm solid-core columns for peak capacity beyond what conventional UHPLC reaches. And Waters' Empower-based automated System Qualification Tool keeps annual qualification time and cost down in regulated environments.

Fast analysis with low delay volume — ultra low delay volume enables faster gradient delivery, helping shorten analysis time and reduce solvent consumption.
Multidimensional UPLC capability — supports multidimensional configurations for improved sample characterization and selective isolation.
Column tracking and sample capacity — eCord Technology records column information and usage, while the Sample Organizer supports up to 20 plates.
Simplified system qualification — the Waters Empower based System Qualification Tool helps reduce the time and cost associated with annual qualification.

faqs.answer: It's a UPLC system for method development and routine analysis, built to decrease time to result while increasing the depth and quality of information from sample analysis.

faqs.question: How much can scaling a method to UPLC save?
faqs.answer: Waters scaled the USP analysis of diclazuril and organic impurities from HPLC to UPLC, achieving a 4× reduction in run time and a 10× reduction in solvent consumption.

faqs.question: What is the difference between the Quaternary and Binary configurations?
faqs.answer: Quaternary blends up to nine solvents and automatically screens column and eluent combinations, built for method development. Binary offers the lowest system volume with high-pressure mixing, built for reproducible routine LC-MS.

faqs.question: Why does low dispersion matter if the system already runs at 15,000 psi?
faqs.answer: High pressure alone doesn't produce sharp peaks. System dispersion has to be matched to the narrow peak widths that sub-2 µm columns generate, or the resolution the chemistry provides is lost in the system.

faqs.question: What is Auto•Blend Plus Technology?
faqs.answer: It automates mobile phase formulation and allows pH and ionic strength to be screened as method parameters, significantly reducing time spent preparing mobile phases in the prep lab.

faqs.question: How many columns can be screened at once?
faqs.answer: Up to six columns of 150 mm length and up to 4.6 mm internal diameter, in independently temperature-controlled compartments with active preheating.

faqs.question: How many solvents can the system blend?
faqs.answer: Up to nine on the Quaternary Solvent Manager with the integrated solvent-select valve, or up to four on the Binary Solvent Manager.

faqs.question: Can methods be transferred from another LC system?
faqs.answer: Yes. Gradient SmartStart adjusts for system volume differences when transferring from an alternative LC system, without altering the method table.

faqs.question: What is the maximum operating pressure and flow rate?
faqs.answer: 15,000 psi, with an operating flow rate range up to 2.2 mL/min.

faqs.question: Which columns does the system support?
faqs.answer: Any analytical LC column, with particle sizes from sub-2 µm to 5 µm.

faqs.question: What is the sample carryover specification?
faqs.answer: ≤0.002% for caffeine under UV conditions, with direct inject sampling using a needle-in-flow-path design for an accurate seal at high pressure.

faqs.question: Does H-Class PLUS work with mass spectrometry?
faqs.answer: Yes. The Binary configuration is built for reproducible everyday LC-MS with any tandem quad or Q-ToF, and pairs with Waters tandem quadrupole technology for routine quantitative UPLC-MS/MS.

faqs.question: Does the system need passivation for metal-sensitive analytes?
faqs.answer: The sample flow path is stainless steel, so metal-sensitive analytes may require passivation. Where that's a recurring problem, the ACQUITY Premier System's inert MaxPeak HPS flow path is designed to remove the need entirely.

faqs.question: What software controls the system?
faqs.answer: Empower, MassLynx, waters_connect, the UNIFI Scientific Information System, and several third-party software packages.

faqs.question: What is the maximum sample capacity?
faqs.answer: Up to 20 plates with the Sample Organizer.

faqs.question: How much bench space does the system need?
faqs.answer: 34.3 cm wide, 71.1 cm high, and 71.2 cm deep in the QSM or BSM, SM-FTN, CHA configuration.

sections.title: UPLC Performance and Method Scaling
sections.description: High pressure and UPLC performance are not the same thing. A system rated to 15,000 psi can still produce broad peaks if its extra-column dispersion is wider than the peaks the column is generating.
body: True UPLC requires system dispersion matched to the peak widths associated with narrow-bore columns packed with sub-2 µm particles — that matching is the design premise here.

Waters showed the difference directly: the same method, the same column, run on a low-dispersion H-Class PLUS versus a higher-dispersion UHPLC system, with the resolution difference visible in the chromatogram.

The productivity case is quantified. Scaling the USP diclazuril and organic impurity analysis from HPLC through UHPLC to UPLC gave a 4× reduction in run time and a 10× reduction in solvent consumption.
Those two numbers move different budget lines: run time reduction increases sample throughput per instrument, solvent reduction cuts consumables spend and waste disposal cost per analysis.
Existing HPLC methods run on the system now, so the transition is gradual rather than a cliff — the lab keeps its validated work while modernizing selectively.
A separate transfer example showed analysis time going from 5 minutes to 3 through direct transfer without gradient delay, a 40% runtime reduction.
Gradient SmartStart handles system volume differences when methods arrive from another LC platform, without requiring the method table to be altered.

body: Advanced Performance LC System — builds on the reliability, ruggedness and configuration flexibility of the ACQUITY UPLC H Class PLUS and I Class PLUS systems.
MaxPeak HPS Technology — provides an inert sample flow path designed to reduce interactions between metal sensitive analytes and system surfaces, improving separation and detection.
Reduced analyte adsorption — helps minimize non specific adsorption that can cause peak broadening, tailing, variable results and analyte loss.
Improved peak shape — Waters reports a 54% reduction in peak tailing for T37 peptide analysis, supporting improved detection of deamidation impurities.
Improved detection of metal sensitive compounds — demonstrated reduced adsorption for phosphorylated peptides and improved peak area and peak shape for dexamethasone sodium phosphate.
First injection performance — designed to provide reproducible performance from the first injection, reducing the need for time consuming system and column passivation.
High pressure operation — supports pressures up to 15,000 psi across a flow rate range of 0.001 to 2.000 mL/min.
Wide operating pH range — supports an operating pH range of 1 to 12.5.
Binary and Quaternary configurations — available with both binary and quaternary pump options to suit different LC workflows.
Controlled solvent conditioning — active preheating is provided as standard for consistent solvent conditioning.
Flexible injection options — supports flow through needle and fixed loop injection, along with direct inject sampling for high precision applications.
Low carryover — provides sample carryover of ≤0.002%, supporting sensitive analytical workflows.
Controlled sample temperature — the sample compartment operates from 4 to 40 °C.
Flexible column capacity — supports up to six columns with lengths up to 150 mm and internal diameters up to 4.6 mm.
eCord column tracking — tracks and archives column usage to support method management and column history.
High sample capacity — the Sample Organizer supports up to 8,064 samples.
Multiple detection options — compatible with TUV, PDA eλ, FLR, charged aerosol, refractive index, evaporative light scattering and mass spectrometer detection.
Designed for metal sensitive analytes — the ACQUITY Premier System and ACQUITY Premier Columns are designed together to reduce analyte losses and improve repeatability.
LC MS compatibility — when paired with a Waters mass spectrometer, the system supports identification and quantification of unknown compounds and detection of trace components in complex samples.
Sustainable system design — the system carries an ACT label and incorporates renewable powered manufacturing, recycled content, responsible chemical management and sustainable packaging.

longForm.heroHook: Compact enough for the flow cabinet. Smart enough to count cells for you.
longForm.heroLead: Cell culture work happens in a sterile hood, on a schedule, usually more than once a day. A microscope that doesn't fit the cabinet, or that demands a manual cell count every single time, is friction the workflow doesn't need. Primovert is built to remove exactly that. The base model handles brightfield and phase contrast for living cells, unstained, exactly as they are. Add iLED fluorescence and GFP-labeled cells become visible too, switching contrast directly at the stand, no separate fluorescence unit to bolt on. Go one step further with Primovert digital, and a built-in 5 MP CMOS camera paired with AI-based analysis in ZEISS Labscope counts cells, measures confluency, and shares results, all with one click. Every version is compact enough to fit inside a laminar flow cabinet, so sterile technique never has to compete with getting a good look at the culture. What it replaces: manual cell counting and a separate fluorescence setup. What it adds with digital: one-click AI cell analysis and instant sharing beyond the sterile workspace. Where it lives: the bench, or the hood, whichever the culture actually needs.

faqs.question: What does pressing the Snap button actually do?

faqs.question: How does AI cell counting work in practice?
faqs.answer: Examine the culture as usual, then take a picture while moving across the vessel. The image is analyzed automatically, and a result, both visual and quantitative, arrives instantly.

faqs.question: Is it suitable for labs with multiple users of different experience levels?
faqs.answer: Yes, the system is built specifically for multi-user environments, with proper operation supported by design regardless of who is using it.
